-660.title: 660 BC
-660.events:
* Extreme [[solar particle event]] comparable with the event detected at AD [[774]]/[[775]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2019/mar/11/radioactive-particles-from-huge-solar-storm-found-in-greenland |title=Radioactive particles from huge solar storm found in Greenland  |work=[[The Guardian]] |author=Ian Sample |date=March 11, 2019 |access-date=March 14, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Multiradionuclide evidence for an extreme solar proton event around 2,610 B.P. (~660 BC) |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |author1=Paschal O'Hare |date=2019 |volume= 116|issue=13 |pages=5961–5966 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1815725116 |pmid=30858311 |pmc=6442557 |bibcode=2019PNAS..116.5961O |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* [[February 11]] - The accession date of the first [[Emperor of Japan]], [[Emperor Jimmu]], converted from the [[Japanese imperial year]] as calculated by the dates in the ''[[Nihon Shoki]].''

-663.title: 663 BC
-663.events:
* The [[Neo-Assyrian Empire|Assyrian Empire]] under [[Ashurbanipal]] drives the [[Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt|Kushites]] from Egypt and conquers the country.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/lapd/hd_lapd.htm|title=Egypt in the Late Period (ca. 712–332 B.C.) - Essay - Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History|date=October 2004 |publisher=The Metropolitan Museum of Art}}</ref>
* Siege of [[Tyre, Lebanon|Tyre]] by the Assyrians under Ashurbanipal.

-656.title: 656 BC
-656.events:
===By place===

==== Egypt ====

* [[Thebes, Egypt|Thebes]] submits to the Egyptian ruler [[Psamtik I]] of [[Sais, Egypt|Sais]], who has allied himself with [[Gyges of Lydia]] and employs [[Libya]]n soldiers in a rebellion against [[Assyria]]n rule with help from [[Caria]]n and [[Ionia]]n mercenaries. Psamtik permits the city's mayor [[Mentuemhat]] to retain his position, who is not only the most powerful Theban but also the fourth [[prophet]] of [[Amun|Amon]].
* Psamtik I extends his control over all [[Egypt]]. The [[Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt|Twenty-fifth Dynasty]], and subsequent [[Nubia]]n period, end in [[Ancient Egypt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/lapd/hd_lapd.htm|title=Egypt in the Late Period (ca. 712–332 B.C.) - Essay - Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History|date=October 2004 |publisher=The Metropolitan Museum of Art}}</ref>

==== Assyria ====

* King [[Shamash-shum-ukin]] of [[Babylon]] forms a secret [[Military alliance|alliance]] with [[Arab people|Arabs]], [[Aramaeans]], [[Elam]]ites, [[Persian people|Persians]], and [[Egyptians]] against his half brother [[Ashurbanipal]].

-667.title: 667 BC
-667.events:
=== By place ===

==== Middle East ====

* King [[Ashurbanipal]] of [[Assyria]] resumes his late father's attack on [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]] (see [[671 BC]]),  the [[Pharaoh]] [[Taharqa]]  withdraws to [[Thebes, Egypt|Thebes]], and [[Memphis, Egypt|Memphis]] is recaptured.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Saggs |first=Henry |title=The Greatness that was Babylon: A Survey of the Ancient Civilization of the Tigris-Euphrates Valley |date=1962 |publisher=Sidgwick and Jackson |edition=1st |language=English}}</ref> The Assyrians begin an offensive into [[Upper Egypt]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saite Dynasty Begins in Egypt {{!}} History {{!}} Research Starters {{!}} EBSCO Research |url=https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/history/saite-dynasty-begins-egypt |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=EBSCO |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Asia Minor ====

* [[Byzantium]] (modern [[Istanbul]]) is founded by [[Megara]]n colonists under [[Byzas]].

-662.title: 660s BC
-662.events:
* [[669 BC]]: [[Taharqa]], king of [[Kingdom of Kush|Kush]], invades and reconquers Egypt from the [[Neo-Assyrian Empire|Assyrian Empire]].
* 669 BC: [[Esarhaddon]], king of Assyria, dies in [[Harran]] on his way to recover Egypt.
* 669 BC: Argos defeats the Spartans at [[Battle of Hysiae (c. 669 BC)|Battle of Hysiae]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sealey |first=Raphael |author-link=Raphael Sealey |title=A History of the Greek City States, 700–338 B.C. |publisher=University of California Press |year=1976 |location=Berkeley |page=41}}</ref>
* [[668 BC]]: [[Ashurbanipal]], son of Esarhaddon, starts to rule Assyria.
* 668 BC: [[Shamash-shum-ukin]], son of [[Esarhaddon]], becomes King of [[Babylon]].
* 668 BC: [[Nineveh]], capital of [[Assyria]] becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from [[Thebes, Egypt|Thebes]] in [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]] (estimation).<ref>{{cite web | url=http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm | title=What Were the Largest Cities Throughout History? | access-date=2006-03-01 | archive-date=2016-08-18 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818124242/http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm | url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[667 BC]]: Traditional date of the founding of [[Byzantium]] by [[Megara]]n colonists under [[Byzas]].
* [[666 BC]]: [[Ashurbanipal]] sends a small Assyrian army corps to Egypt which recovers Lower Egypt from Taharqa's forces.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kitchen|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Kitchen|year=2015|title=The Third Intermediate Period in Egypt (1100–650 BC)|edition=3rd|publisher=Aris & Phillips Limited|location=Oxford|at=§§ 353|isbn=978-0-85668-298-8}}</ref>
* [[664 BC]]: First [[naval battle]] in [[Greece|Greek]] [[recorded history]], between [[Ancient Corinth|Corinth]] and [[Corcyra]].
* 664 BC: [[Tantamani]] succeeds his uncle Taharqa as king of Kush. He invades Egypt to try to take it back.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kitchen|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Kitchen|year=2015|title=The Third Intermediate Period in Egypt (1100–650 BC)|edition=3rd|publisher=Aris & Phillips Limited|location=Oxford|at=§ 354|isbn=978-0-85668-298-8}}</ref>
* 664 BC: [[Necho I]], puppet Pharaoh of Egypt, is killed by invading Kushite forces under Tantamani.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kitchen|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Kitchen|year=2015|title=The Third Intermediate Period in Egypt (1100–650 BC)|edition=3rd|publisher=Aris & Phillips Limited|location=Oxford|at=§§ 117, 138, 354|isbn=978-0-85668-298-8}}</ref>
* 664–663 BC: There was an extreme [[solar particle event]] comparable with the [[774–775 carbon-14 spike]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Multiradionuclide evidence for an extreme solar proton event around 2,610 B.P. (~660 BC) |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |author1=Paschal O'Hare |date=2019 |volume= 116|issue=13 |pages=5961–5966 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1815725116 |pmid=30858311 |pmc=6442557 |bibcode=2019PNAS..116.5961O |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Panyushkina |first1=Irina P. |last2=Jull |first2=A. J. Timothy |last3=Molnár |first3=Mihaly |last4=Varga |first4=Tamás |last5=Kontul’ |first5=Ivan |last6=Hantemirov |first6=Rashit |last7=Kukarskih |first7=Vladymir |last8=Sljusarenko |first8=Igor |last9=Myglan |first9=Vladymir |last10=Livina |first10=Valerie |date=2024-08-23 |title=The timing of the ca-660 BCE Miyake solar-proton event constrained to between 664 and 663 BCE |journal=Communications Earth & Environment |language=en |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=1–9 |article-number=454 |doi=10.1038/s43247-024-01618-x  |doi-access=free|pmid=39185327 |issn=2662-4435|pmc=11343717 |bibcode=2024ComEE...5..454P }}</ref> The estimated strength of the event is about 2 orders of magnitude stronger than anything that has been recorded instrumentally since the beginning of the Space Age.
* [[663 BC]]: Assyrian army captures and sacks [[Thebes, Egypt]], ending the [[Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt|Nubian period]] in Egypt.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kitchen|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Kitchen|year=2015|title=The Third Intermediate Period in Egypt (1100–650 BC)|edition=3rd|publisher=Aris & Phillips Limited|location=Oxford|at=§ 355|isbn=978-0-85668-298-8}}</ref>
* 660 BC: Traditional founding date of [[Japan]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]] on [[11 February]].
* [[660 BC]]: First known use of the [[Demotic Egyptian script|Demotic]] script.
* 660 BC: Mythical founding of the [[Imperial House of Japan|Japanese royal family]].

-652.title: 652 BC
-652.events:
=== Middle East ===
* [[Elam]] withdraws from her [[Military alliance|alliance]] with king [[Shamash-shum-ukin]] of [[Babylon]], who launches a premature attack on his half brother [[Ashurbanipal]] at year's end without waiting for reinforcements that have been promised by the [[Ancient Egypt|Egyptian]] king [[Psamtik I]].

=== Asia ===
* [[Guan Zhong]], Chinese [[chancellor]], urges [[Duke Huan of Qi]] to attack the small neighboring [[Xing (state)|State of Xing]] which is under attack from [[Quanrong|Quan Rong]] nomads. Later, he advises the duke not to ally with a [[vassal]] ruler's son who wishes to depose his father.

-664.title: 664 BC
-664.events:
* First [[Naval warfare|naval battle]] in Greek recorded history, between [[Ancient Corinth|Corinth]] and [[Corcyra]].<ref>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>
* [[Tantamani]] succeeds his uncle [[Taharqa]] as king of [[Kingdom of Kush|Kush]].
* Kushites invade Assyrian-controlled Egypt.
* The [[Neo-Assyrian Empire|Assyrians]] under [[Ashurbanipal]] [[Sack of Thebes|capture and sack Thebes, Egypt]].
* Psamtik I succeeds Necho I as ruler of Lower Egypt.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/lapd/hd_lapd.htm|title=Egypt in the Late Period (ca. 664–332 B.C.) - Essay - Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History|date=October 2004 |publisher=The Metropolitan Museum of Art}}</ref>
* Solar superstorm in 664 BCE recorded in tree rings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://earthsky.org/earth/solar-superstorm-in-664-bce-recorded-in-tree-rings-carbon-14/|title=Solar superstorm in 664 BCE recorded in tree rings|date=28 November 2024 |publisher=Earthsky Communications Inc.}}</ref>

-668.title: 668 BC
-668.events:
=== By Place ===

==== Middle East ====

* King [[Ashurbanipal]] puts down an Egyptian rebellion. He drives out Egypt's [[Ethiopia]]n king [[Taharqa]], and restores [[Necho I]] as [[governor]] of [[Sais, Egypt|Sais]] in the [[Nile Delta]].
* [[Nineveh]], capital of [[Assyria]] becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from [[Thebes, Egypt|Thebes]] in [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]] (estimation).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rosenberg|first1=Matt T.|title=Largest Cities Through History|url=http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm|access-date=2013-08-19|archive-date=2016-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818124242/http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[Shamash-shum-ukin]], second son of the late Assyrian king [[Esarhaddon]], becomes king of [[Babylon]].

-665.title: 665 BC
-665.events: * [[Elam]]ite king [[Urtak (king of Elam)|Urtak]] launches a surprise attack against [[Babylonia]] but is successfully driven back

-666.title: 666 BC
-666.events:
===By place===
====Middle East====

* King [[Ashurbanipal]] undertook a campaign to Egypt.<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jTOxEAAAQBAJ&dq=666+BC+Ashurbanipal&pg=PA320 | isbn=978-0-19-068763-2 | title=The Oxford History of the Ancient Near East | date=14 April 2023 | publisher=Oxford University Press }}</ref>
*One theory is that this is the year [[Psammitichus I]] ascended the throne.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jzEuAAAAYAAJ&dq=666+BC&pg=PA606 | title=The Quarterly Review of the Methodist Episcopal Church, South | date=1856 | publisher=John Early }}</ref>

-669.title: 669 BC
-669.events:
*[[Taharqa]], king of [[Kingdom of Kush|Kush]], invades and reconquers Egypt from the [[Neo-Assyrian Empire|Assyrian Empire]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Welsby |first=Derek A. |title=The Kingdom of Kush |publisher=British Museum Press |year=1996 |isbn=0-7141-0986-X |location=London, UK |pages=158}}</ref>
*[[Esarhaddon]] dies in Harran while on his way to recover [[Egypt]] from the Kushites.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Saggs |first=Henry |title=The Greatness that was Babylon: A Survey of the Ancient Civilization of the Tigris-Euphrates Valley |date=1962 |publisher=Sidgwick and Jackson |edition=1st |language=English}}</ref>
*A [[transit of Venus]] occurs.

-661.title: 661 BC
-661.events: * Queen [[Macha]] of Ireland begins to rule alone, after the death of her husband [[Áed Rúad, Díthorba, and Cimbáeth|Cimbaeth]], according to the ''[[Annals of the Four Masters]]''.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Dooley |editor1-first=Ann |editor2-last=Sheehan |editor2-first=Sarah |title=Constructing Gender in Medieval Ireland |date=5 December 2013 |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |isbn=9781137076380 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Constructing_Gender_in_Medieval_Ireland/fgyxAgAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=macha+of+ireland+661&pg=PT166&printsec=frontcover}}</ref>

-657.title: 657 BC
-657.events:
===By place===

==== Asia Minor ====

* King [[Gyges of Lydia]] establishes a [[Government monopoly|state monopoly]] in metal [[coin]]age, making it illegal for individuals to issue the bean-shaped lumps of [[electrum]] used as a medium of exchange in place of commodities (approximate date).

==== Greece ====

* [[Cypselus]] becomes the first [[tyrant]] of [[Ancient Corinth|Corinth]].

==== China ====

* The [[Li Ji Unrest]], a series of events that ends in [[651 BC]],<ref>{{cite journal |title=Historical and Cultural References |journal=Idle Talk under the Bean Arbor |date=31 December 2017 |pages=223–246 |doi=10.1515/9780295999982-021 |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/unauthorizedDownload/10.1515/9780295999982-021?action=Downloading+PDF&countDenial=true&download=true |access-date=15 March 2026}}</ref> initiates when [[Li Ji (concubine)|Li Ji]], the concubine of [[Duke Xian of Jin]], attempts to have her son [[Xiqi]] placed on the [[throne]] of [[Jin (Chinese state)|Jin]].

-658.title: 658 BC
-658.events:
* End of the rule of Duke Zhuang in [[Yan (state)|Yan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chinese History - The Feudal State of Yan|url=http://www.chinaknowledge.de/History/Zhou/rulers-yan.html|publisher=ChinaKnowledge}}</ref>
* End of the rule of Miltiades in [[Athens]].
* End of the rule of [[Énna Derg]] in [[Ireland]] (according to ''Foras Feasa ar Éirinn'' by [[Geoffrey Keating]]).

-659.title: 659 BC
-659.events: * The enemy city of [[Alba Longa]] is destroyed by the Romans.<ref>{{cite book |last=Blits |first=Jan H. |date=2013 |title=The Heart of Rome: Ancient Rome's Political Culture |publisher=Lexington Books |isbn=9780739189214 |page=169 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Heart_of_Rome/CZBWAgAAQBAJ |access-date=August 22, 2026}}</ref>

-651.title: 651 BC
-651.events:
=== Middle East ===

* King [[Ashurbanipal]] defeats the Babylonian army of his half brother [[Shamash-shum-ukin]] and surrounds the fortified city of [[Babylon]]. Beginning a 3-year [[siege]] during which the [[Neo-Assyrian|Assyrian]]s will defeat Shamash-shum-ukin's allies.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Brereton |first=Gareth |title=I am Ashurbanipal, King of the World, King of Assyria |year=2018 |isbn=978-0-500-48039-7}}</ref>
* King [[Teispes]] of [[Anshan (Persia)|Anshan]] ([[Iran|Persia]]) sends help to Shamash-shum-ukin but his heirs will later be obliged to accept Assyrian overlordship.

=== Asia ===

* The [[Li Ji Unrest]] ends, resulting in the deaths of [[Li Ji (concubine)|Li Ji]], [[Duke Xian of Jin|Xian]], [[Xiqi]] and [[Zhuozi (Jin)|Zhuozi]]. After the revolt [[Duke Hui of Jin]] becomes ruler of the [[Jin (Chinese state)|State of Jin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sturgeon |first=Donald |title=Lie Nü Zhuan : Villainous Concubines : Jin Xiang Li Ji - Chinese Text Project |url=https://ctext.org/lie-nv-zhuan/jin-xian-li-ji |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=ctext.org |language=zh-TW}}</ref>
* [[King Xiang of Zhou|Zhou Xiang Wang]] becomes king of the [[Zhou dynasty]] of [[China]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Loewe, Shaughnessy |first=Michael, Edward |title=The Cambridge History of Ancient China: From the Origins of Civilization to 221 BC |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1999 |isbn=978-0-521-47030-8 |edition=1st}}</ref>

-653.title: 653 BC
-653.events:
===By place===

==== Middle East ====
* [[Elam]]ite forces attack southern [[Babylon]]. A large [[Assyria]]n army sent by king [[Ashurbanipal]] defeat the Elamites, in the [[Battle of Ulai]], and kill their king, [[Teumman]]. He is succeeded by his nephew [[Ummanigash (son of Urtak)|Ummanigash]].

-654.title: 654 BC
-654.events:
* [[Enna]] is founded in Sicily.
* Traditional date of the foundation of [[Abdera, Thrace|Abdera]] in [[Thrace]] by colonists from [[Clazomenae]].<ref name=Bickerman-198>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>
* Traditional date of foundation of [[Akanthos (Greece)|Akanthos]] by [[Andros, Greece|Andros]].<ref name=Bickerman-198/>
* Traditional date of foundation of [[Lampsacus]] by [[Phocaea]].<ref name=Bickerman-198/>

-655.title: 655 BC
-655.events:
===By place===

==== Mesopotamia ====

* The [[Assyria|Assyrian]] army invade [[Elam]] and overtake its twin capital cities [[Darreh Shahr Ancient City|Madaktu]] and [[Susa]] and install a king that is pro-Assyrian on the throne.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Saggs |first=Henry |title=The Greatness that was Babylon: A Survey of the Ancient Civilization of the Tigris-Euphrates Valley |date=1962 |publisher=Sidgwick and Jackson |edition=1st |language=English}}</ref>

==== Greece ====
* [[Stagira (ancient city)|Stagira]] on the [[Chalkidiki]] peninsula is founded by [[Ionia]]n settlers from [[Andros, Greece|Andros]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rashed |first=Marwan |date=2022 |title=ARISTOTE ET ATHÈNES D'APRÈS PTOLÉMÉE «AL-GHARIB» |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/48746865 |journal=Revue des Études Grecques |volume=135 |issue=1 |pages=17 |via=[[JSTOR]]}}</ref>

-648.title: 648 BC
-648.events:
=== Middle East ===

* [[Babylon]] falls to [[Assyria]]n forces after a 3-year [[siege]] (see [[651 BC]]); starved out by his half brother [[Ashurbanipal]], king [[Shamash-shum-ukin]] commits [[suicide]] in his burning palace, as the Assyrians slaughter his city's [[garrison]] and much of its population.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Saggs |first=Henry |title=The Greatness that was Babylon: A Survey of the Ancient Civilization of the Tigris-Euphrates Valley |date=1962 |publisher=Sidgwick and Jackson |edition=1st |language=English}}</ref>

=== Greece ===

* [[Messenia]]ns in the [[Peloponnese (region)|Peloponnese]] revolt against [[Sparta]] under the leadership of king [[Aristomenes]], beginning a struggle that will continue until [[631 BC]].
* [[April 6]] - The earliest [[solar eclipse]] to be chronicled by the Greeks is observed.<ref>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>

-606.title: 606 BC
-606.events: * [[King Ding of Zhou]] succeeds [[King Kuang of Zhou]] the ruler of the [[Zhou dynasty]].

-625.title: 625 BC
-625.events:
* [[Cyaxares]] becomes king of the Medes (approximate date)
* [[Orientalizing period]] of vases ends in [[Ancient Greece]] (approximate date).
* A wine pitcher ([[oenochoe]]) from Rhodes is finished, having been begun in [[650 BC]].

-626.title: 626 BC
-626.events:
* [[Jeremiah]] begins his ministry in the [[Kingdom of Judah]].
* [[23 November]] -- [[Nabopolassar]] revolts against his Assyrian overlords, establishing the [[Neo-Babylonian Empire]].<ref>Date based on the Babylonian computation. E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 157</ref>

-631.title: 631 BC
-631.events:
*[[Cyrene, Libya|Cyrene]], a Greek colony in present-day [[Libya]], [[North Africa]], is founded by emigrants from the island of [[Thera]] (approximate date).<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |title=Cyrene |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Cyrene-ancient-Greek-colony-Libya |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>
*[[Sadyattes]] becomes king of [[Lydia]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

-632.title: 632 BC
-632.events: *[[Cylon of Athens|Cylon]], Athenian [[Nobility|nobleman]], seizes the [[Acropolis, Athens|Acropolis]] in a failed attempt to become king.<ref>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>

-637.title: 637 BC
-637.events: * [[Sadyattes]] becomes king of [[Lydia]].<ref name="Dale">{{cite journal |last=Dale |first=Alexander |date=2015 |title=WALWET and KUKALIM: Lydian coin legends, dynastic succession, and the chronology of Mermnad kings |url=https://www.academia.edu/29719834 |journal=Kadmos |volume=54 |issue= |pages=151–166 |doi=10.1515/kadmos-2015-0008 |access-date=10 November 2021}}</ref>

-640.title: 640 BC
-640.events:
=== Europe ===
* [[Theagenes of Megara|Theagenes]] becomes tyrant at [[Megara]].<ref name=Bickerman-198>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>
* [[Colaeus|Kolaios of Samos]] reaches the [[Strait of Gibraltar]].<ref name=Bickerman-198/>
* The interregnum in Rome ends. [[Ancus Marcius]] becomes the fourth king of [[Rome]]

=== Middle East ===
* King [[Ashurbanipal]] of [[Assyria]] achieves a great victory over [[Elam]]. He captures its last king, [[Humban-haltash III|Khumma-Khaldash III]], and lays waste to the country.
* King [[Teispes]] dies after a 35-year reign in which he has ruled the Elamite city of [[Anshan (Persia)|Anshan]] after being freed from [[Medes|Median]] supremacy.
* [[Josiah]], reigns as the sixteenth King of Judah (r. 640 - 609 BCE)

-641.title: 641 BC
-641.events:
* [[Josiah]] becomes [[Kings of Judah|king]] of [[kingdom of Judah|Judah]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Josiah|title=Josiah {{!}} king of Judah|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2018-12-13}}</ref>
* [[Tullus Hostilius]] dies, beginning the interregnum.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://dante.udallas.edu/hutchison/Seven_kings/king_hostilius.htm|title=Tullus Hostilius|website=dante.udallas.edu|access-date=2018-12-13|archive-date=2018-09-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928091427/http://dante.udallas.edu/hutchison/Seven_kings/king_hostilius.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

-647.title: 647 BC
-647.events:
=== Middle East ===
* [[Elam]] refuses to extradite an [[Arameans|Aramaean]] prince, giving the king [[Ashurbanipal]] of [[Assyria]] an excuse to invade the country.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}} He sacks the city of [[Susa]].<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Álvarez-Mon |editor1-first=Javier |editor2-last=Garrison |editor2-first=Mark B. |title=Elam and Persia |date=23 June 2011 |publisher=Penn State University Press |isbn=9781575066127 |page=357 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Elam_and_Persia/9JUFEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=susa&pg=PA357&printsec=frontcover}}</ref>
* Ashurbanipal and his Queen in the Garden, from the palace at [[Nineveh]] (modern [[Kuyunjik]], Iraq), is made. It is now at the [[British Museum]], [[London]].<ref>{{cite book |author1=Harry Francis Mallgrave |title=Building Paradise Episodes in Paradisiacal Thinking |date=29 September 2011 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=9781000449242 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Building_Paradise/sFw7EAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Ashurbanipal+and+his+Queen+in+the+Garden+647&pg=PT40&printsec=frontcover}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Paradise on earth: the gardens of Ashurbanipal |url=https://www.britishmuseum.org/blog/paradise-earth-gardens-ashurbanipal |website=British Museum |date=4 October 2018}}</ref>

-609.title: 609 BC
-609.events:
* The [[Medes]] and the [[Babylonia]]ns defeat the Assyrians under [[Ashur-uballit II]] and capture [[Harran]]. [[Ashur-uballit II]], the last king of [[Assyria]], disappears from history.
* [[Battle of Megiddo (609 BC)|Battle of Megiddo]]—King [[Josiah]] is killed fighting against [[Necho II]], who was on his way to aid the [[Assyria]]n state.
* King [[Jehoahaz of Judah|Jehoahaz]] succeeds his father [[Josiah]] as king of Judah, though he is killed by Necho II, who instead installs Jehoahaz's brother [[Jehoiakim]].
*The [[Persian Gulf]] recedes by a large portion, extending the [[Tigris]] and [[Euphrates]] rivers by 187 mi (300 km).

-636.title: 636 BC
-636.events: * [[Duke Wen of Jin]] becomes ruler of the [[Jin (Chinese state)|State of Jin]] in [[Zhou dynasty]] [[China]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Barnhart |first1=Richard M. |title=Mandate of Heaven Emperors and Artists in China : Chinese Painting and Calligraphy from The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York |date=1996 |publisher=Museum Rietberg |isbn=9783907070635 |page=39 |url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Mandate_of_Heaven/rKRHAQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=636&dq=636&printsec=frontcover}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=China's Terracotta Warriors: The First Emperor's Legacy |date=2012 |publisher=Minneapolis Institute of Arts |isbn=9780980048490 |page=21 |url=https://archive.org/details/chinasterracotta0000liuy/page/20/mode/2up}}</ref>

-628.title: 628 BC
-628.events: * Traditional date of the foundation of [[Selinus]] by [[Megara Hyblaea]].<ref>E.J. Bickerman, Chronology of the Ancient World (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>

-605.title: 605 BC
-605.events:
*[[Battle of Carchemish]]: [[Nebuchadnezzar II|Crown Prince Nebuchadnezzar]] defeats the allied armies of [[Egypt]] and former [[Assyria]], securing the Babylonian conquest of Assyria (approximate date).<ref name="OBA">{{cite encyclopedia |last=Curtis  |first=Adrian |date=2007 |title=Babylonian Empire |url=https://www.oxfordreference/view/10.1093/acref/9780191001581.001.0001/acref-9780191001581-chapter-14. |encyclopedia=Oxford Bible Atlas |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=19 February 2026 |isbn=9780191001581 |edition=4th}}</ref>
*[[Battle of Hamath]]: [[Nebuchadnezzar II]] defeats the remainder of the Egyptian army after the Battle of Carchemish.
*[[Nebuchadnezzar II]] succeeds his father [[Nabopolassar]] as king of [[Babylonia]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last= |first= |orig-year=2004 |date=2014 |title=Nebuchadnezzar II |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780199546091.001.0001/acref-9780199546091-e-8023|encyclopedia=World Encyclopedia |location= |publisher=Philip's |access-date=19 February 2026 |isbn=9780199546091}}</ref><ref name="OBA" />

-621.title: 621 BC
-621.events: * Draco's laws, the first written laws for Athens (approximate year)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Solon | access-date=February 24, 2024 | title=Solon | series=Encyclopædia Britannica}}</ref>

-627.title: 627 BC
-627.events:
* [[Battle of Xiao]], between the states of [[Jin (Chinese state)|Jin]] and [[Qin (state)|Qin]] in China.
* Traditional date for the foundation of [[Epidamnus]] by [[Ancient Corinth|Corinth]], today [[Durrës]] in [[Albania]].<ref>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>
* [[Sinsharishkun]] succeeds his brother [[Ashur-etil-ilani]] as king of [[Assyria]] (approximate date).

-645.title: 645 BC
-645.events: * The [[Spring and Autumn Annals]], a Chinese book of records, mentions that on December 24 of this year there were five meteors in the sky. It was the first Chinese observation of meteors.

-644.title: 644 BC
-644.events:
=== Asia Minor ===
* Cimmerian forces from [[Anatolia]] conquer [[Sardis]] and reach the peak of their power. King [[Gyges of Lydia]] has spent most of his 28-year reign fighting his southern and western neighbors in an effort to gain [[suzerainty]] over all of Western [[Asia Minor]]. He has helped the rebellion of Psamtik I, but he receives no support from his erstwhile Assyrian ally Ashurbanipal. Gyges falls in a battle against the [[Cimmerians]] under king [[Tugdamme]] (approximate date). 
* [[Ardys of Lydia|Ardys]] succeeds his father Gyges as the second Mermnad king of [[Lydia]]. During his reign he finds payment of [[tribute]] to [[Assyria]] preferable to rule by the Cimmerians, who will be routed a few decades later.

-603.title: 603 BC
-603.events:
=== Science and technology ===
* In the second year of his reign, [[Nebuchadnezzar II]] proclaimed the [[intercalary month]] Ululu II, which begins on September 6.<ref name=":0">Date specification in the [[Gregorian calendar]]; In the [[Julian calendar]] system, 7 days must be added to the Gregorian date. Dating basis are the [https://web.archive.org/web/20141108155909/http://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/phase/phases-0699.html NASA data] considering the T-delta. For Babylonia, the time zone surcharge of 3 hours must be taken into account in addition to ''Universal Time'' (UT)</ref> 
* In the [[Babylonian calendar]], the [[Akitu|Babylonian New Year]] of Nisannu 1 falls on January 14–15. March; the full moon in Nisannu on the 27–28 March and the 1st Tašritu on the 6–7 October.<ref name=":0" />

-649.title: 649 BC
-649.events:
* A revolt led by [[Shamash-shum-ukin]] is crushed by the [[Assyria]]ns.
* Indabigash succeeds Tammaritu as a king of the [[Elamite Empire]].
* Traditional date of the foundation of [[Himera]] by [[Zancle]].<ref>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>

-650.title: 650 BC
-650.events:
* A [[Climate change (general concept)|climate change]] occurs in [[Europe]], affecting all the [[Bronze Age]] cultures with colder and wetter climate, and tribes from [[Scandinavia]] migrate south into the European [[continent]].
* Wine pitcher ([[oenochoe]]) from [[Rhodes]] is begun, finished in [[625 BC]]. It is now at the [[Museum of Fine Arts, Boston|Museum of Fine Arts]], [[Boston]].
* The city of [[Ancient Carthage]] acquires independence from [[Tyre, Lebanon|Tyre]].
*Thales discovered the first theorems related to circles.
*[[Second Messenian War]] ended in 650.<ref>{{Cite web |title=World History 700 – 600 BC — HistoryCentral |url=https://www.historycentral.com/dates/700bc.html |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=www.historycentral.com}}</ref>

-601.title: 601 BC
-601.events:
*Approximate date of the foundation of [[Perinthus]] by settlers from [[Samos]].<ref>E.J. Bickerman, ''Chronology of the Ancient World'' (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1968), p. 198</ref>
*The [[Jewish–Babylonian war]] begins between the [[Kingdom of Judah]] and [[Babylonia]]. It ends in 586 BC.

-622.title: 622 BC
-622.events: * The finding of one of the five books of Moses in Jerusalem by king [[Josiah]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ford |first1=Clayton Howard |title=Who Really Wrote the Bible? |date=February 2010 |publisher=Tate Publishing & Enterprises, LLC |isbn=9781615662241 |pages=32-33 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Who_Really_Wrote_the_Bible/I7tM8qfETOcC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=five+books+of+Moses+622+bc&pg=PA33&printsec=frontcover}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Keller |first1=Werner |author-link=Werner Keller (writer)|title=The Bible as History |date=1982 |publisher=Bantam |isbn=9780553279436 |page=441 |url=https://archive.org/details/bibleashistory0000kell_g4g1/page/440/mode/2up}}</ref>

-560.title: 560 BC
-560.events:
* [[Peisistratus]] seizes the Acropolis in [[Classical Athens|Athens]], becoming the city's tyrant for the first time.<ref name="ECB3">{{cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Peisistratus | title=Peisistratus Tyran of Athens |author=Chester G. Starr|publisher= encyclopaedia britannica | access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref>
* Calf bearer ([[Moscophoros]]),<ref name= MOS1 group="N">Date of creation varies</ref> from the [[Acropolis]], [[Athens]] is made. It is now displayed at the [[Acropolis Museum]], [[Athens]] (approximate date).<ref name="GRA1">{{cite web| url=http://www.theacropolismuseum.gr/en/content/male-statues |title=Male statues. Calf bearer - Around 570 BC | author=Acropolis Museum| access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref><ref name="GI1">{{cite web| url=http://www.gettyimages.de/detail/foto/moschophoros-calf-bearer-marble-votive-statue-offered-stock-fotografie/586895089 | title= Calf beareer, 560 –570 BC |work=Getty Images | access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref>
* Berlin [[Kore (sculpture)|Kore]], begun in [[570 BC]], is finished. It is now displayed in [[Germany]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/artifact?name=Berlin+1750&object=sculpture | title=Berlin 1750 (Sculpture) | access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref>

-600.title: 600 BC
-600.events:
=== By place ===
==== India ====

* Lord [[Mahavira|Mahavir]], the last and 24th Tirthankar, of the ancient Indian religion, [[Jainism]] was born.

==== Middle East ====

*[[Zoroaster]]'s religion becomes popular in Persia. (approximate date)
*[[Smyrna]] is sacked and destroyed by [[Alyattes of Lydia|Alyattes I]]. (approximate date)
*The country of [[Armenia]] is created. (approximate date)

==== Western Europe ====
*The first dwelling at Emain Macha (now [[Navan Fort]]) is built (approximate date).
*[[Milan]] is founded by [[Celts]].
*[[Capua]] is founded by [[Etruscan civilization|Etruscans]]. (approximate date)
*[[Naples]] is founded by the Greeks. (approximate date)<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Jacob Edward |title=Roman Splendor in Pompeii |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/roman-splendor-in-pompeii-59083755/ |website=Smithsonian Magazine |date=15 March 2009}}</ref>
*[[Pompeii]] is founded. (approximate date)<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |title=Pompeii |encyclopedia=Chambers's Encyclopædia A Dictionary of Universal Knowledge |pages=305 |year=1892 |publisher=W. & R. Chambers |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Chambers_s_Encyclop%C3%A6dia/BPlBAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=0 |volume=8}}</ref>
*The Etruscans seize possession of [[Rome]], making it into a prosperous trade center. (approximate date)
*Victorious over the [[Carthaginians]] in a naval battle, the Greeks of [[Phocaea]] establish the city of [[Marseille]] in today's [[France]].
*[[Athens]] is suffering severe economic problems (approximate date).

==== North America ====
*The calendrical system begins appearing in areas with strong [[Olmec]] influence, continuing to appear until [[500 BC]] (approximate date).

=== By topic ===
==== Art and architecture ====
*[[Archaic period in Greece|Archaic period]] of sculpture begins in [[Greece]] (approximate date).
*[[Kouros]] (representation of a male youth) begins to be made, being finished in [[580 BC]] (approximate date).
*[[Pitcher (container)]] ([[olpe (container)|olpe]]), from [[Ancient Corinth|Corinth]], is made. It is now at [[The British Museum]], [[London]]. (approximate date)
*The [[Temple of Artemis]], [[Korkyra (polis)|Korkyra]] in [[Corfu]] begins to be built (approximate date).
*The [[Doric order|Doric]] and [[Ionic order]]s are well developed (approximate date).

-552.title: 552 BC
-552.events: *The [[Battle of Hyrba]] is fought between the [[Medes|Medians]] and the Persians led by [[Cyrus the Great]].<ref>{{cite book |editor-last1=Showalter |editor-first1=Dennis |title=Ancient Wars C.2500BCE–500CE |date=16 September 2013 |publisher=Amber Books Limited |isbn=9781782741176 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Ancient_Wars_c_2500BCE_500CE/BdKmAgAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=hyrba}}</ref>

-553.title: 553 BC
-553.events: * [[Cyrus the Great|Cyrus II of Persia]] revolts against [[Astyages|Astyages of the Medes]].<ref>{{cite book |title=From Cyrus to Alexander: A History of the Persian Empire |year=2002 |publisher=Eisenbrauns |last=Briant |first=Pierre |author-link=Pierre Briant |pages=31 |isbn=978-1-57506-120-7 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lxQ9W6F1oSYC&q=false |access-date=10 November 2020 |archive-date=14 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220514211442/https://books.google.com/books?id=lxQ9W6F1oSYC&q=false |url-status=live}}</ref>

-556.title: 556 BC
-556.events:
* [[Labashi-Marduk]] succeeds [[Neriglissar]] as king of [[Babylon]].
* [[Pisistratus]] is expelled to [[Euboea]] from [[Athens]], and makes his fortune from [[Thrace]]'s mines.
* [[Nabonidus]] succeeds Labashi-Marduk as king of [[Babylon]].

-579.title: 579 BC
-579.events: * [[Servius Tullius]] succeeds [[Lucius Tarquinius Priscus]] as king of Rome upon the latter's assassination. (traditional date)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucius Tarquinius Priscus |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/oi/authority.20110803102143242 |access-date=2024-11-13 |website=Oxford Reference |language=en }}</ref>

-571.title: 571 BC
-571.events:
* [[November 25]] — [[Servius Tullius]], king of Rome, celebrates his victory over the Etruscans with a Roman triumph.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Santangelo |editor1-first=Federico |editor2-last=Richardson |editor2-first=James H. |title=The Roman Historical Tradition Regal and Republican Rome |date=2014 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780199657858 |page=101 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Roman_Historical_Tradition/bWUJBAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Servius+Tullius+25+november+571&pg=PA101&printsec=frontcover}}</ref>
* [[King Ling of Zhou|Zhou Ling Wang]] replaces [[King Jian of Zhou]] as king of the Chinese Zhou Dynasty.

-572.title: 572 BC
-572.events: * 572 BC is the earliest document in the [[Al-Yahudu Tablets]], around 15 years after the destruction of the [[Solomon's Temple]], during the reign of [[Nebuchadnezzar II]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Vukosavović |first1=Filip |title=By the Rivers of Babylon: The Story of the Babylonian Exile |date=2015 |publisher=Bible Lands Museum |isbn=978-9657027271 |ref=FV}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Āl-YāḫūduTexts (ca. 572–477 BCE): A New Window into the Life of the Judean Exilic Community of Babylonia |url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/60/oa_edited_volume/chapter/2502185}}</ref>

-559.title: 559 BC
-559.events:
* [[Cyrus the Great]] succeeds his father [[Cambyses I|Cambyses I of Anshan]].<ref name=ECPB1>{{cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Cyrus-II |title=Cyrus II King of Persia |editor=Encyclopaedia Britannica |author=Richard N. Frye |access-date=2016-07-16}}</ref>
* In the year of his [[coronation|accession]] (560–559 BC), the [[Babylon|Babylonian]] king [[Neriglissar]] commands the declaration of an [[Babylonian calendar|intercalendary month]], so that his first year of [[Monarchy|kingship]] begins on [[Babylonian calendar|Nisan]] 1 of 559 BC.<ref>{{cite book|last=Galil |first=Gershon |title=The Chronology of the Kings of Israel and Judah |editor= E.J. Brill |location=Leiden |date= 1996 | isbn=9004-10611-1}}</ref>

-561.title: 561 BC
-561.events:
* [[Croesus]] becomes king of Lydia (or [[560 BC]]).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Croesus |title=Croesus King of Lydia | editor=encyclopaedia britannica | access-date=2016-07-16}}</ref>
* All eight solar system planets, including the now redefined dwarf planet [[Pluto]], fall into [[Syzygy (astronomy)|planetary alignment]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://curious.astro.cornell.edu/about-us/57-our-solar-system/planets-and-dwarf-planets/orbits/246-when-was-the-last-time-all-9-planets-were-aligned-beginner | title= When was the last time all of the planets were aligned? | author=Dave Kornreich | editor= Cornell | date=2015-07-01 | access-date= 2016-07-17}}</ref>

-568.title: 568 BC
-568.events: * [[Amtalqa]] succeeds his brother [[Aspelta]] as king of [[Kingdom of Kush|Kush]].

-570.title: 570 BC
-570.events:
* Berlin [[Kore (sculpture)|Kore]], from a cemetery at Keratea, near Athens, is begun. It is now at the [[Staatliche Museen zu Berlin]], Germany.
* The [[Satrapy of Armenia]] is established as a province of the [[Achaemenid Empire]]. This is the first polity to bear the name [[Armenia]].
* [[Francois Vase]], black figure decoration on a volute crater, is made by [[Kleitias]] and [[Ergotimos]] (approximate date). It is now in a museum in Italy.
* [[Amasis II]] drives [[Apries]] from the throne of [[Egypt]].

-577.title: 577 BC
-577.events: September or October (3rd of Tishrey): [[Gedaliah]], son of Achikam, murdered by [[Ishmael, son of Kerach]] in Mizpa, Judea (Babylonian Empire).

-558.title: 558 BC
-558.events: * The [[China|Chinese]] state of [[Jin (Chinese state)|Jin]] defeats its rival state of [[State of Qin|Qin]] in battle.

-557.title: 557 BC
-557.events:
* [[May 19]]: The [[Persian people|Persians]] besiege [[Larissa]] ([[Calah]]) but fail to capture it. However, when a [[solar eclipse]] occurs, the inhabitants leave their city and it is taken.<ref>Solar Eclipses and Ancient History. Jennings, S. Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada, Vol.2, pg. 172</ref>

* [[Labashi-Marduk]] is king of [[Babylon]] during this year, succeeding [[Neriglissar]], who reigned three years, and is followed by [[Nabonidus]], who reigns 17 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.studylight.org/dic/hbd/view.cgi?number=T636|title=Babylon, History and Religion of - Holman Bible Dictionary -}}</ref>
* [[Santorini]], [[Greece]] suffers from a [[volcanic eruption]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crossroadsinn.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=22&Itemid=53&lang=en |title=Tinos |access-date=2012-10-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228140757/http://www.crossroadsinn.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=22&Itemid=53&lang=en |archive-date=2014-02-28 }}</ref>

-562.title: 562 BC
-562.events: * [[Amel-Marduk]] succeeds [[Nebuchadnezzar II]] as king of Babylon.<ref>Sack, Ronald H. (Ronald Herbert) (1972). ''Amel-Marduk: 562-560 B.C.; a study based on cuneiform, Old Testament, Greek, Latin and rabbinical sources''. Internet Archive. Kevelaer, Butzon und Bercker; Neukirchen-Vluyn, Neukirchener Verlag d. Erziehungsvereins. {{ISBN|978-3-7666-8552-0}}.</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Saggs |first=Henry |title=The Greatness that was Babylon: A Survey of the Ancient Civilization of the Tigris-Euphrates Valley |date=1962 |publisher=Sidgwick and Jackson |edition=1st |language=English}}</ref>

-575.title: 575 BC
-575.events:
* [[Temple|Temples]] and [[Building|public buildings]] start appearing in [[Rome]]. The [[Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus|main temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus]] is built.
* [[Ishtar Gate]] and throne room wall from [[Babylon]], [[Iraq]] is made. The modified version for installation is now on display in [[Germany]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ishtar Gate {{!}} Processional Way, Babylonian Art, Neo-Babylonian Empire {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Ishtar-Gate |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Battle of Yanling]] in [[Henan]] Province, [[China]] takes place between Jin and Chu forces. The [[Jin (Chinese state)|State of Jin]] is victorious.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Whiting |first=Marvin |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JJQiAz3qTCgC&dq=battle%20of%20yanling&pg=PA43 |title=Imperial Chinese Military History |publisher=iUniverse |isbn=978-0-595-22134-9 |language=en}}</ref>

-573.title: 573 BC
-573.events:
* The [[Nemean Games]] are founded at [[Nemea]], Greece.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Richardson |first=Nicholas J. |date=7 March 2016 |title=Nemean Games |url=https://oxfordre.com/classics/display/10.1093/acrefore/9780199381135.001.0001/acrefore-9780199381135-e-4371 |encyclopedia=Oxford Classical Dictionary|access-date=22 November 2025}} {{subscription required}}</ref> (traditional date)
* The [[Siege of Tyre (586–573 BC)]] ended. It was on-going for 13 years, it also had a significant connection with the [[Book of Ezekiel]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Duncker |first1=Max |last2=Abbott |first2=Evelyn |author1-link=Maximilian Wolfgang Duncker |author2-link=Evelyn Abbott |title=The History of Antiquity. From the German Volume 3 |date=1879 |publisher=Richard Bentley & Son |page=353 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_History_of_Antiquity_From_the_German/rf2cIBsjM1QC?hl=en&gbpv=0}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Keil |first1=Carl Friedrich |author1-link=Carl Friedrich Keil |title=Biblical Commentary on the Prophecies of Ezekiel Volume 2 |date=1876 |publisher=T. & T. Clark |page=11 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Biblical_Commentary_on_the_Prophecies_of/GZME9wBOYZIC?hl=en&gbpv=0}}</ref>
* [[Ezekiel|Prophet Ezekiel]] has a vision of the [[Second Temple]] approximately 60 years before it was built.

-567.title: 567 BC
-567.events:
* Deposed pharaoh [[Apries]] invades Egypt with Babylonian help but is defeated by [[Amasis II]].<ref name="Na'aman">{{cite book |last1=Na'aman |first1=Nadav |editor1-last=Amit |editor1-first=Yaira |title=Essays on Ancient Israel in Its Near Eastern Context A Tribute to Nadav Naʼaman |date=2006 |publisher=Eisenbrauns |isbn=9781575061283 |page=199 |url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Essays_on_Ancient_Israel_in_Its_Near_Eas/Ku4OKVrEd4MC?hl=en&gbpv=0}}</ref>
* [[May 25]]—[[Servius Tullius]], king of Rome, celebrates a triumph for his victory over the [[Etruscans]].

-566.title: 566 BC
-566.events:
=== By place ===
==== Athens ====
*The first known [[Panathenaic Games]] of [[Ancient Greece]] are conducted in [[Athens]].

==== India ====
*Vardhamana attained True Knowledge and became [[Mahavira]].

-509.title: 509 BC
-509.events:
=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
According to the traditional account:

* The [[Roman monarchy]] is [[Overthrow of the Roman monarchy|overthrown]], and the [[Roman Republic|Republican]] period begins (traditional date).
* The first pair of [[Roman consul]]s are elected.
* The [[Tarquinian conspiracy]] is formed yet discovered, and the conspirators are executed.
* Forces of [[Veii]] and [[Tarquinii]], led by the deposed king [[Lucius Tarquinius Superbus]], are defeated in the [[Battle of Silva Arsia]] by the Roman army. Consul [[Publius Valerius Publicola]] celebrates the first republican [[Roman triumph|triumph]] on [[March 1]]. 
* [[September 13]]—The [[Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus]] on [[Rome]]'s [[Capitoline Hill]] is dedicated on the [[ides (calendar)|ides]] of September.
* [[Ancient Carthage|Carthage]] signs a treaty with Rome, delineating their respective spheres.<ref>{{cite book|title=Carthage Must be Destroyed: The Rise and Fall of an Ancient Mediterranean Civilization|first=Richard|last=Miles|year=2010|publisher=Allen Lane|ISBN=9780713997934}}</ref>

-525.title: 525 BC
-525.events:
=== By place ===

==== Egypt ====
* [[Battle of Pelusium (525 BC)|Battle of Pelusium]] - [[Cambyses II]] of [[Achaemenid Empire|Persia]] conquers [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]] by painting cats and other animals sacred to the Egyptians on his soldiers' shields. The Egyptians run in fear of "harming" these animals. It is said that after the battle, Cambyses hurled cats in the faces of the Egyptians in scorn that they would sacrifice their country for the safety of their animals.<ref name="WPCleanerAuto1">{{cite web|last1=Mark |first1=Joshua J. |url=https://www.worldhistory.org/article/43/|title=The Battle of Pelusium: A Victory Decided by Cats|website=[[World History Encyclopedia]] |date=13 June 2017 }}</ref>
* Cambyses takes [[Psamtik III]] prisoner and treats him kindly until he tries to raise a revolt, at which point Psamtik is executed.<ref name="WPCleanerAuto1" />
* The [[Twenty-sixth Dynasty]] ends, and the [[Twenty-seventh Dynasty]] begins.
'''Somalia'''

* After conquering Egypt, the Persian king [[Cambyses II]] sent ambassadors to Macrobia, bringing luxury gifts for the Macrobian king to entice his submission. The Macrobian king replied instead with a challenge for his Persian counterpart in the form of an unstrung [[Bow and arrow|bow]]: if the Persians could manage to string it, they would have the right to invade his country; but until then, they should thank the gods that the Macrobians never decided to invade their empire.<ref>{{Cite book |last=White |first=John S. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PuFRDwAAQBAJ&q=Macrobians+unstrung+bow |title=The Boys ́ and Girls ́ Herodotus |date=2018-04-05 |publisher=BoD – Books on Demand |isbn=978-3-7326-5420-8 |language=en}}</ref>

-528.title: 520s BC
-528.events:
* [[529 BC]]—The Chinese state of [[Zhoulai]] is conquered by [[Wu (state)|Wu]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Cook |first=Constance A. |title=Defining Chu: Image And Reality In Ancient China |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |year=1999 |isbn=0-8248-2905-0 |page=33}}</ref>
* [[528 BC]]—[[Gautama Buddha]] attains [[Enlightenment (Buddhism)|Enlightenment]], and begins his ministry.<ref>{{cite book |last=Schumann |first=Hans Wolfgang |title=The Historical Buddha: The Times, Life, and Teachings of the Founder of Buddhism |publisher=Motilal Banarsidass |year=2004 |isbn=8120818172}}</ref>
*[[527 BC]]—[[Jainism|Jain]] [[Tirthankara]] [[Mahavira]] attains [[Moksha (Jainism)|Moksha]], according to the [[Śvētāmbara|Swetambara]] Tradition. 
* 527 BC—[[Peisistratos of Athens|Peisistratos]] a [[tyrant]] of [[Athens]] dies: his son [[Hippias (tyrant)|Hippias]] inherits his power.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Starr|first=Chester|date=April 2019|title=Peisistratus: TYRANT OF ATHENS|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Peisistratus|website=Encyclopedia Britannica}}</ref>
* [[526 BC]]—[[Psammetichus III]] succeeds [[Amasis II]] as king of [[History of ancient Egypt|Egypt]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Lloyd |first=Alan B. |editor-last=Shaw |editor-first=Ian |title=The Oxford History of Ancient Egypt |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2000 |isbn=978-0192804587 |pages=364–367}}</ref>
* 526 BC—[[King Liao of Wu]] ascends to power in the [[Wu (state)|State of Wu]] in [[China]] during the [[Zhou dynasty]].
* [[525 BC]]—[[Cambyses II]], ruler of [[Achaemenid Empire|Persia]], conquers [[History of ancient Egypt|Egypt]], defeating [[Psammetichus III]]. This is considered the end of the [[Twenty-sixth dynasty of Egypt|Twenty-sixth Dynasty]], and the start of the Persian [[History of Achaemenid Egypt#The first Egyptian satrapy|Twenty-seventh Dynasty]].
* {{Circa|525 BC}}—[[Coin]]s start to have an image on two sides.
* [[522 BC]]—[[Bardiya]] succeeds [[Cambyses II]] as ruler of [[Iran|Persia]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Briant |first=Pierre |title=From Cyrus to Alexander: A History of the Persian Empire |publisher=Eisenbrauns |year=2002 |isbn=978-1575060316 |pages=98–101}}</ref>
* 522 BC—[[Babylon]] rebels against [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian]] rule.
* 522 BC—[[Darius I of Persia|Darius I]] succeeds [[Bardiya]] as ruler of [[Iran|Persia]]. He is the son of a government official.
* 521 BC—The [[Babylonia|Babylonian]] rebellion against [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian]] rule is suppressed.
* [[520 BC]]—[[King Dao of Zhou|Dao]] becomes King of the [[Zhou dynasty]] of [[China]] but dies before the end of the year.
* 520 BC—[[Cleomenes I]] succeeds [[Anaxandridas II|Anaxandridas]] as king of [[Sparta]] (approximate date).
* c. 520 BC—[[Darius I]] decrees that work on Jerusalem resume as per the decree of [[Cyrus the Great]].
* c. 520 BC—Kore, from [[Chios]](?), is made. It is now at [[Acropolis Museum]], [[Athens]].
* c. 520 BC—[[Sarcophagus]], from [[Cerveteri]] is made. It is now at [[National Etruscan Museum]], [[Rome]] (approximate date).
* 520 BC–[[510 BC]]—The Priam Painter makes "Women at a Fountain House", black-figure decoration on a [[hydria]]. It is now at [[Museum of Fine Arts, Boston]].

-536.title: 536 BC
-536.events: *[[List of state leaders in 530s BC#Europe|Phrynaeus]] is appointed [[archon]] of [[Athens]].

-538.title: 538 BC
-538.events:
=== By place ===
==== Near East ====
* The [[Babylonian captivity]] of the [[Jews]] in [[Babylon]] ends when [[Cyrus the Great]], king of Persia, allows them to return to [[Jerusalem]] under the leadership of [[Zerubbabel]] and [[Joshua the High Priest]];<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/History/exile2.html|title = Timeline of Judaism after the Babylonian Exile (538 BCE-70 CE)}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=Rainer|last=Albertz|title=Israel in exile: the history and literature of the sixth century BCE|page=xxi}}</ref><ref>1–6 [[Book of Ezra|Ezra]].</ref> possible start of construction of the [[Second Temple]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Yisrael|last=Shalem|title=Second Temple Period (538 B.C.E. to 70 C.E.): Persian Rule|work=Jerusalem: Life Throughout the Ages in a Holy City|publisher=Ingeborg Rennert Center for Jerusalem Studies, [[Bar-Ilan University]]|location=[[Ramat-Gan]], Israel|year=1997|url=https://www.biu.ac.il/JS/rennert/history_4.html|access-date=2020-01-08|archive-date=2018-11-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103074019/https://www.biu.ac.il/js/rennert/history_4.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

-501.title: 501 BC
-501.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Mediterranean ====
* [[Cleisthenes]] reforms the [[democracy]] in [[Athens]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Boule - ancient Greek council |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/boule-ancient-Greek-council |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |access-date=4 June 2018 |language=en}}</ref>
* In response to [[Roman-Sabine_wars#Bloodless_war.2C_501_BC|threats]] by the [[Sabines]], [[Republican Rome|Rome]] creates the office of [[Roman dictator|dictator]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Orosius |first1=Paulus |title=Seven Books of History Against the Pagans |date=2010 |publisher=Liverpool University Press |isbn=9781846312397 |page=81 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s49zf3smkwwC&pg=PA81|language=en}}</ref>
* Gadir (present-day [[Cádiz]]) is captured by [[Carthage]]. (approximate date)<ref>{{cite web |title=Cádiz - Spain |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Cadiz-Spain |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |access-date=4 June 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

==== Asia ====
* [[Confucius]] is appointed governor of [[Chung-tu]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Crystal |first1=David |title=The Penguin encyclopedia |date=2004 |publisher=Penguin Books |page=[https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780140515435/page/367 367] |isbn=978-0-14-051543-5 |url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780140515435|url-access=registration |language=en}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-502.title: 502 BC
-502.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Mediterranean ====
* The island of [[Naxos]] rebels against the [[Persian Empire]].<ref>[[Herodotus]], ''[[Histories (Herodotus)|Histories]]'', [https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/cgi-bin/ptext?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.01.0126&layout=&loc=5.28 V, 28–30].</ref>
* [[Republican Rome|Rome]] suppresses the [[Roman–Latin wars#Pometian_revolt|Pometian revolt]].<ref>[[Livy]], ''[[Ab urbe condita libri (Livy)|Ab urbe condita]]'', [[s:From the Founding of the City/Book 2#17|2.17]]</ref><ref>[[Dionysius of Halicarnassus]], ''Romaike Archaiologia'', v. 49.</ref>
* [[December 4]]—A [[solar eclipse]] darkens [[Egypt]] (computed, no clear historical record of observation).<ref>{{cite web |title=Five Millennium Catalog of Solar Eclipses: −0599 to −0500 |url=https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEcat5/SE-0599--0500.html |publisher=NASA Goddard Space Flight Center |access-date=25 February 2026}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-503.title: 503 BC
-503.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* The Latin towns of [[Suessa Pometia|Pometia]] and [[Cori, Lazio|Cora]], with the assistance of the [[Aurunci]], [[Roman–Latin wars#The Pometian revolt|revolt]] against [[Roman Republic|Rome]].</onlyinclude>

-504.title: 504 BC
-504.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* A [[Roman-Sabine wars#War with the early republic 505-4 BC|war]] between [[Ancient Rome|Rome]] and the [[Sabines]] ends, having begun in [[505 BC]].
</onlyinclude>

-505.title: 505 BC
-505.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* A [[Roman–Sabine wars#War_with_the_early_republic_505–504_BC|war]] between [[Ancient Rome|Rome]] and the [[Sabines]] begins, concluding in [[504 BC]].<ref>[[Livy]], ''[[Ab urbe condita libri (Livy)|Ab urbe condita]]'', [[s:From the Founding of the City/Book 2#16|2.16]]</ref><ref>[[Dionysius of Halicarnassus]], ''Romaike Archaiologia'', v. 37–47.</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-507.title: 507 BC
-507.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Greece ====
* [[Cleisthenes]] takes power in the city-state of [[Athens]] and institutes reforms that lead historians to consider him the father of democracy.<ref name="Times-2007">{{cite book |author=The New York Times |editor=John W. Wright |title=The New York Times Guide to Essential Knowledge, Second Edition: A Desk Reference for the Curious Mind |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-BIGv9vIoqcC&pg=PA628 |access-date=31 January 2017 |date=30 October 2007 |publisher=St. Martin's Press |location=New York |isbn=978-0-312-37659-8 |page=628 |orig-year=1st pub:2004}}</ref>
* Athenians send an embassy to the [[Achaemenid Empire|Achaemenid]] satrap of [[Asia Minor]] - in the capital city of Sardis - for help in defending against Spartan threats, but refuse to accept Persian terms, which demanded the return of [[Hippias (tyrant)|Hippias]]' tyranny.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Waters |first=Matt |title=Ancient Persia: A Concise History of the Achaemenid Empire, 550–330 BCE. |date=2014 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9781107009608 |pages=84–85}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-506.title: 506 BC
-506.events:
=== By place ===

==== China ====
*[[Battle of Boju]] ({{zh|t=柏舉之戰}})—During the [[Spring and Autumn period]] of [[History of China#Ancient China|ancient China]], forces of the [[Wu (state)|state of Wu]] under [[Sun Tzu]] decisively defeat forces of the [[Chu (state)|state of Chu]], destroying the Chu capital of Ying and forcing [[King Zhao of Chu|King Zhao]] to flee.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last1=Mark |first1=Joshua J. |url=https://www.worldhistory.org/warfare/|title=Warfare|encyclopedia=World History Encyclopedia |date=2 September 2009 |publisher=[[World History Encyclopedia]]}}</ref>

-510.title: 510 BC
-510.events:
=== By place ===
==== Europe ====
* [[Hippias (tyrant)|Hippias]], tyrant of [[Athens]], is expelled  by his people with the assistance of [[Cleomenes I|Cleomenes]], King of Sparta
* The reign of [[Lucius Tarquinius Superbus]], last king of the traditional seven [[Kings of Rome]], concludes. The [[Roman Kingdom|Kingdom of Rome]] falls and is replaced by the [[Roman Republic]]. (or [[509 BC]])
* [[Ariston of Sparta|Ariston]] is succeeded as King of Sparta by [[Demaratus]].
* [[Stelae]] begin to be banned in Athenian cemeteries (approximate date; ends c. [[430 BC]]).
* [[Scylax of Caryanda]] becomes the first mariner to have passed the [[Indian Ocean]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Davidson|first=Basil|title=The Lost Cities of Africa|publisher=[[Little, Brown and Company]]|year=1959|pages=174}}</ref>

-547.title: 547 BC
-547.events:
* [[Croesus]] seizes the Persian city of [[Pteria (Cappadocia)|Pteria]] and enslaves its inhabitants. Meanwhile, Cyrus invites the Ionians to join him in battle.
* The Battles of [[Battle of Thymbra|Thymbra]] and [[Battle of Pteria|Pteria]] are fought between [[Croesus]] of Lydia and [[Cyrus the Great]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Davis |first1=Paul K. |title=100 Decisive Battles From Ancient Times to the Present |date=2001 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780195143669 |page=7 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/100_Decisive_Battles/nv73QlQs9ocC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=battle+of+thymbra+547&pg=PA7&printsec=frontcover}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Hall |first1=H. R. |author1-link=Henry Hall (Egyptologist) |title=The Ancient History of the Near East From the Earliest Times to the Battle of Salamis |date=22 December 2015 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=9781317271642 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Ancient_History_of_the_Near_East/NqBACwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=croesus+pteria+547&pg=RA1-PT533&printsec=frontcover}}</ref>
* Cyrus [[Siege of Sardis (547 BC)|besieges]] and captures Sardis.<ref>{{cite book |editor-last1=Showalter |editor-first1=Dennis |title=Ancient Wars C.2500BCE–500CE |date=16 September 2013 |publisher=Amber Books Limited |isbn=9781782741176 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Ancient_Wars_c_2500BCE_500CE/BdKmAgAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=siege+of+sardis+547&pg=PT40&printsec=frontcover}}</ref>

-546.title: 546 BC
-546.events:
* [[Lydia]] is conquered by [[Persia]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Falk |first1=Avner |title=A psychoanalytic history of the Jews |date=1996 |publisher=Fairleigh Dickinson University Press |isbn=9780838636602 |page=193 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/A_Psychoanalytic_History_of_the_Jews/z10-Xz9Kno4C?hl=en&gbpv=1}}</ref>
* [[Cyrus the Great|Cyrus]] makes [[Pasargadae]] the capital of [[Persia]].
* [[Peisistratus]] takes power in [[Athens]].
* [[Eupalinos]] of Megara, a Greek architect, builds aqueducts that supply water to Athens.
* Cyrus establishes a garrison in Sardis and incorporates the Greek cities of Ionia in Asia Minor into the [[Achaemenid Empire]].
* A coup takes place in the state of [[Qi (Shandong)|Qi]].
* [[Jin (Chinese state)|Jin]] and [[Chu (state)|Chu]] agreed to the [[truce of Mibing]], ending their constant military engagement.

-511.title: 511 BC
-511.events: * The Greek tragic poet [[Phrynichus (tragic poet)|Phrynicus]] wins his first theatrical contest in [[Athens]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theoi.com/Text/ListTragedians.html|title = GREEK TRAGIC POETS INDEX 1 - Theoi Classical Texts Library}}</ref>

-512.title: 512 BC
-512.events:
=== By place ===
==== China ====
* [[Sun Tzu]], author of ''[[The Art of War]]'', begins serving King [[Helü]] of the [[Wu (state)|State of Wu]] as his general and [[Military strategy|military strategist]] (approximate date).<ref>[[Sima Qian]], ''[[Records of the Grand Historian|Shiji]]'', ch. 65 (Biographies of Sun Tzu and Wu Qi).</ref>
* The [[Xu (state)|State of Xu]] is disestablished following attacks by the states of [[Wu (state)|Wu]] and [[Chu (state)|Chu]].<ref>''[[Zuo Zhuan]]'', Duke Zhao, 30th year.</ref>

-513.title: 513 BC
-513.events:
===By place===
====Asia====
* [[Darius the Great]] subdues the [[Getae]] and east [[Thrace]] in his war against the [[Scythians]]. To accomplish this, he builds a massive pontoon bridge across the [[Bosphorus Strait]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.angelfire.com/empire2/unkemptgoose/Persian.html|title=Persia|website=[[Angelfire]]}}</ref>
* [[West India|Western India]], which includes the [[Indus Valley]], becomes the Persian satrapy [[Hindush]].

====Europe====
* [[Amyntas I of Macedon]] submits to Darius and offers women as concubines to a Persian embassy. His son, [[Alexander I of Macedon|Alexander I]], objects to this and tricks them by substituting the women with clean-shaven men (or [[512 BC]]).<ref>Borza, Eugene. In the Shadow of Olympus. Princeton: Princeton University, 1992. Web. 22 October 2014. 101.</ref>
* [[European Scythian campaign of Darius I]]

-514.title: 514 BC
-514.events:
=== By place ===
==== China ====
* [[Helü of Wu|King Helü of Wu]] ascends to the throne of the [[Wu (state)|state of Wu]] and orders [[Wu Zixu]] to build a new capital at what is now [[Suzhou]].<ref>[[Sima Qian]], ''[[Records of the Grand Historian|Shiji]]'', ch. 31, "Hereditary House of Wu Taibo".</ref>

==== Greece ====
* [[Hipparchus (brother of Hippias)|Hipparchus]], son of [[Pisistratus]] and co-ruler of [[Athens]], is assassinated by [[Harmodius and Aristogeiton]] at the [[Panathenaic Games|Panathenaea]].<ref>[[Thucydides]], ''[[History of the Peloponnesian War]]'', 6.54–59.</ref>

-515.title: 515 BC
-515.events:
=== By topic ===

====Art and architecture====
* [[February 25]] – The [[Second Temple]] in Jerusalem is completed.
* Construction of [[Persepolis]] begins.
* [[Euphronios]] creates the ''[[Euphronios Krater|Death of Sarpedon]]'', a red-figure decoration on a [[Krater|calyx krater]]. It is now in the collection of the [[National Archaeological Museum of Cerveteri]].

-516.title: 516 BC
-516.events:
=== By place ===
==== Greece ====
* [[Cleomenes I]] of [[Sparta]] receives an embassy from Maeandrius of [[Samos]] asking for help to expel the tyrant [[Syloson]], a puppet of the [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian Empire]], which is at the time subjugating the city-states of the eastern [[Aegean Sea]].<ref>[[Herodotus]], ''[[Histories (Herodotus)|Histories]]'', 3.148.</ref>

==== India ====
* The Persian king [[Darius the Great|Darius I]] occupies [[Punjab]] (approximate date).<ref>[[Herodotus]], ''[[Histories (Herodotus)|Histories]]'', 4.44.</ref>

-518.title: 518 BC
-518.events:
=== By topic ===
==== Architecture ====
* [[Darius I]] begins constructing [[Persepolis]], a new capital for the [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian Empire]] (approximate date).
* Construction begins on the [[Apadana]] (audience hall) of Darius and Xerxes, ceremonial complex, at [[Persepolis]], [[Persia]].

-520.title: 520 BC
-520.events:
=== By place ===
==== China ====
*[[King Dao of Zhou|King Dao]] becomes king of the [[Zhou Dynasty (1122 BC - 256 BC)|Zhou Dynasty]] of [[China]] but dies before the end of the year.

-519.title: 519 BC
-519.events:
=== By place ===
==== Greece ====
*  Herodotus tells that Cleomenes happened to be in the vicinity of Plataia, when the Plataians requested an alliance with Sparta, which he rejected, but instead he advised them to ally with Athens, because he wanted to stir a border conflict between Thebes and Athens, two of the most powerful poleis of central Greece.

==== China ====
*[[King Jing of Zhou (Gai)|Zhou Jing Wang]]/Ji Gail becomes King of the [[Zhou dynasty|Zhou Dynasty]] of [[China]].

-522.title: 522 BC
-522.events:
=== By place ===
==== Persian Empire ====
* [[Bardiya]] succeeds [[Cambyses II]] as ruler of [[Iran|Persia]].<ref name="Briant">{{cite book|last=Briant|first=Pierre|title=From Cyrus to Alexander: A History of the Persian Empire|year=2002|publisher=Eisenbrauns |page=98}}</ref>
* [[Babylon]] rebels against [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian]] rule.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Dandamaev|first=Muhammad A.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ms30qA6nyMsC&pg=PA116 |title=A Political History of the Achaemenid Empire|publisher=BRILL|year=1989|isbn=978-9004091726|page=116 }}</ref>
* December {{En dash}} [[Darius I of Persia|Darius I]] succeeds [[Bardiya]] as ruler of [[Iran|Persia]]. He is the son of a government official.<ref name="Briant" />

-544.title: 544 BC
-544.events:
* People of [[Teos]] migrate to [[Abdera, Thrace]] to escape the yoke of [[Persia]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}}
* [[King Jing of Zhou (Gui)|Zhou jing wang]] becomes King of the [[Zhou Dynasty (1122 BC - 256 BC)|Zhou Dynasty]] of [[China]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}}

-524.title: 524 BC
-524.events:
=== By place ===
==== Southern Italy ====
*[[Battle of Cumae (524 BC)|Battle of Cumae]] - An army of [[Umbria]]ns, [[Daunia]]ns, [[Etruscan civilization|Etruscans]], and others is defeated by the Greeks of [[Cumae]], present-day [[Italy]]. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://periklisdeligiannis.wordpress.com/2014/06/04/the-battle-of-cumae-italy-524-bc/|title=THE BATTLE OF CUMAE, ITALY (524 BC)|date=4 June 2014|publisher=}}</ref>

-537.title: 537 BC
-537.events:
=== By place ===
==== Judea ====
*The [[Jews]] lay the foundations for the [[Second Temple]].<ref>''Against Apion'', Book I, chapter 21, Flavius Josephus</ref>

-539.title: 539 BC
-539.events:
=== By place ===
[[File:Cyrus Cylinder.jpg|thumb|The Cyrus cylinder: a contemporary [[cuneiform script]] proclaims [[Cyrus the Great]] as legitimate king of Babylon.]]

==== Near East ====
* [[September 25]]–[[September 28|28]]? – [[Battle of Opis]]: Troops of the Persian [[Achaemenid Empire]] under [[Cyrus the Great]] decisively defeat those of the [[Neo-Babylonian Empire]].
* [[October 29]] – [[Fall of Babylon]]: Achaemenid troops under [[Gobryas (general)|Gobryas]] enter [[Babylon]] unopposed. Cyrus enters the city, incorporating the Neo-Babylonian Empire into the Achaemenid Empire and turning the latter into the largest in the history of the world up until that point.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McShane |first=Roger B. |date=2022 |title=Fall Of Babylon |url=https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/history/fall-babylon |website=EBSCO}}</ref>

-543.title: 543 BC
-543.events:
* North Indian Prince [[Vijaya of Sri Lanka|Vijaya]] invades [[Ceylon]] and establishes a [[Sinhalese monarchy|Sinhalese dynasty]] after he was banished from his father's kingdom<ref>{{Cite book|title=Sri Lanka|last=Wanasundera|first=Nanda P.|date=2002|publisher=Marshall Cavendish|isbn=0761414770|location=New York|oclc=49558713|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780761414773}}</ref>
* [[Pisistratus]], tyrant of [[Athens]], purifies the island of [[Delos]]. (approximate)
* Guided by Chinese statesman [[Zi Chan]], the [[State of Zheng]] institutes a formal code of law.

-550.title: 550 BC
-550.events:
* [[Greek colonization]] ends (approximate date).{{clarify|date=March 2021}}
* [[Cyrus II the Great]] overthrows [[Astyages]] of the [[Medes]], establishing the [[Achaemenid Empire]].
* [[Mago I of Carthage|Mago I]] begins his rule of [[Carthage]] and founds the [[Magonid dynasty]].
* The Kingdom of [[Colchis]] is established.
* [[Abdera, Thrace|Abdera]] is destroyed by the [[Thrace|Thracians]].
* The [[Temple of Artemis]] is completed in [[Ephesus]].
* The Temple of Hera I is built in what is now [[Paestum]], [[Italy]] (approximate date).
* [[Siddhartha Gautama]] founds [[Buddhism]] in [[Northern India]] after achieving [[Enlightenment in Buddhism|enlightenment]] after six years of practicing [[penance]] and [[meditation]].

-548.title: 548 BC
-548.events:
*[[Diognetus]] of [[Crotone|Croton]] wins the stadion race at the [[Ancient Olympic Games|Olympic Games]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.attalus.org/translate/eusebius2.html#201|title=Eusebius: Chronicle (2) - translation|first=Andrew|last=Smith|publisher=}}</ref>
*The [[Temple of Apollo (Delphi)|Temple of Apollo]] at [[Delphi]], [[Greece]] is damaged in a fire. The [[Alcmaeonids]] rebuild the structure.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ancientlibrary.com/smith-bio/0115.html |title=Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology, page 106 (V. 1) |access-date=2013-08-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131013221824/http://www.ancientlibrary.com/smith-bio/0115.html |archive-date=2013-10-13 |url-status=usurped }}</ref>

-549.title: 549 BC
-549.events:
=== By place ===
==== Persia ====
* King [[Cyrus the Great|Cyrus II]] ('''the Great''') captures the Median capital of [[Ecbatana]], conquering the nation of [[Media (region)|Media]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Brown|first=Stuart |date=15 December 1997 |title=ECBATANA |url=https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ecbatana/ |encyclopedia=Encyclopædia Iranica}}</ref>

==== Asia ====
* Emperor [[Emperor Suizei|Suizei]] dies after a 32-year reign and is succeeded by his son [[Emperor Annei|Annei]] as emperor of [[Japan]].<ref name="Jien">{{cite book |author1=Jien |author1-link=Jien |editor1-last=Brown |editor1-first=Delmer M. |editor2-last=Ishida |editor2-first=Ichirō |editor1-link=Delmer Brown |title=The Future and the Past A Translation and Study of the Gukanshō, an Interpretative History of Japan Written in 1219 |date=1979 |publisher=University of California Press |pages=250-251 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/%E6%84%9A%E7%AE%A1%E6%8A%84/w4f5FrmIJKIC?hl=en&gbpv=1}}</ref>

-540.title: 540 BC
-540.events:
*[[Cyrus the Great|Cyrus]] attacks [[Babylonia]].
*[[Ancient Greece|Greek]] city of [[Velia|Elea]] of [[southern Italy]] is founded (approximate date).
*[[Achaemenid Empire|Persians]] conquer [[Lycia]]n city of [[Xanthos]] (approximate date).
*[[Amasis Painter]] makes [[Dionysos]] with [[maenad]]s, black-figure decoration on an [[amphora]].
*[[Exekias]] makes ''The Suicide of [[Ajax the great|Ajax]]'', black-figure decoration on an [[amphora]].
*[[Amyntas I of Macedon|Amyntas I]] becomes king of [[Macedon]]ia (approximate date).
*[[Comet Hale–Bopp]] appears in the evening sky, making its closest approach to Earth. Its next appearance occurs in 1997.

-535.title: 535 BC
-535.events:
=== By place ===
==== Europe ====
* Phocaean Greek colonists clash with [[Ancient Carthage|Carthaginian]] and [[Etruscan civilization|Etruscan]] ships in the [[Battle of Alalia]] (near Corsica).

==== Asia ====
* The [[Sungai Batu]] Civilization in [[Malaysia]] begins.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2016/05/23/sg-batu-declared-seas-oldest-civilisation/ |title=Sg Batu declared SEA's oldest civilisation |date=May 23, 2016 |website=www.freemalaysiatoday.com}}</ref>

-534.title: 534 BC

-532.title: 532 BC

-530.title: 530 BC
-530.events:
=== By place ===
==== Asia ====
* [[Cyrus the Great|Cyrus II]] is killed in battle against unknown tribes and succeeded by [[Cambyses II]].
=== By topic ===
==== Chronology ====
* [[Royal Arch Masons]] use this year for dating their documents Anno Inventionis, after the beginning of the Second Temple by [[Zerubbabel]].

==== Art and architecture ====
* The [[Temple of Apollo (Delphi)|Temple of Apollo]] at [[Delphi]] is built (approximate date).
* Peplos Kore, from the [[Acropolis]] in Athens, is made. It is now at [[Acropolis Museum]], [[Athens]] (approximate date).
* Kroisos Kouros, from a cemetery at Anavysos near [[Athens]], is made. It is now at the [[National Archaeological Museum, Athens|National Archaeological Museum]], Athens (approximate date).
* The [[Siphnian Treasury]] in [[Delphi]] is begun (approximate date).
* Battle between the Gods and the Giants, fragments of the north frieze of the Siphnian Treasury, from the Sanctuary of Apollo, [[Delphi]], is begun (approximate date). It is now at the Delphi Archaeological Museum.
* [[Ennigaldi-Nanna]]'s Museum at [[Ur]] is established, the earliest known public [[museum]] with the oldest known [[museum label]]s (approximate date).

-481.title: 481 BC
-481.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Persian Empire ====
* The [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian]] King [[Xerxes I of Persia|Xerxes I]] arrives at [[Sardis]] and begins to build up his great army and navy for the invasion of [[Ancient Greece|Greece]]. [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]] contributes 481 ships.

==== Greece ====
* The [[Congress at the Isthmus of Corinth]], under the presidency of [[Sparta]], brings together a number of the Greek city states, who agree to the end of the war between [[Athens]] and [[Aegina]]. They also discuss the threat from the [[Achaemenid Empire|Persians]]. Athens is unwilling to place her forces under Sparta and its king [[Leonidas I|Leonidas]]. [[Gelo]], [[tyrant]] of [[Syracuse, Sicily|Syracuse]], wants high command, but Sparta and Athens refuse. However, during the Congress, Gelo has to withdraw due to [[Carthage]]'s plans to invade [[Sicily]]. Finally, Themistocles agrees that Athens' navy serve under a Spartan admiral to achieve the unity of the Greek states. Nevertheless, [[Thebes, Greece|Thebes]] and [[Thessaly]] are unwilling to support Athens against the Persians and [[Crete]] decides to remain neutral.

==== China ====
* The [[Spring and Autumn period]], which had begun in [[722 BC]], ends and compilation of the ''[[Spring and Autumn Annals]]'' ceases.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Loewe |first=Michael |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cHA7Ey0-pbEC&pg=PA545 |title=The Cambridge History of Ancient China: From the Origins of Civilization to 221 BC |last2=Shaughnessy |first2=Edward L. |date=1999-03-13 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-47030-8 |pages=546 |language=en}}</ref> It gives way to the [[Warring States period]].

==== Rome ====
* The [[Aequi]] [[Roman-Aequian wars#Ongoing hostilities from 485 BC|lay siege]] to [[Ortona, Latium|Ortona]] but are defeated by the Romans.  Tensions between the Roman classes flare during the battle.
* Continuation of [[Roman–Etruscan Wars#The Fabian war with Veii in 483-476 BC|hostilities]] with [[Veii]].  The Veientine army threatens to besiege Rome but nothing notable occurs.
* The tribune [[Spurius Licinius]] unsuccessfully advocates an [[agrarian law]].
</onlyinclude>

-499.title: 499 BC
-499.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Greece ====
* After a failed attack on the rebellious island of [[Naxos Island|Naxos]] in {{circa}} [[501 BC]] (on behalf of the [[Achaemenid Empire|Persians]]), [[Aristagoras]], tyrant of [[Miletus]], to save himself from the [[Anger|wrath]] of Persia, plans a revolt with the Milesians and the other Ionians. With the encouragement of [[Histiaeus]] (his father-in-law and former tyrant of Miletus), Aristagoras induces the Ionian cities of [[Asia Minor]] to revolt against Persia, thus instigating the [[Ionian Revolt]] and beginning the [[Greco-Persian Wars]] between [[Ancient Greece|Greece]] and Persia.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Guo |first=Ming |title=Proceedings of 3rd International Symposium on Social Science (ISSS 2017) |chapter=The Study of Two International (Regional) Systems before and after the Greco-Persian Wars |date=May 2017 |chapter-url=https://www.atlantis-press.com/proceedings/isss-17/25876988 |language=en |publisher=Atlantis Press |pages=221–224 |doi=10.2991/isss-17.2017.49 |isbn=978-94-6252-341-8|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=FORTIS |first=LUCA |date=2010 |title=Iran's Mediterranean shores |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/42740908 |journal=Rivista di Studi Politici Internazionali |volume=77 |issue=3 (307) |pages=373–381 |jstor=42740908 |issn=0035-6611}}</ref> The pro-Persian tyrant of [[Mytilene]] is stoned to death.
* [[Miltiades the Younger]], the ruler of the [[Thracian Chersonese]], which has been under Persian [[suzerainty]] since approximately [[514 BC]], joins the Ionian revolt. He seizes the islands of [[Lemnos]] and [[Imbros]] from the Persians.
* Aristagoras seeks help with the revolt against the Persians from [[Cleomenes I]], king of [[Sparta]], but the Spartans are unwilling to respond.
</onlyinclude>

-479.title: 479 BC
-479.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Greece ====
* The [[Achaemenid Empire|Persian]] commander [[Mardonius (general)|Mardonius]], now based in [[Thessaly]], wins support from [[Amfilochiko Argos|Argus]] and western [[Arcadia (ancient region)|Arcadia]]. He tries to win over [[Athens]], but fails.
* Mardonius attacks Athens once more and the Athenians are forced to retreat, whereupon he razes the city. The [[History of Sparta|Spartans]] march north to support Athens against the Persians.
* [[August 27]]
** The [[Battle of Plataea]] in [[Boeotia]] ends the Persian invasions of [[Ancient Greece|Greece]] as the Persian general Mardonius is routed by the Greeks under [[Pausanias (general)|Pausanias]], nephew of the former Spartan King, [[Leonidas I]].<ref name="IX59">Herodotus [https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Hdt.+9.59&fromdoc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.01.0126 IX.59]</ref> The Athenian contingent is led by the repatriated [[Aristides]]. Mardonius is killed in the battle and the Greeks capture enormous amounts of loot. [[Thebes, Greece|Thebes]] is captured shortly thereafter and the Theban collaborators executed by Pausanias.
** Meanwhile at sea, the Persians are defeated by a Greek fleet headed by [[Leotychidas]] of Sparta and [[Xanthippus]] of Athens in the [[Battle of Mycale]], on the coast of [[Ionia]] in [[Anatolia|Asia Minor]].
* [[Potidaea]] is struck by a [[tsunami]].</onlyinclude>
* In 479 BC, when Persian soldiers besieged the Greek city of Potidaea, the tide retreated much further than usual, leaving a convenient invasion route, but this was not a stroke of luck. Before they had crossed halfway, the water returned in a wave higher than anyone had ever seen, drowning the attackers. The Potiidaeans believed they had been saved by the wrath of Poseidon, but what really saved them was likely the same phenomenon that has destroyed countless others: a tsunami.

==== Rome ====
* The Roman consul [[Caeso Fabius Vibulanus (consul)|Caeso Fabius]] proposed an [[agrarian law]] to distribute land won in recent wars amongst the plebs, but this was rejected by the senate.
