-137.title: 137 BC
-137.events:
<onlyinclude>
=== By place ===
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Tiberius Gracchus]], [[quaestor]] in Spain, observes that slave labor has displaced small freeheld farms.
* [[Numantine War]] begins, [[Quintus Pompeius]] and [[M. Popilius Laenas]] are defeated and disgraced by the [[Numantia]]ns in subsequent years.
* Q. Pompeius is brought to trial by Q.Metellus and others, but acquitted.
</onlyinclude>

-127.title: 127 BC
-127.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Parthia ====
* The [[Scythians]] defeat the [[Parthian Empire|Parthians]] in a battle around [[Medes|Media]].

==== China ====
* January: Emperor [[Wu of Han]] begins a policy of pressuring the [[Kings of the Han dynasty|client kings]] of the [[Han dynasty]] into dividing their kingdoms. Previously, only the eldest son would inherit a kingdom. However, in an edict, Wu permits the kings of [[Liang Kingdom|Liang]] and [[Chengyang Kingdom|Chengyang]] to divide the land of their states and distribute the land to their younger brothers. Wu grants these brothers titles and promises to do the same if other kings grant land to younger brothers and younger sons. This precedent pressures other kings to do likewise, and Wu places the younger brothers and younger sons under the jurisdiction of the imperial prefectures.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 138–139|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
* [[Wei Qing]] defeats a Xiongnu army near Gaoque. He then invades the [[Ordos Plateau]], defeats the [[Xiongnu]] and their Baiyang and Loufan allies in the battles of Puni and Fuli, and then defeats the main Xiongnu force. The conquered territory becomes [[Shuofang Commandery]]. Wu orders the foundation of Shuofang City, and the system of defenses that had been built by the [[Qin dynasty]] general [[Meng Tian]] are repaired.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 140–141|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
* The Han rationalize the northern frontier, abandoning the remote region of Zaoyang to the Xiongnu.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 140|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-123.title: 123 BC
-123.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Gaius Gracchus]] elected [[Roman Republic|Roman]] [[tribune]] for the first time. He waits until after his re-election the following year before pushing forward the various civil and agrarian reforms that his [[Tiberius Gracchus|brother]] championed in [[133 BC]].
* [[Aix-en-Provence]] founded under the name of ''Aquae Sextiae'' by the [[Roman consul]] [[Gaius Sextius Calvinus (consul 124 BC)|Sextius Calvinus]].
* [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Balearicus|Quintus Caecilius Metellus]] conquers the [[Balearic Islands]] for Rome, for which he earns the agnomen "Balearicus." He settles 3,000 Roman and Iberian colonists on the islands and founds the cities of [[Palma, Majorca|Palma]] and [[Alcúdia|Pollentia]].

==== China ====
* Spring: The [[Han dynasty|Han]] General-in-Chief [[Wei Qing]] launches two invasions of Xiongnu territory from Dingxiang, defeating two Xiongnu armies and killing or capturing several thousand of the enemy. 
:* During the second expedition, the force under Su Jian and [[Zhao Xin (general)|Zhao Xin]] is surrounded and almost entirely destroyed by the army of [[Yizhixie Chanyu]]. Zhao Xin defects to the Chanyu.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 158–159}}</ref>
:* For these two campaigns, [[Emperor Wu of Han]] orders Wei Qing to make his eighteen-year-old nephew [[Huo Qubing]] the commander of a force of 800 cavalry. Raiding deep into enemy territory, Huo's force kills or captures a Xiongnu Prime Minister and a Household Administrator, kills the Marquis of Jiruo (an elder relative of Yizhixie Chanyu), and captures the Chanyu's uncle Luogubi.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 159–160}}</ref>
* A conspiracy led by [[Liu An]], king of [[Huainan]], is discovered. Liu An commits suicide, and his queen and crown prince are executed. Huainan becomes Jiujiang Prefecture.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 151–158}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-143.events:
<onlyinclude>

* The [[Celtiberian War]] ends when [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Macedonicus]] crushes the rebels.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Badian |first=Ernst |author-link=Ernst Badian |date=2012 |title=Caecilius (RE 94) Metellus Macedonicus, Quintus |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-1226 |encyclopedia=The Oxford Classical Dictionary |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=23 December 2025 |edition=4th |isbn=9780191735257}}</ref></onlyinclude>

* In the [[Battle of Antioch (145 BC)|Battle of Antioch]], [[Ptolemy VI Philometor]] defeats the [[Seleucid dynasty|Seleucid]] usurper [[Alexander Balas]], but dies in the battle.

* [[Ptolemy VII of Egypt|Ptolemy VII]] becomes king of Egypt briefly, then is assassinated by [[Ptolemy VIII of Egypt|Ptolemy VIII]] the following year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ptolemy VII Neos Philopator {{!}} king of Egypt |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ptolemy-VII-Neos-Philopator |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |access-date=15 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

-125.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Syria ====
* [[Cleopatra Thea]] succeeds to the rule of the [[Seleucid Empire]] on the death of Seleucus V.<ref>{{cite book|last=Salisbury|first=Joyce|authorlink= Joyce E. Salisbury |title=Encyclopedia of Women in the Ancient World|url=https://archive.org/details/encyclopediawome00sali|url-access=limited|year=2001|publisher=ABC-CLIO|page=[https://archive.org/details/encyclopediawome00sali/page/n93 56]}}</ref> She appoints [[Antiochus VIII Grypus]] as co-ruler.

==== Roman Republic ====
* In [[ancient Rome|Rome]], [[Marcus Fulvius Flaccus (consul 125 BC)|Marcus Fulvius Flaccus]] proposes the extension of [[Roman citizen]]ship to the northern Italians, but the Senate reacts by sending him off to deal with disturbances around [[Marseille|Massilia]]. And in so doing, commences the conquest of [[Transalpine Gaul]].
* Completion of [[Aqua Tepula]] aqueduct in Rome.<ref>{{cite book | first=John E. | last=Stambaugh | title=The Ancient Roman City | year=1988 | place=Baltimore | publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press | page=37 | isbn=0-8018-3574-7}}</ref>

==== China ====
* In retaliation for the [[Han dynasty|Han]] conquest of the [[Ordos Plateau]] two years prior, three [[Xiongnu]] forces raid the Prefectures of Dai, Dingxiang and Shang.
* The Xiongnu Tuqi (Worthy Prince) of the Right (West), especially angry at the loss of the Ordos Plateau, invades the region and kills or carries off a large number of officials and other inhabitants.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 141–142}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-147.title: 147 BC
-147.events:
=== By place ===
====Ireland====
*[[Corlea Trackway]] completed.

==== Roman Republic ====
* Despite being the five years below the minimum age required, [[Scipio Aemilianus]] is elected [[Consul]] under popular pressure.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Abrecht |first=Ryan R. |date=2010 |title=Scipio Aemilianus |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780195170726.001.0001/acref-9780195170726-e-1134 |encyclopedia=The Oxford Encyclopedia of Ancient Greece and Rome |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=27 December 2025 |isbn=9780195388398}}</ref>

* [[Demetrius II of Syria]] returns to [[Syria]] (approximate date).
* [[Jonathan Maccabaeus]] conquers [[Jaffa, Israel|Joppa]].

 |title=E. R. Bevan: The House of Ptolemy • Chap. IX

-122.title: 122 BC
-122.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Marcus Fulvius Flaccus (consul 125 BC)|Marcus Fulvius Flaccus]] and [[Gaius Gracchus]] become [[tribune]]s and propose a number of radical reforms in [[ancient Rome|Rome]].
* Gracchus passes a law requiring the state to provide weapons and equipment for the soldiers in the [[Roman army]]. 

==== China ====
* [[Emperor Wu of Han]] appoints [[Liu Ju]], his son by Empress [[Wei Zifu]], as Crown Prince.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 224|publisher= Algora}}</ref>

-124.title: 124 BC
-124.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Fregellae's revolt]] against [[Roman Republic|Rome]] begins in [[Latium]]. Later the city is captured and destroyed by the Romans.

==== Parthia ====
* [[Mithridates II of Parthia|Mithridates II]] succeeds [[Artabanus I of Parthia|Artabanus I]] as King of [[Parthia]].

==== Egypt ====
* [[Cleopatra II of Egypt]] and her brother [[Ptolemy VIII of Egypt]] reconcile.

==== China ====
* Spring: The [[Han dynasty|Han]] general [[Wei Qing]], with an army of 30,000 cavalry, proceeds from Gaoque into [[Xiongnu]] territory, and in a night attack surrounds the [[Tuqi King]] of the Right in his camp. The Tuqi escapes, but numerous petty chiefs are captured in this and a second engagement.
* Li Xi and Zhang Cigong invade Xiongnu territory from Youbeiping Prefecture but encounter no enemy forces.
* Emperor [[Wu of Han]] rewards Wei Qing by making him General-in-Chief.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 142–143|publisher= Algora}}</ref>

</onlyinclude>

-112.title: 112 BC
-112.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* The [[Roman Senate]] declares war against [[Jugurtha]] following the [[Siege of Cirta]] (ends [[105 BC]]).

==== Asia ====
*[[Han-Nanyue War]]
:* [[Lü Jia (Nanyue)|Lü Jia]], Premier of the [[Han dynasty|Han]] vassal state of [[Nanyue]], opposes increased Han control and refuses to appear before the king of Nanyue and the envoys of Han. He rebels against the Han when [[Emperor Wu of Han|Emperor Wu]] sends an armed force of 2,000 men to kill him and his allies. Lü kills king [[Zhao Xing]] and his regent, Queen Dowager Jiu, massacres the Han force, and installs [[Zhao Jiande]] as king.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 179–182}}</ref>
:* Autumn – Emperor Wu launches a major invasion of Nanyue, sending five riverine fleets to invade under [[Lu Bode]], Yang Pu and three former Yue generals.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 182|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
:* The king of [[Minyue|Dongyue]], Zou Yushan, sends an army to link up with Yang Pu, but he secretly sends an envoy to Zhao Jiande and halts the transport fleet to await the war's outcome, claiming that the weather is preventing its advance.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 186|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
* Emperor Wu executes his favourite necromancer Luan Da for fraud.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 174|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-113.title: 113 BC
-113.events:
<onlyinclude>

===By place===

====Roman Republic====
* [[Battle of Noreia]]: The [[Cimbri]] and [[Teutones]] cross the [[Danube]] and enter the lands of the [[Celts|Celtic]] tribe, the [[Taurisci]] (centered in what is now [[Austria]] and north-eastern [[Italy]]). The latter sent emissaries to [[Ancient Rome|Rome]], seeking help in dealing with the migration. The [[Roman Senate|Senate]] sends consul [[Gnaeus Papirius Carbo (consul 113 BC)|Gnaeus Papirius Carbo]] across the [[Julian Alps]], to deal with the migration at the head of an army (some 30,000 men). He offers guides to escort them out of the territory of the Taurisci. The guides are instructed to lead the tribes to the town of [[Noreia]], where Carbo sets an ambush. The Cimbri manage to discover Carbo's plan, they turn the tables and defeat the Romans during an ambush. Carbo manages to escape with the remnants of his consular army (some 6,000 men) during a heavy thunderstorm. Later, he is indicted by the Senate for losing the battle, but escapes conviction by committing suicide.<ref>Duncan, Mike (2017). ''The Storm before the Storm'', p. 103. New York: Public Affairs. {{ISBN|978-1-5417-2403-7}}.</ref><ref>Fields, Nic (2023). Osprey: CAM - 393: ''The Cimbrian War 113–101 BC - The Rise of Caius Marius'', pp. 47–48. {{ISBN|978-1-4728-5491-9}}.</ref> 
* [[Germanic tribes]] attack [[Gaul]] and northern [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberia]].
*[[Celtiberians]] lead a war against the Romans.

====Syria====
* [[Antiochus IX Cyzicenus]] becomes king of the [[Seleucid Empire]].

====Numidia====
* [[Cirta]] is [[Siege of Cirta|besieged]] by [[Jugurtha]].

====China====
* The state of [[Nanyue]], a vassal of the [[Han dynasty]], agrees to submit to Han laws and receives envoys to oversee the succession of the young king [[Zhao Xing]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 179}}</ref>

===By topic===
====Art====
* An incense burner, later found in the tomb of [[Liu Sheng, Prince of Zhongshan]] in [[Mancheng]], [[Hebei]], is made during the [[Han dynasty]]. It is now kept at [[Hebei Provincial Museum]], [[Shijiazhuang]].</onlyinclude>

* Horos, son of Haruotes, a resident of the temple of Isis in Egypt, attacked a worshiper at the temple.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tebtunis Papyri, 114 BCE {{!}} Center for Online Judaic Studies |url=https://cojs.org/tebtunis_papyri-_114_bce/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Roller |date=2012 |title=Marius, Gaius |editor-last1=Gates |editor-first1=Henry Louis |editor1-link=Henry Louis Gates Jr. |editor-last2=Akyeampong |editor-first2=Emmanuel |editor2-link=Emmanuel K. -119.title: 119 BC
-119.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* The [[second Dalmatian war]] begins.

==== China ====
* Spring: [[Han China|Han Chinese]] forces under the General-in-Chief [[Wei Qing]] and the cavalry general [[Huo Qubing]] invade the [[Xiongnu|Xiongnu Empire]].
:*[[Battle of Mobei]]: Wei Qing crosses the [[Gobi Desert]], defeats [[Yizhixie Chanyu]] and kills or captures 19,000 Xiongnu.
:*Huo Qubing crosses the eastern Gobi, defeats and executes Bijuqi, defeats the Tuqi (Worthy Prince) of the Left (East), and captures three kings. He reaches as far as [[Lake Baikal]].
:* Failing to reconnoiter with Wei Qing's army, general [[Li Guang]] commits suicide after learning that Wei has prepared charges against him.
:* [[Emperor Wu of Han|Emperor Wu]] creates the rank of Grand Marshal and gives it to both Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, thereby making Huo's rank and salary equal to that of Wei.
* Emperor Wu suspends further campaigning against the Xiongnu due to a shortage of horses.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 164–168|publisher= Algora}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=Sima|last= Qian|title=Records of the Grand Historian, Section: Xiongnu, Section: Wei Qing & Huo Qubing}}</ref> 
* Government monopolies are established in [[Iron (material)|iron]], [[salt]] and [[liquor]].
</onlyinclude>

-120.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Europe ====
* The [[Teutons]] and the [[Cimbri]] migrate south and west to the [[Danube]] valley where they encounter the expanding [[Roman Republic]] (approximate date).

* [[Mithridates VI Eupator]] becomes [[king of Pontus]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |editor-last1=Kerr |editor-first1=Anne |editor-last2=Wright |editor-first2=Edmund |date=2015 |title=Mithridates VI |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780199685691.001.0001/acref-9780199685691-e-2427 |encyclopedia=A Dictionary of World History |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=21 December 2025}}</ref>

==== China ====
* Retaliating against the [[Han dynasty|Han]] conquest of the [[Hexi Corridor]] in the previous year, the [[Xiongnu]] invade the provinces of Youbeiping and Dingxiang, killing or capturing over 1000 inhabitants.<ref>{{cite book|first=Sima|last= Qian|title=Records of the Grand Historian, Section: Xiongnu, Section: Wei Qing & Huo Qubing}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-121.title: 121 BC
-121.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* The [[Roman Senate]] passes the motion ''senatus consultum ultimum'', which the [[Roman consul|consul]] [[Lucius Opimius]] interprets as giving him unlimited power to preserve the [[Roman Republic|Republic]]. He gathers an armed force of Senators and their supporters to confront [[Gaius Gracchus]]. A pitched battle is fought inside [[Rome]], resulting in the death of Gracchus and many of his followers.
* A tribunal is established in Rome that executes 3,000 followers of Gracchus.
* [[Consul]] [[Quintus Fabius Maximus Allobrogicus|Quintus Fabius Maximus]], allied with the [[Aedui]], defeats the [[Arverni]] and [[Allobroges]] in [[Transalpine Gaul]], thus establishing the province for Rome.
* The finest vintage of [[Falernian wine]], known as the Opimian vintage, is bottled from vines grown on Mt Falernus between Latium and Campania.

==== China ====
* Spring - The [[Han dynasty|Han]] general [[Huo Qubing]] attacks the Supu, vassals of the [[Xiongnu]], and kills their king. He then invades the [[Hexi Corridor]], where he fights a six-day running battle against a son of [[Yizhixie Chanyu]]. The Xiongnu are defeated, and the ruler of Lan and king Lu, both vassals of the Xiongnu, are killed in the fighting. Huo Qubing then attacks and defeats the Hunye, capturing the son of the Hunye king and his ministers and chief commandants.
* Summer - Huo Qubing again invades the Hexi Corridor. In an engagement in the [[Qilian Mountains]], he captures the king of the Qiutu. In a second engagement, he then captures five vassal kings of the Xiongnu and a consort of the Chanyu, killing or capturing more than 30,000 Xiongnu soldiers.
* Generals [[Li Guang]] and [[Zhang Qian]] ride north from Youbeiping, but Zhang Qian, with the larger army, is slow to rendezvous with Li Guang. As a result, Li Guang loses more than half his army in battle against the Tuqi (Worthy Prince) of the Left (East).
* Autumn - Yizhixie Chanyu plans on executing the Hunye and [[Xiutu]] kings for their failures against Huo Qubing, but learning of this, the vassal kings inform the Han of their intention to surrender. Emperor [[Wu of Han]] sends Huo Qubing across the Yellow River with an army to oversee their surrender. Some of the enemy troops and leaders then refuse to surrender, but Huo Qubing massacres 8000 of them as they attempt to flee. Huo Qubing receives the surrender of thirty-two Xiongnu vassals, and the Hunye king and other vassals are enfeoffed as marquises in China. 
* The rapid conquest of the Hexi Corridor provides the traditional western provinces of China with greater security. As a result, Emperor Wu halves the number of soldiers garrisoning the provinces of [[Longxi Commandery|Longxi]], [[Beidi Commandery|Beidi]] and [[Shang Commandery|Shang]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 159–163|publisher= Algora}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=Sima|last= Qian|title=Records of the Grand Historian, Section: Xiongnu, Section: Wei Qing & Huo Qubing}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-73.title: 73 BC
-73.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Third Servile War]]: [[Spartacus]], a Thracian gladiator, escapes with around 70 [[Gladiator|slave-gladiator]]s from a gladiator school at [[Capua]]. They defeat a small Roman force and equip themselves with captured military equipment as well with gladiatorial weapons. Spartacus and his band of gladiators [[Looting|plunder]] the region surrounding Capua and retire to a defensible position on [[Mount Vesuvius]].<ref>Appian, ''Civil Wars'', [https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Appian/Civil_Wars/1*.html#116 1:116]; Florus, ''Epitome'', [[Wikisource:Epitome of Roman History/Book 2#8|2.8]]; - Florus and Appian make the claim that the slaves withdrew to Mount Vesuvius, while Plutarch only mentions "a hill" in the account of Glaber's siege of the slave's encampment.</ref>
* [[Battle of Mount Vesuvius]]: Spartacus defeats a Roman [[militia]] force (3,000 men) under [[Gaius Claudius Glaber]]. The rebel slaves spend the winter of 73–72 BC training, arming and equipping their new recruits, as well as expanding their raiding territory, which includes the towns of [[Nola]], [[Nocera Inferiore|Nuceria]], [[Thurii]] and [[Metapontum]].
* On the [[Iberian Peninsula]] (part of the [[Roman Republic]]) rebel leader [[Quintus Sertorius]] is [[Assassination|assassinated]] by some of his own lieutenants (lead by [[Marcus Perperna Veiento|Marcus Perperna]]).{{efn|the year of his assassination is disputed – the debate is whether he was assassinated in 73 or 72 BCE}} Perperna takes command of the rebel army.

-71.title: 71 BC
-71.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Third Servile War]] ends; [[Slave rebellion]] under leadership of [[Spartacus]] is crushed by a Roman army under [[Marcus Licinius Crassus]]. Slaves taken prisoner are [[Crucifixion|crucified]] naked along the [[Via Appia]].
* [[Marcus Antonius Creticus|Marcus Antonius]] is defeated by the [[Crete|Cretans]], who have made an [[Military alliance|alliance]] with the [[Piracy|pirates]]. He is compelled to concede a humiliating peace. Antonius dies in office the same year and is awarded, posthumously, with the [[cognomen]] ''Creticus''.<ref>Pompey, Command (p. 20). Nic Fields, 2012. {{ISBN|978-184908-572-4}}</ref>
* [[Nessebar]] in modern-day [[Bulgaria]] comes under Roman rule.

-100.title: 100 BC
-100.events:
<onlyinclude>
=== By place ===
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Lucius Valerius Flaccus (consul 100 BC)|Lucius Valerius Flaccus]], [[Gaius Marius]] (Marius's sixth consulship).
* [[Manius Aquillius (consul 101 BC)|Manius Aquillius]] celebrates an [[ovation]] for victories in the [[Second Servile War]].
* [[Lucius Appuleius Saturninus]], a [[tribune]], passes a law to [[Redistribution (economics)|redistribute]] land to [[Veteran|military veterans]]. The law requires that all senators swear to abide by it. [[Quintus Caecilus Metellus Numidicus]] refuses and is exiled. He goes to [[Rhodes]] to study philosophy.
* Late summer–autumn: Saturninus stands for tribune again for the following year, and is elected. His associate, the praetor [[Gaius Servilius Glaucia]], attempts to stand for the consulship (illegally, as praetors cannot immediately become consul). A rival candidate, [[Gaius Memmius (proconsul of Macedonia)|Gaius Memmius]], is found murdered by agents of Saturninus and Glaucia, who are declared public enemies by the [[Roman Senate|Senate]]. The Senate issues the ''[[senatus consultum ultimum]]'', and Marius, as consul, defeats his former ally in battle in the [[Roman Forum|Forum]]. Saturninus and his followers surrender on condition that their lives are spared, but they are stoned to death with roof tiles in the [[Curia Hostilia]] by renegade senators.
* The building of the Sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia, [[Palestrina, Lazio|Palestrina]], [[Italy]], is begun. The model of it is now kept at the [[Naples National Archaeological Museum|Museo Archeologico Nazionale]], Italy (approximate date).

==== Asia Minor ====
* [[Tigranes II of Armenia]] is placed on the [[Armenia]]n throne by the [[Parthia]]ns in exchange for the cession of "seventy valley" (approximate date).

==== Judea ====
* The [[deuterocanonical books]] of [[1 Maccabees|1]] and [[2 Maccabees]] are written.

==== India ====
* [[Gandhara]] and [[Punjab region|Punjab]] are ruled by the [[Indo-Greek Kingdom|Indo-Greek]] king [[Demetrius III Aniketos]].

==== China ====
* [[War of the Heavenly Horses]]: the [[Han dynasty|Han]] expedition under [[Li Guangli]] returns victorious to China. He is followed by dynastic representatives sent by various Central Asian kings, so that they may pay tribute to [[Emperor Wu of Han]]. Emperor Wu keeps these representatives as hostages and sends soldiers to build pavilions and reclaim wasteland along the route to the west to provide food and shelter for Han envoys.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 202–203|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
* [[Han-Xiongnu War]]: the Han general Zhao Ponu escapes Xiongnu custody and returns to China.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 208|publisher= Algora}}</ref>

==== America ====
* Mural room in the [[Maya civilization|Maya]] pyramid at [[San Bartolo (ruins)|San Bartolo]], [[Guatemala]], painted.

-52.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius Scipio Nasica]] and [[Pompey|Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus]].
* Gnaeus Pompeius marries [[Cornelia Metella]].
* [[Titus Annius Milo|Milo]] is tried for the [[murder]] of Clodius. Despite [[Cicero]]'s legal defence (''[[Pro Milone]]'') he is found guilty and exiled in Massilia (modern [[Marseille]]).
* [[Gallic Wars]] ([[Julius Caesar]]):
** March – Siege and capture of [[Avaricum]] ([[Bourges]]).
** April–May – Siege and repulse from [[Gergovia]].
** July – [[Battle of the Vingeanne]]: Julius Caesar rebuffs, with his German [[auxiliaries]], a Gallic cavalry attack of [[Vercingetorix]].
** Summer – Siege of [[Alesia (city)|Alesia]]: Julius Caesar spreads out his legions around the ''[[Oppidum]]'' and builds a string of fortifications surrounding the stronghold of Alesia. 
** September – [[Battle of Alesia]]: Julius Caesar defeats the Gallic allies coming to aid Vercingetorix, led by his cousin Vercassivellanus. Vercingetorix surrenders on October 3, signalling the Roman conquest of Gaul. The final pacification of [[Gaul]] is completed the following year.
** Winter – Julius Caesar crosses [[Cévennes|Mons Cevenna]] (central [[Gaul]]) and sends  his army through the passes covered with [[snowdrift]]s to take the rebellious [[Arverni]] by surprise.<ref>Julius Caesar, Command (p. 34). Nic Fields, 2010. {{ISBN|978-1-84603-928-7}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

==== Asia ====
* [[Han-Xiongnu War]]
:* The Han general [[Li Guangli]] marches west from [[Jiuquan]] with 30,000 cavalrymen to attack the [[Tuqi King]] of the Right in the [[Tian Shan]] Mountains. After an initial victory, the Han are surrounded, and they lose more than 20,000 men while breaking out of the encirclement.
:* The Han generals [[Lu Bode]] and [[Gongsun Ao]] march into the Zhuoxie Mountains, but they encounter no Xiongnu forces and turn back.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 208–209|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
:* Autumn – The Han general [[Li Ling]] leads 5000 crack infantry and a cavalry force from [[Juyan Lake]] into the eastern [[Altay Mountains]] but is pursued by [[Qiedihou|Qiedihou Chanyu]]. After a desperate fighting retreat across more than 500km of Xiongnu territory, the Han expedition runs out of arrows. Li Ling surrenders and his force disintegrates in the Tihan Mountains, about 50km from the [[Great Wall of China]].
:* [[Emperor Wu of Han]] has the 'Grand Historian' [[Sima Qian]] castrated after the latter argues in defense of Li Ling's surrender.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 213–218|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-53.title: 53 BC
-53.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Parthian Empire ====
* The [[Parthian Empire]] achieved a decisive victory against Rome at the [[Battle of Carrhae]], where [[General Surena]] defeated and killed Roman triumvir [[Marcus Licinius Crassus]]. According to some historical interpretations, the [[Mahestan]] (Parthian noble council) supported preparations for the defense of the empire and advised the king during the military mobilization.<ref name="ParthavaMahestan">{{cite web |title=Fundamentals of the Parthian Statehood |url=https://www.parthava.org/2022/05/27/fundamentals-of-the-parthian-statehood/ |website=Parthava |date=27 May 2022 |access-date=5 August 2025}}</ref>
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Marcus Valerius Messalla Rufus|Marcus Valerius Messalla]] and [[Gnaeus Domitius Calvinus]].
* [[Roman–Parthian Wars|Parthian War]]: 
** [[Marcus Licinius Crassus|Crassus]] sacks the Temple of [[Hierapolis]] and the [[Temple in Jerusalem]] on his way to engage the Parthians.
** [[May 6]] – [[Battle of Carrhae]]: Romans defeated, and Crassus killed, by Parthians led by General [[Surena]].
* [[Gallic Wars|Gallic War]]:
** [[Julius Caesar]] suppresses a [[Ambiorix's revolt|revolt]] led by [[Ambiorix]] near [[Sambre|Sabis]] (Northern [[Gaul]]).
** At [[Cenabum]] (modern [[Orléans]]) Roman [[merchant]]s are massacred by the [[Carnutes]].
** [[Vercingetorix]], an [[Arverni]] chieftain, leads a revolt against Caesar in Central Gaul.
** Winter – Caesar enrolls non-citizen soldiers in [[Gallia Narbonensis|Gallia Transalpina]], genesis of ''[[Legio V Alaudae]]''. He increases his army to ten [[Roman legion|legion]]s.<ref>Nic Fields (2010). Osprey: Command – Julius Caesar, (p. 20). {{ISBN|978-1-84603-928-7}}</ref>

==== Armenia ====
* [[Artavasdes II of Armenia|Artavasdes II]] becomes king of [[Armenia]].
</onlyinclude>

-54.title: 54 BC
-54.events:
<onlyinclude>
=== By place ===
==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Appius Claudius Pulcher (consul 54 BC)|Appius Claudius Pulcher]] and [[Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus (consul 54 BC)|Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Cadoux |first1=Theodore John |last2=Seager |first2=Robin J. |author2-link=Robin Seager |date=2012 |title=Claudius (RE 297) Pulcher (3), Appius |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-1640?rskey=Og8k2L&result=4 |encyclopedia=
The Oxford Classical Dictionary |edition=4th |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=12 December 2025 |isbn=9780191735257}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Badian |first=Ernst |author-link=Ernst Badian |date=2012 |title=Domitius (RE 27) Ahenobarbus (1), Lucius |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-2276?rskey=5jZrr9&result=1 |encyclopedia=
The Oxford Classical Dictionary |edition=4th |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=12 December 2025 |isbn=9780191735257}}</ref>
* Fifth year of [[Julius Caesar]]'s [[Gallic Wars]]:
** July – Second of [[Caesar's Invasions of Britain]]: Julius Caesar receives nominal submission from the tribal chief [[Cassivellaunus]] and installs [[Mandubracius]] as a friendly king.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last= |first= |date=2007 |title=Cassivellaunus |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780192801463.001.0001/acref-9780192801463-e-416 |encyclopedia=The Oxford Dictionary of the Classical World |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=12 December 2025 |isbn=9780191727061}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Cannon |first1=John |author1-link=John Cannon (historian) |last2=Hargreaves |first2=Anne |date=2009 |title=Mandubracius |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780199559220.001.0001/acref-9780199559220-e-372 |encyclopedia=The Kings and Queens of Britain |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=12 December 2025 |isbn=9780191727252}}</ref>
** Winter – [[Ambiorix's revolt|Ambiorix revolts]] in [[Gaul]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Scullard |first1=Howard Hayes |author1-link=Howard Hayes Scullard |last2=Drinkwater |first2=John Frederick |author2-link=John F. Drinkwater |date=2012 |title=Ambiorix |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-345?rskey=Dqx9ZG&result=1 |encyclopedia=
The Oxford Classical Dictionary |edition=4th |location= |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=12 December 2025 |isbn=9780191735257}}</ref> He joins with [[Catuvolcus]] in an uprising against the [[Roman army]]. Caesar's senior officers [[Lucius Aurunculeius Cotta]] and [[Quintus Titurius Sabinus]] are ambushed by the [[Eburones]], and killed along with almost their entire forces.
* [[Pompey]] builds the first permanent [[theatre]] in [[Ancient Rome|Rome]].
* [[Crassus]] arrives in [[Syria]] as [[proconsul]] and invades the [[Parthian Empire]], initiating the [[Roman–Persian Wars]], which were to last nearly seven centuries.
* [[Octavia the Younger]] and [[Gaius Claudius Marcellus (consul 50 BC)|Gaius Claudius Marcellus]] marry.</onlyinclude>

-55.title: 55 BC
-55.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Marcus Licinius Crassus]] and [[Pompey|Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus]].
* Consuls [[Marcus Licinius Crassus]] and [[Pompey|Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus]] pass the [[Lex Trebonia]].
* [[Theatre of Pompey|Pompey's Theater]], the first permanent (non-wooden) theatre in [[Rome]] is built. Built of stone on the [[Campus Martius|Field of Mars]], it included a temple to [[Venus (mythology)|Venus Victorious]], a public courtyard, and a meeting hall or ''[[curia]]'' in the far end near the "Sacred Area".
* Fourth year of [[Julius Caesar]]'s [[Gallic Wars]]:
** Spring – Julius Caesar starts the season campaigning in [[Illyricum (Roman province)|Illyricum]] (in the [[Balkans|Balkan]] region) against the [[List of ancient tribes in Illyria#Pirustae|Pirustae]], who have been raiding Roman territory.<ref>Nic Field (2014). Osprey: ''Alesia 52 BC – The final struggle for Gaul'', p. 14. {{ISBN|978-1-78200-922-1}}.</ref>
** Summer – Julius Caesar defeats the [[Usipetes]] and the [[Tencteri]], two Germanic tribes who have been driven across the [[Rhine]] River by the [[Suebi]]. He spreads [[Roman law]] and order, and makes the whole country as far as the [[English Channel|Channel]] accessible to [[trade]].
** May – Julius Caesar defeats a Germanic army and massacres the women and children near the [[Meuse]] and Rhine Rivers (now known as the city of [[Kessel, Limburg|Kessel]] in the [[Netherlands]]).
** June – Julius Caesar crosses the Rhine River near modern-day [[Koblenz]]. He constructs a wooden [[Caesar's Rhine bridges|bridge]] between [[Andernach]] and [[Neuwied]] ([[Germany]]).

==== Britain ====
* [[August 22]] or [[August 26]] – Julius Caesar commands his first [[Caesar's invasions of Britain|invasions of Britain]], likely a reconnaissance-in-force expedition, in response to the [[Celtic Britons|Britons]] giving military aid to his Gallic enemies. Caesar retreats back to [[Gaul]] when the majority of his force is prevented from landing by storms.

==== Egypt ====

[[Ptolemy XII Auletes]] is restored to the [[Ptolemaic Kingdom|Egyptian]] throne by the aid of [[Aulus Gabinius]], [[Roman Republic|Roman]] governor of [[Roman Syria|Syria]], and has his daughter [[Berenice IV]] executed for rebellion.
==== Parthia ====
* [[Mithridates IV of Parthia|Mithridates IV]], claimant to the throne of [[Parthia]], supported by [[Aulus Gabinius]], [[Roman Republic|Roman]] [[governor]] of [[Syria]], is defeated by [[Surena]], [[general]] under [[Orodes II of Parthia|Orodes]], in the Battle of [[Seleucia]].
</onlyinclude>

-56.title: 56 BC
-56.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* Roman [[Consul]]s are [[Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus Marcellinus]] and [[Lucius Marcius Philippus (consul 56 BC)|Lucius Marcius Philippus]].
* [[Clodia (wife of Metellus)|Clodia]] accuses her former lover [[Marcus Caelius Rufus]] of trying to [[poison]] her. The trial ends with the defendant acquitted thanks to the ''[[Pro Caelio]]'' speech of [[Cicero]]. There is no more reference to the formerly well-known Clodia.
* Third year of [[Julius Caesar]]'s [[Gallic Wars]]: 
** [[Battle of Morbihan]]: [[Decimus Junius Brutus Albinus]], one of Caesar's subordinates, defeats the [[Veneti (Gaul)|Veneti]] of [[Brittany]]. The Gauls lose most of their warships to the Romans in a sea battle at modern-day [[Quiberon Bay]]. The strongholds on the coast are stormed, and the population is slaughtered or sold into [[slavery]].
** The three Roman politician-generals of the [[First Triumvirate]] — [[Julius Caesar|Caesar]], [[Pompey]] and [[Crassus]] — meet at the [[Luca Conference]] at the town of Luca (modern [[Lucca]], in [[Tuscany]]), near [[Pisa]], where they renewed their fraying political alliance, and further cemented the three men's increasing consolidation of power in the [[Roman Republic]].
** Autumn – Julius Caesar leads an attack on the [[Morini]] and the [[Menapii]] tribes of the [[Belgae]] on the [[North Sea]]. They withdraw into their forests, creating difficulties for Caesar's supply lines. The onset of bad weather forces him to pull back into [[Gallia Belgica]].<ref>Nic Fields (2014). Osprey: ''Alesia 52 BC – The final struggle for Gaul'', p. 14. {{ISBN|978-1-78200-922-1}}.</ref>

==== Britain ====
* This year, or possibly the following year, the king of the [[Trinovantes]] called [[Imanuentius]], is overthrown and killed by his rival [[Cassivellaunus]]. His son [[Mandubracius]] flees to [[Gaul]] and appeals to Julius Caesar for help.
</onlyinclude>

-57.title: 57 BC
-57.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Publius Cornelius Lentulus Spinther]] and [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos (consul 57 BC)|Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos]].
* Second year of [[Julius Caesar]]'s [[Gallic Wars]]:
** Spring – Julius Caesar raises a further two legions ([[Legio XIII Gemina|Legio XIII]] and [[Legio XIV Gemina|Legio XIV]]), bringing his army in [[Gaul]] to eight legions (at which strength it remains until [[54 BC]]).
** Caesar sends [[Servius Sulpicius Galba (praetor 54 BC)|Servius Sulpicius Galba]] with [[Legio XII Fulminata|Legio XII]] into the territory of the [[Nantuates]], [[Seduni]] and the [[Veragri]]. He occupies Octodurus (modern-day [[Martigny]]) in [[Switzerland]].
** Caesar defeats a Belgic army near Bibrax (modern-day [[Laon]]) in the territory of the [[Remi]]. He moves northwards against the Belgic tribes, the [[Nervii]] and the [[Atuatuci|Aduatuci]].<ref>Nic Fields (2014). ''Alesia 52 BC: The Final struggle for Gaul'', p. 13. {{ISBN|978-1-78200-922-1}}.</ref>
** May – [[Battle of the Axona]]: Caesar defeats the forces of the [[Belgae]] under King Galba of the [[Suessiones]].
** July – [[Battle of the Sabis]]: Caesar defeats the Nervii, Roman forces are almost annihilated in an ambush.
** September – The siege and capture of Aduatuca (modern-day [[Tongeren]]) by Caesar.

==== Parthia ====
* [[Mithridates IV of Parthia|Mithridates IV]] becomes king of Parthia.

==== Asia ====
* King [[Vikramaditya]] establishes the [[Vikram Samvat|Vikram era]].
* [[Bak Hyeokgeose of Silla|Bak Hyeokgeose]] becomes the first ruler of the kingdom of [[Silla]] (traditional date).<ref>{{cite web |title=List of Rulers of Korea |url=https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/koru/hd_koru.htm |website=www.metmuseum.org |access-date=21 April 2019}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-58.title: 58 BC
-58.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus (consul 58 BC)|Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus]] and [[Aulus Gabinius]].
* [[Publius Clodius Pulcher]], Roman [[tribune]], institutes a monthly corn dole for poor Romans, and exiles [[Cicero]] from the city.
* [[Cyprus]] becomes a [[Roman province]].
* First year of [[Julius Caesar]]'s [[Gallic Wars]]:
** Julius Caesar becomes a provincial governor ([[proconsul]]) and leads a Roman army (6 [[Roman legion]]s; [[Legio VII Claudia|Legio VII]], [[Legio VIII Augusta|Legio VIII]], [[Legio IX Hispana|Legio IX]], [[Legio X Fretensis|Legio X]], and newly levied [[Legio XI]] and [[Legio XII Fulminata|Legio XII]]) into [[Gaul]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=1&division=div2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020232/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=1&division=div2|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title="De Bello Gallico" and Other Commentaries by Julius Caesar, Book1|pages=1.7, 1.8, 1.10|access-date=March 23, 2021}}</ref> He deploys [[auxilia]]ries as part of this army, including [[Balearic slinger|Balearic slingers]], [[Numidians|Numidian]] and [[Classical crete|Cretan]] archers,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=2&division=div2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020249/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=2&division=div2|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title=Caesar's Commentaries on the Gallic and Civil Wars: with the Supplementary Books attributed to Hirtius. Book Two|date=2011-01-11|page=2.7, 2.10, 2.19, 2.24|access-date=2017-12-29}}</ref> and Celtic/Gallic cavalry (such as the allied [[Aedui]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=1&division=div2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020232/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=1&division=div2|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title=Caesar's Commentaries on the Gallic and Civil Wars: with the Supplementary Books attributed to Hirtius.|date=2011-01-11|page=1.15|access-date=2017-12-29}}</ref>).
** Caesar builds a 19-mile earthwork, complete with fortifications and [[watchtower]]s, between [[Lake Geneva]] and the [[Jura Mountains]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=1&division=div2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020232/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=1&division=div2|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title=Caesar's Commentaries on the Gallic and Civil Wars: with the Supplementary Books attributed to Hirtius.|date=2011-01-11|page=1.8|access-date=2017-12-29}}</ref>
** June – Caesar defeats the migrating [[Helvetii]] in the [[Battle of the Arar]] ([[Saône]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020128/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title=Caesar's Commentaries on the Gallic and Civil Wars: with the Supplementary Books attributed to Hirtius.|date=2011-01-11|page=1.12|access-date=2017-12-29}}</ref>
** July – Caesar decisively defeats the Helvetii in the [[Battle of Bibracte]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020128/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title=Caesar's Commentaries on the Gallic and Civil Wars: with the Supplementary Books attributed to Hirtius.|date=2011-01-11|pages=1.21–1.30|access-date=2017-12-29}}</ref>
** September – Caesar decisively defeats the [[Suebi]] led by King [[Ariovistus]] in the [[Battle of Vosges (58 BC)|Battle of Vosges]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images/modeng&data=/texts/english/modeng/parsed&tag=public&part=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111020128/http://etext.lib.virginia.edu/etcbin/toccer-new2?id=CaeComm.sgm&images=images%2Fmodeng&data=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fparsed&tag=public&part=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2011|title=Caesar's Commentaries on the Gallic and Civil Wars: with the Supplementary Books attributed to Hirtius.|date=2011-01-11|pages=1.31–1.54|access-date=2017-12-29}}</ref>
** Winter – Caesar leaves his legions in winter quarters among the [[Sequani]] (located in modern-day [[Burgundy]]) far to the north of the formal boundary of [[Gallia Narbonensis|Gallia Transalpina]]. He returns to [[Cisalpine Gaul|Gallia Cisalpina]], carrying out judicial and administrative activities.<ref>Nic Fields (2014). ''Alesia 52 BC: The final struggle for Gaul'', p. 13. {{ISBN|978-1-78200-922-1}}.</ref>

==== Egypt ====
* [[Berenice IV]] becomes queen of [[Ptolemaic Kingdom|Egypt]] after temporarily dethroning her father, King [[Ptolemy XII Auletes]].

==== Asia ====
* Base year of the [[Vikrama Samvat|Vikrama Era]], founded by [[Vikrama]], king of [[Ujjain]] in [[India]].

-60.title: 60 BC
-60.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Julius Caesar|Gaius Julius Caesar]] suppresses an uprising and conquers all of [[Lusitania]] for [[Ancient Rome|Rome]].<ref name=Dupuy>{{cite book| first1=Richard Ernest|last1=Dupuy|first2=Trevor Nevitt|last2=Dupuy|title=The Harper Encyclopedia of Military History: From 3500 BC to the Present|publisher=HarperCollins|location=New York|year=1993|isbn=978-0-06270-056-8|page=105}}</ref><ref name=leglay>{{cite book | title=A History of Rome | edition=Second | first1=Marcel | last1=LeGlay | first2=Jean-Louis | last2=Voisin | first3=Yann | last3=Le Bohec | page=128 | publisher=Blackwell | place=Malden, Massachusetts | year=2001 | isbn=0-631-21858-0}}</ref>
* Creation of the [[First Triumvirate]], an informal political alliance between [[Julius Caesar]], [[Pompey|Pompey the Great]] and [[Marcus Licinius Crassus]] (or [[59 BC]]).<ref name=Dupuy/>

==== Syria ====
* The [[Seleucid Empire]] comes to an end with the last two emperors being murdered on orders from Rome.{{cn|date=February 2024}}

==== China ====
* The [[Han dynasty]] government establishes the [[Protectorate of the Western Regions]], the highest military position of a military commander on the Western frontier ([[Tarim Basin]]).{{cn|date=February 2024}}
</onlyinclude>

-61.title: 61 BC
-61.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Pompey]] returns to Rome with a [[Roman triumph|triumph]] in honor of his victories in the eastern provinces.<ref>{{cite book | first=John E. | last=Stambaugh | title=The Ancient Roman City | year=1988 | place=Baltimore | publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press | page=41 | isbn=0-8018-3574-7}}</ref>
* [[Marcus Pupius Piso Frugi Calpurnianus|Marcus Pupius Piso Frugi]] as [[Roman consul|consul]] attempts to gain ratification of Pompey's Eastern Settlement.
* [[Julius Caesar]] becomes governor in [[Hispania]] and creates ''[[Legio X Gemina]]'' (3,500 men). He puts down the [[Callaici]] and [[Lusitani]] rebellions.
</onlyinclude>

-62.title: 62 BC
-62.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[January 5]] – The forces of the conspirator [[Catiline]] are defeated by the loyal Roman armies of [[Antonius Hybrida]] led by [[Marcus Petreius]] in the [[Battle of Pistoria]].
* [[Julius Caesar]] divorces [[Pompeia (wife of Julius Caesar)|Pompeia]], following the sacrilege of [[Publius Clodius Pulcher]].
* [[Cicero]] delivers his [[Pro Archia Poeta]] in defense of [[Aulus Licinius Archias]]' claim to [[Roman citizenship]].
* [[Cato the Younger]], as [[tribune]], presents a ''lex frumentaria'' ([[Promulgation|enacting]] a grain [[Welfare spending|dole]]).
* [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Nepos (consul 57 BC)|Metellus Nepos]], also tribune, leaves [[Ancient Rome|Rome]].
* Caesar and Bibulus are [[praetors]].

==== Commagene ====
* King [[Antiochus I Theos of Commagene]] builds his mountain-top tomb-sanctuary at [[Mount Nemrut]].
</onlyinclude>

-63.title: 63 BC
-63.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Lucullus]] holds a [[Roman triumph|triumph]], then retires from war and politics to live a life of refined [[wikt:luxury|luxury]].
* Establishment of the [[Decapolis]] and Year 1 of the [[Pompeian era]].
* [[Pompey]] conquers the people of [[Phonecia]], [[Coele-Syria]], and [[Judea]] for the [[Roman Republic]].
* Roman annexation of the [[Seleucid Empire]] and of Judea as a [[client kingdom]]. King [[Judah Aristobulus II]] removed from power, while his brother [[John Hyrcanus II]] is reappointed king ([[ethnarch]]) under Roman [[suzerainty]] and high priest, until [[40 BC]].
* Massacre of over 12,000 [[Jew]]s on the [[Temple Mount]] in [[Jerusalem]] by Roman troops, in support of John Hyrcanus II against Aristobulus II.
* [[Julius Caesar]] is elected [[Pontifex Maximus]] and praetor for 62 BC.<ref name=leglay>{{cite book | title=A History of Rome | edition=Second | first1=Marcel | last1=LeGlay | first2=Jean-Louis | last2=Voisin | first3=Yann | last3=Le Bohec | page=128 | publisher=Blackwell | place=Malden, Massachusetts | year=2001 | isbn=0-631-21858-0}}</ref>
* [[Marcus Tullius Cicero]] is senior [[consul]]. He is the first ''[[novus homo]]'' (new man) to be elected to the [[consulship]] in 31 years.
* [[Gaius Antonius Hybrida]] is junior consul.
* [[Cato the Younger]] is elected [[tribune]] of the people for 62 BC, taking office in early December 63 BC.
* [[Servilius Rullus]], a Roman [[tribune]], proposes an [[agrarian reform]] law.
* [[Second Catilinarian Conspiracy]] against the [[Roman Republic]] is foiled by [[Cicero]].

==== Pontus ====
* [[Pharnaces II of Pontus|Pharnaces II]] becomes King of [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontus]].
</onlyinclude>

-65.title: 65 BC
-65.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* In response to the illegal exercise of [[citizen rights]] by foreigners, the [[Roman Senate]] passes the ''Lex Papia'', which expels all foreigners from [[Rome]]<ref>Husband, R. (1916). * [[Aristobulus II]] becomes king and high priest of [[Judea]], until [[63 BC]].

-67.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Manius Acilius Glabrio (consul 67 BC)|Manius Acilius Glabrio]] and [[Gaius Calpurnius Piso (consul 67 BC)|Gaius Calpurnius Piso]].
* During [[Pompey]]'s war against the pirates, he raises a fleet of 500 [[galley|warships]] and fights with great success.
* The ''[[lex Gabinia]]'' gives Pompey command of the [[Mediterranean]] and its coasts for 50 miles inland for three years. He defeats the pirates in three months and pacifies [[Cilicia]].
* Pompey divides the Mediterranean into 13 zones – six in the West and seven in the East –<ref>Salvatore Marino, "Toward the Assignment of Extraordinary Commands to Pompey in 67-66 BCE ", ''in Pompey’s New Order in the Mediterranean East (67–61 BCE) (Roman Relations, vol. 3),'' 2025'','' p. 26.</ref> to each of which he assigns a fleet under an [[admiral]].
* Pompey offers the ex-pirates and their families [[clemency]], he settles them in [[agriculture|agricultural]] [[Colony|colonies]] in eastern Mediterranean lands.
* Pompey takes over the command of [[Lucullus|Lucius Licinius Lucullus]] in [[Third Mithridatic War|the war]] against [[Mithridates VI of Pontus]], and [[Harvest|reaps]] the fruit of the latter's victories.
* [[Lex Acilia Calpurnia]]: permanent exclusion from office in cases of electoral corruption.
* [[Lex Roscia theatralis]].
* [[Julius Caesar]] reconciles with Pompey and [[Crassus]]<ref name=leglay>{{cite book | title=A History of Rome | edition=Second | first1=Marcel | last1=LeGlay | first2=Jean-Louis | last2=Voisin | first3=Yann | last3=Le Bohec | page=128 | publisher=Blackwell | place=Malden, Massachusetts | year=2001 | isbn=0-631-21858-0}}</ref>
* Julius Caesar marries Pompeia, a granddaughter of [[Sulla]]<ref name=leglay/>

==== Judea ====
* [[Hyrcanus II]] becomes king of [[Judea]], for first time (until [[66 BC]]), upon the death of his mother, [[Salome Alexandra]].

==== Pontus ====
* Mithridates VI invades [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontus]] and defeats a Roman army at the [[Battle of Zela (67 BC)|Battle of Zela]].
* After his victory at Zela, Mithridates starts consolidating his power in Pontus; restoring his rule over his old kingdom.
* Lucullus returnes to Pontus, but his troops refuse to campaign for him any longer and he withdrew to [[Galatia]].

==== China ====
* December – The army of the [[Han dynasty]] Chinese commander [[Zheng Ji (Han dynasty)|Zheng Ji]] is victorious over the [[Xiongnu]] in the [[Battle of Jushi]].

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Lucius Julius Caesar (consul 90 BC)|Lucius Julius Caesar]] and [[Publius Rutilius Lupus]].
* [[Social War (91–87 BC)|Social War]] continues: [[Pompeius Strabo]] and [[Gaius Marius]] distinguish themselves.
* The [[Etruscans]] are granted [[Roman citizen]]ship.
* [[Corfinium]] in south-central [[Italy]] is the center of a rebellion against [[Ancient Rome|Rome]].
* The ''[[Lex Iulia]]'' grants citizenship to all [[Italians]] who did not oppose Rome during the Social War.
* [[Cicero]] starts to serve in the [[Roman army]].

==== Asia Minor ====
* [[Arshak I of Iberia|Arshak I]] becomes king of [[Kingdom of Iberia (antiquity)|Caucasian Iberia]] after overthrowing [[Farnadjom of Iberia|Farnadjom]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Toumanoff |first1=Cyril |author1-link=Cyril Toumanoff |title=Chronology of the Early Kings of Iberia |journal=Traditio |date=January 1969 |volume=25 |pages=1–33 |doi=10.1017/S0362152900010898 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/traditio/article/abs/chronology-of-the-early-kings-of-iberia/BC87B05B526C70E06283211D3C38C286 |language=en |issn=0362-1529|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* [[Nicomedes IV of Bithynia]] is defeated in battle by a coalition of Nicomedes' brother Socrates, and [[Mithridates VI of Pontus]]. Nicomedes flees to Rome.

==== China ====
* The [[Xiongnu]] invade the Prefectures of [[Wuyuan County, Inner Mongolia|Wuyuan]] and [[Jiuquan]] and kill the commandants of both Prefectures.
* [[Emperor Wu of Han]] sends three armies against the Xiongnu under General-in-Chief [[Li Guangli]], Ma Tong and Shang Qiucheng, marching from Wuyuan, Jiuqian and Xihe respectively. An army of Central Asian vassals of Han, under Cheng Mian, captures the king of the vassal state of Jushi, who is suspected of treachery. The Xiongnu General-in-Chief and the former Han general [[Li Ling]] fight indecisively against Shang's army.
* Li Guangli and his in-law Prime Minister Liu Qumao seek to recommend Liu Bo, Li Guangli's nephew, as the new Crown Prince, and while Li Guangli is on campaign, Liu Qumao and his wife are executed and Li Guangli's wife imprisoned, having been charged with cursing the emperor and seeking to replace him with Liu Bo.
* Wishing to please the emperor, Li Guangli and his 70,000 men penetrate as far as the [[Selenga River]]. A detachment crosses the river and defeats an army of 20,000 under the Xiongnu Left General-in-Chief, who is killed. However, Li Guangli is then defeated by [[Hulugu|Hulugu Chanyu]]'s army of 50,000 in the [[Khangai Mountains]] and surrenders. Li Guangli marries Hulugu's daughter, and Emperor Wu exterminates Li's clan.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 233–235}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Roman consul|Consul]]s: [[Sextus Julius Caesar (consul 91 BC)|Sextus Julius Caesar]] and [[Lucius Marcius Philippus (consul 91 BC)|Lucius Marcius Philippus]].
* The tribune [[Marcus Livius Drusus (reformer)|Marcus Livius Drusus]] proposes extending [[Roman citizenship]] to allied Italian cities, but is assassinated, leading to the [[Social War (91–87 BC)|Social War]].

==== China ====
* Witchcraft Trials
:*[[Emperor Wu of Han]] executes Prime Minister Gongsun He (the brother-in-law of Empress [[Wei Zifu]]) and his clan because Gongsun's son is accused of adultery with the emperor's daughter Princess Yangshi and witchcraft.
:* Following further accusations of witchcraft, the emperor executes hundreds of imperial officials and concubines.
:* After convincing the emperor that his ill health is caused by witchcraft, the prosecutor Jiang Chong is given charge of investigating the matter. People accuse each other of witchcraft, and tens of thousands are executed across China, including former generals Zhao Ponu and [[Gongsun Ao]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 224–227|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
* 'Rebellion' of [[Liu Ju]]
:* July - After Jiang Chong frames Crown Prince Liu Ju of witchcraft and prevents communication between the prince and his father, Liu Ju kills Jiang, former general Han Yue and their followers. Due to miscommunication, the emperor misinterprets this as a rebellion against himself, and he orders Prime Minister Liu Qumao to march against Liu Ju. 
:* After being defeated in Chang'an, Liu Ju and his mother, Empress Wei Zifu, commit suicide. Emperor Wu exterminates the followers of Liu Ju and their families.
:* Learning that the charges against Liu Ju were fabricated, Emperor Wu orders further executions.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 227–233}}</ref>
* September - The [[Xiongnu]] invade the prefectures of Shanggu and Wuyuan.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 233}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Gnaeus Octavius (consul 87 BC)|Gnaeus Octavius]] and [[Lucius Cornelius Cinna]] are inaugurated as consuls. With Cinna seeking to [[Elections in the Roman Republic|enrol]] the [[Socii|Italians]] into all the [[Tribal assembly|tribes]] {{lang|la|[[Political violence|per vim]]}}, he is expelled from the city by Octavius and replaced as consul by [[Lucius Cornelius Merula (consul 87 BC)|Lucius Merula]]. Mobilising against the regime at Rome, Cinna [[Bellum Octavianum|marches on the city]], occupies it with the support of [[Gaius Marius]], and regains his consulship. In the aftermath Octavius is killed, Merula is forced to suicide.{{sfn|Broughton|1952|pp=45–46}}
* [[First Mithridatic War]]: [[Siege of Athens and Piraeus (87–86 BC)|Siege of Athens (87–86 BC)]] – [[Sulla]] arrives in [[Greece]] and from Autumn besieges [[Athens]]. He orders [[Lucullus|Lucius Licinius Lucullus]] to raise a fleet from Rome's allies around the eastern Mediterranean.

==== China ====
* [[March 29]] – [[Emperor Wu of Han]] dies after a 54-year reign in which he leads the [[Han dynasty]] ([[China]]) through its greatest expansion. The Empire's borders span from modern [[Kyrgyzstan]] in the west, to [[Mongolia]] in the north, to [[Korea]] in the east, and to northern [[Vietnam]] in the south.
* [[March 30]] – The eight-year-old [[Liu Fuling]] becomes emperor, with [[Huo Guang]] General-in-Chief and regent.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|page= 239|publisher= Algora}}</ref>

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Consul]]s: [[Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo]] and [[Lucius Porcius Cato]].
* [[Social War (91–87 BC)|Social War]]:
** Roman forces under [[Lucius Porcius Cato]] are defeated by the Italian rebels in the [[Battle of Fucine Lake]], Cato is killed.
** The Roman army of [[Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo]] decisively defeats the rebels in the [[Battle of Asculum (89 BC)|Battle of Asculum]].
* ''[[Lex Plautia Papiria]]'' extends citizenship to all [[Italians]] who applied for it within 60 days. The new citizens are enrolled in eight designated tribes, to prevent domination of the assemblies.
* ''Lex Pompeia'' grants Latin rights to cities in [[Cisalpine Gaul]].
* [[Pompeii]] is annexed by the [[Roman Republic]].
* [[Cicero]] ends his service in the [[Roman army]].

==== Asia Minor ====
* [[Mithridates VI]] of [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontus]] invades [[Bithynia]] and [[Cappadocia]], thus beginning the [[First Mithridatic War]].

==== Xiongnu ====
* The former [[Han dynasty|Han]] General-in-Chief [[Li Guangli]], now the son-in-law of [[Hulugu|Hulugu Chanyu]], is arrested and sacrificed to the gods to restore the health of Hulugu's mother.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 235–236|publisher= Algora}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-88.title: 88 BC
-88.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* The [[Social War (Italian)|Social War]] ends with the defeat of the Italian allies by the [[Roman Republic|Romans]].
* August: The consul [[Sulla|Lucius Cornelius Sulla]] becomes the first Roman commander to [[March on Rome (88 BC)|march on Rome]] with his army and to capture the city by force. This extraordinary act is prompted by his desire to maintain his proconsular command for the [[First Mithridatic War]] in [[Asia Minor]].<ref>Pompey, Command (p. 11). Nic Fields, 2012. {{ISBN|978-1-84908-572-4}}</ref> Sulla then murdered his enemy [[P. Sulpicius Rufus]] and forced [[Gaius Marius]] to flee to [[Africa]].
* The [[Dardani]], [[Scordisci]], and the [[Maedi]] attack the Roman province of [[Macedonia (Roman province)|Macedonia]].

==== Greece ====
* May – King [[Mithridates VI]] of [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontus]] invades [[Greece]]. Defeating the Roman forces four times in succession, he conquers [[Bithynia]], [[Phrygia]], [[Mysia]], [[Lycia]], [[Pamphylia]], [[Ionia]] and [[Cappadocia]]. The Roman province of [[Asia (Roman province)|Asia]] is dismantled. On the king's orders, the local authorities in every city of the province round up and [[Asiatic Vespers|put to death all resident Italians]] in a single day (App.''Mith''.§§85–91). Plutarch (Sulla 24.4) says that 150,000 are killed, other sources calculate a figure of 80,000 people.<ref>Pompey, Command (p. 39). Nic Fields, 2012. {{ISBN|978-1-84908-572-4}}</ref>
==== China ====
* [[Emperor Wu of Han]] makes preparations for the six-year-old [[Liu Fuling]] to be made Crown Prince and establishes [[Huo Guang]] as the future regent. The emperor executes Fuling's mother [[Lady Gouyi]] so that she cannot dominate the state while Fuling is a child emperor.<ref>{{cite book|first=Hing Ming|last= Hung|title=The Magnificent Emperor Wu: China's Han Dynasty|year= 2020|isbn=978-1628944167|pages= 237–239}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-86.title: 86 BC
-86.events:
<onlyinclude>
=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[First Mithridatic War]]
** [[March 1]] – [[Siege of Athens and Piraeus (87–86 BC)|Siege of Athens (87–86 BC)]] ends when [[Sulla]] captures [[Athens]] from the [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontic]] army, removing the tyrant [[Aristion]].
** [[Lucullus|Lucius Licinius Lucullus]] decisively defeats the Mithridatic fleet in the [[Battle of Tenedos (86 BC)|Battle of Tenedos]].
** The [[Roman Republic|Roman]] forces of [[Lucius Cornelius Sulla]] defeat the [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontic]] forces of [[Archelaus (Pontic army officer)|Archelaus]] in the [[Battle of Chaeronea (86 BC)|Battle of Chaeronea]].
** The [[Dardani]] ally with Pontus and are defeated by Sulla soon after.</onlyinclude>

-85.title: 85 BC
-85.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[First Mithridatic War]]: [[Lucius Cornelius Sulla]] again defeats [[Archelaus (Pontic army officer)|Archelaus]] in the decisive [[Battle of Orchomenus]].
</onlyinclude>

-84.title: 84 BC
-84.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Asia ====
* [[Battle of Cana]]: The Arab [[Nabataean Kingdom]] decisively defeats the Greek [[Seleucid Empire]], slaying King [[Antiochus XII Dionysus]], at modern-day [[Umm Qais]] in [[Jordan]].

==== Roman Republic ====
* The [[First Mithridatic War]] comes to an end.
* [[Julius Caesar]] marries Cornelia<ref>{{cite book | title=A History of Rome | edition=Second | first1=Marcel | last1=LeGlay | first2=Jean-Louis | last2=Voisin | first3=Yann | last3=Le Bohec | page=128 | publisher=Blackwell | place=Malden, Massachusetts | year=2001 | isbn=0-631-21858-0}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-83.title: 83 BC
-83.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* Spring – [[Lucius Cornelius Sulla]] returns to [[Italy]] from his campaigns in [[Ancient Greece|Greece]] and lands with his [[Roman legion|legions]] unopposed at [[Brindisi|Brundisium]]. He defeats the popular forces of [[Gaius Norbanus]] in the [[Battle of Mount Tifata]].
* [[Pompey|Gnaeus Pompeius]], age 22, raises, on his own initiative, a private army of three legions from his father's veterans and ''{{lang|la|clientelae}}'' in [[Picenum]].<ref>Nic Fields (2012). Osprey series: Command - Pompey, p. 7. {{ISBN|978-1-84908-572-4}}.</ref>
* [[Lucius Licinius Murena (propraetor in Asia)|Lucius Licinius Murena]], the [[Roman Republic|Roman]] governor of [[Asia (Roman province)|Asia]], clashes with the [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontic]] forces of [[Mithridates VI]], starting the [[Second Mithridatic War]].
* A fire breaks out which burns down the [[Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus|Temple of Jupiter]] (Jupiter Capitolinus) and destroys the collection of [[Sibylline Books]].
* Two new buildings were completed on the [[Capitoline Hill]] in Rome: the [[Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus]] and the [[Tabularium]].<ref>{{cite book | first=John E. | last=Stambaugh | title=The Ancient Roman City | year=1988 | place=Baltimore | publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press | page=40 | isbn=0-8018-3574-7}}</ref>

==== Syria ====

* [[Tigranes the Great]], King of [[Kingdom of Armenia (antiquity)|Armenia]] was invited by a faction in the [[Seleucid Dynastic Wars|Seleucid civil wars]], entered Syria and effectively ended [[Seleucid Empire|Seleucid]] rule.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Litovchenko |first=Sergey |date=2015 |title=Царствование Тиграна II Великого в Сирии: проблемы хронологии |trans-title=The reign of Tigranes the Great in Syria: chronology problems |url=https://www.academia.edu/30065529 |journal=Ancient World and Archaeology |issue=17 |pages=176–191}}</ref> Though a weakened Seleucid monarchy was briefly restored after Roman victories, ongoing instability led [[Pompey]] to abolish the dynasty and annex [[Roman Syria|Syria as a Roman province]] in 63 BC.</onlyinclude>

-82.title: 82 BC
-82.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* April: [[Sulla]] defeats the consul [[Gaius Marius the Younger]] at the [[Battle of Sacriportus]], and takes control of Rome.
* [[November 1]]: Sulla defeats an army of [[Samnites]] and [[Lucanians]] alliance in the [[Battle of the Colline Gate (82 BC)|Battle of the Colline Gate]].<ref name=":0">[[François Hinard]], ''Les proscriptions de la Rome républicaine'', Rome, Ecole française de Rome, 1985, pp. 108, 109, 116. ISBN 2728300941</ref>
* [[November 2]]: Sulla slaughters the Samnite prisoners in the [[Villa publica]]; the senate rejects his proscription plan.<ref name=":0" />
* [[November 3]]: Sulla passes his [[Sulla's proscription|proscription]] through a [[Citizens' assemblies of the Roman Republic|popular assembly]]; he publishes a list of 520 senators and [[equites]] to be murdered on sight.<ref name=":0" />
* [[Gaius Marius the Younger]] is besieged at the fortress city of [[Praeneste]] in [[Latium]]. After a fierce resistance, Marius commits suicide.
* [[Pompey]] is ordered by Sulla to stamp out Marian rebels in [[Sicily]] and [[Africa]], after his campaigns in he gets the insulting [[nickname]] of ''adulescentulus carnifex'', the "teenage butcher".
* [[Lucius Licinius Murena (triumphator)|Lucius Licinius Murena]] launches a raid against [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontus]] in the [[Battle of Halys]], starting the [[Second Mithridatic War]].

==== Dacia ====
* [[Burebista]] unifies the Dacian population forming the first (and biggest) unified [[Dacia|Dacian Kingdom]], on the territory of modern [[Romania]] and surroundings. 82 BC is also the starting year of his reign.

=== By topic ===

==== Astronomy ====
* The Aurigid shower parent comet [[C/1911 N1 (Kiess)]] returns to the inner solar system and sheds the dust particles that one revolution later cause the 1935, 1986, 1994, and 2007 Aurigid meteor outbursts on Earth.
</onlyinclude>

-81.title: 81 BC
-81.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Lucius Cornelius Sulla|Sulla]] is appointed ''[[Roman dictator|dictator]]'', executes his political enemies in a series of proscriptions, and implements aristocratic reforms to the [[Roman Republic|Roman]] government.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Badian |first=Ernst |author-link=Ernst Badian |date=2003 |title=Sulla |url=https://www-.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780192801074.001.0001/acref-9780192801074-e-504 |encyclopedia=Who's Who in the Classical World |location= |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |access-date=2 August 2026 |isbn=9780191727894 |via=[[Oxford Reference]]}}</ref>
* The [[Second Mithridatic War]] ends with the ''[[status quo]]''.
* [[Cicero]] wins his first case.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Balsdon |first1=John Percy Vyvian |author-link1=J. P. V. D. Balsdon |last2=Griffin |first2=Miriam T. |author-link2=Miriam T. Griffin |last3=Powell |first3=Jonathan G. F. |author-link3=Jonathan Powell (classicist) |last4=Simon |first4=John Hedley |author-link4= |last5=Obbink |first5=Dirk |author-link5=Dirk Obbink  |date=2014 |title=Cicero |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/view/10.1093/acref/9780198706779.001.0001/acref-9780198706779-e-143 |encyclopedia=The Oxford Companion to Classical Civilization |location= |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |access-date=2 August 2026 |isbn=9780191778483 |via=[[Oxford Reference]]}}</ref>

==== China ====
*[[Sang Hongyang]] and 60 [[Confucianism|Confucian]] scholars debate over the [[Discourses on Salt and Iron|state monopoly of Iron and Salt]].
</onlyinclude>

-80.title: 80 BC
-80.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Quintus Sertorius]] re-enters [[Iberia]] with a tiny army (2,600 men) and opens a successful campaign against the Sullan forces.
* [[Battle of the Baetis River]]: A force of Populares exiles under Sertorius defeat the legal [[Roman army]] of Lucius Fulfidias in [[Hispania Citerior|Hispania]], starting the [[Sertorian War]]; [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius]] takes command on behalf of [[Sulla]].
* [[Pompeii]] becomes the Roman colony ''Colonia Cornelia Veneria Pompei'' when Sulla occupies the city with at least 4,000 soldier-colonizers.<ref>{{cite book | first=John E. | last=Stambaugh | title=The Ancient Roman City | year=1988 | place=Baltimore | publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press | page=263 | isbn=0-8018-3574-7}}</ref>

==== Egypt ====
* [[Ptolemy XII]] Auletes succeeds [[Ptolemy XI Alexander II]] to the throne of [[History of Ptolemaic Egypt|Egypt]].
* Ptolemy XI marries [[Berenice III of Egypt|Berenice III]], but murders his bride for unknown reasons.
* [[Alexandria]] comes under Roman jurisdiction.

=== By topic ===

==== Art ====
* Roman artists begin to extend the space of a room visually with painted scenes of figures on a shallow [[Stage (theatre)|stage]] or with a [[landscape]] or [[cityscape]].

==== Literature ====
* [[Meleager of Gadara|Meleager]] publishes his ''Garland'', the earliest known anthology of [[Greek literature|Greek]] [[poetry]].
</onlyinclude>

-78.title: 78 BC
-78.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* In [[Rome]], [[Marcus Aemilius Lepidus (120-77 BC)|Marcus Aemilius Lepidus]] becomes [[consul]]. He attempts to undermine the Sullan reforms, quarrels with his consular colleague, is sent to govern [[Transalpine Gaul]], and initiates [[Lepidus's Rebellion|a rebellion]] against the Senate with his army there.
* The [[Roman Senate|Senate]] sends [[Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus (consul 79 BC)|Publius Servilius Vatia]] to [[Cilicia]] as governor, where he fights a successful campaign against the [[Piracy]] in southern [[Anatolia]] ([[Lycia]], [[Pamphylia]] and [[Isauria]]), he is thereafter known by the agnomen Isauricus.
* The [[Tabularium]] is built in the Forum.
* The Third Dalmatian war begins.
* [[Julius Caesar]] returns to Rome after about two years of service in the army<ref>{{cite book | title=A History of Rome | edition=Second | first1=Marcel | last1=LeGlay | first2=Jean-Louis | last2=Voisin | first3=Yann | last3=Le Bohec | page=128 | publisher=Blackwell | place=Malden, Massachusetts | year=2001 | isbn=0-631-21858-0}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-79.title: 79 BC
-79.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman republic ====
* [[Sulla]] renounces his [[Roman dictator|dictator]]ship.
* [[Cicero]] travels to [[Athens]] and then to [[Rhodes]] to continue his studies of [[philosophy]] and [[Public speaking|oratory]].
</onlyinclude>

-74.title: 74 BC
-74.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Nicomedes IV of Bithynia|Nicomedes IV]], last king of [[Bithynia]] bequeaths his kingdom to the [[Roman Senate]] upon his death (75/4 BC)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Bithynia#ref84381|title=Bithynia|access-date=31 August 2026|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|date=29 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://silver.kbr.be/Nicomedes_IV_of_Bithynia_(king_of_Bithynia,_c._94-74_BC)|title=Nicomedes IV of Bithynia (king of Bithynia, c. 94-74 BC)|website=Royal Library of Belgium (KBR)|access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>
* [[Third Mithridatic War]]: [[Battle of Cyzicus (74 BC)|Battle of Cyzicus]]: [[Roman Republic|Roman]] forces under [[Lucius Lucullus]] defeat the forces of [[Mithridates VI of Pontus]].
* [[Marcus Antonius Creticus|Marcus Antonius]] (father of [[Mark Antony]]), a [[praetor]], receives wide-ranging powers and considerable resources to fight the [[Piracy|pirates]] in the [[Mediterranean Sea]].
* [[Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus (consul 79 BC)|Publius Servilius Vatia]] returns to [[Ancient Rome|Rome]], where he has triumphed against the pirates in [[Anatolia]], and is given the [[agnomen]] ''Isauricus''. 
* [[Cyrene, Libya|Cyrene]] becomes a Roman province.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.africanworldheritagesites.org/cultural-places/frontiers-of-the-roman-empire/cyrene.html|website=African World Heritage Sites|title=Archaeological site of Cyrene - Libya|access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>

==== Spain ====
* [[Pamplona]] is founded.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pamplona.es/en/the-city/discover-pamplona|title=Discover Pamplona|access-date=31 August 2026|website=Ayuntamiento de Pamplona}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

-75.title: 75 BC
-75.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* In [[Roman Republic|Rome]], the tribune Quintus Opimius speaks out against Sullan restrictions on the tribunate, in orations noted for sarcasm against conservatives.
* [[Cicero]] is [[quaestor]] in Western Sicily.
* [[Nicomedes IV]] of [[Bithynia]] bequeaths his kingdom to [[Roman Republic|Rome]] on his death (75/4 BC).   Angered by the arrangement, [[Mithridates VI]] of [[Kingdom of Pontus|Pontus]] declares war on Rome and invades Bithynia, [[Cappadocia]] and [[Paphlagonia]], thus starting the [[Third Mithridatic War]].
* [[Third Mithridatic War]]: [[Marcus Aurelius Cotta (consul 74 BC)|Marcus Aurelius Cotta]] is defeated by [[Mithridates VI of Pontus|Mithridates]] in the [[Battle of Chalcedon (75 BC)|Battle of Chalcedon]].
* [[Julius Caesar]] travels to [[Rhodes]] and is taken captive by pirates<ref>{{cite book | title=A History of Rome | edition=Second | first1=Marcel | last1=LeGlay | first2=Jean-Louis | last2=Voisin | first3=Yann | last3=Le Bohec | page=128 | publisher=Blackwell | place=Malden, Massachusetts | year=2001 | isbn=0-631-21858-0}}</ref>
* In the [[Roman Republic|Roman]] province of [[Hispania Citerior]] a [[Roman Republic|republican]] army under [[Pompey|Pompey the Great]] defeats an army of [[Sertorian War|Sertorian rebels]] at the [[Battle of Valentia (75 BC)|Battle of Valentia]].
* In the [[Roman Republic|Roman]] province of [[Hispania Ulterior]] a [[Roman Republic|republican]] army under [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius]] defeats an army of [[Sertorian War|Sertorian rebels]] at the [[Battle of Italica]].
* In the [[Roman Republic|Roman]] province of [[Hispania Citerior]] an army of [[Sertorian War|Sertorian rebels]] under [[Quintus Sertorius]] himself defeats a [[Roman Republic|republican]] army under [[Pompey|Pompey the Great]] at the [[Battle of Sucro]].
* At the [[Battle of Saguntum (75 BC)|Battle of Saguntum]] the [[Roman Republic|republican forces]] on the [[Iberian Peninsula]] and the [[Sertorian War|Sertorian]] rebels fight each other to a draw. [[Quintus Sertorius]] is forced to withdraw leaving the battlefield to [[Pompey]] and [[Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius|Metellus]] (the republican commanders).

==== Greece ====
* [[Julius Caesar]] travels to [[Rhodes]] to study under [[Apollonius Molon]]. On his way across the [[Aegean Sea]], he is kidnapped by [[Cilician]] pirates and held prisoner in the [[Dodecanese]] islet of [[Farmakonisi|Pharmacusa]]. The young Caesar is held for a ransom of twenty [[talent (measurement)|talents]], but he insists they ask for fifty. After his release Caesar raises a fleet at [[Miletus]], pursues and [[crucifixion|crucifies]] the pirates in [[Pergamon]].

=== By topic ===

==== Literature ====
* Start of [[Golden Age of Latin Literature]].
</onlyinclude>

-77.title: 77 BC
-77.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Roman Republic ====
* [[Marcus Aemilius Lepidus (consul 78 BC)|Marcus Aemilius Lepidus]], Roman proconsul of Transalpine Gaul and [[leader]] of the Populares faction in the senate, is defeated by [[Quintus Lutatius Catulus Capitolinus|Quintus Lutatius Catulus]] at the Milvian bridge outside [[Rome]]. The remnants of the rebels are wiped out by [[Pompey]] in [[Etruria]].
* Lepidus, with some 21,000 troops, manages to escape to [[Sardinia]]. Soon afterwards he becomes ill and dies, his battered army, now under command by [[Marcus Perperna Vento]], sails on to the [[Iberian Peninsula]].<ref>Pompey, Command (p. 12). Nic Fields, 2012. {{ISBN|978-1-84908-572-4}}.</ref>
