<onlyinclude>
* [[July 11]] – The [[Armenian calendar]] is introduced.

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[July 1]] – [[Battle of Taginae]]: [[Narses]] crosses the [[Apennine Mountains|Apennines]] with a Byzantine army (25,000 men). He is blocked by a [[Goths|Gothic]] force under King [[Totila]] near [[Gualdo Tadino|Taginae]] ([[Central Italy]]). In a narrow mountain valley, Narses deploys his army in a "crescent shaped" formation.<ref>Rance, Philip. "Narses and the Battle of Taginae (Busta Gallorum)". ''Historia: Zeitschrift für Alte Geschichte'' Vol. 54, No. 4 (2005), p. 424</ref> He dismounts his [[Lombards|Lombard]] and [[Heruli]] cavalry mercenaries, placing them as a [[Phalanx formation|phalanx]] in the center. On his left flank he sends out a mixed force of foot and [[Mounted archery|horse archer]]s to seize a dominant height. The Goths open the battle with a determined [[cavalry]] charge. Halted by [[Enfilade and defilade|enfilading]] fire from both sides, the attackers are thrown back in confusion on the infantry behind them. The Byzantine [[cataphract]]s (''[[Clibanarii]]'') sweep into the milling mass. More than 6,000 Goths, including Totila, are killed. The remnants flee, and Narses proceeds to [[Rome]], where he captures the city after a brief [[siege]].
* Emperor [[Justinian I]] dispatches a small Byzantine force (2,000 men) under [[Liberius (praetorian prefect)|Liberius]] to [[Hispania]], according to the historian [[Jordanes]]. He conquers [[Cartagena, Spain|Cartagena]] and other cities on the southeastern coast.<ref>''Getica'', p. 303</ref> 
* Justinian I receives the first [[silk]]worm eggs from two [[Church of the East|Nestorian]] monks at [[Constantinople]]. They were sent to [[Central Asia]] (see [[550]]) and [[Smuggling of silkworm eggs into the Byzantine Empire|smuggled the precious eggs]] from [[China]] hidden in rods of [[bamboo]].

==== Europe ====
* [[Battle of Asfeld]]: The Lombards under King [[Audoin]] defeat the [[Gepids]].
* [[Cynric of Wessex|Cynric]], king of [[Wessex]], captures the fortress city of [[Old Sarum]].<ref name=Leeds>{{cite journal |last=Leeds |first=E.T. |year=1954 |title=The Growth of Wessex |journal=[[Oxoniensia]] |volume=LIX |pages=55–56 |publisher=[[Oxfordshire Architectural and Historical Society|Oxford Architectural and Historical Society]] |url=http://oxoniensia.org/oxo_volume.php?vol=59 |access-date=6 October 2011}}</ref>
* The [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Meath]] is established in [[Ireland]].
* [[Teia]] becomes the last king of the [[Ostrogoths]] in [[Italy]].

==== Asia ====
* [[July 11]] – First year of the [[Armenian calendar]].
* [[Emperor Yuan of Liang|Yuan Di]] succeeds [[Xiao Dong]] as emperor of the [[Liang dynasty]].
* [[Bumin Qaghan]] dies; the new khagan is [[Issik Qaghan]] of the Turkic Empire.
* [[Buddhism in Japan]] is introduced, according to the [[Nihon Shoki]].

=== By topic ===
==== Industry ====
* [[Smuggling of silkworm eggs into the Byzantine Empire]] by monks allows development of the [[Byzantine silk]] industry in the Empire.

==== Religion ====
* [[Eutychius of Constantinople|Eutychius]] becomes [[Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople|patriarch of Constantinople]].</onlyinclude>

554.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[August 13]] – Byzantine Emperor [[Justinian I]] issues [[Pragmatic Sanction of Justinian I|a pragmatic sanction]] reorganizing Italy, and rewards the praetorian prefect [[Liberius (praetorian prefect)|Liberius]] for over 60 years of distinguished service, granting him extensive [[Estate (land)|estate]]s in Italy.<ref>James J. O'Donnell, [https://www.jstor.org/stable/27831089 "Liberius the Patrician", ''Traditio''], '''37''' (1981), p. 69</ref>
* [[August 15]] – The [[554 Anatolia earthquake]] takes place in the southwest coasts of [[Anatolia]] (Asia Minor). It affects the [[Güllük Gulf]] (Mandalya Gulf), and the island of [[Kos]].<ref>{{citation | last1=Antonopoulos | first1= J. | title=''Data from investigation of seismic Sea waves events in the Eastern Mediterranean from 500 to 1000 A.D.'' | year=1980 | publisher=Annals of Geophysics | url =https://www.annalsofgeophysics.eu/index.php/annals/article/viewFile/4702/4786}}</ref>
* [[October]] – [[Battle of the Volturnus (554)|Battle of the Volturnus]]: During the spring Butilinus (Buccelin) has marched north; the Frankish army (infected by an [[epidemic]] of [[dysentery]] which kills their leader Leutharis (Lothair)) is reduced to about 30,000 men. The [[Byzantine army]], with 18,000 men (including a contingent of [[Goths]] under [[Aligern]]), marches south to meet them at [[Casilinum]] (on the banks of the [[Volturno|River Volturno]]). Byzantine eunuch general [[Narses]] sends a cavalry force under [[Chanaranges (Italy)|Chanaranges]] to destroy the supply wagons of the [[Franks]]. Outmanoeuvring Butilinus, he chooses a disposition similar to that at [[Battle of Taginae|Taginae]]. After a [[frontal assault]] on the Byzantine centre, the Franks and the [[Alamanni]] are annihilated, thus effectively ending the [[Gothic War (535–554)]]. Narses garrisons an army of 16,000 men in [[Italy]]. The recovery of the [[Italian Peninsula]] has cost the empire about 300,000 pounds of gold.<ref>{{cite book|author-link=John Julius Norwich|first=John Julius|last=Norwich|title=Byzantium: The Early Centuries|page=233}}</ref>

==== Europe ====
* Byzantine forces under Liberius seize [[Granada]] ([[Andalusia]]) and occupy the old province of [[Hispania Baetica|Baetica]]. Justinian I calls [[Belisarius]] out of retirement, to complete the consolidation of reconquered regions of Southern [[Spain]].
* [[Athanagild]] is crowned as king of the [[Visigoths]] and succeeds [[Agila I]]. He acknowledges the [[suzerainty]] of the [[Byzantine Empire]].

==== Asia ====
* [[Al-Mundhir III ibn al-Nu'man]] is defeated and killed by the [[Ghassanids]] under [[al-Harith ibn Jabalah]], at the battle of [[Yawm Halima]]; [['Amr III ibn al-Mundhir]] succeeds as king of the [[Lakhmid kingdom]].
* [[Baekje]] and the [[Gaya Confederacy]] wage war upon [[Silla]], one of the [[Three Kingdoms of Korea]], but are defeated.
* [[Wideok of Baekje|Wideok]] becomes king of the Korean kingdom of [[Baekje]].<ref>{{cite web |title=List of Rulers of Korea |url=https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/koru/hd_koru.htm |website=www.metmuseum.org |access-date=21 April 2019}}</ref>
* [[Muqan Qaghan]] succeeds his brother [[Issik Qaghan]] as emperor (''[[khagan]]'') of the [[Göktürks]]. 
* The second and larger of the two [[Buddhas of Bamyan]] is erected in central [[Afghanistan]].<ref>[[Roger Cohen|Cohen, Roger]]. "Return to Bamiyan", ''The New York Times'', October 29, 2007. Accessed October 29, 2007.</ref>

==== China ====
* [[Emperor Gong of Western Wei|Gong Di]] succeeds his brother [[Emperor Fei of Western Wei|Fei Di]] as emperor of [[Western Wei]]. He is deposed by general [[Yuwen Tai]] who puts him to death.
* Siege and Fall of Jiangling: The Western Wei forces launched a military campaign against the Liang dynasty, targeting Jiangling, the Liang capital.
* After a protracted siege, Jiangling fell to the Western Wei army.
* Emperor Yuan of Liang (Xiao Yi) was captured during this assault and was subsequently executed.
* Mass Enslavement and Destruction: Following the capture of Jiangling, the city faced extensive looting and destruction. Historical records indicate that a large portion of the population was either killed or enslaved. The fall of Jiangling significantly weakened the Liang dynasty, leading to further internal strife and fragmentation. Power vacuums emerged, causing shifts in control among the remaining regional powers.  
* [[Wei Shou]] completes compilation of the ''[[Book of Wei]]''.

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* [[Cassiodorus]], Roman statesman, founds the [[Cassiodorus#|Monastery at Vivarium]] (approximate date).<ref>Jean Leclerq, ''"The Love of Learning and the Desire for God"'', 2nd revised edition (New York: Fordham, Fordham University Press, (1977), p. 25</ref>
</onlyinclude>
* [[Pope Vigilius]] was allowed to return to Rome after years of pressure from Emperor Justinian regarding the [[Second Council of Constantinople]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pope Vigilius |url=https://www.catholic.com/encyclopedia/pope-vigilius |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=Catholic Answers |language=en}}</ref>

558.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[May 7]] – In [[Constantinople]], the [[dome]] of the [[Hagia Sophia]] collapses due to an [[earthquake]]. Emperor [[Justinian I]] orders the dome to be rebuilt.

==== Europe ====
* The [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] and the [[Slavic peoples|Slavs]] occupy the [[Great Hungarian Plain|Hungarian Plain]] on the [[Balkans]]. The threat of Avar domination prompts the [[Lombards]] to [[Human migration|migrate]] to [[Italy]].<ref>{{cite book| author = Michael Whitby| title = Rome at War AD 293-696| date = 2002-11-13| publisher = Osprey Publishing Company| isbn = 978-1-84176-359-0| page = 59 }}</ref>  
* [[December 13]] – King [[Chlothar I]] reunites the [[Francia|Frankish Kingdom]] after his brother [[Childebert I]] dies, becoming sole ruler of the [[Franks]].
* [[December 23]] - [[Chlothar I]] is crowned [[List of Frankish kings|King of the Franks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Chlothar I |url=https://www.worldhistory.org/Chlothar_I/ |website=worldhistory.org |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref>
* [[Conall mac Comgaill]] becomes king of [[Dál Riata]], a [[Gaels|Gaelic]] overkingdom on the western coast of [[Scotland]].

==== Asia ====
* [[Istämi]], ruler of the [[Western Turkic Khaganate]], establishes [[Diplomacy|diplomatic]] relations with the [[Byzantine Empire]].

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* [[December 23]] – The [[Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés]] is dedicated by [[Germain of Paris|Germain]], [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Paris|bishop of Paris]].
* The [[Bangor Abbey]] is founded by the Irish [[abbot]] [[Comgall]] in [[Northern Ireland]] (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

559.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* Winter – The [[Kutrigurs]] and [[Huns]] under [[Zabergan]] cross the frozen [[Danube|Danube River]], and invade the [[Balkans]]. They raid [[Thracia]] and [[Macedonia (Roman province)|Macedonia]], but are driven back near [[Constantinople]] by a [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] force under [[Belisarius]].
* [[Battle of Melantias]]: Outside the [[Defensive wall|city walls]] of Constantinople, Belisarius defeats the combined "barbarians" with his veteran cavalry (''[[Bucellarius|bucellarii]]''), and a few thousand hastily raised levies.

==== Britain ====
* [[Glappa of Bernicia|Glappa]] succeeds his father [[Ida of Bernicia|Ida]] as king of [[Bernicia]] ([[North East England]]). During his rule, [[Angles (tribe)|Anglian]] settlers expand their territory in what is now southeastern [[Scotland]].

==== Asia ====
* First successful human flight: a [[kite]] carrying [[Yuan Huangtou]] lands in the proximity of [[Ye (Hebei)|Ye]]. Emperor [[Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi|Wen Xuan Di]] sponsors the flight; Yuan is taken prisoner; other imprisoned kite flyers also fly, but those die and Yuan survives. Yuan is executed afterwards.<ref>（永定三年）使元黄头与诸囚自金凤台各乘纸鸱以飞，黄头独能至紫陌乃堕，仍付御史中丞毕义云饿杀之。 (Rendering: [In the 3rd year of Yongding, 559], Gao Yang conducted an experiment by having Yuan Huangtou and a few prisoners launch themselves from a tower in Ye, capital of the Northern Qi. Yuan Huangtou was the only one who survived from this flight, as he glided over the city-wall and fell at Zimo [western segment of Ye] safely, but he was later executed.) [[Zizhi Tongjian]] 167.</ref> 
* [[Emperor Wen of Chen|Wen Di]], age 37, succeeds his uncle [[Emperor Wu of Chen|Chen Wu Di]] as emperor of the [[Chen dynasty]]. During his reign, he consolidates the state against the rebellious [[warlord]]s.
* The city-state [[Ara Gaya]], a member of the [[Gaya Confederacy|Gaya confederacy]], surrenders to [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]].
* [[Pyeongwon of Goguryeo|Pyeongwon]] becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of [[Goguryeo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=List of Rulers of Korea |url=https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/koru/hd_koru.htm |website=www.metmuseum.org |access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

560.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Europe ====
* [[Alboin]] succeeds his father [[Audoin]] after his death, as king of the [[Lombards]].

==== Britain ====
* [[Adda of Bernicia|Adda]] succeeds his brother [[Glappa of Bernicia|Glappa]] as king of [[Bernicia]] (approximate date).
* [[Ælla of Deira|Ælla]] becomes king of [[Deira (kingdom)|Deira]] (this according to the ''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]'').
* [[Ceawlin of Wessex|Ceawlin]] succeeds his father [[Cynric of Wessex|Cynric]] as king of [[Wessex]] (approximate date).
* [[List of kings of Dumnonia#Dumnonian kings|Custennin ap Cado]] abdicates as king of [[Dumnonia]] ([[South West England]]).
* [[Kingdom of Strathclyde|Elidyr of Strathclyde]] invades [[Kingdom of Gwynedd|Gwynedd]] ([[Wales]]) and tries to expel his brother-in-law, King [[Rhun ap Maelgwn]].

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* [[Columba]] quarrels with [[Finnian of Moville]] over authorship of a [[psalter]], leading to a pitched battle the next year.
</onlyinclude>

561.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Europe ====
* [[November 29]] – King [[Chlothar I]] ("the Old") dies at [[Compiègne]] at age 64. The [[Merovingian dynasty]] is continued by his four sons ([[Charibert I]], [[Guntram]], [[Sigebert I]] and [[Chilperic I]]), who divide the [[Francia|Frankish Kingdom]] and rule from the capitals at [[Paris]], [[Orléans]], [[Reims]] and [[Soissons]], respectively.

==== Britain ====

* The Battle of Cúl Drebene (modern [[Ireland]]) is fought between the Northern and Southern [[Uí Néill]] (approximate date).

==== Asia ====
* Winter – [[Emperor Wucheng of Northern Qi|Wu Cheng Di]] succeeds his brother [[Emperor Xiaozhao of Northern Qi|Xiao Zhao Di]], who dies from injuries suffered while [[hunting]], as Chinese emperor of [[Northern Qi]].

==== Americas ====
* [[Sky Witness (ruler)|Sky Witness]] is crowned as leader of [[Calakmul]].

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* [[March 4]] – [[Pope Pelagius I]] dies in [[Rome]] after a five-year reign, and is succeeded by [[Pope John III|John III]] as the 61st [[pope]].
* [[Jnanagupta]], a Buddhist [[monk]] from [[Gandhara]] ([[Pakistan]]), begins translating [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] texts into [[Chinese language|Chinese]].
* The [[First Council of Braga]] is held. The council condemns the doctrine of [[Priscillianism]].

563.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* Emperor [[Justinian I]] pardons [[Belisarius]]; he orders his release from [[prison]], and  restores his properties and [[honour]]s. He permits the general to live in obscurity, and gives him a veterans' [[pension]].
* The new [[Hagia Sophia]] (cost: 20,000 pounds of [[gold]]<ref>P. Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire: ''"A New History of Rome and the Barbarians"'', p. 283</ref>), with its numerous [[chapel]]s and [[shrine]]s, octagonal [[dome]] and [[mosaic]]s, becomes the centre and most visible monument of [[Eastern Orthodox Church|Eastern Orthodoxy]].

==== Europe ====
* [[Tauredunum event]]:<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/switzerland/9639046/Lake-Geneva-may-face-tsunami-risk.html|newspaper=Daily Telegraph|title=Lake Geneva 'may face tsunami risk'|date=28 October 2012|access-date=28 October 2012}}</ref> A mountain landslide into the [[Rhone]] river destroys a fort and two villages, and creates a [[tsunami]] in [[Lake Geneva]]. The wave which reaches [[Lausanne]] is thirteen metres high, and eight metres high by the time it hits [[Geneva]]. Describing the event, [[Marius Aventicensis]] writes that the tsunami "devastated very old villages with their men and cattle, it even destroyed many sacred places", and swept away "the bridge in Geneva, windmills and men".<ref>[http://passeurdesciences.blog.lemonde.fr/2012/10/28/des-chercheurs-reconstituent-le-tsunami-du-lac-leman-de-563/ "Des chercheurs reconstituent le tsunami du lac Léman de l’an 563"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905012101/http://passeurdesciences.blog.lemonde.fr/2012/10/28/des-chercheurs-reconstituent-le-tsunami-du-lac-leman-de-563/ |date=September 5, 2017 }}, ''[[Le Monde]]'', 28 October 2012</ref>

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* [[Columba]], Irish [[missionary]] [[monk]], travels to [[Scotland]] with twelve companions. He lands on the [[Mull of Kintyre|Kintyre]] Peninsula, near [[Southend, Argyll|Southend]], and begins his [[Evangelism|evangelising]] mission to the [[Picts]]. On the island of [[Iona]], he founds a monastery ([[Iona Abbey]]) on the west coast in the [[Inner Hebrides]].
</onlyinclude>

573.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====

* [[Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591|Byzantine–Sassanid War]]: [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]] forces under the command of King [[Khosrau I]] [[Siege of Dara (573)|capture]] the [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] stronghold of [[Dara (Mesopotamia)|Dara]], after a six-month [[siege]]. Meanwhile, a smaller Persian army under [[Adarmahan]] advances from [[Babylon]] through the [[desert]], crosses the [[Euphrates|Euphrates River]] and ravages [[Syria (Roman province)|Syria]]. The cities of [[Apamea, Syria|Apamea]] and [[Antioch]]ia are plundered.<ref>{{harvnb|Greatrex|Lieu|2002|pp=146–149, 150}}</ref>

==== Europe ====
* King [[Sigibert I]] goes to war against his half brother [[Chilperic I]] of [[Neustria]] at the urging of his wife, [[Brunhilda of Austrasia|Brunhilda]]. He appeals to the [[Germans]] on the right bank of the [[Rhine]] for help, and they obligingly attack the environs of [[Paris]] and [[Chartres]].   
* The [[Lombards]] again raid Southern [[Gaul]], but are defeated by the [[Franks]] under [[Mummolus]], ''[[Patrician (post-Roman Europe)|patricius]]'' and son of the [[Gallo-Roman culture|Gallo-Roman]] count of [[Auxerre]], and are driven out.
* King [[Cleph]] completes the Lombard conquest of [[Tuscany]] ([[Central Italy]]) and extends his [[dominion]] to the gates of [[Ravenna]].   
* Sigibert I appoints [[Gregory of Tours|Gregory]] to succeed his mother's cousin, [[Eufronius]], as [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Tours|bishop of Tours]] (approximate date).

==== Britain ====
* [[Battle of Arfderydd]]: Leading his warband, [[Gwenddoleu ap Ceidio]] is slain by the sons of Eliffer, Gwrgi and [[Peredur]]. [[Myrddin Wyllt]] goes mad watching this defeat (according to the ''[[Annales Cambriae]]'').<ref>Myles Dillon and Nora Chadwick, ''The Celtic Realms'' (New York: New American Library, 1967), p. 81</ref>

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* [[Pope John III]] is forced by the Lombards to retire from [[Rome]], and takes up residence at the [[Catacombs]] along the [[Appian Way|Via Appia]] (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

577.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591|Byzantine–Sassanid War]]: A [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] expeditionary force under command of [[Justinian (magister militum per Orientem)|Justinian]] (''[[magister militum]]'') invades [[Caucasian Albania]], launching raids across the [[Caspian Sea]] against the [[Sassanid Empire|Persians]].
* Summer – [[Tiberius II Constantine|Tiberius]], Byzantine co-ruler (''[[Caesar (title)|Caesar]]''), establishes a [[naval base]] at [[Derbent]] on the Caspian Sea to construct a [[Byzantine fleet]] (approximate date).
* Winter – [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]] is appointed commander-in-chief of the [[Byzantine army]] in the East. He succeeds Justinian, despite complete lack of military experience.

==== Europe ====
* [[Battle of Deorham]]: The [[Anglo-Saxons]] under [[Ceawlin of Wessex]] invade the lower [[Severn Valley (England)|Severn Valley]], and defeat the British [[Celt]]s at [[Dyrham]] ([[South West England]]). After the battle, the Saxons occupy the three cities: [[Cirencester]], [[Gloucester]] and [[Bath, Somerset|Bath]], bringing their advance to the [[Bristol Channel]] (according to the ''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]'').
*[[Reccopolis]] (modern [[Zorita de los Canes]]) in [[Hispania]] is founded by King [[Liuvigild]], in honour of his son [[Reccared I|Reccared]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=GRIG|first=LUCY|date=2013-03-19|title=Cities in the 'long' Late Antiquity, 2000–2012 – a survey essay|journal=Urban History|volume=40|issue=3|pages=554–566|doi=10.1017/s0963926813000369|s2cid=144860106 |issn=0963-9268}}</ref>

==== Asia ====
* Winter – [[Northern Qi]], one of the [[Southern and Northern Dynasties|Northern Dynasties]], is conquered by [[Northern Zhou]] under Emperor [[Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou|Wu Di]]. He orders the last ruler ([[Gao Wei]]) and other members of the Gao [[clan]] to commit suicide. [[North China Plain|Northern China]], above the [[Yangtze River]], is once again brought under the control of a single power.<ref>Imperial Chinese Armies (p. 23). C.J. Peers, 1995. {{ISBN|978-1-85532-514-2}}</ref>

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* The [[Temple of Dendur]], dedicated to the [[Egypt]]ian gods [[Isis]], Harpocrates ([[Horus]]) and [[Osiris]], is converted for use as a [[Christianity|Christian]] church (approximate date).
* [[Eutychius of Constantinople|Eutychius]] is restored as [[Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople|patriarch of Constantinople]], after an [[exile]] of 12 years at [[Amasya|Amasia]] (modern [[Turkey]]).<ref>{{cite DCBL|first=W. M. |last=Sinclair|wstitle=Eutychius}}</ref>
* [[Muhammad]], age 6, returns to his immediate family, but within a year his mother [[Aminah bint Wahb]] dies.

==== Science and Invention ====
* A predecessor of the modern [[match]], small sticks of [[pine]]wood impregnated with [[sulfur]], are first used in [[China]]. Besieged by military forces of [[Northern Zhou]] and [[Chen Dynasty|Chen]], [[Northern Qi]] court ladies use the "lighting sticks" to start fires for [[cooking]] and heating.<ref name="temple">{{cite book|author=Temple, Robert|year=1986|title=The Genius of China: 3,000 Years of Science, Discovery, and Invention|url=https://archive.org/details/geniusofchina00robe|url-access=limited|place=New York|publisher=Simon and Schuster, Inc|isbn=0-671-62028-2|page=[https://archive.org/details/geniusofchina00robe/page/98 98]}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

581.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[Byzantine–Sasanian War of 572–591|Byzantine–Sasanian War]]: A [[Byzantine army]] commanded by [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]], and supported by [[Ghassanids|Ghassanid]] forces under King [[Al-Mundhir III ibn al-Harith|Al-Mundhir III]], fails to capture the [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]] capital, [[Ctesiphon]], along the [[Euphrates]].<ref>Treadgold, p. 226</ref>
* Maurice accuses Mundhir III of [[treason]], and brings him to [[Constantinople]] to face trial. Emperor [[Tiberius II Constantine]] treats him well, and allows Mundhir with his family a comfortable [[Dwelling|residence]].<ref>Martindale, Jones& Morris 1992, p. 36</ref><ref>Shahîd 1995, p. 459–462</ref> 
* [[Al-Nu'man VI ibn al-Mundhir|Al-Nu'man VI]], son (''de facto'') of Mundhir III, revolts with the Ghassanids against the [[Byzantine Empire]], after his father is treacherously arrested.

==== Europe ====
* Palace coup in [[Austrasia]]: New advisors break the [[peace treaty]] with King [[Guntram]], and make a new [[Military alliance|alliance]] with his half brother [[Chilperic I]], in which [[Childebert II]], age 11, is recognized as Chilperic's heir.
* The [[Lombards]] under [[Zotto]], [[Duchy of Benevento|Duke of Benevento]], sack the [[abbey]] of [[Monte Cassino]] near [[Naples]]. The [[Order of Saint Benedict|Benedictine]] monks who survive flee to Rome, but they return to the site, and rebuild the [[monastery]].
* The [[Göktürks]] under [[Taspar Qaghan]] besiege the city of [[Chersonesos Taurica]] (modern [[Ukraine]]), located at the [[Black Sea]]; their cavalry keep [[Looting|plundering]] the steppes of the [[Crimean Peninsula]] until 590.<ref name="Grousset81">Grousset 81</ref>

==== Britain ====
* The [[Anglo-Saxons]] under [[Ælla of Deira|Ælla]] conquer [[Deira]] ([[Northern England]]) from the [[Celtic Britons|Britons]]. He becomes the first king of Deira (according to the ''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]'').

==== Asia ====
* The  [[Northern Zhou|Northern Zhou dynasty]] ends: [[Emperor Wen of Sui|Yáng Jiān]] executes the last ruler, 8-year-old [[Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou|Jing Di]], along with 58 royal relatives at [[Chang'an]]. He proclaims himself emperor, and establishes the [[Sui dynasty]] in China.
* The "Great City of Helu", situated on the shores of [[Lake Tai|Taihu Lake]], is renamed [[Suzhou, Jiangsu|Suzhou]] during the Sui dynasty (approximate date).
* In the [[Göktürks|Turkic Empire]] an interregnum begins, since there are several candidates to the throne: [[Talopien]] (late [[khagan]]'s candidate), [[Ishbara Qaghan|Ishbara]] ([[Kurultai]]'s choice) and [[Tardu]] (western [[yabghu]]).
* Ishbara Qaghan, grandson of [[Bumin Qaghan]], becomes the new ruler (''[[khagan]]'') of the [[Göktürks|Turkic Khaganate]] (Central Asia).
* The Sui dynasty begins.

=== By topic ===

==== Literature ====
* Maurice writes an encyclopedic work on the science of war (the ''[[Strategikon of Maurice|Strategikon]]''), which exercises a major influence on the military system.

==== Religion ====
* [[Second Council of Mâcon]]: In a [[Synod|council]] of Christian [[bishop]]s in [[Mâcon]] ([[Burgundy]]), Jews are prohibited from serving as [[judge]]s or customs officers.
</onlyinclude>

584.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Europe ====
* [[September]] – King [[Chilperic I]] is stabbed to death while returning from a [[Hunting|hunt]] near [[Chelles, Seine-et-Marne|Chelles]], after a 23-year reign over a territory extending from [[Aquitaine]], to the northern seacoast of what later will be [[France]].  His wife [[Fredegund]], who has paid for his [[assassination]], seizes his wealth, flees to [[Paris]] with her son [[Chlothar II]], and persuades the [[Nobility|nobles]] to accept him as legitimate heir while she serves as [[regent]], continuing her power struggles with [[Guntram]], king of [[Kingdom of Burgundy|Burgundy]], and her sister [[Brunhilda of Austrasia|Brunhilda]], queen mother of [[Austrasia]].
* The [[Lombards]] re-establish a unified monarchy after a 10-year [[interregnum]] ([[Rule of the Dukes]]). Threatened by a [[Franks|Frankish]] invasion that the [[Dux|duke]]s have provoked, they elect [[Authari]] (son of [[Cleph]]) as their king and give him the capital of [[Pavia]] ([[Northern Italy]]).
* The [[Visigoths]] under King [[Liuvigild]] capture the city of [[Seville]], after a [[siege]] of nearly 2 years. His rebellious son [[Hermenegild]] seeks refuge in a church at [[Córdoba, Spain|Córdoba]], but is arrested and banished to [[Tarragona]].<ref>[[John of Biclaro]], ''Chronicle'', chapter 69. Translated by Kenneth Baxter Wolf, ''Conquerors and Chroniclers of Early Medieval Spain'', second edition (Liverpool: University Press, 1999), p. 70 {{ISBN|0853235546}}</ref> His wife [[Ingund (wife of Hermenegild)|Inguld]] flees with her son to [[Diocese of Africa|Africa]].
* The [[Exarchate of Ravenna]] is founded, and organised into a group of [[Duchy|duchies]], mainly coastal cities on the [[Italian Peninsula]]. The civil and military head of these [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] territories is the ''[[exarch]]'' (governor) in [[Ravenna]]. 
* The [[Slavs]] push south on the [[Balkan|Balkan Peninsula]] – partly in conjunction with the [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] under their ruler (''[[khagan]]'') [[Bayan I]] – ravaging the cities [[Athens]] and [[Ancient Corinth|Corinth]], and threatening the [[Walls of Constantinople|Long Walls]] of [[Constantinople]].<ref>Michael Whitby (2002), ''Rome at War (AD 293–696)'', p. 60. {{ISBN|1-84176-359-4}}</ref>
* King [[Eboric]] is deposed by his mother (second husband [[Andeca]]) who becomes the new ruler of the [[Kingdom of Galicia]] (Northern [[Spain]]) and the [[Suebi|Suevi]].<ref>John of Biclaro, ''Chronicle'', chapter 68; translated by Kenneth Baxter Wolf, ''Conquerors and Chroniclers'', p. 70</ref>
* [[Gundoald]], illegitimate son of [[Chlothar I]], tries to expend his territory from [[Brive-la-Gaillarde]] (Burgundy) and proclaims himself king (approximate date).

==== Britain ====
* [[Ceawlin of Wessex#584: Fethan leag|Battle of Fethanleigh]]: King [[Ceawlin of Wessex]] is defeated by the [[Celtic Britons|Britons]]. He [[Looting|ravage]]s the surrounding countryside in revenge (approximate date).

==== Asia ====
* Emperor [[Emperor Wen of Sui|Wéndi]] of the [[Sui dynasty]] organises the [[Grand Canal (China)|Grand Canal]]. He builds ships for transportation and [[Cereal|grain]] stores are located at strategic points.<ref>Imperial Chinese Armies (p. 33). C.J. Peers, 1995. {{ISBN|978-1-85532-514-2}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

585.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Europe ====
* King [[Childebert II]], age 15, takes up his sole rule of [[Austrasia]]. A [[Franks|Frankish]] army under King [[Guntram]] marches to [[Comminges]] ([[Pyrenees]]), and besieges the [[citadel]] of [[Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges|Saint-Bertrand]].
* [[July]] – [[Gundoald]], [[Merovingian dynasty|Merovingian]] usurper king, and his followers are defeated during the [[siege]] of Saint-Bertrand. He is executed and Guntram stages a triumphal entry into [[Orléans]].<ref>Ian Wood, ''The Merovingian Kingdoms, 450-751'' (Harlow: Longman, 1994), p. 94 {{ISBN|978-0-582-49372-8}}</ref>
* The [[Visigoths]] under King [[Liuvigild]] devastate the [[Suebic Kingdom of Galicia|Suevic Kingdom]] in [[Gallaecia]] (northwest [[Spain]]). <!-- After the conquest, Liuvigild reintroduces the [[Arianism|Arian Church]] among the [[Suebi|Sueves]]. --><ref>Roger Collins, ''Early Medieval Spain'', second edition (New York: St. Martin's, 1995), p. 49 {{ISBN|978-0-312-12662-9}}</ref>

==== Persia ====
* The [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]] commander, [[Kardarigan (6th century)|Kardarigan]] ("black hawk"), begins an unsuccessful [[siege]] of [[Kızıltepe|Monokarton]] (modern [[Turkey]]).

==== Britain ====

* [[Hussa of Bernicia|Hussa]] succeeds his brother [[Frithuwald of Bernicia|Frithuwald]] as king of [[Bernicia]] (approximate date).
* [[Creoda of Mercia|Creoda]] becomes king of [[Mercia]] (according to the ''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]'').

==== Asia ====
* [[September 15]] – [[Emperor Bidatsu]], age 47, dies of [[smallpox]] after a 13-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother [[Emperor Yōmei|Yōmei]] as the [[List of emperors of Japan|31st emperor]] of [[Japan]].
* Emperor [[Emperor Jing of Western Liang|Xiao Jing Di]] succeeds his father [[Emperor Ming of Western Liang|Xiao Ming Di]] as ruler of the [[Liang dynasty]] ([[China]]).

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* King [[Wideok of Baekje]] ([[Three Kingdoms of Korea|Korea]]) sends an official escort (bearing [[tribute]]), along with a master of [[Buddhism|Buddhist meditation]], a reciter of Buddhist [[incantation|magic spells]], a temple architect, and a [[Sculpture|sculptor]] of [[Buddhist art|Buddhist image]]s, to the Chinese court of the [[Sui dynasty]] (approximate date).
* The [[Armenia]]n bishop Kardutsat goes with 7 [[priest]]s, on a missionary trip to the [[steppe]]s north of the [[Caucasus]]. He succeeds in [[Baptism|baptizing]] many [[Huns]] and in translating books into their language.<ref>Zachariah of Mitylene, Syriac Chronicle (1899), Book 12</ref> 
* [[Columbanus]], Irish [[missionary]], gathers 12 companions for his journey to [[Great Britain|Britain]], probably to the [[Scotland|Scottish]] coast. After a short time, he crosses the [[English Channel]] and lands in [[Brittany]] ([[France]]).<ref>Edmonds, Columba (1908)</ref>
* [[Zhiyi]], Chinese [[Bhikkhu|monk]], returns to the city of [[Nanjing|Jinling]], where he completes his commentarial works on the [[Lotus Sutra]].
</onlyinclude>

586.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* Spring – Emperor [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]] rejects a peace proposal of the [[Persian people|Persians]], in exchange for renewed payments in [[gold]].<ref>{{harvnb|Greatrex|Lieu|2002|p=168}}; {{harvnb|Whitby|Whitby|1986|pp=41–43}}</ref>
* [[Battle of Solachon]]: A [[Byzantine army]] under command of [[Philippicus (comes excubitorum)|Philippicus]] defeats the [[Sassanid Empire|Sassanid Persians]], near [[Dara (Mesopotamia)|Dara]].
* The [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] besiege [[Thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] ([[Central Macedonia]]), the second city of the [[Byzantine Empire]].<ref>History of the Byzantine Empire from DCCXVI to MLVII, George Finlay, p. 316</ref>
* The [[Vlachs]] are first mentioned in a Byzantine chronicle (approximate date).

==== Europe ====
* [[April 21]] – King [[Liuvigild]] dies at [[Toledo, Spain|Toledo]] after an 18-year reign, and is succeeded by his second son [[Reccared I]].
* [[Slavs]] advance to the gates of [[Thessaloniki]] and the [[Peloponnese]].
* [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] destroy a lien of Roman camps along the [[Danubian Limes]], including [[Colonia Ulpia Oescus|Oescus]] and [[Ratiaria]].

=== By topic ===

==== Art ====
* The Page with the [[Crucifixion of Jesus|Crucifixion]], from the "[[Rabbula Gospels]]", at the Monastery of St. John in Beth Zagba ([[Syria]]), is completed. It is now kept at the [[Laurentian Library|Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana]], [[Florence]], [[Italy]].

==== Religion ====
* Japanese [[Buddhism in Japan|Buddhism]] comes under attack as a "foreign" religion.
* [[Comgall|Saint Comgall]] founds an [[abbey]] in [[Bangor, County Down|Bangor, Northern Ireland]].
* King [[List of kings of Dumnonia#Dumnonian kings|Custennin]] of [[Dumnonia]] is converted to [[Christianity]].
</onlyinclude>

587.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Eastern Roman Empire ====
* Emperor [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]] builds more [[fortification]]s along the [[Danube]] frontier, separating the [[Byzantine Empire]] from the realm of the [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] and [[Slavs]] (approximate date).
* [[Comentiolus]], Byzantine general (''[[magister militum]]''), assembles an army of 10,000 men at [[Pomorie|Anchialus]] (modern [[Bulgaria]]). He prepares an [[ambush]] for the Avars in the [[Haemus Mons|Haemus Mountains]].<ref>{{harvnb|Martindale|Jones|Morris|1992|p=322}}</ref>

==== Europe ====
* King [[Guntram]] sends envoys to [[Brittany]], to stop the raiding on [[Franks|Frankish]] territory. He compels obedience from [[Waroch II]] and demands 1,000 ''[[Solidus|solidus]]'' for [[looting]] [[Nantes]].
* King [[Reccared I]] renounces [[Arianism]] and adopts [[Catholicism]].<ref>[[John of Biclaro]], ''Chronicle'', chapter 85. Translated by Kenneth Baxter Wolf, ''Conquerors and Chroniclers of Early Medieval Spain'', second edition (Liverpool: University Press, 1999), p. 72 {{ISBN|0853235546}}</ref> Many [[Visigoths|Visigothic]] nobles follow his example, but in [[Septimania]] (Southern [[Gaul]]) there are Arian uprisings.
* [[November 28]] – [[Treaty of Andelot]]: Guntram recognizes King [[Childebert II]] of [[Austrasia]] as heir. He signs a treaty with Queen [[Brunhilda of Austrasia|Brunhilda]] at [[Andelot-Blancheville]].
* Winter – Childebert II appoints [[Uncelen]] as the [[Duke of Swabia|Duke of Alemannia]] (approximate date).

==== Britain ====

* [[Sledd of Essex|Sledd]] succeeds his father [[Æscwine of Essex|Æscwine]] as king of [[Kingdom of Essex|Essex]] (approximate date).

==== Asia ====
* [[Teibi Incident|Battle of Shigisan]]: The [[Soga clan]], which has intermarried with the royal [[Yamato period|Yamato]] clan, fights the [[Mononobe no Moriya|Mononobe]] and [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi]] clans over influence in selecting a new successor for the Japanese [[throne]], after Emperor [[Emperor Yōmei|Yōmei]] dies. The Soga favor importing [[Buddhism in Japan|Buddhism]] from the [[Asia]]n mainland, described there as the [[religion]] of the most civilized. The Mononobe and Nakatomi hold that Buddhism would be an affront to the gods. The Soga win the [[civil war]] and [[Emperor Sushun|Sushun]], age 66, becomes the [[List of emperors of Japan|32nd emperor]] of [[Japan]].
* Fall – The [[Liang dynasty]] ends: Emperor [[Emperor Wen of Sui|Wéndi]] of the [[Sui dynasty]] abolishes Western Liang and expands his territory into the lower valley of the [[Yangtze River]]. He sends his official [[Gao Jiong]] to the capital [[Jiangling County|Jiangling]], to pacify the citizens. The former emperor [[Emperor Jing of Western Liang|Xiao Jing Di]] becomes a [[vassal]] and is named the Duke of Liang.
* [[Bagha Qaghan]] becomes the seventh ruler (''[[khagan]]'') of the [[Göktürks|Turkic Kaganate]].

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* The [[filioque clause]] is first used in the [[Nicene Creed]], against the Arians in [[Visigothic Kingdom|Visigothic Spain]] (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

588.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591|Byzantine-Sassanid War]]: Unpaid [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] troops [[mutiny]] against [[Priscus (magister militum)|Priscus]] (''[[magister militum]] per [[Diocese of the East|Orientem]]''). King [[Hormizd IV]] begins a [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]] offensive, but is defeated at [[Silvan, Turkey|Martyropolis]] (modern [[Turkey]]). 
* Summer – [[Guaram I]] of Iberia, Georgian prince in [[exile]], is sent by Emperor [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]] to the city of [[Mtskheta]] ([[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]). He restores the monarchy and is bestowed with the Byzantine [[Byzantine aristocracy and bureaucracy|court title]] of ''[[curopalates]]''.

==== Europe ====
* The [[Franks]] and [[Burgundians]] under King [[Guntram]] and his nephew [[Childebert II]] invade [[Northern Italy]], but suffer a disastrous defeat against the [[Lombards]].
* The [[Kingdom of the Lombards|Lombard Kingdom]] ([[Italy]]) is converted to [[Roman Catholicism]] under the rule of King [[Authari]] (approximate date).

==== Britain ====

* [[Æthelric of Deira|Æthelric]] succeeds his father [[Ælla of Deira|Ælla]] as king of [[Deira]] in [[Northern England]].<ref>''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]'' (MS A) s.a. 588</ref>

==== Persia ====
* [[First Perso-Turkic War]]: A Persian army (12,000 men) under [[Bahrām Chobin]], supported by [[Cataphract]]s ([[heavy cavalry]]), ambush the invading [[Göktürks|Turks]], and win a great victory at the Battle of the Hyrcanian Rock.<ref>Tony Jaques, ''Dictionary of Battles and Sieges: F–O'', (Greenwood Publishing Group, 2007), p. 463</ref>

==== Asia ====
* Emperor [[Emperor Wen of Sui|Wéndi]] of the [[Sui dynasty]] prepares a campaign against the [[Chen dynasty]]. He amasses 518,000 troops along the northern bank of the [[Yangtze River]], stretching from [[Sichuan]] to the [[Pacific Ocean]].<ref>''Zizhi Tongjian'', vol. 176</ref>

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* The [[Skellig Michael]] monastery is founded on a steep rocky island off the coast of [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] (approximate date).
* The [[Guanghua Temple (Putian)|Guanghua Temple]] in [[Putian]] ([[China]]) is built during the [[Chen dynasty]], under Emperor [[Emperor Wu of Chen|Chen Wu Di]].<ref>[http://www.fzu.edu.cn/fujian/eput.html Litchi City Putian] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522183140/http://www.fzu.edu.cn/fujian/eput.html |date=May 22, 2011 }}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

551.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Byzantine Empire ====
* After the death of his cousin [[Germanus (cousin of Justinian I)|Germanus]], [[Justinian I]] appoints [[Narses]] new supreme commander, and returns to [[Italy]]. In [[Salona]] on the [[Adriatic Sea|Adriatic]] coast, he assembles a [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] expeditionary force totaling 20,000 or possibly 30,000 men and a contingent of foreign allies, notably [[Lombards]], [[Heruli|Heruls]] and [[Bulgars]].<ref name="Norwich251">J.Norwich, ''Byzantium: The Early Centuries'', p. 251</ref>  
* [[Gothic War (535-554)|Gothic War]]: Narses arrives in [[Venice|Venetia]] and discovers that a powerful [[Ostrogoths|Gothic]]-[[Franks|Frank]] army (50,000 men), under joint command of the kings [[Totila]] and [[Theudebald]], has blocked the principal route to the [[Po Valley]]. Not wishing to engage such a formidable force and confident that the Franks would avoid a direct confrontation, Narses skirts the [[lagoon]]s along the Adriatic shore, by using vessels to [[Leapfrogging (strategy)|leapfrog]] his army from point to point along the coast. In this way he arrives at the capital [[Ravenna]] without encountering any opposition. He attacks and crushes a small [[Goths|Gothic]] force at Ariminum (modern [[Rimini]]).
*Spring – The [[551 Malian Gulf earthquake]] takes place in the vicinity of the [[Malian Gulf]]; it affects the cities of [[Echinus (Thessaly)|Echinus]] and [[Tarphe]].<ref name="Antonopoulos">Antonopoulos, 1980</ref>
* [[July 9]] – [[Beirut]] is destroyed by an [[551 Beirut earthquake|earthquake and tsunami]]. Its [[epicenter]] has an estimated magnitude of about 7.2 or 7.6, and according to reports of [[Antoninus of Piacenza (pilgrim)|Antoninus of Piacenza]], Christian [[pilgrim]], some 30,000 people are killed.<ref name="Sbeinati">{{cite journal|last=Sbeinati|first=M.R.|author2=Darawcheh R. & Mouty M|year=2005|title=The historical earthquakes of Syria: an analysis of large and moderate earthquakes from 1365 B.C. to 1900 A.D.|journal=Annals of Geophysics|volume=48|issue=3|pages=347–435|url=http://www.earth-prints.org/bitstream/2122/908/1/01Sbeinati.pdf |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20221009/http://www.earth-prints.org/bitstream/2122/908/1/01Sbeinati.pdf |archive-date=2022-10-09 |url-status=live|access-date=2 March 2011}}</ref>
* Autumn – [[Battle of Sena Gallica (551)|Battle of Sena Gallica]]: The [[Byzantine navy|Byzantine fleet]] (50 warships) destroys the Gothic naval force under [[Indulf (6th century)|Indulf]] near Sena Gallica ([[Senigallia]]), some 17 miles (27 km) north of [[Ancona]]. It marks the end of the Gothic supremacy in the [[Mediterranean Sea]].

==== Europe ====
* [[Athanagild]] revolts against the [[Visigoths|Visigothic]] king [[Agila I|Agila]]. Their armies meet at [[Seville]] ([[Andalusia]]), and Agila is defeated.<ref>Isidore of Seville, ''[[Historia de regibus Gothorum, Vandalorum et Suevorum]]'', chapter 46. Translation by Guido Donini and Gordon B. Ford, ''Isidore of Seville's History of the Goths, Vandals, and Suevi'', second revised edition (Leiden: E.J. Brill, 1970), p. 22</ref>
* 12,000 Kutrigurs appear in Europe led by Chinialus and others to assist the Gepids.

==== Persia ====

* Spring – [[Lazic War]] - [[Siege of Petra (550–551)]]: The [[Byzantine army]] and their [[Sabir people|Sabir]] allies (some 6,000 men) under [[Bessas (magister militum)|Bessas]] recapture the strategic Byzantine fortress of [[Petra, Lazica|Petra]], located on the coast of the [[Black Sea]]. He orders the [[Defensive wall|city walls]] razed to the ground.<ref>Bury (1958), p. 116</ref><ref>Greatrex & Lieu (2002), p. 118-119</ref>

==== Asia ====
* Autumn – [[Xiao Dong]], great-nephew of the rebellious general [[Hou Jing]], succeeds [[Emperor Jianwen of Liang|Jianwen Di]] as emperor of the [[Liang Dynasty]]. Xiao Dong has no real power and Hou Jing controls the imperial government at the capital [[Jiankang]].
* [[Bumin Qaghan]], chieftain of the [[Göktürks]], founds the [[Qaghans of the Turkic khaganates|Turkic Khaganate]]. He unites the local [[Turkic people|Turkic tribes]] and throws off the yoke of [[Rouran Khaganate|Rouran]] domination.

=== By topic ===

==== Arts and sciences ====
* [[Jordanes]], Roman [[bureaucrat]], publishes ''[[Getica|"The Origin and Deeds of the Goths"]]'' (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

553.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[Battle of Mons Lactarius]]:<ref>{{cite book|author1=Peter Connolly|author2=John Gillingham|author3=John Lazenby|title=The Hutchinson Dictionary of Ancient and Medieval Warfare|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1LUoDAAAQBAJ&pg=PT457|date=13 May 2016|publisher=Taylor & Francis|isbn=978-1-135-93681-5|pages=457–}}</ref> King [[Teia]] secretly marches to join forces with his brother [[Aligern]] in [[Campania]], to relieve the [[siege]] of [[Cumae]]. Meanwhile at ''Mons Lactarius'' (modern [[Monti Lattari]]), [[Narses]] lays an [[ambush]]. The combined [[Ostrogoths|Gothic]] force is crushed in a hopeless [[last stand]] for two days (south of [[Naples]]), and Teia is killed in the fighting. Aligern escapes, but surrenders a few months later.
* The [[Ostrogothic Kingdom]] ends after 60 years of rule in [[Italy]]. The [[Goths]] are allowed to return to their homes in peace and (re)settle in modern-day [[Austria]]. Some 7,000 people retreat to [[Campsas]] (Southern [[Gaul]]), and resist with minimal help from the [[Franks]] against the [[Byzantine Greeks|Byzantines]] until [[554]].
* The [[Sasanian Empire|Sassanid]] commander [[Mihr-Mihroe]] force the Byzantines to retreat from Telephis and later Ollaria. (See [[Mihr-Mihroe's campaign of 554|Battle of Telephis–Ollaria]]).

==== Europe ====
* [[Gothic War (535–554)|Gothic War]]: Frankish invasion — Two [[Franks|Frankish]]-[[Alemanni]] dukes, brothers Lothair and Buccelin, cross the [[Alps]] from [[Germany]] with a force of 75,000 men, mostly Frankish infantry. In the [[Po Valley]], they win an easy victory over a much smaller Byzantine force at [[Parma]], and are joined by remnants of the Gothic armies, bringing the total strength of the invaders to about 90,000 men. Narses, gathering his forces as quickly as possible, marches north to harass the Franks, but is not strong enough to engage them in battle. In [[Samnium]] ([[Southern Italy]]) the brothers divide their forces: Lothaire goes down the east coast, then returns to the north, to winter in the Po Valley. Buccelin follows the west coast into [[Calabria]], where he spends the winter — his army being seriously wasted by [[attrition warfare|attrition]] and disease.

==== Asia ====
* King [[Seong of Baekje]] attacks the kingdoms of [[Goguryeo]] and [[Silla]]. However, under a secret agreement, Silla troops attack the exhausted [[Baekje]] army, and take possession of the entire [[Han River (Korea)|Han River]] valley. 
* In the [[Göktürks|Turkic Khaganate]] Istemi is appointed governor (''[[yabgu]]'') in the west of the empire (modern [[Turkestan]]), and [[Muqan Qaghan]] succeeds his brother [[Issik Qaghan]] as emperor (''[[khagan]]'') of the [[Göktürks]].

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* [[May 5]] – The [[Second Council of Constantinople|Fifth Ecumenical Council]] is held in [[Constantinople]]. In an edict, Emperor [[Justinian I]] condemns the [[Three-Chapter Controversy|Three Chapters]], causing further [[schism]]s and [[Heresy|heresies]] of [[monoenergism]] and [[monothelitism]].
</onlyinclude>

555.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== [[Byzantine Empire]] ====
* By this date, the Roman Empire under [[Justinian I]] has reached its height. Justinian I has reconquered many former territories of the [[Western Roman Empire]], including [[Praetorian prefecture of Italy|Italy]], [[Praetorian prefecture of Illyricum|Dalmatia]], [[Praetorian prefecture of Africa|Africa]] and Southern [[Hispania Baetica|Hispania]].
* An [[earthquake]] devastates the city of [[Latakia]] (modern [[Syria]]).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Robertson |first1=A. H. F. |last2=Parlak |first2=Osman |last3=Ünlügenç |first3=Ulvi Can |title=Geological Development of Anatolia and the Easternmost Mediterranean Region |date=2013 |publisher=Geological Society of London |isbn=9781862393530 |page=461 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z-9uO9uGDUsC&pg=PA461|language=en}}</ref>

==== Europe ====
* King [[Chlothar I]] annexes the [[Franks|Frankish]] territories of [[Metz]] and [[Reims]], after the death of his great-nephew [[Theudebald]].

==== Britain ====
* King [[Erb of Gwent]] (in Southern [[Wales]]) dies; his kingdom is divided into [[Kingdom of Gwent|Gwent]] and [[Ergyng]] (approximate date).<ref name="Griffiths">{{cite book|author=Ralph Alan Griffiths|title=The Gwent County History: Gwent in prehistory and early history|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=63RnAAAAMAAJ|date=29 June 2004|publisher=University of Wales Press|isbn=978-0-7083-1826-3}}</ref>

==== Persia ====
* Summer – [[Lazic War]]: The [[Byzantine army]] under [[Bessas (magister militum)|Bessas]] is repulsed, and forced to retreat out of [[Nokalakevi|Archaeopolis]] ([[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]). 
* King [[Gubazes II of Lazica|Gubazes II]] is invited to observe the [[siege]] of a [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]]-held fortress, and is murdered by the Byzantine [[Staff (military)|military staff]] after accusing them of incompetence.<ref>{{harvnb|Martindale|Jones|Morris|1992|pp=560, 841, 1103–1104}}; {{harvnb|Bury|2011|p=118}}; {{harvnb|Greatrex|Lieu|2002|pp=120–121}}</ref>

==== Asia ====
* Chinese [[Liang dynasty]]: [[Emperor Jing of Liang|Jing Di]], age 12, succeeds his father [[Emperor Yuan of Liang|Yuan Di]] and is declared emperor by general [[Emperor Wu of Chen|Chen Baxian]]. 
* The [[Rouran Khaganate]] ends; it is defeated by the [[Göktürks]] under [[Muqan Qaghan]], who expands his rule in [[Central Asia]].

=== By topic ===
==== Arts and sciences ====
* Around this time, the historian [[Jordanes]] writes several books, among them ''De origine actibusque Getarum'' (''[[The origin and deeds of the Goths]]'').
* [[Taliesin]], British [[poet]], becomes court bard to King [[Brochwel Ysgithrog|Brochwel]] of [[Kingdom of Powys|Powys]] (approximate date).

==== Religion ====
* [[June 7]] – [[Pope Vigilius]] dies at [[Syracuse, Sicily|Syracuse]] on his journey back home. His body is brought to [[Rome]] and buried in the [[San Martino ai Monti]]. 
* [[Cybi|Cybi Felyn]], abbot of [[Holyhead]], dies at his [[monastery]] in [[Caer Gybi (fort)|Caer Gybi]] (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

556.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Europe ====
* King [[Chlothar I]] suppresses a revolt of the [[Saxons]] and [[Thuringi]] in [[Saxony]] ([[Germany]]). For some time he exacts a [[tribute]] of 500 [[Cattle|cow]]s every year.

==== Britain ====
* King [[Cynric of Wessex|Cynric]] and his son [[Ceawlin of Wessex]] fight against the [[Celtic Britons|Britons]] at Beranburh, now identified as [[Barbury Castle]] ([[Wiltshire]]) in [[South West England]].<ref>Myres, p. 162</ref>

==== Persia ====
* [[Lazic War]]: A [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] expeditionary force under [[Justin (consul 540)|Justin]] retakes [[Nokalakevi|Archaeopolis]] (modern [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]), and routs the [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]] army.<ref>{{harvnb|Bury|2011|p=119}}; {{harvnb|Martindale|Jones|Morris|1992|pp=752, 845–846}}; {{harvnb|Greatrex|Lieu|2002|p=121}}</ref>
* [[Siege of Phasis]]: The Persians are defeated at the besieged town of [[Phasis (town)|Phasis]] in [[Lazica]], held by the [[Byzantine Greeks|Byzantines]].<ref name="PLRE">Martindale, Jones & eMorris (1992), p. 81–82</ref>
* King [[Khosrau I]] opens negotiations with [[Justinian I]], leading to the establishment of a 50 year [[Peace treaty|peace agreement]] in [[562]].

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* [[April 16]] – The [[Diplomacy|diplomatic]] representative (''[[apocrisiarius]]'') to [[Constantinople]] is elected as [[Pope Pelagius I]], succeeding [[Pope Vigilius|Vigilius]] as the 60th [[pope]] of [[Rome]].</onlyinclude>

557.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===   

==== Europe ====
* The [[Avar Khaganate|Avars]] arrive in the northern region of the [[Caucasus]], between the [[Black Sea]] and the [[Caspian Sea]]. They send envoys to the [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantines]] in [[Lazica]] (modern [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]). Like the [[Huns]], the Avars are the former elite of a central Asian federation, which has been forced to flee westwards.<ref>Rome at War (AD 293–696), p. 59. Michael Whitby, 2002. {{ISBN|1-84176-359-4}}</ref>

====Byzantine Empire====
* [[December 14]] – The [[557 Constantinople earthquake]] occurs.

==== Asia ====
* The [[Western Wei]] Dynasty ends: [[Yuwen Hu]] deposes emperor [[Emperor Gong of Western Wei|Gong Di]], and places [[Yuwen Tai]]'s son [[Emperor Xiaomin of Northern Zhou|Xiaomin]] on the throne. Yuwen Hu becomes [[regent]] and establishes the [[Northern Zhou]] dynasty in China. 
* [[Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou|Ming Di]] is made emperor, after his younger brother Xiao Min Di is arrested while trying to assume power. Xiao Min Di is deposed and executed by Yuwen Hu.
* The [[Liang dynasty]] ends: [[Emperor Wu of Chen|Chen Wu Di]], a distinguished general, becomes the first emperor of the [[Chen dynasty]] in Southern China.
* The [[Göktürks]] under [[Muqan Qaghan]] ally with the [[Sasanian Empire|Persian Empire]], and destroy the [[Hephthalite Empire|Hephthalites]] (White Huns) in Central Asia.

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* King [[Chlothar I]] of the [[Franks]] founds the [[Abbey of St. Medard, Soissons|Abbey of St. Medard]] at [[Soissons]] (Northern France).
* The [[Jiming Temple]] in [[Nanjing]] is built; the [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] [[pagoda]] is located near [[Xuanwu Lake]].
</onlyinclude>

562.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== [[Byzantine Empire]] ====
* Emperor [[Justinian I]] signs a [[peace treaty]] with the [[Sasanid Empire]]. The ''[[status quo ante bellum|status quo ante]]'' is restored, with [[Lazica]] (modern [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]) in Byzantine hands.
* [[Belisarius]] stands trial for [[Political corruption|corruption]] in [[Constantinople]], possibly with [[Procopius]] acting as ''[[praefectus urbi]]''. He is found guilty and sent to [[prison]].
* End of the [[Lazic War]]: In the [[Fifty-Year Peace Treaty]], King [[Khosrau I]] recognises Lazica as a Byzantine vassal state for an annual payment of 5,000 pounds of gold each year.<ref>Frye Ancient Iran</ref> 
* [[December 23]] – Justinian I re-consecrates [[Hagia Sophia]] after its [[dome]] is rebuilt. [[Paul the Silentiary]], Byzantine poet, writes an epic [[Poetry|poem]] (''[[Ekphrasis]]'').
* The last [[Ostrogothic Kingdom|Ostrogothic]] strongholds at [[Verona]] and [[Brixia (city)|Brixia]] are taken by the Byzantine Empire, ending the [[Gothic War (535–554)|Gothic War]].

==== Europe ====
* King [[Sigebert I]] repels an attack on [[Austrasia]] by the [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] at [[Regensburg]] ([[Germany]]). He moves his capital from [[Reims]] to [[Metz]] (approximate date).

==== Asia ====
* Spring – [[Emperor Ming of Western Liang|Xiao Ming Di]], age 20, succeeds his father [[Emperor Xuan of Western Liang|Xuan Di]] as emperor of the Chinese [[Liang Dynasty]].
* [[Silla]], by order of king [[Jinheung of Silla|Jinheung]], wages war upon [[Gaya Confederacy|Gaya]] ([[Three Kingdoms of Korea]]) and conquers it.
* The secondary capital [[Taiyuan]] in [[Northern Qi]] is rebuilt and becomes a center of [[Buddhism]].

==== Mesoamerica ====
* [[First Tikal-Calakmul War]]: The [[Maya civilization|Maya]] state of [[Caracol, Belize|Caracol]] ([[Belize]]) defeats King [[Tikal#Rulers|Wak Chan K'awiil]] (Double Bird) of [[Tikal]] in battle,<ref>Arlen Chase and Diane Chase 2008. "What the Hieroglyphs Don't Tell You": Archaeology and History at Caracol, Belize. Mayab 20: 103-108</ref> ending his dynasty.
</onlyinclude>

564.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Britain ====
* [[Cadoc]], abbot of [[Llancarfan]] ([[Wales]]), settles in [[Weedon, Buckinghamshire|Weedon]] and is made [[bishop]] (approximate date). 
* [[August 22]] – [[Columba]] reports seeing the [[Loch Ness Monster]] at the [[River Ness]] (according to the ''[[Loch Ness Monster#Saint Columba (565)|"Life of St. Columba"]]'').

==== Mesoamerica ====
* [[Tulum]], Maya [[Defensive wall|walled city]], on the [[Yucatán Peninsula]] (modern [[Mexico]]) is first mentioned on a [[stele]] inscription.<ref>[http://havecamerawilltravel.com/tulum-maya-riviera-mexico Photos of Tulum Archeological Site]</ref>

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* [[Samson of Dol]], [[Brittany#Religion|one of seven founder saints of Brittany]], attends a council in [[Paris]] and witnesses several [[Decree|royal decree]]s (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

565.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[November 15]] – [[Justin II]] succeeds his uncle [[Justinian I]] as emperor of the [[Byzantine Empire]]. He begins his reign by refusing subsidies to the [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]], who conduct several large-scale raids through the [[Balkans|Balkan Peninsula]].
* Justin II recalls his cousin [[Justin (consul 540)|Justin]] ([[pretender]] to the [[throne]]) to [[Constantinople]]; after accusations against him, he is placed under [[house arrest]].
* Justin II sends his son-in-law [[Baduarius]] (''[[magister militum]]'') with a [[Byzantine army]], to support the [[Gepids]] in their war against the [[Lombards]].<ref>Rovagnati 2003, p. 30</ref><ref name="JJ22">Jarnut 1995, p. 22.</ref><ref>Martindale 1992, ''s.v. Baduarius (2)'', p. 64–65.</ref>
* The [[Madaba Map]] is made in the Byzantine church of [[Saint George]]. The floor [[mosaic]] contains the depiction of the [[Holy Land]] (approximate date).

==== Britain ====
* [[Columba]], an Irish [[missionary]], spots the [[Loch Ness Monster]] on the [[River Ness]] (in present day [[Scotland]]) and saves the life of a [[Picts|Pict]] (approximate date).

==== Europe ====
* Summer – A war erupts between [[Alboin]], the king of the Lombards, and King [[Cunimund]], the leader of the Gepids. (approximate date).

==== Asia ====
* [[Gao Wei]] succeeds his father [[Emperor Wucheng of Northern Qi|Wu Cheng Di]] as ruler of the Chinese [[Northern Qi|Northern Qi Dynasty]]. Wu Cheng Di becomes a regent and [[Taishang Huang|Grand Emperor]].
* The [[Uyghur people|Uyghurs]] are defeated by the [[Göktürks]], who expand their territory in [[Central Asia]] (approximate date).

==== Central America ====
* [[February 6]] – [[Kʼan Joy Chitam I]], ruler of the [[Maya rulers|Mayan city-state]] of [[Palenque]], in what is now the state of [[Chiapas]] in southern [[Mexico]], dies after a reign of exactly 36 years.
* [[May 2]] – [[Ahkal Moʼ Nahb II]] becomes the new ruler of [[Palenque]] and reigns until his death in [[570]].

=== By topic ===
==== Arts and sciences ====
* [[Agathias]] begins to write a history, beginning where [[Procopius]] finished his work.

==== Religion ====
* [[January 22]] – Patriarch [[Eutychius of Constantinople]] is deposed as [[Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople]] by [[Justinian I]] after he refuses the Byzantine Emperor's order to adopt the tenets of the [[Aphthartodocetae]], a sect of [[Monophysitism|Monophysites]]. From [[April 12]] he is replaced by [[John Scholasticus]].
* Columba begins preaching in the [[Orkney Islands]] (approximate date).</onlyinclude>

566.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* A [[Byzantine army]], under command of [[Baduarius]], assists the [[Gepids]] in their war against the [[Lombards]]. The [[Byzantine Greeks|Byzantines]] win the first battle in the lower [[Danube]] ([[Moesia]]), but Gepid King [[Cunimund]] refuses to hand back the fortress city of [[Sirmium]] (modern [[Serbia]]), as he had promised. 
* Emperor [[Justin II]], facing an empty [[treasury]], breaks the treaty with the Gepids that has existed since [[Cunimund#Rule|565]]. King [[Alboin]] of the Lombards makes an [[Military alliance|alliance]] with the [[Pannonian Avars|Avars]] under [[Bayan I]], at the expense of tough conditions. They demand a tenth of the Lombards' [[cattle]] and half of the war [[Looting|booty]].
* Justin II sends his cousin [[Justin (consul 540)|Justin]] to [[exile]] in [[Alexandria]], where he is installed as ''[[List of governors of Roman Egypt|Augustal prefect]]'' of [[Diocese of Egypt|Egypt]]. There he is murdered in his sleep, and his head is cut off and brought to [[Constantinople]] (most likely by assignment of Empress [[Sophia (empress)|Sophia]]).<ref>Martindale, Jones & Morris (1992) p. 753–754</ref>

==== Europe ====
* [[Ainmuire mac Sétnai]] becomes [[High King of Ireland]], and rules from 566–569 (this according to the [[Book of Leinster]]).

==== Francia ====

*A poet from Italy named [[Venantius Fortunatus]] arrives at the [[Merovingian dynasty|Merovingian]] court at [[Metz]]. With a strong grasp of traditional Roman poetry, Fortunatus impresses and entertains the Frankish royalty and aristocracy. The success of a Latin poet in Francia suggests that Roman culture persisted well after the Roman Empire disintegrated in Gaul in the late 5th century.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Wickham|first=Chris|title=Framing the Early Middle Ages|year=2005|pages=175}}</ref>

==== Asia ====
* [[Emperor Fei of Chen|Fei Di]], age 12, succeeds his father [[Emperor Wen of Chen|Wen Di]], as emperor of the Chinese [[Chen dynasty]]. He honors his grand-aunt [[Empress Zhang Yao'er|Zhang Yao'er]] with the title of [[Grand empress dowager|Grand Empress]], and she becomes his [[regent]].
* [[Kirtivarman I]] succeeds his father [[Pulakeshin I]] as king of the [[Chalukya dynasty]] ([[India]]). During his rule he completes the subjugation of the [[Kadamba dynasty|Kadambas]] and annexes the port of [[Goa]].

==== Unidentified ====
* A major [[volcanic eruption]] occurs in the Antarctic.<ref>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Connor|title=Our explosive past is written in the Antarctic ice|newspaper=[[i (British newspaper)|i]]|location=London|date=2014-07-07|page=17}}</ref></onlyinclude>

567.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Europe ====
* The [[Lombard–Gepid War (567)]] ends with a [[Lombards|Lombard]]-[[Pannonian Avars|Avar]] victory, and the annihilation of the [[Gepids]].
* [[Sigebert I]], king of [[Austrasia]], marries [[Brunhilda of Austrasia|Brunhilda]], and his half brother [[Chilperic I]] marries [[Galswintha]], both daughters of the Visigothic king [[Athanagild]].
* King [[Charibert I]] dies without an heir; his [[realm]] (region [[Neustria]] and [[Aquitaine]]) is divided between his brothers [[Guntram]], Sigebert I and Chilperic I.<ref name="James317">''Charibert I'', Edward James, ''The Oxford Dictionary of Late Antiquity'', ed. Oliver Nicholson, (Oxford University Press, 2018), 317.</ref> 
* [[Liuva I]] succeeds his predecessor Athanagild, after an [[interregnum]] of five months, and becomes king of the [[Visigoths]].<ref>Isidore, chapter 46; translated by Donini and Ford, p. 22</ref>

====China====
*[[Three Disasters of Wu]]: Emperor [[Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou|Wu Di]] of the [[Northern Zhou dynasty]] initiates the second persecution of Buddhists in China. This persecution continues until he is succeeded by his son Emperor [[Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou|Xuan]].

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* The [[Second Council of Tours]] is held. It decrees that any [[Clergy|cleric]] found in bed with his wife will be [[Excommunication|excommunicated]].
* [[John Scholasticus|John III]], [[Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople|patriarch of Constantinople]], organizes a compromise between the [[Council of Chalcedon|Chalcedonians]] and [[Monophysites]].
</onlyinclude>

569.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Byzantine Empire ====
* Emperor [[Justin II]] and his wife [[Sophia (empress)|Sophia]] send a [[relic]] of the "[[True Cross]]" to the [[Franks|Frankish]] princess [[Radegund]], who has founded a [[monastery]] at [[Poitiers]].
* The [[Garamantes|Garamantian Kingdom]] (modern [[Libya]]) signs a [[peace treaty]] with the [[Byzantine Empire]]. The capital city of [[Germa|Garama]] is converted to [[Christianity]].<ref>John of Biclar, Chronicle 3, ''Chronica Minora'' 2, p. 212</ref>

==== Europe ====
* [[September]] – The [[Lombards]] conquer Forum Iulii (Cividale del Friuli) in northeastern Italy. Later in the year, the Lombards conquer [[Milan]]. 
* [[Gisulf I of Friuli|Gisulf I]], nephew of Alboin, is appointed as the first [[Dukes and margraves of Friuli|duke of Friuli]] (approximate date).

==== Arabia ====
* [[Al-Mundhir III ibn al-Harith|Al-Mundhir III]] succeeds his father [[Al-Harith ibn Jabalah|Al-Harith V]] and becomes king of the [[Ghassanids]].

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* The [[Nubia]]n kingdom of [[Alodia]] is converted to Christianity by Byzantine [[Missionary|missionaries]] (according to [[John of Ephesus]]).
* John of Ephesus completes his ''"Biographies of Eastern Saints"'' (approximate date).
* [[November 19]] – In Poitiers the ''"[[Vexilla Regis]]"'' is first sung during the [[Processional hymn|Procession]].
</onlyinclude>

574.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[December 7]] – Emperor [[Justin II]] retires due to recurring seizures of [[insanity]]; he abdicates the [[throne]] in favour of his general [[Tiberius II Constantine|Tiberius]]. Justin proclaims him ''[[Caesar (title)|Caesar]]'' and adopts him as his own son.<ref>[http://www.brittanica: Tiberius II Constantine]{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}.</ref>
* Winter – Empress [[Sophia (empress)|Sophia]] and Tiberius agree to a one year truce with the [[Persian people|Persians]], at the cost of 45,000 ''[[Solidus|solidi]]''. The truce applies only to the [[Mesopotamia]]n front; in the [[Caucasus]], war continues.<ref>{{harvnb|Greatrex|Lieu|2002|p=136}}.</ref>

==== Europe ====
* King [[Cleph]] is murdered after an 18-month reign by a [[Bodyguard|guard]], a slave who he has mistreated. For the next decade, the [[Kingdom of the Lombards|Lombard Kingdom]] is governed by independent [[Lombard duchies|duchies]] ([[Rule of the Dukes]]).<ref>[http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/346673/Lombard Lombard] (2008).</ref>
* The [[Visigoths]] under King [[Liuvigild]] invade [[Duchy of Cantabria|Cantabria]] (Northern [[Spain]]), and destroy the city of [[Amaya, Burgos|Amaya]] ([[Province of Burgos|Burgos]]). He massacres the inhabitants and adds the province to the [[Visigothic Kingdom]].
* [[Áedán mac Gabráin]] becomes [[List of kings of Dál Riata|king of Dál Riata]] ([[Scotland]]) (approximate Date).

==== Asia ====
* The [[Sassanid Empire|Persian Empire]] overthrows the [[Kingdom of Aksum|Axumite]]- and [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]]-affiliated regimes in [[Yemen]] ([[Arabian Peninsula]]).<ref name="The Oxford Dictionary of Islam">Esposito (2003). ''The Oxford Dictionary of Islam'', {{ISBN|0-19-512558-4}}.</ref>

==== Unidentified ====
* A major [[volcanic eruption]] occurs in the Antarctic.<ref>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Connor|title=Our explosive past is written in the Antarctic ice|newspaper=[[i (British newspaper)|i]]|location=London|date=2014-07-07|page=17}}</ref>

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* [[July 13]] – [[Pope John III]] dies at [[Rome]] after a 13-year tenure. The [[Holy See]] becomes ''[[sede vacante]]'' until June of the following year.
* [[Marius Aventicensis]] is made [[bishop]] of ''[[Aventicum]]'' (modern [[Avenches]]).
</onlyinclude>

579.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591|Byzantine-Sassanid War]]: King [[Khosrau I]] seeks peace, but dies before an agreement can be reached. The [[Mesopotamia]]n front becomes stalemated, and [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]] (''[[magister militum]]'' of the East) fortifies the borders in [[Armenia]] and [[Syria]].

====Central America====
*[[September 2]] – [[Scroll Serpent|Uneh Chan]] becomes the [[Maya rulers|ruler of the Mayan city state]] of [[Calakmul]] in southern [[Mexico]] and reigns until [[611]].

==== Europe ====
* [[Hermenegild]], son of [[Visigoths|Visigothic]] king [[Liuvigild]], marries [[Ingund (wife of Hermenegild)|Ingund]]. He rebels against his father, starting in [[Seville]] (Southern [[Spain]]), and declares himself [[Catholicism|Catholic]]. 
* Heavy [[tax]]es levied by [[Merovingian dynasty|Merovingian]] king [[Chilperic I]] of [[Neustria]] produce a revolt at [[Limoges]] (central [[France]]), as he sells [[Episcopal see|bishopric]]s to the highest bidder.

==== Britain ====

* [[Frithuwald of Bernicia|Frithuwald]] succeeds his brother [[Theodric of Bernicia|Theodoric]] as king of [[Bernicia]] ([[Scotland]]). He rules from 579–585 (approximate date).

==== Persia ====
* Khosrau I dies after a 48-year reign, during which he has extended his realm from the [[Amu Darya|River Oxus]] to the [[Red Sea]]. He is succeeded by his son [[Hormizd IV]], who becomes king of the [[Sassanid Empire|Persian Empire]].
* Summer – Hormizd IV refuses to give up territories, and breaks off negotiations with the [[Byzantine Empire]].<ref>{{harvnb|Greatrex|Lieu|2002|pp=160–162}}</ref> The [[Göktürks|Türks]] invade [[Greater Khorasan|Khorasan]] and reach [[Hyrcania]] on the [[Caspian Sea]].

==== Asia ====

* Emperor [[Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou|Xuan Di]] abdicates the [[throne]] to his son [[Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou|Jing Di]], age 6, and rules as [[Regency|regent]] the [[Northern Zhou|Northern Zhou dynasty]].
* [[Jinpyeong of Silla|Jinpyeong]] becomes king of the Korean kingdom of [[Silla]].<ref>{{cite web |title=List of Rulers of Korea |url=https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/koru/hd_koru.htm |website=www.metmuseum.org |access-date=21 April 2019}}</ref>

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* [[July 30]] – [[Pope Benedict I]] dies after a 4-year reign, and is succeeded by [[Pope Pelagius II|Pelagius II]] as the 63rd [[pope]]. During the [[Lombards|Lombard]] siege of [[Rome]], he labors to solve the problems of [[famine]].
* Pelagius II sends [[Pope Gregory I|Gregory]] as his ''[[apocrisiarius]]'' (ambassador to the imperial court in [[Constantinople]]).<ref>Ekonomou, 2007, p. 8</ref> He is part of a Roman [[Diplomatic mission|delegation]] to ask for military aid against the Lombards. 
* [[Leander of Seville|Leander]], [[Catholicism|Catholic]] bishop of Seville, is [[exile]]d by Liuvigild and withdraws to Constantinople. At the Byzantine court he composes works against [[Arianism]] (approximate date).
</onlyinclude>

590.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Byzantine Empire ====
* [[Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591|Byzantine–Sassanid War]]: Emperor [[Maurice (emperor)|Maurice]] defeats the Persian forces under [[Bahrām Chobin]] at [[Nusaybin|Nisibis]] (modern [[Turkey]]), and drives them back into [[Armenia]].
* [[Comentiolus]], commander ({{lang|la|[[magister militum]]}}) of the eastern army, receives the legitimate Persian king, [[Khosrau II]], as a [[refugee]] in his headquarters at [[Manbij|Hierapolis]].
* Maurice establishes the [[Exarchate of Africa|Exarchate of Carthage]] in [[Africa]]. He combines the civil authority of a ''[[praetorian prefect]]'' and the military authority, based at [[Carthage]].
* [[March 26]] – [[Theodosius (son of Maurice)|Theodosius]], eldest son of Maurice, is proclaimed as co-emperor. He becomes his father's heir to the [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] throne.<ref>Martindale, Jones & Morris 1992, p. 1293</ref>
* [[Stephen I of Iberia|Stephen I]] succeeds his father [[Guaram I]] as king of [[Principality of Iberia|Iberia]] ([[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]) (approximate date).

==== Europe ====
* The [[Franks]] and [[Burgundians]] under King [[Guntram]] invade [[Italy]]. They capture the cities [[Milan]] and [[Verona]], but are forced to leave by a [[Bubonic plague|plague]] outbreak in the [[Po Valley]].
* The Franks again invade Italy; they capture [[Modena]] and [[Mantua]]. Several [[Lombards|Lombard]] dukes defect: [[Gisulf I of Friuli|Gisulf I]], [[Dukes and margraves of Friuli|duke of Friuli]], is defeated and replaced by his son [[Gisulf II of Friuli|Gisulf II]].
* [[September 5]] – King [[Authari]] dies (possibly by [[poison]]) after a six-year reign, and is succeeded by [[Agilulf]], duke (''[[dux]]'') of [[Turin]], who marries his widow [[Theodelinda]].
* Frankish rebellion led by [[Basina, daughter of Chilperic I]].

==== Britain ====

* [[Æthelberht of Kent|Æthelberht]] succeeds his father [[Eormenric of Kent|Eormenric]] as king (''[[bretwalda]]'') of [[Kingdom of Kent|Kent]] (according to the ''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]''). 
* [[Lindisfarne|Siege of Lindisfarne]]: A [[Celtic Britons|Brythonic]] coalition lays siege to King [[Hussa of Bernicia]] at [[Lindisfarne Castle]] (Holy Island).
* [[Owain mab Urien]] succeeds his father [[Urien]], as Brythonic king of [[Rheged]] in [[Northern England]] (approximate date).

==== Persia ====
* Spring – King [[Hormizd IV]] dismisses Bahrām Chobin as commander (''[[Spahbed|Eran spahbed]]''). He revolts and marches with the support of the Persian army towards [[Ctesiphon]]. 
* [[February 15]] – Hormizd IV is deposed and assassinated by Persian [[Nobility|nobles]]. Having ruled since [[579]], he is succeeded by his son Khosrau II as king of the [[Sassanid Empire|Persian Empire]].
* September – Bahrām Chobin defeats the inferior forces of Khosrau II near Ctesiphon. He seizes the [[throne]] and proclaims himself as king [[List of kings of Persia|Bahrām IV]] of Persia.

==== Asia ====
* [[Kadungon]] becomes king of the [[Pandyan Dynasty|Pandyan Kingdom]] in [[South India]] (approximate date).
* [[Yeongyang of Goguryeo|Yeongyang]] becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of [[Goguryeo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=List of Rulers of Korea |url=https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/koru/hd_koru.htm |website=www.metmuseum.org |access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref>

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* [[February 7]] – [[Pope Pelagius II]] falls victim to the plague that devastated [[Rome]].<ref name=LP>''[[Liber Pontificalis]]'', chapters 65 & 66. Translated by Raymond Davis, ''The Book of Pontiffs (Liber Pontificalis)'' (Liverpool: University Press, 1989), p. 61; R.A. Markus, ''Gregory the Great and his World'' (Cambridge: University Press, 1997), p. 13 {{ISBN|0521586089}}</ref> He is succeeded by [[Pope Gregory I|Gregory I]], age 50, as the 64th [[pope]], and the first from a monastic background.
* [[Egidius (bishop of Reims)|Egidius]], bishop of [[Reims]], is tried at [[Metz]] before a council of bishops for a [[Conspiracy (political)|conspiracy]] against King [[Childebert II]]; he is found guilty and [[exile]]d to [[Strasbourg]].
* Gregory I begins a vigorous program of rebuilding [[Aqueduct (watercourse)|aqueduct]]s and restoring Rome. He feeds the citizens with doles of [[Cereal|grain]], as under [[Roman Empire|Roman imperial]] rule.
* [[Columbanus]], Irish [[missionary]], obtains from King Guntram the [[Gallo-Roman culture|Gallo-Roman]] castle ''Luxovium'' ([[Luxeuil-les-Bains]]), where he founds the [[Luxeuil Abbey|Abbey of Luxeuil]].<ref name=jonas-17>Jonas 643, p. 17</ref>
* [[John of Biclaro]], Visigoth [[chronicle]]r, finishes his ''"Chronicle"'' before he is appointed [[bishop]] of [[Girona]] ([[Catalonia|Catalonia, Spain]]).
</onlyinclude>

570.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===
==== Europe ====
* [[Battle of Gwen Ystrad]]: A British alliance is forged between the kingdoms of [[Strathclyde]], [[Bernicia#British ''Bryneich''|Bryneich]] and [[Elmet]] (approximate date).
* [[Spoleto]] becomes the capital of an independent [[Duchy of Spoleto|duchy]], under the [[Lombards|Lombard]] chieftain [[Faroald I of Spoleto|Faroald]] (approximate date).
* [[Liutfrid, Duke of Alsace|Leutfred]] becomes [[Duke of Swabia|duke of Alemannia]] (modern [[Germany]]).

==== Persia ====
* [[Ctesiphon]], capital of the [[Sassanid Empire]], becomes the largest city in the world, taking the lead from [[Constantinople]], capital of the [[Byzantine Empire]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm |title=Geography at about.com |access-date=March 1, 2006 |archive-date=August 18, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818124242/http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==== Arabia ====
* [[Muhammad]], [[Prophets in Islam|Islamic prophet]], is born in [[Mecca]] (today's [[Saudi Arabia]]). His father [[Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib]] dies a few months before his birth, so he and his mother [[Aminah bint Wahb]] are protected by Muhammad's paternal grandfather, [[Abdul Muttalib]], who is recognized as the leading figure in his tribe, the [[Quraysh tribe|Quraysh.]]<ref>David Nicolle, ''Essential Histories: "The Great Islamic Conquests AD 632–750". The birth of Islam and the unifying of Arabia'' (2009), page 19.</ref> 
* [[Abraha]], Christian ruler of coastal [[Yemen]], who was acting as a general for the Christian kingdom in Abyssinia, begins a military expedition in [[Arabian Peninsula|Arabia]] against the predominantly [[pagan]] Quraysh of Mecca,<ref>Walter W Müller, ''"Outline of the History of Ancient Southern Arabia"''in Werner Daum (education) Yemen: ''"3000 Years of Art and Civilization in Arabia Felix"'' (1987)</ref> known as the [[Year of the Elephant]].

=== By topic ===
==== Religion ====
* A [[limestone]] statue of [[Boddhisattva]] is created in [[Henan]] (approximate date).
* The first mention is made of the [[Holy Lance|Spear of Destiny]] (approximate date).
* The [[Jew]]s of [[Clermont-Ferrand]] are forced to convert to [[Christianity]].
* [[Year of the Elephant]], according to [[Islam]]ic tradition.
</onlyinclude>
* The [[Anonymous pilgrim of Piacenza|anonymous Pilgrim of Piacenza]] travels the Holy Sites of Christianity in Syria, Palestine and Sinai, an experience that he later writes down as a travel report (approximate date).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Meyers |first1=Eric M. |title=Galilee Through the Centuries Confluence of Cultures |date=1999 |publisher=Pennsylvania State University Press |isbn=9781575060408 |page=353 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=znYoChYVIrcC |access-date=6 January 2024}}</ref>

571.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== By place ===

==== Europe ====
* The [[Visigoths]] under King [[Liuvigild]] invade the [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] province of [[Spania]] (modern [[Andalusia]]), and seize the city of [[Córdoba, Spain|Córdoba]].   After the death of his brother [[Liuva I]], he becomes sole ruler of the [[Visigothic Kingdom]] (approximate date). 
* [[Benevento]] becomes the capital of an independent [[Duchy of Benevento|duchy]], under the [[Lombards|Lombard]] chieftain [[Zotto]] (approximate date).

==== Britain ====
* [[Timeline of conflict in Anglo-Saxon Britain#6th century|Battle of Bedcanford]]: The [[Anglo-Saxons]] under King Cuthwulf fight against the [[Celtic Britons|Britons]], and conquer the settlements of [[Aylesbury]], [[Benson, Oxfordshire|Benson]], [[Eynsham]] and [[Limbury]] (according to the ''[[Anglo-Saxon Chronicle]]'').
* [[Wuffa of East Anglia|Wuffa]] becomes the first [[Kingdom of East Anglia|king of East Anglia]], as recorded in the [[Anglo-Saxon royal genealogies]] (approximate date).

=== By topic ===

==== Religion ====
* The [[Monophysitism|Monophysites]] again reject the [[Council of Chalcedon]], causing another [[schism]].
</onlyinclude>

572.events:
<onlyinclude>

===By place===
====Byzantine Empire====
*[[Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591]]: Emperor [[Justin II]] refuses to pay the annual [[tribute]] to [[Khosrau I]], putting an end to the 50-year [[peace treaty]] established ten years earlier. The [[Armenia]]ns are considered allies to the [[Byzantine Empire]], and Justin sends a [[Byzantine army]] into [[Sassanid Empire|Persian]] territory, besieging the fortress city of [[Nusaybin|Nisibis]] (modern [[Turkey]]).<ref name="ancient">{{cite book|last=Frye|first=Richard N.|title=The History of Ancient Iran|year=1983}}</ref>

====Europe====
