* [[February 1]] – King [[John of Bohemia]] (of the [[Teutonic Order]]) [[Siege of Medvėgalis|captures]] [[Medvėgalis]], an important fortress of the pagan [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania]], and baptizes 6,000 of its defenders.<ref name=batura>{{cite book| first=Romas |last=Batūra |title=Laukuva |volume=I|publisher=Versmė |series=Lietuvos valsčiai |year=2005 |chapter=Laukuvos žemė Medvėgalio prieigų gynyboje XIV amžiuje|chapter-url=http://www.llt.lt/pdf/laukuva/istorija-medvegalis.pdf |isbn=9789955589013 |pages=186–187}}</ref>
* [[February 18]] – [[Amda Seyon I]], [[Emperor of Ethiopia]], begins his campaigns in the southern [[Muslim]] provinces (possibly in [[1332]]).
* [[March 27]] – [[Pope John XXII]] issues a bull condemning some teachings of [[Meister Eckhart]] (who died last year) as heretical.
* [[April]] – [[Antipope Nicholas V]] is [[Excommunication|excommunicated]] by [[Pope John XXII]].
* [[June 6]] – [[Edward III of England]] pays homage to [[Philip VI of France]] for [[Aquitaine]].
* [[June 7]] – [[David II of Scotland|David II]] becomes [[King of Scots]] at age 5; he will rule Scotland for nearly 42 years.
* [[June 10]] – [[Braganstown massacre]], [[County Louth]], [[Lordship of Ireland|Ireland]]: Over 160 are killed.<ref>F. Lydon, James (1977). Journal of the County Louth Archaeological and Historical Society, Volume 19, No.1. Journal of the County Louth Archaeological and History Society. pp. 5–10. JSTOR 27729435.</ref>
* [[June 11]] – [[Battle of Pelekanon|Battle of Maltepe (Pelekanon)]]: [[Ottoman Turks]] defeat the [[Byzantine Empire]].<ref>Bartusis, Marc C. The Late Byzantine Army: Arms and Society, 1204–1453, University of Pennsylvania Press, 1997.</ref>
* [[August 4]] – Wittelsbach possessions are divided by the [[Treaty of Pavia (1329)|Treaty of Pavia]] into those of the Bavarian line and those of Palatinate line. Both lines will be reunited in 1777.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Aimone of Savoy]] becomes [[Kings of Savoy|Count of Savoy]].
* Construction begins on the [[Archcathedral Basilica of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint Andrew in Frombork]], Poland.
* [[Michael of Cesena]] is deposed as General of the [[Franciscan]]s.
* [[Stefan Uroš IV Dušan of Serbia]] defeats [[Stephen II, Ban of Bosnia]].
* [[Wiesbaden]] is granted the right of coinage by [[Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor]].

1330.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* May – [[Odoric of Pordenone]] narrates the story of his 10 years of missionary travel to China, from which he is newly returned, to Friar William of Solagna in Padua, who records it as the ''Relatio''.<ref>{{EB1911|wstitle=Odoric|volume=20|first1=Henry|last1=Yule|author1link= Henry Yule|first2=C. Raymond|last2=Beazley|author-link2=Raymond Beazley|page=10}}</ref>
* [[July 28]] – [[Battle of Velbazhd]]: The [[Second Bulgarian Empire|Bulgarians]] under Tsar [[Michael Shishman of Bulgaria|Michael Shishman]] (who is mortally wounded) are beaten by the [[Kingdom of Serbia (medieval)|Serbs]]. Bulgaria does not lose any territory to [[Serbia]], but is powerless to stop the Serbian advance towards the predominantly Bulgarian-populated [[Macedonia (region)|Macedonia]].
* [[October 19]] – King [[Edward III]] of England starts his personal reign, arresting his regent [[Roger Mortimer, 1st Earl of March|Roger Mortimer]], and having him executed.
* [[November 9]]–[[November 12|12]] – [[Battle of Posada]]: The [[Wallachia]]ns, under [[Basarab I]], defeat the [[Hungarians]], though heavily outnumbered, thus making a firm statement towards the independence of [[Wallachia]].<ref>Djuvara, Neagu. Thocomerius – Negru Vodă. Un voivod de origine cumană la inceputurile Țării Românești. Bucharest: Humanitas, 2007. ISBN 978-973-50-1731-6.</ref>
* [[December 6]] – The [[British Isles]] are hit by a great [[storm]], creating large areas of [[sand dunes]] on [[Anglesey]].
* ''Undated''
** [[Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria|Ivan Alexander]] becomes the [[Despotate of Lovech|despot of Lovech]].
** [[Vilnius]], [[Lithuania]] receives its [[coat-of-arms]], granted to the city in the seventh year of its existence.<ref>Miesčionaitienė, Eugenija; Misevičius, Juozas; Stanaitis, Stanislovas; Valaitytė, Violeta (2009). Lietuviai inteligentai tautos laisvės ir pažangos kelyje (PDF). Vilnius: VĮ Mokslotyros institutas. p. 60. ISBN 978-9986-795-61-2. Retrieved June 11, 2023.</ref></onlyinclude>

1332.events:
* [[February 18]] – [[Amda Seyon I]], [[Emperor of Ethiopia]], begins his campaigns in the southern Muslim provinces (possibly in [[1329]]).
* [[August 10]]–[[August 11|11]] – [[Battle of Dupplin Moor]]: [[Edward Balliol]] rebels, and the [[Kingdom of England|English]] defeat the loyalists of [[David II of Scotland|David II]] in [[Kingdom of Scotland|Scotland]].<ref name=Dupplin>{{Historic Environment Scotland|num=BTL8|desc=Battle of Dupplin Moor|access-date=11 April 2019}}</ref>
* [[September]] – Edward Balliol crowns himself [[King of Scotland]].<ref name=Dupplin/>
* [[November 7]] – [[Lucerne]] joins the [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Swiss Confederation]] with [[Canton of Uri|Uri]], [[Schwyz]], and [[Unterwalden]].
* [[December 16]] – [[Battle of Annan]]: The loyalists of [[David II of Scotland|David II]] defeat [[Edward Balliol]] in [[Scotland]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Jaques |first1=Tony |title=Dictionary of Battles and Sieges: A-E |date=2007 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=9780313335372 |page=54 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3amnMPTPP5MC&pg=PA54|language=en}}</ref>
* The city of [[Marosvásárhely]] (in Transylvania, today [[Târgu Mureș]] in [[Romania]]) is first documented in the papal registry, under the name ''Novum Forum Siculorum''.

1335.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* [[May 2]] – [[Otto, Duke of Austria|Otto the Merry]], Duke of Austria, becomes Duke of [[Carinthia (duchy)|Carinthia]]. 
* [[July 30]] – [[Battle of Boroughmuir]]: [[John Randolph, 3rd Earl of Moray]] defeats [[Guy II, Marquis of Namur|Guy, Count of Namur]] in [[Scotland]].
* [[November 30]] – [[Battle of Culblean]]: [[David II of Scotland|David Bruce]] defeats [[Edward Balliol]] in Scotland.
* [[December 1]] – [[Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan]] dies, a victim of the plague that ravages the [[Ilkhanate]]. This is an early outbreak of the [[Black Death]].<ref>Continuity and Change in Medieval Persia By Ann K. S. Lambton</ref> His death without a clear heir causes the Ilkhanate to disintegrate.
*[[October 22]] – Ex-emperor Hanazono (95th emperor of japan) becomes a Zen priest.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Georgians]] under King [[George V of Georgia|George V]] (the Brilliant) finally defeat the [[Mongols|Mongolians]] in a decisive battle. After that George V returns the Grave of Christ from the [[Muslims]].
* [[Slavery]] is abolished in [[Sweden]].
* [[Congress of Visegrád (1335)|Congress of Visegrád]]: The monarchs of [[Kingdom of Bohemia|Bohemia]], [[Kingdom of Hungary|Hungary]], and [[Poland]] form an anti-[[Habsburg]] alliance.
* [[Carinthia (duchy)|Carinthia]] and [[Carniola]] come under [[Habsburg]] rule. After the death of Duke [[Henry of Bohemia|Henry]], the duchies are bestowed by [[Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor|Louis the Bavarian]] on the [[Archduchy of Austria|Dukes of Austria]]. From that time onwards, what is today [[Slovenia]] is ruled jointly with [[Austria]] until [[1918]].
* [[Pope Benedict XII]] begins to reform the [[Cistercians]].
* The [[excommunication]] of [[Frederick III of Sicily]] and the [[Interdict (Catholic canon law)|interdict]] placed on [[Sicily]] end.
* Construction begins on the [[papacy|papal]] palace in [[Avignon]].
* [[Aabenraa municipality|Aabenraa]] is chartered as a city.
* The School of Arts in [[Zaragoza]], [[Spain]] is founded (later known as the [[University of Zaragoza]] in the 16th Century).
</onlyinclude>

1337.events:
<onlyinclude>

===January–December===
* [[March 16]] – [[Edward the Black Prince]] establishes the [[Duchy of Cornwall]], becoming the first [[English people|English]] [[Duke]].<ref name="Pocket On This Day">{{cite book|title=Penguin Pocket On This Day|publisher=Penguin Reference Library|isbn=0-14-102715-0|year=2006}}</ref>
* [[May 24]] – [[Philip VI of France]] confiscates [[Gascony]] from English control.<ref name=CBH>{{cite book|last=Palmer|first=Alan|last2=Palmer |first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=100–102|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[August]] – [[Second War of Scottish Independence]]: English forces relieve [[Stirling Castle]], ending [[Edward III]] of England's last campaign in Scotland.<ref name=CBH/>
* [[October]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: [[Edward III]] of England formally rejects Philip VI's claim to the French throne, initiating hostilities between France and England.<ref name=CBH/><ref name="Cassell's Chronology">{{cite book|last=Williams|first=Hywel|title=Cassell's Chronology of World History|url=https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will|url-access=registration|location=London|publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson|year=2005|isbn=0-304-35730-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/159 159–161]}}</ref>
* [[November]] – [[Battle of Cadzand]]: English troops raid the [[County of Flanders|Flemish]] island of [[Cadzand]].

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Bisham Priory]] is founded in [[Kingdom of England|England]].
* The [[Scaligeri]] Family loses control of [[Padua]]; [[Alberto II della Scala|Alberto della Scala]], patron of the [[music of the Trecento]], moves to [[Verona]].
* [[Petrarch]], "father" of [[Renaissance humanism]], first visits Rome to wander its mysterious ruins, with an eye for aesthetics as well as for history, exciting a renewed interest in [[Classical antiquity|Classical]] civilisation.
* The [[Sofia Psalter]] is produced in [[Bulgaria]].
* The [[Despotate of Epirus]] is conquered by the [[Byzantine Empire]].
* The [[Chinese famine of 1333–1337|famine in China]], which had lasted since [[1332]] and killed 6,000,000, comes to an end.</onlyinclude>
* [[Siege of Nicomedia]]: After its foundation by [[Osman I]] in about 1299, the [[Ottoman Empire]] expanded across [[Bithynia]] in north-west [[Anatolia]] by capturing territory from the [[Byzantine Empire]].

1339.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* [[June]] – [[Battle of Laupen]]: The Canton of [[Bern]] defeats the forces of [[Fribourg]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The European Magazine, and London Review|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PPMRAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA429|year=1822|publisher=Philological Society of London|pages=429–}}</ref>
* [[September 18]] – [[Emperor Go-Murakami]] accedes to the throne of [[Japan]].
* [[September 24]] (or 28)<ref>{{cite book|first1=George Bruce |last1=Malleson|title=Studies from Genoese History|url=https://archive.org/details/studiesfromgeno01mallgoog|year=1875|publisher=Longmans, Green, and Company|pages=[https://archive.org/details/studiesfromgeno01mallgoog/page/n13 336]}}</ref> – [[Simone Boccanegra]] is elected, as the first [[Doge of Genoa]].

=== Date unknown ===
* Shams-ud-Din [[Shah Mir]], having defeated [[Kota Rani]], [[Hindu]] queen regnant of [[Kashmir]], in battle at Jayapur (modern Sumbal), asks her to marry him, but she commits suicide rather than do so; thus he takes over sole rule of Kashmir, beginning the [[Muslim]] [[Shah Mir Dynasty]].
* All [[street]]s in the city of [[Florence]] are [[Pavement (material)|paved]], the first European city in post-Roman times where this has happened.
* The [[Moscow Kremlin]] is first referred to as a [[Kremlin (fortification)|kremlin]].</onlyinclude>

1345.events:
<onlyinclude>
* [[January 17]] – The Turks attack [[Smyrna]].
* [[March 15]] – The [[Miracle of the Host]] occurs (as commemorated in [[Amsterdam]]).
* [[March 4]] – [[Guy de Chauliac]] observes the planets Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars conjoined in the sky, under the sign of Aquarius, and a solar eclipse on the same day. This sign is interpreted as foreboding by many, and Chauliac will later blame it for the [[Black Plague]].<ref name="pgs. 143-148 ASIN B000K6TDP2">pgs. 143–148 ASIN B000K6TDP2</ref><ref name="Horrox, Rosemary 1994. pg.104-105">Horrox, Rosemary. ''The Black Death''. Manchester: Manchester University Press, 1994. {{ISBN|978-0-7190-3498-5}} pg.104–105</ref>
* [[April]] – [[Edward III of England]] offers "defiance" of [[Philip VI of France]].
* [[April 22]] – [[Battle of Gamenario]]: The [[Lombards]] defeat the [[Capetian House of Anjou|Angevins]] in the northwest region of present-day Italy, just southeast of [[Turin]].
* [[May]] – The Turks, led by [[Umur Beg]], sail from Asia Minor to the Balkan Peninsula, and raid Bulgarian territory.<ref name="Ioannes Cantacuzenus p.530">Ioannes Cantacuzenus. ''Historiarum...'' 2, p.530</ref>
*"Summer" (undated) – [[Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor|Louis IV]]'s son, [[Louis II, Elector of Brandenburg|Louis VI the Roman]], marries Cunigunde, a Lithuanian princess.<ref>{{cite book|title=Germans and Poles in the Middle Ages: The Perception of the 'Other' and the Presence of Mutual Ethnic Stereotypes in Medieval Narrative Sources|author1=Andrzej Pleszczynski|author2= Grischa Vercamer|publisher=Brill|year=2021|ISBN=9789004466555|page=216}}</ref>
* [[July 7]] – [[Battle of Peritheorion]]: the forces of [[Momchil]], autonomous ruler of the [[Rhodope Mountains|Rhodope]], are defeated by the Turkish allies of [[John VI Kantakouzenos]].<ref name="Nicephorus Gregoras p.729">Nicephorus Gregoras. ''Byzantina historia''. 2, p.729</ref>
* [[August]] – [[Gascon campaign of 1345]] -  [[Battle of Bergerac]], [[Gascony]]: English troops are victorious over the French.<ref>Jonathan Sumption, ''The Hundred Years War: Trial by Battle'', Vol. I, (Faber & Faber, 1990), {{ISBN|978-0-571-20095-5}}, p. 465.</ref>
* [[September]] – [[Holland]], [[County of Hainaut|Hainaut]] and [[Zeeland]] are inherited by [[Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], and remain part of the imperial crown domain until [[1347]].
* [[September 18]] – [[Andrew, Duke of Calabria]], is assassinated in Naples (d. in [[Aversa]]).
* [[September 26]] – [[Battle of Warns]]: The [[Frisians]] defeat the forces of [[Holland]] under [[William II, Count of Hainaut]], in the midst of the Friso-Hollandic Wars.<ref>{{cite book|author=E. Howard Harris|title=The Literature of Friesland|publisher=Van Gorcum & Comp|year=1956|page=13}}</ref>
* [[October 21]] – [[Battle of Auberoche]] in [[Gascony]]: The English defeat the French.<ref>Jonathan Sumption, ''The Hundred Years War: Trial by Battle'', Vol. I, (Faber & Faber, 1990), {{ISBN|978-0-571-20095-5}}, pp. 467–470.</ref>
* [[November 8]] – The English take [[La Réole]] in Gascony.<ref>Jonathan Sumption, ''The Hundred Years War: Trial by Battle'', Vol. I, (Faber & Faber, 1990), {{ISBN|978-0-571-20095-5}}, p. 474.</ref>
* [[December]] – The English take [[Aiguillon, Lot-et-Garonne|Aiguillon]] in Gascony.</onlyinclude>

1359.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
[[File:Spain and Western North Africa 1360.jpg|200px|thumb|The various kingdoms in Iberia and Spain in 1359]]
* [[January 9]] – The [[Zayyanid dynasty|Zayanids]] under [[Abu Hammu Musa II]] recapture the [[Kingdom of Tlemcen]] in [[Algeria]].
* [[January 25]] – In Holland, [[Floris I van Borselen]], keeper of the seal for the former count of Holland, [[William I of Bavaria|Willem V]], reconciles with the new count, [[Albert I, Duke of Bavaria|Albert of Bavaria]].
* [[January 28]] – [[Shaykh Uways Jalayir]], ruler of [[Iraq]], loses control of the city of [[Tabriz]] to Akh Juq after the Emir Ali Pilan loses a battle at [[Nakhchivan (city)|Nakhchivan]] (now in the Republic of Azerbaijan)
* [[February 20]] – [[Hook and Cod wars]]: The siege of [[Heusden Castle]] in Holland ends after a siege of almost six months.
* [[March 11]] – [[Hook and Cod wars]]: With the city of [[Delft]] in Holland in rebellion, the regent for Holland, Albert of Bavaria, orders the blocking of all waterways around Delft before beginning a formal siege if Delft does not surrender by April 1. 
* [[March 24]] – 
**The [[Second Treaty of London]] is signed by the monarchs of England (King Edward III) and France (King Jean II, a prisoner of war since 1356 and signing under duress) with a goal of ending the two kingdom's conflict in the [[Hundred Years' War]]. Under its terms, which Jean's son the [[Charles V of France|Dauphin Charles]] refuses to ratify, would have led to the cession of half of France's territory— including Brittany, Normandy, Anjou, Touraine and Maine— to England. King Edward then makes plans to invade France in October.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mortimer |first=Ian |title=The Perfect King: The Life of Edward III, Father of the English Nation |date=2007 |publisher=Pimlico |location=London |pages=334–335|isbn=978-1-84413-530-1}}</ref>
**[[Hook and Cod wars]]: The siege of [[Marquette Castle|Heemskerk Castle]], which was started on Dedcember 4 by Albert of Bavaria, administrator of Holland, for the Hook partisans, ends after three months with Heemskerk falling to Albert.<ref name=Wagenaar>{{citation |last=Wagenaar |first=Jan |year=1770 |title=Vaderlandsche historie |volume=III |publisher=Isaak Tirion, Amsterdam |pages=296–297 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iHEUAAAAQAAJ }}</ref> During the siege, however, the city of Delft, controlled by the Cod sympathizers, has revolted.

=== April–June ===
* [[April 1]] – [[Hook and Cod wars]]: [[Albert I, Duke of Bavaria]] the Habsburg regent for Holland, begins the [[:nl:Beleg van Delft (1359)|siege]] of [[Delft]], a stronghold for the rebellious Cods. After 10 weeks, Delft surrenders in June under terms of dismantling the city walls and the payment to the Hooks of 40,000 [[Écu|ecus]].<ref name=Wagenaar/>
* [[April 19]] – A 1357 truce agreed upon by England and France expires after two years, clearing the way for hostilities to resume.<ref>{{cite book |last=Hoskins |first=Peter |date=2011 |title=In the Steps of the Black Prince: The Road to Poitiers, 1355–1356 |url= |location=Woodbridge, Suffolk |publisher=Boydell |page=201 |isbn=978-1-84383-611-7}}</ref>
* [[May 25]] – The [[Estates General (France)|French States-General]] repudiates the terms of the [[Second Treaty of London]], signed earlier in the year between [[Kingdom of England|England]] and [[Kingdom of France|France]].<ref>name="Tout1905">{{cite book|title=The Political History of England, Volume 3|year=1905|page=395|last=Tout|first=T. F.|publisher=Longmans, Green And Co.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oz0fAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA395}}</ref> 
* [[May 29]] – The [[:nl:Beleg van Delft (1359)|siege of Delft]] ends after two months as the city, a center for the Cods in the [[Hook and Cod wars]], surrenders to the Hooks and the army of the Count of Holland, the regent Albert of Bavaria.
* [[June 11]] – The [[Battle of Barcelona (1359)|Battle of Barcelona]] between the Spanish kingdoms of Castile (with aid from Portugal) and Aragon in the [[War of the Two Pedros]], a naval battle off the coast of Barcelona, ends after two days. Althogh the Castilian Navy of more than 120 ships vastly outnumbers the 10 galleys of Aragon, the Aragonese make the first use of naval artillery and employs its new weapon, a bombard mounted on one of its ships. 
* [[June 20]] – Upon the death of [[Eric XII of Sweden|Erik Magnusson]], his claims to the [[Sweden|Swedish]] throne die with him, and power is restored undivided to his father, King [[Magnus IV of Sweden|Magnus]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://sok.riksarkivet.se/Sbl/Presentation.aspx?id=15403 |title= Erik Magnusson|website=Svenskt biografiskt lexikon |access-date= June 19, 2023}}</ref> With this unexpected death of [[Eric XII of Sweden|Erik Magnusson]], a previous promise to give [[Helsingborg]] to Denmark was reneged on by [[Magnus IV Eriksson]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url   =http://worldtimeline.info/sweden/swed1300.htm|title=Chronology of Sweden|publisher = worldtimeline.info |access-date=August 1, 2018}}</ref> But [[Valdemar IV Atterdag]] was far too ambitious a ruler to have his plan to reassemble the Danish kingdom fall into pieces, and so he proceeded to invade Scania the next year with his mercenary army.<ref name="auto"/>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 4]] – [[Francesco II Ordelaffi]] surrenders to the Papal commander, [[Gil Álvarez Carrillo de Albornoz|Gil de Albornoz]].<ref>Rendina, Claudio (1994). I capitani di ventura. Rome: Newton Compton.</ref>
* [[August 23]] – (28 [[Ramadan]] [[Islamic calendar|760 AH]]In what is now [[Spain]], [[Ismail II of Granada|Ismail II]] becomes the new [[Emirate of Granada|Sultan of Granada]] in a coup d'etat against his half-brother, [[Muhammad V of Granada|Muhammed V]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Harvey|first=L. P.|title=Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=td3tcLWvSNkC|year=1992|publisher=University of Chicago Press|pages=209-210|isbn=978-0-226-31962-9}}</ref>. About 100 men under Ismail's command scale the walls of the royal palace, the [[Alhambra]], overpower the guards and kill the hajib Ridwan. Muhammad V is away from the palace and flees eastward to the city of [[Guadix]], where his authority is still recognized.
* [[August]] – [[Qulpa]] becomes Khan of the [[Blue Horde]] after the death of [[Berdi Beg]].
* [[September]] – [[Margaret, Countess of Tyrol]], and her second husband, [[Louis V, Duke of Bavaria]], are absolved from [[excommunication]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 28]] – King Edward III of England lands at [[Calais]]] to begin the [[Reims campaign]], a second invasion of France, after peace negotiations fail, and is determined to reach [[Reims]] in order to be crowned as the [[King of France]].<ref>{{DNB|last=Hunt |first=William  |wstitle=Edward III  |volume=17 |page=62–63}} endnote</ref>  
* [[November 4]] – The deposed Granadan sultan Muhammad V flees Europe after conceding defeat and sails to Africa, where he and other former officials end up at [[Fez, Morocco|Fez]] in what is now [[Morocco]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=The Three Great Sultans of al-Dawla al-Ismā'īliyya al-Naṣriyya Who Built the Fourteenth-Century Alhambra: Ismā'īl I, Yūsuf I, Muḥammad V (713–793/1314–1391) |first=Antonio |last=Fernández-Puertas |journal=Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society |series=Third Series |volume=7 |number=1 |date=1997|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] on behalf of [[Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland]]|location=London|pages=15–16}}</ref>
* [[December 14]] – [[Cangrande II della Scala]], [[Lords of Verona|Lord of Verona]], a city-state in [[Italy]], since 1351, is assassinated on orders of his younger brother, [[Cansignorio della Scala]], who becomes the new ruler.<ref>{{DBI |first=Gian Maria |last=Varanini |title=DELLA SCALA, Cangrande |url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/cangrande-della-scala_res-2fb3665a-87ec-11dc-8e9d-0016357eee51_%28Dizionario_Biografico%29/ | volume = 37}}</ref>
* [[December 19]] – The [[General Court of Catalonia]] (parliament) is held in [[Cervera]], giving birth to the Deputation of the General of Catalonia (''Diputació del General de Catalunya''), also called [[Generalitat of Catalonia]] (''Generalitat de Catalunya'').<ref>Adam J. Kosto (3 May 2001). Making Agreements in Medieval Catalonia: Power, Order, and the Written Word, 1000-1200. Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-521-79239-4}}. Retrieved 19 June 2021.</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Abu Salim Ali II overthrows Muhammad II as-Said as ruler of the [[Marinid dynasty]], in modern-day [[Morocco]].
* Shah Mahmud overthrows his brother, Shah Shuja, as leader of the [[Muzaffarids of Iran|Muzaffarid]] tribe in Persia.
* Ananda Patel (considered common ancestor for most of the modern-day population of Bhadran) moves to [[Bhadran, Gujarat|Bhadran]] from [[Anklav]]. 
* [[Berlin]] joins the [[Hanseatic League]].
* ''probable date'' – [[Battle of Megara (1359)|Battle of Megara]]: A Christian coalition defeats a Turkish raider fleet.<ref>Luttrell, Anthony (1975). "The Hospitallers at Rhodes, 1306–1421". In Setton, Kenneth M.; Hazard, Harry W. (eds.). A History of the Crusades, Volume III: The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries. Madison and London: University of Wisconsin Press. pp. 278–313. {{ISBN|0-299-06670-3}}.</ref><ref>Topping, Peter (1975). "The Morea, 1311–1364". In Setton, Kenneth M.; Hazard, Harry W. (eds.). A History of the Crusades, Volume III: The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries. Madison and London: University of Wisconsin Press. pp. 104–140. {{ISBN|0-299-06670-3}}.</ref>
* ''earliest possible date'' – [[Bogdan I of Moldavia|Bogdan I]] becomes Prince of [[Moldavia]] (modern-day Moldova) after freeing it from [[Kingdom of Hungary|Hungarian]] control. He will be ancestor of the [[House of Bogdan]], who will rule [[Moldavia]] for more than three centuries.<ref>{{cite book|last=Georgescu|first=Vlad|author-link=Vlad Georgescu|year=1991|title=The Romanians: A History|url=https://archive.org/details/romanianshistory0000geor|url-access=registration|publisher=Ohio State University Press|isbn=0-8142-0511-9|page=18}}</ref></onlyinclude>

1389.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 19]] – In [[Ming dynasty]] China, General [[Lan Yu (general)|Lan Yu]] is rewarded by the Emperor [[Hongwu Emperor|Zhu Chongba]] of the Hongwu era for his victory over Mongol invaders in 1388. Lan Yu is given the title Duke of Liang, with rule over what is now the [[Gansu]] province.<ref>{{Cite book |editor-last1=Goodrich |editor-first1=L. Carrington |url=https://archive.org/details/dictionaryofming0001asso |title=Dictionary of Ming Biography, 1368–1644 |editor-last2=Fang |editor-first2=Chaoying |location=New York |publisher=Columbia University Press |year=1976 |pages=788-790|isbn=0-231-03801-1}}</ref>
* [[January 24]] – The [[University of Cologne]] (Universität zu Köln) begins operations <ref>Willehad Paul Eckert,  ''Kleine Geschichte der Universität Köln'' (''A Short History of the University of Köln'' (Bachem, 1961)</ref> and continues for more than 400 years before closing in [[1798]]. It will be re-established in [[1918]].
* [[February 24]] – Queen [[Margaret I of Denmark|Margaret]] of Norway and Denmark defeats [[Albert, King of Sweden]] in battle and becomes ruler of all three kingdoms. Albert is deposed from the Swedish throne and taken prisoner.
* [[March 14]] – The unpopular Sultan [[Tughluq Khan]] of [[Delhi Sultanate|Delhi]] is murdered and succeeded by his brother, [[Abu Bakr Shah]]. The assassins, including Abu Bakr, kill the Sultan Tughluq and his [[vizier]], Jahan Khan.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Jackson |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Jackson (historian) |url=https://archive.org/details/TheDelhiSultanateAPoliticalAndMilitaryHistoryCambridgeStudiesInIslamicCivilization/page/n353/mode/1up |title=the Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History |date=April 1999 |page=353|publisher=Cambridge University Press}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 1]] – Following the [[Battle of Sempach]], a seven-year peace agreement is concluded between the [[Duchy of Austria]] and the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]].<ref>{{HDS|8871|Battle of Sempach}}</ref> 
* [[April 19]] – [[Lithuania]], the last state in Europe to be Christianized, is given full recognition by [[Pope Urban VI]] as a Roman Catholic state.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Eidintas |first1=Alfonsas |title=The History of Lithuania |date=2015 |publisher=Eugrimas Publishing House |location=Vilnius |isbn=978-609-437-163-9 |page=51 |url=https://urm.lt/uploads/default/documents/Travel_Residence/history_of_lithuania_new.pdf |archive-date=2021-01-28 |access-date=2026-03-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128190626/https://urm.lt/uploads/default/documents/Travel_Residence/history_of_lithuania_new.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
* [[May 3]] – [[Richard II of England|Richard II]] takes control of England, away from the Lords Appellant.
* [[May 19]] – [[Vasili I of Russia|Vasili I]] becomes [[Grand Duchy of Moscow|Grand Prince of Moscow]] after the death of his father, [[Dmitry Donskoy]].
* [[May 21]] – Sir [[John Roches]] is made [[Admiral of the North and Western Fleets]] of the English Navy by King Richard II, but serves for only a month, until June 22.<ref>{{cite web|last=Woodger|first=L. S.|title=Roches, Sir John (c.1333-1400), of Bromham, Wilts.|url=http://www.historyofparliamentonline.org/volume/1386-1421/member/roches-sir-john-1333-1400|url-status=dead|accessdate=25 July 2017|website=History of Parliament Online|publisher=Institute of Historical Research, University of London|archive-date=8 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230508191939/http://www.historyofparliamentonline.org/volume/1386-1421/member/roches-sir-john-1333-1400}}</ref>
* [[June 2]] – [[Al-Salih Hajji]] becomes the Mamluk Sultan of Egypt and Syria a second time, replacing the Sultan [[Sayf ad-Din Barquq]] after having previously reigned from 1381 to 1382.<ref>Caroline Williams, et al., ''Islamic Monuments in Cairo: The Practical Guide'' (American University in Cairo Press, 2002) pp.16-176 {{ISBN|9789774246951}}</ref> Al-Salih rules until 1 February 1390, when he is overthrown by Barquq.
* [[June 11]] – The [[Hättebröder]], a group of German-speaking burghers during the reign of the German Albrecht as King of Sweden, arrest and imprison the Swedish mayor of Stockholm, Bertil Brun, and two other city officials, whom they hold for ransom.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heidenstam |first=Verner von |title=XXIII. I kung Albrekts dagar. Hättebröder och kapare (Svenskarna och deras hövdingar) |url=https://runeberg.org/svenhovd/230.html |access-date=2025-10-01 |website=runeberg.org |language=sv}}</ref> Brun and the other two officials become victims two weeks later of the [[Käpplinge murders]].
* [[June 15]] – At the [[Battle of Kosovo]], The [[Ottoman Empire]] and the [[Serbs]] fight an inconclusive clash, with both sides suffering heavy losses. Both Sultan [[Murad I]] and Serbian Prince [[Lazar Hrebeljanovic]] are killed in the battle. 
* [[June 16]] – The day after the Battle of Kosovo, [[Bayezid I]] succeeds his father [[Murad I]] as [[Ottoman Sultan]], and [[Stefan Lazarević]] succeeds his father Lazar as ruler of Serbia.<ref>"Bayezid I", by Halil Inalcik, in ''The Encyclopedia of Islam'', Vol. I, ed. by H.A.R. Gibb, et al. (Brill, 1986) p. 1118</ref> 
* [[June 17]] – On the night of the Feast of Corpus Christi, the [[Käpplinge murders]] (''Käpplingemorden'') take place in Sweden at [[Blasieholmen|Käpplingeholmen]] when 76 Swedish men are taken prisoner, convicted of treason, then burned alive in a barn.<ref>Astrid Heyde, "Käpplingemorden år 1389: ett 600-årsminne?" (Sankt Eriksårsbok publishing, 1989) pp. 9-18 </ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 12]] – English poet [[Geoffrey Chaucer]], who has recently started writing of the works that will be assembled in ''[[The Canterbury Tales]]'', is given a job to supplement his income as a writer when he is appointed by King Richard II of England as [[Clerk of works|Clerk of the King's Works]], overseer of the construction of royally-sponsored buildings.<ref> Henry Morley, ''English Writers: an attempt towards a history of English literature'', Vol. 5 (London: Cassell & Co., 1890) p. 245</ref> 
* [[July 18]] – The [[Hundred Years' War]] is temporarily halted as the [[Truce of Leulinghem]] goes into effect after having been signed in June by the [[Kingdom of England]] and [[Kingdom of France]]. The peace will last for 13 years.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Hundred Years War: Divided Houses| year=2009| last=Sumption|first=Jonathan|isbn=978-0-571-13897-5 |publisher=University of Pennsylvania Press|page=813-818}}</ref>
* [[August 11]] – [[Spyridon of Serbia]], Patriarch of the [[Serbian Orthodox Church]] since 1380, dies and the former Patriarch, [[Ephraim of Serbia|Jefrem]], takes his place.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Radojičić|first=Đ. Sp.|title=Grigorije iz Gornjaka|journal=Историјски часопис|issue=3|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=U1R_CgAAQBAJ&pg=PA85|year=1952|publisher=Istorijski institut|pages=86|id=GGKEY:73HS377YS6Y}}</ref>
* [[August 23]] – [[Isabeau of Bavaria]], who married King [[Charles V of France]] on July 17, 1385, is crowned as Queen consort of France.(1978).<ref>Barbara W. Tuchman, ''A Distant Mirror: The Calamitous 14th Century''(New York: Ballantine, 1978) pp.455-457 {{ISBN|978-0-345-34957-6}}</ref> 
* [[August 24]] – [[Qutbu'd-Din Shah]], the [[Kashmir Sultanate|Sultan of Kashmir]], dies after a reign of 16 years and is succeeded by his 9-year-old son, [[Sikandar Shah Miri]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Retzlaff |first1=Ralph H. |last2=Hasan |first2=Mohibbul |date= |title=Kashmir under the Sultans |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/595144 |journal=Journal of the American Oriental Society |pages=53 |doi=10.2307/595144 |jstor=595144 |issn=0003-0279|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Sikandar's mother, Queen Subhata, serves as the regent of Kashmir during his minority.
* [[September 8]] – [[Erik of Pomerania]] becomes the new [[King of Norway]] with the regnal name of Erik III after being elected at [[Trondheim]] by the [[Thing (assembly)|Ting]], the kingdom's assembly.<ref>{{cite web|url =  https://snl.no/Erik_av_Pommern|title=Erik Av Pommern|publisher=Store norske leksikon|author=Erik Opsahl|access-date=1 June 2018}}</ref>
* [[September 10]] – In Greece, [[Andronikos Asen Zaccaria]], chief law enforcement officer of the Principality of Achaea, ruled by the [[Republic of Genoa]], imprisons the [[Duke of Athens]], [[Nerio I Acciaioli|Nerio Acciaioli]], after the Navarrese commander [[Pedro de San Superano]] had invited Acciaioli to discuss peace.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Setton |first=Kenneth M. |chapter=The Catalans in Greece, 1311–1380; The Catalans and Florentines in Greece, 1380–1462 |title=The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries |series=[[Wisconsin Collaborative History of the Crusades|The History of the Crusades]] |volume=Three  |year=1975 |publisher=[[The University of Wisconsin Press]] |pages=248 |isbn=978-0-299-06670-3}}</ref>
* [[September 22]] – The [[Republic of Siena]] and the [[Duchy of Milan]] enter into a 10-year alliance.<ref>{{cite book | last = Caferro | first=William | title = John Hawkwood: An English Mercenary in Fourteenth-Century Italy | year = 2006 | location = Baltimore | publisher = The Johns Hopkins University Press |pages=285–288 |isbn = 0-8018-8323-7 }}</ref>
* [[September 30]] – King Charles VI of France and the Bishop Liébauld de Cousans of Verdun sign a treaty granting the Roman Catholic Church dominion over the city of Verdun. The treaty is approved five months later by Pope Clement VI on February 13, 1390.<ref>Louis Clouêt, (1870), ''Histoire de Verdun et du pays verdunois.'', volume 3 {{in lang|fr}}. (Verdun: Ch. Laurent, 1870) p.41</ref>

=== October –December ===
* [[October 25]] – The [[1389 conclave|papal conclave]] to elect a new Pope opens at the Apostolic Palace in Rome with 13 cardinals, all of whom had been selected by Pope Urban during the years from 1378 to 1384.<ref name=Miranda>Salvator Miranda, [https://cardinals.fiu.edu/conclave-xiv.htm Papal Elections of the 14th Century (1303–1394)] (1998)."</ref>The three absentees (from France, England and Hungary) had also been elevated to the college of cardinals by Pope Urban.
* [[November 1]] – The [[Antipope John XXIII]], reigning from Avignon, crowns [[Louis II of Anjou]] as [[Kingdom of Naples|King of Naples]], although the underage [[Ladislaus of Naples|King Ladislaus]] has been recognized as the rightful monarch by the late Pope Urban VI of Rome.<ref>{{cite book |last=Kekewich |first=Margaret L. |year=2008 |title=The Good King: René of Anjou and Fifteenth Century Europe |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |page=51|isbn=978-1-4039-8820-1}}</ref> Louis II will move to Naples on August 6, 1390, while Ladislaus flees, but since his troops cannot occupy the entire Neapolitan kingdom, Louis is only recognized in the French-occupied areas of Naples.<ref>{{cite book |last=Sumption |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Sumption, Lord Sumption |year=2009 |title=The Hundred Years War, Volume III: Divided Houses |publisher=Faber and Faber |page=781 |isbn=978-0-571-24012-8}}</ref>
* [[November 2]] – Pietro Tomacelli Cybo of Naples is elected as the successor of the late [[Pope Urban VI]], and takes the name [[Pope Boniface IX]].<ref name=Miranda/>
* [[December 31]] – In the [[Goryeo]] Revolution in Korea, 9-year-old [[Chang of Goryeo|King Wang Chang]] of Goryeo, and his father, the former [[U of Goryeo|King Wang U]] are assassinated by [[Gongyang of Goryeo|Prince Gongyang]]. The ten-year-old Chang and his predecessor, [[U of Goryeo|U]], are both assassinated later in the year.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Mircea I of Wallachia]] and Polish king [[Władysław II Jagiełło]] sign their first treaty, to protect their countries against Ottoman expansion.
* Hadji II is restored as [[Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo)|Mamluk]] Sultan of [[Egypt]], after overthrowing Sultan [[Barquq]].
* [[Wikramawardhana]] succeeds [[Hayam Wuruk]], as ruler of the [[Majapahit Empire]].
* Biri II succeeds Kade Alunu as King of the [[Kanem Empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] (now eastern [[Chad]] and [[Nigeria]]), and the Empire loses its land in present-day Chad to the [[Bilala]].
* [[Sandaki]] overthrows [[Magha II]], as [[Mansa (title)|Mansa]] of the [[Mali Empire]].
* Abd ar-Rahmân II succeeds Musa II as ruler of the [[Ziyanid]] Dynasty, in present-day western [[Algeria]].
* Abu Tashufin II succeeds his nephew, [[Abu Hammu II]], as ruler of the [[Abdalwadid]] Dynasty in present-day eastern [[Algeria]].
* [[Carmo Convent (Lisbon)|Carmo Convent]] is built in [[Lisbon]], [[Kingdom of Portugal|Portugal]].
</onlyinclude>

1380.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
[[File:明太祖画像.jpg|thumb|120px|the Emperor Hongwu]]
* [[January 1]] – The Republic of Venice's Admiral [[Carlo Zeno]] returns to [[Venice]] with 18 ships, after the city is on the verge of falling to conquest by the [[Republic of Genoa]].<ref name=Lane/>
* [[January 16]] – The fourth parliament of King Richard II assembles at Westminster after being summoned on October 20 for a six week session. The House of Commons elects Sir [[John Guildesborough]] as Speaker of the House.
* [[January 30]] – [[Simon Sudbury]], the [[Archbishop of Canterbury]], becomes the new [[List of lord chancellors and lord keepers|Lord Chancellor of England]], succeeding [[Richard Scrope, 1st Baron Scrope of Bolton|Baron Scrope of Bolton]]. Sudbury will continue in office as both archbishop and lord chancellor until his assassination on June 14, 1381, during the [[Peasants' Revolt]].
* [[February 12]] – [[Hu Weiyong]], the [[Grand chancellor (China)|Grand Chancellor]] of [[Ming dynasty]] [[China]], is accused of treason and executed as the [[Hongwu Emperor|Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang]] (Emperor Hongwu) begins a purge of over 30,000 people perceived as opponents of the Imperial government.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Dreyer |first=Edward L.|url=https://archive.org/details/earlymingchinapo0000drey |title=Early Ming China: a political history, 1355-1435 |publisher=Stanford University Press |year=1982 |page=135|isbn=0-8047-1105-4}}</ref>
* [[March 3]] – The 4th English parliament of King Richard II adjourns, and the King gives royal assent to the Assize of Cloths Act 1379 (providing a penalty for "the aulneger that setteth his seal to faulty cloths" and to the Farming of Benefices for Aliens Act 1379 (providing that "None shall take any [[benefice]] of an alien, or convey money to him.")<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of and Index to the Statutes |edition=13th |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1896 |volume=1: To the End of the Session 59 Vict. Sess. 2 (1895) |url={{GBurl|EfcZAAAAYAAJ|page=29}} |pages=29 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[March 4]] – The impostor [[Paul Palaiologos Tagaris]] becomes noticed by the Eastern Orthodox church when he donates a purported Christian relic, the skull of [[James the Just]], the [[1st century]] leader of the [[Early Christianity|Church of Jerusalem]], to the city of [[Ancona]].<ref name=Nicol>{{cite journal |last=Nicol |first=Donald M. |title=The Confessions of a bogus Patriarch: Paul Tagaris Palaiologos, Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem and Catholic Patriarch of Constantinople in the fourteenth century |journal=The Journal of Ecclesiastical History |volume=21 |issue=4 |year=1970 |pages=294–295}}</ref>
* [[March 13]] – The southern England town of [[Winchelsea]] in [[East Sussex]] is attacked and burned by an expeditionary force from France for a second time.<ref name=Fires>"Fires, Great", in ''The Insurance Cyclopeadia: Being an Historical Treasury of Events and Circumstances Connected with the Origin and Progress of Insurance'', Cornelius Walford, ed. (C. and E. Layton, 1876) p27</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 17]] – The impostor Tagaris follows his donation of relics to Ancona with what he claims is one of the nails from the [[True Cross]] upon which [[Jesus Christ|Jesus of Nazareth]] had been crucified in the first century, as well as a foot from the skeleton of [[Saint Anne]], mother of the [[Virgin Mary]] and grandmother of Jesus. His claims are believed by the leaders of Ancona and he is appointed as the [[Latin Patriarch of Constantinople]] by [[Pope Urban VI]] .<ref name=Nicol/>
* [[May 31]] – [[Grand Duke of Lithuania]] [[Jogaila]] signs the secret [[Treaty of Dovydiškės]], with the [[Teutonic Knights]]. This sparks a civil war with his uncle [[Kęstutis]].<ref>Kiaupa, Zigmantas; Jūratė Kiaupienė; Albinas Kuncevičius (2000) [1995]. ''The History of Lithuania Before 1795'' (in Lithuanian) (English ed.). Vilnius: Lithuanian Institute of History. pp. 124–126. {{ISBN|9986-810-13-2}}.</ref>
* [[June 24]] – At the [[Battle of Chioggia]], the navy of the [[Republic of Venice]], with 48 [[galley]]s,  defeats the invading fleet of the [[Republic of Genoa]], clearing a blockade of the Venetian harbor, regaining control of the Adriatic Sea, and beginning the dominance of the Venetian Navy. Venice supplements its fleet with the capture of 17 of Genoa's ships.<ref name=Lane>Lane, Frederic C. ''Venice: A Maritime Republic'' (Johns Hopkins University Press, 1973) pp. 192-196 Print.</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 29]] – At the age of 10, King [[Olaf II of Denmark]] is proclaimed as King Olaf IV of [[Norway]], with his mother [[Margaret I of Denmark|Margete]]) as regent. [[Iceland]] and the [[Faroe Islands]], as parts of [[Norway]], pass under the Danish crown.<ref>Bjørkvik, Halvard; Opsahl, Erik: ''Håkon 6. Magnusson'' i ''Store norske leksikon'' på snl.no. Henta 3. november 2025 frå https://snl.no/H%C3%A5kon_6._Magnusson</ref>
* [[August 26]] – King Richard II of England summons the [[English Parliament]] five months after the dissolution of the previous meeting, and directs the members of the House of Commons and House of Lords to assemble on November 5 at Westminster. 
* [[August]] – At [[Kayseri]] (now in [[Turkey]], [[Muhammad II Chelebi]] is crowned at the age of 7 as the new [[Eretnid dynasty|Sultan of Eretna]] upon the death of his father, [[Ali of the Eretnids|Sultan Ala al-Din Ali]], from a plague.
* [[September 8]] – At the [[Battle of Kulikovo]], Russian forces under Grand Prince [[Dmitry Donskoy]] of Moscow resist a large invasion, led by [[Mamai|Mamai Khan]], commander of the [[Blue Horde]] of [[Lithuania]] and [[Ryazan]], stopping their advance.<ref>[[Battle of Kulikovo#CITEREFKirpichnikov1980|Kirpichnikov 1980]], pp. 100–104.</ref><ref> (2017-07-19). "The Battle of Kulikovo: When the Russian Nation Was Born", by A. Timofeychev, in  Russia Beyond the Headlines</ref>
* [[September 16]] –  [[Charles V of France]] is succeeded by his twelve-year-old son, [[Charles VI of France|Charles VI]].<ref>[[Charles VI of France#CITEREFSumption2009|Sumption 2009]], p. 397.</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 2]] – [[Caterina Visconti]] marries her first cousin, [[Gian Galeazzo Visconti]], later Duke of Milan, at the Church of San Giovanni in Conca.<ref>Hoeniger, Cathleen (2006). "The Illuminated "Tacuinum sanitatis" Manuscripts from Northern Italy ca. 1380-1400: Sources, Patrons, and the Creation of a New Pictorial Genre". In Givens, Jean Ann; Reeds, Karen; Touwaide, Alain (eds.). ''Visualizing Medieval Medicine and Natural History, 1200-1550''. Ashgate Publishing. pp. 51–82.</ref>
* [[November 3]] – [[Charles VI of France]], who succeeded  his father ([[Charles V of France]]) in September, is crowned.<ref>Sumption 2009, p. 397.</ref>
* [[November 5]] – The English parliament assembles, and the House of Commons re-elects Sir [[John Guildesborough]] as its speaker.
* [[November 7]] – [[Sheikh Karimul Makhdum]], a Syrian Sunni Muslim missionary, brings the religion of [[Islam]] to the [[Philippine Islands]] by establishing [[Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Mosque|a mosque]] on the island of [[Tawi-Tawi]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Aben |first1=Ellie |title=Oldest Philippine mosque stands witness to centuries of Islamic heritage |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/2353616 |access-date=10 November 2023 |work=Arab News |date=11 August 2023 |language=en}}</ref> The date of November 7 is now celebrated annually as a holiday in the [[Bangsamoro]] region of the Philippines.<ref>{{cite news |date=November 6, 2007 |title=Nov. 7 is Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Day in the ARMM; declared a holiday |url=https://mindanews.com/press-release/2007/11/nov-7-is-sheikh-karimul-makhdum-day-in-the-armm-declared-a-holiday/ |work=[[MindaNews]] |access-date=July 17, 2025}}</ref>
* [[December 6]] – The English parliament adjourns and King Richard II gives royal assent to laws passed during the 31 day session, including an act providing that "All vessels of wine, honey, and oil brought into this realm shall be gauged" and a general pardon of "escapes and felons and clerks convict."<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |pages=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}
</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Sir [[William Walworth]], a member of the Fishmongers Guild, becomes [[Lord Mayor of London]] for the second time.
* Khan [[Tokhtamysh]] of the [[White Horde]] dethrones [[Mamai]] of the [[Blue Horde]]. The two hordes unite to form the [[Golden Horde]].<ref>Howorth 1880: 216, 226; Grousset 1970: 407, 436; Seleznëv 2009: 182–183; Počekaev 2010: 160–161.</ref>
* [[Makhdum Karim|Karim Al-Makhdum]] arrives in [[Jolo]], and builds a mosque.
* The [[Hongwu Emperor]] purges the [[chancellor of China]], Hu Weiyong, and abolishes that office, as he imposes direct imperial rule over the [[Ming dynasty#Government|six ministries]] of central government, for the [[Ming dynasty|Ming Empire]].
* The last islands of [[Polynesia]] are discovered and inhabited.
* The [[Companhia das Naus]] is founded by [[Ferdinand I of Portugal|King Ferdinand I of Portugal]].<ref>[[Fernão Lopes|Lopes, Fernão]] (1380–1460). ''Chronica de el-rei D. Fernando (vol. II)'' (PDF) (in Portuguese). Escriptorio, 147 - Rua dos Retrozeiros, Lisbon.</ref>
* The imposter [[Paul Palaiologos Tagaris]], having been appointed [[Latin Patriarch of Constantinople]] by [[Pope Urban VI]], takes up residence in his see at [[Chalcis]].</onlyinclude>

1364.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 3]] – [[John II of France|Jean II le Bon]] ("John the Good"), King of France, voluntarily returns to imprisonment in England to secure the payment of his remaining ransom under the [[Treaty of Brétigny]] and in order to free the other hostages who had taken his place upon his release in 1363. King Jean's incarceration takes place as house arrest at the [[Savoy Palace]] in [[London]], where he resides until his death on April 8.<ref>{{cite book|first=Françoise|last=Autrand|title=Charles V, le Sage|trans-title=Chrles V the Wise|location=Paris |publisher=Fayard|year=1994|page=446|isbn=2-213-02769-2|url=http://www.persee.fr/web/revues/home/prescript/article/ahess_0395-2649_1995_num_50_3_279387_t1_0612_0000_001}}</ref> 
* [[February 4]] – [[Zhu Yuanzhang]], the Duke of Wu, proclaims himself as "King of Wu" after defeating the rebel [[Chen Youliang]] at the [[Battle of Lake Poyang]]. At the same time, the rebel [[Zhang Shicheng]] also claimed the same title in the lower [[Yangtze]] River region.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mote |first=Frederick W |title=The Cambridge History of China Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1988 |isbn=0521243327 |location=Cambridge |page=55 |chapter=The rise of the Ming dynasty, 1330–1367}}</ref>
* [[February 15]] – Joint kings [[Magnus IV of Sweden|Magnus Eriksson]] and [[Haakon VI of Norway|Haakon Magnusson]] of Sweden are both deposed by noblemen, who instead elect Magnus's nephew [[Albert of Sweden|Albrekt of Mecklenburg]] the new king of [[Sweden]]. Albrekt is crowned as King on February 18 at a ceremony at the [[Stones of Mora]] of [[Knivsta]], near [[Uppsala]].
* [[February 20]] – [[David II of Scotland]] marries [[Margaret Drummond, Queen of Scotland|Margaret Drummond]].<ref>{{cite web |title=5 forgotten queens and princesses of Scotland |url=https://www.scotsman.com/regions/5-forgotten-queens-and-princesses-scotland-548776 |website=www.scotsman.com |date=April 2019 |access-date=4 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[March 3]] – In Italy, peace is worked out between the Duchy of Mirandola and the anti-Milan league after the January 10 attack on the city of Mirandola.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Felice Ceretti |year=1877 |title=Una pagina da aggiungersi alla genealogia Pico della Mirandola: Giovanni di Nicoló Pico |trans-title=A page to be added to the Pico della Mirandola genealogy: Giovanni di Nicolò Pico |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lrKJE-v3F5MC&pg=PA43 |magazine=Giornale araldico-genealogico-diplomatico |location=Pisa |publisher=Accademia Araldica Italiana|pages=42–47 |language=it}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 1]] – [[Pope Urban V]] issues a series of seven [[papal bull]]s to fund the [[Savoyard Crusade]] to be led by Count [[Amadeus VI of Savoy]] against the Moslem Ottoman Turks who control the [[Holy Land]] in the area surrounding [[Jerusalem]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Setton |first1=Kenneth M. |title=The Papacy and the Levant, 1204–1571 |volume=I |publisher=American Philosophical Society |location=Philadelphia |date=1976|page=285}}</ref>
* [[April 8]] – [[Charles V of France|Charles V]] becomes [[monarch|King]] of [[Kingdom of France|France]] upon the death of his imprisoned father, [[John II of France|Jean II]], in England.<ref>{{cite web |title=Charles V {{!}} king of France |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Charles-V-king-of-France |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |access-date=22 August 2018 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[May 12]] – The [[Jagiellonian University]] is founded in [[Kraków]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Maciej |last=Iłowiecki |title=Dzieje nauki polskiej. |trans-title=History of Polish Science |location=Warsaw |publisher=Wydawnictwo Interpress |year=1981 |page=23 |isbn=83-223-1876-6}} .</ref>   
* [[May 16]] – The [[Battle of Cocherel]] is fought in France over the matter of claim to the French throne recently vacated by the April death of King John the Good. Less than 3,000 troops commanded by General [[Bertrand du Guesclin]], on behalf of King John's son [[Charles V of France|Charles of Valois]] defend against a larger force of more than 5,000 soldiers and 300 archers sent by a rival claimant, [[Charles II of Navarre|King Carlos II of Navarre]] and commanded by [[Jean III de Grailly]], with the help of English troops led by [[John Jouel]]. Guesclin is able to deceive the Navarrese and English troops by retreating and then surrounding the enemy, and King Charles is formally crowned three days later.<ref>{{cite web|author=Jean Froissart|url=https://www.dhi.ac.uk/onlinefroissart/ |title=The Online Froissart: transcriptions and reproductions of many manuscripts of the Chronicles|volume=1|year=1391}}</ref>
* [[May 19]] – The coronation of [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]] of France takes place at the [[Reims Cathedral]] in [[Reims]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Jonathan |last=Sumption |title=The Hundred Years War: Trial by Fire|publisher=(University of Pennsylvania Press |year=2001 |page=511}}</ref>
* [[June 2]] – King [[Charles V of France]] issues a letters patent to recognize that the King's youngest son, [[Philip the Bold]], as the rightful [[Duke of Burgundy|Duke]] of the autonomous [[Duchy of Burgundy]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Bertrand |last=Schnerb |title=L'État bourguignon|trans-title=The Burgundian State|publisher=Tempus|location=Paris|year=2005|page=44 |isbn=978-2-262-02360-7}}</ref> King John II, Philip's late grandfather, had been allowed Philip to serve as Duke since September 6.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 28]] – [[Battle of Cascina]]: Forces of the [[Republic of Florence]], led by [[Galeotto Malatesta]], defeat those of the [[Republic of Pisa]].
* [[August 6]] – [[Ignatius Saba I]] becomes the [[Syriac Orthodox Church|Syriac Orthodox]] [[Patriarch of Tur Abdin]].<ref>{{cite book | last1 =Barsoum| first1 =Aphrem|date=2008|title=The History of Tur Abdin|publisher=Gorgias Press|translator=Matti Moosa|author-link=Ignatius Aphrem I Barsoum|page=95}}</ref>
* [[September 10]] – [[Philip II of Taranto|Philip]] of [[Duchy of Anjou|Anjou]] becomes [[Latin Empire|Titular Emperor of Constantinople]] and [[Taranto|Prince of Taranto]].
* [[September 29]] – [[Battle of Auray]]: The [[Breton War of Succession]] ends, with the victory of the [[Montfort of Brittany|House of Montfort]] over [[Charles of Blois]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 8]] – [[Philotheos Kokkinos]] is appointed by the Byantine Emperor [[John V Palaiologos]] to the position of the [[Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople]] for the second time in his life, as leader of the Eastern Orthodox Christians.<ref>[https://www.oca.org/saints/lives/2020/10/11/102905-venerable-philotheus-patriarch-of-constantinople Venerable Philotheus, Patriarch of Constantinople], in ''The Lives of the Saints'' (The Orthodox Church in America, 2020)</ref> He had previously been the Patriarch from 1353 to 1354.
* [[November 16]] – [[Vladislav I of Wallachia|Vladislav I]] (also known as Vlaicu-Vodă) becomes voivode of [[Wallachia]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Vladislav I, 1364-1377|first=Constantin I.|last=Istrati|location=Bucharest|publisher=Editura Militara|year=1979}}</ref>
* [[December 4]] – King Edward III of England summons the English Parliament and directs the members of the House of Lords and the House of Commons to assemble at Westminster on January 20.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Bogdana Monastery]] is built in [[Moldavia]].
* Rana Kshetra Singh succeeds Rana Hamir Singh, as ruler of [[Mewar]] (part of modern-day western [[India]]).
* Anavema Reddy succeeds Anavota Reddy, as ruler of the [[Reddy]] Dynasty in [[Andhra Pradesh]] (part of modern-day southern [[India]]).
* The [[Kingdom of Ava]] is established by [[Thado Minbya]] in modern-day northern [[Burma]]. Some [[Burmese chronicles|chronicles]] and sources however date the event in 1365. 
</onlyinclude>

1365.events:
=== January–March ===
* [[January 20]] – The [[English Parliament]] assembles at [[Westminster]] to begin a four week session but adjourns on [[February 17]] without any legislation of record having been enacted.
* [[February 20]] – In Italy, [[Paolo Alboino della Scala]], Lord of Verona, is arrested on orders of his brother [[Cansignorio della Scala]], on charges of "conjuring" and imprisoned for the rest of his life, before being strangled to death in 1375.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Gian Maria Varanini , Della Scala, Paolo Alboino|encyclopedia= Dizionario biografico degli italiani |volume=37|publisher=Institute of the Italian Encyclopedia|editor=Gian Maria Varanini |year=1989}}</ref>
* [[February 25]] – (6th waxing of [[Tabaung]] The Burmese King [[Thado Minbya]] proclaims the founding of the [[Kingdom of Ava]] at what are now the ruins of [[Inwa]] near what is now [[Manadalay]] in [[Myanmar]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Royal Historical Commission of Burma |title=[[Hmannan Yazawin]] |volume=1 |orig-year=1832 |location=Yangon |language=my |year=2003 |publisher=[[Ministry of Information, Myanmar]]|pages=396–398}}</ref> 
* [[March 3]] – At the [[Battle of Gataskogen]], [[Albert, King of Sweden|King Albrekt of Sweden]] defeats and captures the former King, [[Magnus IV of Sweden|Magnus Eriksson]], whom he had overthrown on February 18, 1364, confirming his entitlement to the [[Sweden]].<ref>{{cite web |title = The Age of the King |work = A 14th century political history of Sweden |date = August 3, 2012 |url = https://albrechts.se/a-14th-century-political-history-of-sweden-part-3-the-age-of-the-king}}</ref>
* [[March 6]] – The [[:es:Tratado de Pamplona|
Treaty of Pamplona]] is signed by King Carlos II of Navarre and King Charles V of France to begin a truce between the two kingdoms.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QC8VAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA304 |title=Cours d'histoire des Etats Européens |publisher=Maximilian-Samson-Friedrich Schöll Publié par Gide Fils |year=1830}}</ref>
* [[March 12]] – The [[University of Vienna]] is founded by [[Rudolf IV of Austria|Rudolf IV, Duke of Austria]], commemorated  more than 650 years later as the oldest university in the German-speaking world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=University of Vienna: 650 Years |url=https://www.austrianinformation.org/fall-2015/university-of-vienna-650-years |date=November 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711170631/https://www.austrianinformation.org/fall-2015/university-of-vienna-650-years |archive-date=July 11, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 12]] – The [[Treaty of Guérande (1365)|Treaty of Guérande]] is signed at [[Guérande]] between the English Duke [[John IV of Brittany]] and King [[Charles V of France]], ending the [[War of the Breton Succession]] after 24 years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-22 |title=War of the Breton Succession {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/War-of-the-Breton-Succession |access-date=2026-08-18 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Princely Power in Late Medieval France: Jeanne de Penthièvre and the War for Brittany |first=Erika |last=Graham-Goering |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2020 |page=76|isbn=9781108805544 }}</ref>
* [[May 14]] – The [[Apt, Vaucluse#Ecclesiastical history|Council of Apt]] is held in France between the archbishops and bishops of [[Arles]], [[Embrun, Hautes-Alpes|Embrun]] and [[Aix-en-Provence]] and results in the publication of 28 decrees, including the granting of 11 days of [[indulgence]] to persons who visit "with pious sentiments", the Church of the Blessed Virgin at Apt on the feast of the [[Exaltation of the Holy Cross]] and venerate there certain relics of the Cross.<ref>{{CE1913|wstitle=Council of Apt|first=Thomas Joseph|last= Shahan }}</ref> 
* [[May 17]] – [[Otto V of Bavaria|Otto of Wittelsbach]] becomes the sole [[Elector of Brandenburg]] in the Holy Roman Empire upon the death of his brother, [[Louis II of Brandenburg|Ludwig II]].<ref>{{Cite ADB|24|663|669}}</ref>
* [[May 28]] – [[Raymond Berengar (Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller)|Raymond Berengar]] becomes the new [[Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller]] upon the death of the Grand Master [[Roger de Pins]], who had led the [[Hospitaller Rhodes|island of Rhodes]] since 1355.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Grand Masters |url=https://www.orderofmalta.int/history/the-grand-masters/ |website=Sovereign Order of Malta |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Delaville Le Roulx |first=Joseph |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=umn.31951002017276f |title=Les Hospitaliers à Rhodes jusqu'à la mort de Philibert de Naillac (1310–1421) |trans-title= The Hospitallers in Rhodes until the death of Philibert de Naillac (1310–1421) |year=1913 |pages=130–133 |language=fr}}</ref>
* [[June 2]] – The [[Hungarian occupation of Vidin]] begins, with the capture of the city by the forces of [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]] and the capture of the Tsar [[Ivan Sratsimir of Bulgaria]], as a prisoner of war.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Vidin, Siege of|first=Rossina |last=Kostova|encyclopedia=The Oxford Encyclopedia of Medieval Warfare and Military Technology|editor=Clifford J. Rogers |publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2010}}</ref>
* [[June 4]] – At a coronation ceremony held at the [[Church of St. Trophime, Arles|Church of St. Trophime]] at [[Arles]], [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], is crowned as the [[Kingdom of Arles|King of the two Burgundies]].<ref name=Cox/>
* [[June 27]] – King Peter II of Cyprus and Duke Amadeus of Savoy depart from [[Venice]] in 165 ships to begin the  [[Alexandrian Crusade]] to attack Egypt.<ref name=Cox>{{cite book|first=Eugene L. |last=Cox |title=The Green Count of Savoy: Amadeus VI and Transalpine Savoy in the Fourteenth Century|location=Princeton NJ|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=1967|pages=199–205|isbn=978-1-4008-7499-6}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 21]] – [[Marco Cornaro]] is elected as the new [[Doge of Venice|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Venice]], three days after the death of [[Lorenzo Celsi]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Cornaro, Marco|encyclopedia= Dizionario biografico degli italiani |volume=29|publisher=Institute of the Italian Encyclopediayear=1983}}</ref> 
* [[July 27]] – [[Albert III of Austria|Albrecht III]] and [[Leopold III, Duke of Austria|Leopold III]] become the joint rulers of the Duchy of Austria and the lands of the Habsburg family upon the death of their older brother, Rudolf IV.<ref name="Jaschke102">{{cite book |chapter=From Famous Empresses to Unspectacular Queens |first=Karl-Ulrich |last=Jaschke |title=Queens and Queenship in Medieval Europe |editor-first=Anne J. |editor-last=Duggan |publisher=The Boydell Press |year=1997 |page=102 |isbn=9780851158815 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8uJVS6cBOrgC&pg=PA102 }}</ref>
* [[August 16]] – The warlord [[Bolad Temür]], who has held control of the court of the Yuan dyanasty Chinese Emperor Huizong as father of the ailing Empress Consort Bayan Khutugh, is assassinated by Bayan Dar on orders of the Emperor.<ref>{{cite book|author=Ke Shaomin |chapter=Emperor Huizong |title=New History of Yuan Dynasty|publisher=Republic of China|language=zh|quote=In the seventh month of autumn, on the day of Yiyou, Boluo Temur was executed}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Mote |first1=Frederick |title=The Cambridge History of China Volume 7 The Ming Dynasty, 1368-1644, Part I |last2=Twitchett |first2=Denis |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1988 |page=22|isbn=978-0-521-24332-2}}</ref>
* [[September 8]] – Öljei Khutuk, the Korean born wife of the [[Toghon Temür|Emperor Huizong]] of [[List of emperors of the Yuan dynasty|Yuan dynasty China]], becomes his primary consort upon the death of at age 42 Huizong's primary wife, the Empress consort [[Bayan Khutugh]]. In December, Öljei is proclaimed by Huizong as the [[Empress Gi]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Keith McMahon|title=Celestial Women: Imperial Wives and Concubines in China from Song to Qing|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield Publishers|year=2016|pages=66–67}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 9]] – [[Alexandrian Crusade]]: The city of [[Alexandria]] in the [[Mamluk Sultanate]] of [[Egypt]] is sacked by an allied force of King [[Peter I of Cyprus]] and the knights of the [[Knights Hospitaller|Order of St. John of Jerusalem]] after a three day siege. After the killing of more than 20,000 civilians and the capturing of 5,000 others to be sold into slavery, the knights abandon Alexandria.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Sack of Alexandria (1365)|author=[[Alexander Mikaberidze]] |encyclopedia=[[Conflict and Conquest in the Islamic World: A Historical Encyclopedia]] |volume=1 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |year=2011 |page=72}}</ref>
* [[November 22]] – The [[:da:Freden i Vordingborg (1365)|Peace of Vordingborg]] is signed between representatives of the Kingdom of Denmark and the Hanseatic League to temporarily end the [[Danish–Hanseatic War (1361–1370)|Danish–Hanseatic War]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://historiskerejser.dk/dansk-hanseatisk-krig-1362-65/ |last=Eriksen |first=Anders Bager |year=2017 |title=Dansk-Hanseatisk Krig (1362-65) |trans-title=The Danish-Hanseatic War (1362-65) |website=Historiskerejser.dk |language=da-DK}}</ref> The war will resume in [[1367]].
* [[November 30]] – The ''[[Nagarakretagama]]'', a Javanese eulogy chronicling the journey of the [[Majapahit]] king, [[Hayam Wuruk]], through his kingdom, is completed by [[Mpu Prapanca]].
* [[December 6]] – [[Edward the Black Prince]], son of King Edward III of England, sends a latter to King [[Charles V of France]] demanding that the French monarch's intervention in Edward's conflict with Count [[Gaston III of Foix]] and threatening an armed conflict if Charles refuses.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Tucoo-Chala |first=Pierre |url=http://archive.org/details/gastonfebusungra0000tuco |title=Gaston Fébus : un grand prince d'Occident au XIVe siècle |location=Pau |publisher=Marrimpouey|year=1976 |page=122}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Adrianopole]] (modern-day Edirne) becomes the capital city of the [[Ottoman Sultanate]].
* In modern-day southern [[India]], [[Bahmani Sultan]] [[Mohammed Shah I]] invades the [[Vijayanagara Empire]].
* The [[Sukhothai Kingdom]] in northern [[Thailand]] becomes a tributary state of the [[Ayutthaya Kingdom]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}
* [[Muhammad V of Granada|Muhammed V]] begins building the [[Maristan of Granada]] (a hospital) in [[Granada]] (in modern-day [[Spain]]).
* The [[Chagatai Khanate]] defeats Timur in the [[Battle of Tashkent]].

1388.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 24]] – [[Eleanor of Arborea]], regent for her son Marianus V of the independent [[Judicate of Arborea]], on the island of [[Sardinia]], signs a peace agreement with the [[Crown of Aragon]] in [[Spain]], ending a war between the two nations.<ref>Bianca Pitzorno, ''Vita di Eleonora di Arborea, principessa medioevale di Sardegna'' (3rd ed.), (Milan: Mondadori, 2010) p.555</ref>
* [[February 2]] – Queen [[Margaret I of Denmark]] is proclaimed the Queen of Norway after the death of her son, [[Olaf II of Denmark|Olav IV Haakonsson]].
* [[February 3]] – The five [[Lords Appellant]], regents for [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] open a new session of the House of Commons and the House of Lords with the goal of exposing King Richard's attempt to make peace with France in order to drive them from power. After hearing the case of the Lords Appellant, the Parliament convicts five of King Richard's associates— Lord Chancellor [[Michael de la Pole, 1st Earl of Suffolk|Michael de la Pole]]; London's former Lord Mayor [[Nicholas Brembre]]; Duke of Ireland [[Robert de Vere, 9th Earl of Oxford|Robert de Vere]]; Archbishop of York [[Alexander Neville (bishop)|Alexander Neville]]; and Chief Justice [[Robert Tresilian]]— guilty of ""living in vice, deluding the said king" and embracing the mammon of iniquity for themselves".<ref>Thomas Favent, [https://www.arts.cornell.edu/prh3/310/texts/favent.html "History or Narration Concerning the Manner and Form of the Miraculous Parliament at Westminster"], trans. by Andrew Galloway", in ''The Letter of the Law: Legal Practice and Literary Production in Medieval England'', ed. by [[Emily Steiner]] and Candace Barrington (Ithaca, NY: Cornell University Press, 2002), pp. 231–252. {{ISBN|0-8014-8770-6}}</ref>
* [[February 19]] – Chief Justice [[Robert Tresilian]], one of the five advisors to King Richard convicted of treason in absentia, is discovered hiding in sanctuary at Westminster and is dragged by a mob into the Parliament. Because he was already convicted, Tresilian is hanged in publicon the same day.<ref>{{cite book|first=Gerald|last=Harriss|authorlink=G. L. Harriss|title=Shaping the Nation: England, 1360–1461|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=Oxford|year=2005|page=464|isbn=0-19-822816-3}}</ref>
* [[February 20]] – London's Lord Mayor Bembre is hanged in public at [[Tyburn]] after having been imprisoned in the [[Tower of London]].<ref name="S88">{{cite book|last=Sumption |first=Jonathan|title=Divided Houses: Hundred Years War |year=2009 |publisher=Faber & Faber|location=London|isbn=978-0-57124-012-8|volume=3|pages=643–647}}</ref>
* [[March 12]] – [[Pope Urban VI]] issues a [[papal bull]] permitting the Lithuanian capital, [[Vilnius]], to establish a cathedral, acknowledging that pagan objects have been discarded and that Christianity has come to the Baltic nation.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lituanus.org/1987/87_4_03.htm |title=The Conversion of Lithuania 1387 |access-date=2026-03-27 |archive-date=2020-07-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200727151454/http://www.lituanus.org/1987/87_4_03.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 9]] – At the [[Battle of Näfels]], the [[Canton of Glarus]], in alliance with the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]], decisively defeats the [[Duchy of Austria]] and the [[Habsburg]]s, despite being outnumbered 16 to one.<ref>{{HDS|8873|"Battle of Nafels"}}, by Ernst Temp, in the online ''Historical Dictionary of Switzerland''</ref>
* [[May 18]] – 
**At the [[Battle of Buyur Lake]], an invasion force from Ming dynasty China, under General [[Lan Yu (general)|Lan Yu]] defeats a large [[Mongolia]]n army led by [[Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür]], and captures 100 members of the [[Northern Yuan Dynasty]]. Uskhal Khan will be killed later while trying to escape. The invading Chinese army destroys [[Karakorum]], the capital of the Mongol Empire.<ref name="lang98-159">{{cite book |last=Langlois |first = John D. Jr. |title=The Cambridge History of China, Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1 |year = 1998 |publisher = Cambridge University Press |location= Cambridge |ISBN=0-521-24332-7 |chapter=The Hung-wu reign, 1368–1398 |page=159}}</ref>
**[[Cozia Monastery]] is consecrated in the Principality [[Wallachia]] by Prince Mircea the Elder in the town of [[Călimănești]] (now in Romania)
* [[May 21]] – Permission to create the [[University of Cologne]] is granted to the city of [[Köln]] by [[Pope Urban VI]]. By the 21st century it will be the largest university in Germany.
* [[May 22]] – [[Wihwado Retreat]]: In Korea, [[Taejo of Joseon|General Yi Song-gye]] disregards the orders of the Emperor [[U of Goryeo]] to attack China, leads his troops away from Wihwa Island, and leads an attack on the Korean capital, [[Kaesong]].
* [[June 3]] – General Yi Song-gye overthrows the Emperor U of Goryeo and installs U's son, [[Chang of Goryeo]], as the new Emperor.
* [[June 4]] – The [[Merciless Parliament]] ends its session after four months spent primarily in trying officials for treason and further restricting the authority of King Richard II.<ref name="S88"/>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 8]] –[[John of Gaunt]], the uncle of [[Richard II of England]], makes peace with [[Crown of Castile|Castile]] and gives up [[John of Gaunt's claims to the Castilian throne|his claim to the Castilian throne]], by allowing his daughter [[Catherine of Lancaster]] to marry [[Henry III of Castile|Prince Henry]], the eldest son of [[John I of Castile]].
* [[August 5]] – [[Battle of Otterburn]]: A Scottish army, led by [[James Douglas, 2nd Earl of Douglas|James Douglas]], defeats an English army, capturing their leader, [[Henry Percy (Hotspur)|Harry Hotspur]]. Douglas is killed during the battle.
* [[August 27]] – [[Battle of Bileća]]: The [[Bosnians]] check the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] advance.
* [[September 17]] –The title of [[Prince of Asturias]] is created for the heir to the Spanish Crown, initially by King Juan of Castile for his son Enrique.
* [[September 9]] – The [[16th Parliament of King Richard II]], the first since the adjournment of the Merciless Parliament, opens at the [[Barnwell Priory]] in [[Cambridge]] for a five-week session, during which the members bring their complaints against the Lords Appellant.<ref name=Tuck>{{cite journal|last=Tuck |first=J. A. |title=The Cambridge Parliament, 1388 |journal=The English Historical Review |year=1969 |volume=84 |issue=331 |pages=228–232}}</ref>
* [[September 20]] –[[Ghiyas-ud-Din Tughluq II]] succeeds [[Firuz Shah Tughlaq]] as Sultan of [[Delhi Sultanate|Delhi]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 17]] – The Cambridge Parliament adjourns.<ref name=Tuck/>
* [[November 18]] – [[Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür]], the [[List of Northern Yuan khans|Emperor of the Northern Yuan dynasty]] in [[Mongolia]], is killed by the [[Ming dynasty|Ming Chinese]] General [[Jorightu Khan Yesüder]] , who becomes the new Emperor.<ref>Reuven Amitai and David Morgan, ''The Mongol Empire and Its Legacy'' (Leiden: Brill, 2000), p. 293 {{ISBN|9789004119468}}</ref>
* [[December 3]] –Upon reaching the age of 20, [[Charles VI of France]] takes complete control of the government, ending the regency of his uncle, [[Philip the Bold]].
* [[December 12]] – [[Maria of Enghien, Lady of Argos and Nauplia|Maria of Enghien]] sells the [[Lordship of Argos and Nauplia]] to the [[Republic of Venice]].
* [[December 27]] – At [[Hanoi|Thăng Long]], [[Trần Thuận Tông|Tran Ngung]] overthrows and kills [[Trần Phế Đế|Tran Hien]] as [[List of emperors of the Trần dynasty|Emperor]] of [[Đại Việt|Dai Viet]] (now Vietnam).

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Mircea I of Wallachia]] takes control of the region of [[Dobruja]], thus preventing its occupation by the Ottomans.
* [[Petru II of Moldavia|Petru of Moldavia]] receives [[Pokuttya]], as a pawn for a loan to the Polish king.
* The revision of [[Wycliffe's Bible]] is completed by [[John Purvey]], and Wyclif's followers, known as the [[Lollards]], begin to be persecuted in [[Kingdom of England|England]].
* [[September 17]] –The title of [[Prince of Asturias]] is created for the heir to the Spanish Crown, initially by King Juan of Castile for his son Enrique.
* [[Ramesuan (king of Ayutthaya)|Ramesuan]] is reinstated as King of [[Ayutthaya Kingdom|Ayutthaya]] (modern-day southern [[Thailand]]), after dethroning and executing 17-year-old King Thong Lan.
* Goryeo Revolution: General [[Taejo of Joseon|Yi Seong-gye]] begins a four year revolution in [[Goryeo]] (modern-day Korea), after being ordered by King [[U of Goryeo]] to attack the superior Chinese army. King [[U of Goryeo|U]] is forced from power, and replaced by his son [[Chang of Goryeo|Chang]].
* Omar I is succeeded by Sa'id, as King of the [[Kanem Empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] (modern-day east [[Chad]] and [[Nigeria]]). Sa'id is succeeded in the same year by Kade Alunu. Omar and Sa'id are both killed by [[Bilala]] invaders from the west.
* [[Ljubostinja]] Monastery is built in [[Serbia]].</onlyinclude>

1394.events:
=== January–March === 
* [[January 10]] – [[Antonio Venier]], [[List of doges of Venice|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Venice]] appoints Desiderato Lucio as the [[Grand chancellor (Republic of Venice)|Grand Chancellor]]. Lucio serves until April 23, 1396.<ref>Andrea Da Mosto, ''L'Archivio di Stato di Venezia'' (The Archive of the State of Venice) (Rome: Biblioteca d'Arte editrice, 1937)</ref>
* [[January 11]] – The [[List of Neapolitan monarchs|King of Naples]], [[Ladislaus of Naples|Ladislao of Anjou-Durazzo]], grants Neapolitan-controlled Greece to [[Nerio I Acciaioli|Nerio Acciaioli]] as the [[Duchy of Athens]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Setton |first1=Kenneth M.|last2=Hazard|first2=Harry W.|chapter=The Catalans in Greece, 1311–1380; The Catalans and Florentines in Greece, 1380–1462 |title=The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries |url=https://search.library.wisc.edu/digital/ALYOXG7V45YSNF9D |series=[[Wisconsin Collaborative History of the Crusades|The History of the Crusades]] |volume=Three  |year=1975 |publisher=[[The University of Wisconsin Press]] |pages=254|isbn=978-0-299-06670-3}}</ref>
* [[January 15]] – [[Grand Prince Chinan]] of the [[Joseon]] kingdom in [[Korea]], eldest son of King Taejo and heir to the throne, dies at the age of 39 from complications of [[alcoholism]].
* [[January 20]] – In [[India]], [[Ala ud-din Sikandar Shah]] becomes the new [[Delhi Sultanate|Sultan of Delhi]] upon the death of his father, [[Muhammad Shah III]].<ref name=Sen>{{Cite book |last=Sen |first=Sailendra |title=A Textbook of Medieval Indian History |publisher=Primus Books |year=2013 |isbn=978-9-38060-734-4 |pages=100-102}}</ref>
* [[January 28]] – The English Parliament, summoned by King Richard II of England, opens it session after having been summoned on November 13, 1393, and elects Sir [[John Bussy]] as its speaker.
* [[February 1]] – Sikandar Shah is crowned Sultan in a ceremony at [[Delhi]].<ref name=Sen/>
* [[February 28]] – [[Richard II of England]] grants [[Geoffrey Chaucer]] 20 pounds a year for life, for his services as a diplomat and Clerk of The King's Works.<ref>{{cite book|author=Geoffrey Chaucer|title=The Poetical Works of Geoffrey Chaucer|url=https://archive.org/details/poeticalworksge04morrgoog|year=1866|publisher=Bell and Daldy|pages=[https://archive.org/details/poeticalworksge04morrgoog/page/n63 37]}}</ref>
* [[March 6]]  – The English Parliament closes after a 37 day session. Among the acts receiving royal assent are the Money Act (prohibiting the melting of money and the import of foreign money), the Cloths Act ("Every person may make cloth of what length and breadth he will."), and the Exportation of Corn Act (allowing all of the King's subjects to ship grain from the Kingdom.)<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=27}} |pages=27 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[March 8]]  – [[Mahmud Shah II]] becomes the new Sultan of Delhi when his brother, Sikandar, dies after less than seven weeks as monarch.<ref name=Sen/> At the same time, another claimant to the throne, [[Nasir-ud-din Nusrat Shah Tughluq]], proclaims his rule at the royal palace in  [[Firozabad]].<ref>Mohammed Habib, (1970, reprint 2006) ''A Comprehensive History of India'', Volume V, Part 1 (People's Publishing House, 2014, reprint of 1970) {{ISBN|978-81-7007-1617}}, p.624</ref>

=== April–June === 
* [[April 26]]  – Martín Yáñez de la Barbudo of the [[Kingdom of Castile]], master of the [[Order of Alcántara]] military group and leader of [[Battle of Puerto Lope|a crusade]] against the Muslim [[Emirate of Granada]], leads an army across the border into the Emirate and marches toward the capital. Granadan Emir Muhammad VII sends emissaries to [[Henry III of Castile|King Enrique III]] of Castile to complain about the violation of the truce between them, and then mobilizes the Granadan Army to repel the invasion by Barbuda, who is killed in the battle along with hundreds of other Castilians.<ref>{{cite book|last=Harvey|first=L. P.|title=Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=td3tcLWvSNkC|year=1992|publisher=University of Chicago Press|location=[[Chicago]]|pages=226-227|isbn=978-0-226-31962-9}}</ref>
