* [[May 17]]  – By order of King Taejo of the Joseon dyanasty of Korea, who had taken power in 1392 by overthrowing the Goryeo dynasty, the former monarch, [[Gongyang|King Gongyang]], is executed by strangulation at the prison in [[Samcheok]], along with [[Crown Prince Jeongseong]] and the remaining survivors of the Goryeo royal family.<ref>{{cite book|author=Lee Han-woo|date=2018|script-title=ko:이한우의 태종실록 재위 8년: 새로운 해석, 예리한 통찰|trans-title=Hanwoo Lee's 8th year of reign in the Annals of Taejong: New interpretations, sharp insights|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TN9qDwAAQBAJ&dq=%EC%A0%95%EC%84%B1%EA%B5%B0&pg=PT121|language=ko|publisher=Book21 Publishing Group|isbn=9788950976309}}</ref>
* [[June 3]]  – At [[Tunis]], [[Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II|Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz al-Mutawakkil]] becomes the new of Caliph of the [[Hafsid dynasty|Hafsid Sultanate]] of [[Ifriqiya]] in [[North Africa]] (now part of [[Algeria]], [[Tunisia]] and [[Libya]] after the death of his father [[Abu al-Abbas Ahmad II]], 
* [[June 11]]  – The [[Republic of Venice|Venetians]] take over possession of [[Argos, Peloponnese|Argos]], from Despot [[Theodore I Palaiologos]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Manuel II Palaeologus (Emperor of the East)|title=Manuel II Palaeologus: Funeral Oration on His Brother Theodore|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ImpoAAAAMAAJ|year=1985|publisher=Association for Byzantine Research|page=19}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 9]] – [[Philip the Bold]], Duke of Burgundy, and the mentally unstable, [[Charles VI of France|King Charles VI of France]], agree that Philip's first granddaughter would marry King Charles's son and heir apparent, the two-year-old [[Dauphin of France|Dauphin]] [[:fr:Charles de France (1392-1401)|Charles de France]]. The agreement will not achieve a result, in that the Dauphin   and will die at age nine in 1401.<ref>{{cite book |first=Richard |last=Vaughan |title=Philip the Bold: The Formation of the Burgundian State |publisher=The Boydell Press |year=2005 |pages=91-92}}</ref>
* [[July 16]] – The agreement between the [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]] (the cantons of Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz and Unterwaldeden) and the [[Duchy of Austria]], originally signed on April 1, 1389, following the 1386 [[Battle of Sempach]], is extended by amendment.<ref>{{HDS|8871|Battle of Sempach}}</ref>
* [[July 24]] – General [[Paolo Savelli]] of the [[Republic of Venice]] and [[:it:Giovanni Colonna (cardinale XV secolo)|Giovanni Colonna]], Lord of [[Palestrina, Lazio|Palestrina]], attempt a coup d'etat to overthrow the government of Rome and the rule of [[Pope Urban VI]] by attacking [[Capitoline Hill]], but fail to get support.<ref>{{DBI |last=Brunelli |first=Giampiero |title=Savelli, Paolo |url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/paolo-savelli_res-5aed0730-2d10-11e8-8b9a-00271042e8d9_(Dizionario-Biografico) |volume=90}}</ref>
* [[August 2]] &ndash (5th day of the 7th month of [[Meitoku|Meitoku 5]]), the [[Meitoku]] [[Japanese era name|Era]] in [[Japan]] is declared to be at an end because of the misfortune of a [[smallpox]] [[epidemic]], and the [[Ōei]] era begins.
* [[August 15]] – Two months after being captured by [[Sigismund of Luxembourg|King Zsigmond]] of Hungary, the Serbian rebel [[John Horvat|Janos Horvati]], is brutally executed at [[Pécs]] by [[dismemberment]] to avenge the 1387 execution of the former Queen consort of Hungary, [[Elizabeth of Bosnia]].<ref>János Thuróczy, ''Chronicle of the Hungarians'' (Helikon Publishing, 1986) ISBN 963-207-518-8</ref>
* [[September 17]] – King [[Charles VI of France]] orders the expulsion of all Jews from [[Kingdom of France|France]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=Zosa Szajkowski|author2=Soza Szajkowski|title=Jews and the French Revolutions of 1789, 1830 and 1848|url=https://archive.org/details/jewsfrenchrevolu0000szaj|url-access=registration|year=1970|publisher=KTAV Publishing House, Inc.|isbn=978-0-87068-000-7|pages=[https://archive.org/details/jewsfrenchrevolu0000szaj/page/220 220]}}</ref>
* [[September 28]] – Cardinal Pedro Martínez de Luna of the [[Kingdom of Aragon]], opposed to the rule of the Roman [[Pope Urban VI]], is elected at [[Avignon]] as the [[antipope Benedict XIII]] to succeed the antipope [[Antipope Clement VII|Clement VII]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Sir Frederick Dixon Hartland |title=A Chronological Dictionary or Index to the Genealogical Chart of the Royal and Distinguished Houses of Europe |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nEJfAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA14|year=1854|pages=14}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 10]] – At the [[Battle of Karanovasa]],  [[Wallachia]] (now southern [[Romania]]) repels an invasion by the army of the [[Ottoman Empire]] and its [[Serb]] and [[Bulgaria]]n vassals.<ref>{{cite book|author=Vladislav Boskovic|title=Some Notes on Marko Kraljevic (Prince Marko)|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dlPX-0pvkFcC&pg=PP3|date=3 July 2009|publisher=GRIN Verlag|isbn=978-3-640-36481-7|pages=3}}</ref>
* [[October 11]] – The antipope Benedict XIII begins his reign.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/09431c.htm |last=Kirsch |first=Johann Peter |title=Pedro de Luna |encyclopedia=The Catholic Encyclopedia |publisher=Robert Appleton Company |year=1910 }}</ref>
* [[November 29]]  – The capital city of the [[Joseon dynasty]] (in present-day Korea) is moved from Gaegyeong (now [[Gaeseong]]) to Hanseong (now [[Seoul]]).
* [[December 6]] – The [[Astronomical clock, St. Nicholas Church, Stralsund|astronomical clock of St. Nicholas Church in Stralsund]] is finished and signed by [[Nikolaus Lilienfeld]].

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]]s conquer [[Thessaly]] (now eastern Greece) and begin an eight-year siege of [[Constantinople]], in the [[Byzantine Empire]]. In the same year, they begin building the [[Anadoluhisarı]] fortress to defend themselves during the siege.<ref>{{cite book|author=John Cleave|title=Istanbul: City of Two Continents|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kM46fjXmxjMC&pg=PA10|year=2008|publisher=Editions Didier Millet|isbn=978-981-4217-52-1|pages=10}}</ref>
* [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]] retires as ''[[shōgun]]'' of Japan, and is succeeded by his son, [[Ashikaga Yoshimochi]].
* [[Gyeongbokgung]] Palace and the [[Jongmyo]] royal ancestral shrine are built in Hanseong (now [[Seoul]]).
* After the death of Sultan Mahmud II, civil war breaks out in the [[Delhi Sultanate]], splitting the state between east and west.
* [[Battle of Ros-Mhic-Thriúin]]: The Kingdom of [[Leinster]], led by King Art mac Art MacMurrough-Kavanagh, defeats an invading army from England, led by King [[Richard II of England]] and [[Roger Mortimer, 4th Earl of March]].
* [[Stephen I of Moldavia|Ştefan I]] succeeds [[Roman I of Moldavia|Roman I]], as Prince of [[Moldavia]] (now [[Moldova]] and eastern [[Romania]]). 
* Abu Zayyan II succeeds his brother, Abul Hadjdjadj I, as ruler of the [[Abdalwadid]] dynasty in present-day eastern [[Algeria]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Anuario de estudios medievales|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3ShpAAAAMAAJ|year=1990|publisher=Instituto de Historia Medieval de España|page=157}}</ref>
* Abd al-Aziz II succeeds Abu al-Abbas Ahmad II, as ruler of the [[Hafsid dynasty]] in present-day [[Tunisia]].<ref>{{cite book  |last =  Fossier  |first = Robert  |author2=Jacques Verger |author3=Robert Mantran |author4=Catherine Asdracha |author5=Charles de La Roncière |title = Storia del medioevo III: Il tempo delle crisi (1250–1520)  |publisher =  Giulio Einaudi editore
  |year = 1987
  |isbn =  88-06-58404-9
  |page = 368
  }}</ref>
* The [[Allgäuer Brauhaus]] brewery is founded in present-day Germany.<ref>{{cite book|title=Adressbuch ... 8960 Kempten, Allgäu: bearb. nach d. amtl. Unterlagen d. Stadtverwaltung u. eigenen Erhebungen d. Verl. 1986|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l7JjYpo3b4kC|publisher=Bleicher|page=26}}</ref>
* The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of the [[Ming dynasty]] in China orders the Ministry of Public Works to issue a public notice, that every 100 households in the ''lijia'' system are to set aside 2 ''mu'' (1,390 m<sup>2</sup>) of land, for planting [[mulberry]] and [[jujube]] trees.

1360.events:
=== January–March ===
*[[January 11]] – [[Reims campaign]]: The Army of France, led by the regent Charles, breaks the Kingdom of England's siege of [[Reims]], then leads the worn-out soldiers into the  [[Duchy of Burgundy]] to recuperate at [[Tonnerre, Yonne|Tonnerre]].
*[[January 18]] – In Italy, [[Guido Gonzaga]] becomes the new [[Capitano del popolo]] (Captain of the People) and leader of the city-state of [[Mantua]] upon the death of his father, [[Ludovico I Gonzaga]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Voices of the Renaissance: Contemporary Accounts of Daily Life |editor-first=John A. |editor-last=Wagner |publisher=Greenwood |year=2022 |page=285}}</ref>
*[[January]] – The Goryeo Army of Korea launches a counterattack against the invasion by China's Red Turbans, and recaptures Seogyeong only 20 days after it had been lost.<ref>{{cite web |title=조선 수군, 칠천량 해전에서 대패하다|language=ko |publisher=History Net|url=https://contents.history.go.kr/mobile/kc/view.do?levelId=kc_i201500|trans-title=The Red Turban Rebellion:Bandits with Red Headscarves Push into Goryeo 1362 (11th year of King Gongmin).}}</ref>
*[[February 19]] – The French Army relocates to [[Guillen]] on the borders of Burgundy and remains for a month.
*[[February 28]] – [[Qulpa|Qulpa of Borjigin]], [[List of khans of the Golden Horde|Khan of the Golden Horde]], is assassinated after a reign of only six months that followed the murder of his brother, [[Berdi Beg]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Karpov |first=S. P. |title=Načalo smuty v Zolotoj Orde i perevorot Navruza |trans-title=The Onset of Turmoil in the Golden Horde and the Coup of Navruz |journal=Zolotoordynskoe obozrenie (Review of the Golden Horde)|volume=6|year=2018 |pages=528-536}}</ref>
*[[March 10]] – [[Reims campaign]]: [[Philip of Rouvres]], Duke of Burgundy, reaches an agreement with King Edward III of England and [[Edward the Black Prince]] to avoid an invasion of the Duchy in return for the payment of 200,000 gold moutons.<ref>{{cite DNB|last=Hunt |first=William |wstitle=Edward the Black Prince |volume=17 |page=62}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
*[[April 3]] – King Edward III summons the English Parliament to assemble at Westminster on May 15.
*[[April 5]] – King [[Peter I of Cyprus]] is crowned as [[King of Jerusalem]] at a ceremony at [[Lala Mustafa Pasha Mosque|Saint Nicholas Cathedral]] at [[Famagusta]] in [[Cyprus]]. Although King Peter will never visit Jerusalem, and Palestine has been under Muslim control since [[1291]], the Kings of Cyprus have continued to claim the title for 70 years.<ref>{{cite book |first=Peter |last=Lock |title=The Routledge Companion to the Crusades |publisher=Taylor & Francis |year=2013 |page=186}}</ref>
*[[April 6]] – [[Reims campaign]]: King Edward III and the English troops withdraw from [[Saint-Germain-lès-Arpajon]] and march toward the English-ruled territory of [[Brittany]], intending to refresh and to make another attempt to attack Paris later in the year. They stop at the gates of [[Chartres]], hoping to provoke the Dauphin of France, Charles, into leading his outnumbered party into battle.
*[[April 13]] – [[Reims campaign]]: On what is later called "[[Black Monday (1360)|Black Monday]]", a freak [[hail storm]] strikes at Chartres, where the English are leading a siege. The unsheltered English troops are caught in a severe thunderstorm, accompanied by a drop in the temperature and huge hailstones began falling from the sky, killing more than 1,000 of the 10,000 English troops and 6,000 horses in half an hour. King Edward concludes that the strom is a sign from [[God]] to halt the [[Reims campaign]] and to drop all claims to the French throne.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0uq3738Jy9gC|title=The Wars of Edward III: Sources and Interpretations|last=Rogers|first=Clifford J.|date=1999-01-01|publisher=Boydell & Brewer|isbn=9780851156460|language=en}}</ref>
*[[April 14]] – The day after the Black Monday hailstorm, French emissary [[Androin de la Roche]], the Abbot of Clurry, arrives at the English camp and proposes a peace agreement to end the war between England and France.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BmRoOIwLWhsC|title=A Distant Mirror: The Calamitous 14th Century|last=Tuchman|first=Barbara W.|date=2011-08-03|publisher=Random House |isbn=9780307793690|language=en}}</ref> King Edward begins the withdrawal of his army from the gates of [[Chartres]].
*[[April 18]] – [[Jayarjunadeva]] is proclaimed as the ceremonial King of Nepal, though his actual assumption of office waits until the death of his father, [[Jayarajadeva]], in 1361.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Regmi |first=D.R. |url=https://ia902902.us.archive.org/9/items/ancientandmedievalnepalregmir.d._931_W/Ancient%20And%20Medieval%20Nepal%20%20Regmi%20R.D.%20.pdf |title=Ancient and Medieval Nepal |publisher=Prem Printing Press |year=1952 |location=Lucknow|page=155}}</ref>
*[[May 8]] – The [[Treaty of Brétigny]] is drafted by the [[Charles V of France|Dauphin Charles of France]] and six English knights at the [[Hôtel de Sens]], the Dauphin's residence, in [[Paris]] to set terms for the end of the ongoing war between the kingdoms of England and France.<ref name=Sumption>{{cite book |title=The Hundred Years War |volume=II: Trial by Fire |first=Jonathan |last=Sumption |publisher=University of Pennsylvania Press |year=2001 |pages=447-448}}</ref>
*[[May 15]] – The [[English Parliament]] opens at Westminster, but history does not record when it adjourned and what, if any legislation it enacted.
*[[June 7]] – (8th waning of [[Nayon]], [[Burmese calendar|722 ME]]) In what is now [[Myanmar]], the coronation of [[Narathu of Pinya|King Narathu]] the [[Pinya kingdom]] in the Mandalay Region of Myanmar. Narathu has reigned since March 19, 1359 after the death of his father, [[Kyawswa II of Pinya|Kyawswa II]].<ref>{{cite book |title=[[Yazawin Thit]]|author=Twinthin Taikwun Maha Sithu |editor=Myint Swe |editor2=Kyaw Win |editor3=Thein Hlaing |publisher=Ya-Pyei Publishing |location=Yangon |orig-year=1798 |year=2012 |edition=2nd printing |language=my |volume=1 |page=170 }}</ref>
*[[June 14]] – [[John II of France|King Jean II of France]], who has been held as a prisoner of war in England since 1356, signs the Treaty of Brétigny at a banquet attended by England's King [[Edward III]], [[Edward the Black Prince|Edward, Prince of Wales]], and other French prisoners of war. Under the treaty, King Edward obtains 19 territories on the French mainland in return for renouncing any claims to the French throne, while King Jean obligates France to pay a ransom of 3,000,000 gold [[écu]] coins for the release of himself and the other French prisoners, with the condition that he will be allowed to return to France after the first one million écus is paid and send two of his sons to England as hostages, along with more than 40 French citizens.<ref name=Sumption/>
*[[June 22]] – Russian prince [[Dmitry of Suzdal|Dmitry Konstantinovich]] is installed by the Khan of the Golden Horde as the new [[Grand Prince of Vladimir]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Middleton |first1=John |title=World Monarchies and Dynasties |date=2015 |publisher=Routledge |page=806 |isbn=978-1-317-45158-7 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/World_Monarchies_and_Dynasties/R63ACQAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref>
*[[June 30]] – King Jean II of France is released from the [[Tower of London]] after having been taken as a prisoner of war since 1356, and is feted with a farewell dinner at [[Eltham Palace]], hosted by [[Philippa of Hainault|Queen consort Philippa]], then begins his journey back to France.<ref name=Stanley/>
*[[June]] – 
**[[Khiḍr Khan]] is enthroned as the [[List of khans of the Golden Horde|Khan of the Golden Horde]]
**[[Valdemar IV Atterdag]] attacks [[Skåne]] and conquers  [[Lindholmen Castle]].<ref name="Chronology of Sweden. worldtimeline.info">Chronology of Sweden". worldtimeline.info. Retrieved June 15, 2023.</ref>

=== July–September ===
*[[July 8]] – King Jean II of France returns to the continent after four years as a prisoner of war in England, landing at [[Calais]], in order to raise the 3,000,000 gold crown ransom owed to England under the terms of the Treaty of Brétigny. To take his place, Jean's son [[Louis I of Anjou]] boards the English ship to be held as a hostage in England.<ref name=Stanley>{{cite book|last=Stanley |first=Arthur Penrhyn |title=Historical Memorials of Canterbury |location=London |publisher=J. M. Dent & Co. |year=1906 |pages=234, 276–279}}</ref> 
*[[July 13]] – (27 [[Shaban]] [[Islamic calendar|761 AH]]) Sultan [[Ismail II of Granada]] is assassinated, less than a year after he ascended the throne on August 23, 1359.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last=Vidal Castro|first=Francisco |ref={{harvid|Vidal Castro: Ismail II}} |title=Ismail II|encyclopedia=Diccionario Biográfico electrónico|publisher=[[Real Academia de la Historia]]|url=http://dbe.rah.es/biografias/16900/ismail-ii|language=es}}</ref> He is succeeded by [[Muhammad VI of Granada|Muhammad VI]] of the [[Nasrid dynasty]].
*[[August 10]] – Peace is concluded between Sweden and Denmark with the arbitration in Helsingborg. [[Magnus IV Eriksson]] cedes the Scanian lands except northern Halland to Denmark. In return, [[Valdemar IV Atterdag]] must help Magnus against his domestic enemies.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Geschichte_von_R%C3%BCgen_und_Pommern/32MPAAAAQAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22August+1360%22+helsingborg&pg=PA434&printsec=frontcover|first=Friedrich Wilhelm |last=Barthold |title=Geschichte von Rügen und Pommern |trans-title= |volume=3 |publisher=F. Perthes|year=1834|page=434|quote=Ehe noch der Frieden zu Helsingborg (10. August 1360) diese Umfehe der Dinge und die Billigung derselben und durch Albrecht von Mecklenburg, den Echwager des unwurbigen Schwedenkonigs, zu verburgen sebien, sehen wie die Rathsboten der wendischen Stadte in geipanntze Ermartung bein Valdemar in Kopenhagen. (Even before the Peace of Helsingborg (August 10, 1360)—which was to guarantee this turn of events and its endorsement by Albert of Mecklenburg, the unworthy Swedish king’s brother-in-law, could be concluded, we see the envoys of the Wendish towns awaiting Valdemar in Copenhagen in a state of tense anticipation.)}}</ref><ref>Mikael Nordberg, I kung Magnus tid (In the Times of King Magnus) ISBN 91-1-952122-7</ref>
* [[September 26]] – [[Philip of Rouvres]], [[Duke of Burgundy]], becomes the Count of Auvergne upon the death of his mother, the Queen consort [[Joan I of Auvergne]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 24]] – The [[Treaty of Brétigny]] is ratified at [[Calais]], marking the end of the first phase of the [[Hundred Years' War]]. Under its terms, [[Edward III of England]] gives up his claim to the French throne, and releases King [[John II of France]] in return for French land, including [[Calais]] and [[Gascony]].<ref>Sumption 2001, p. 448.</ref>
* [[November 20]] – King Edward III summons the English Parliament, directing the members of the Lords and Commons to assemble at Westminster on January 24.
* [[December 5]] – The [[French franc]], worth one ''[[livre tournois]]'' and consisting of 3.73 grams of gold, is minted for the first time as the ''[[:fr:franc à cheval|franc à cheval]]'' after King Jean of France returns from captivity, and is designed initially to paid the ransom of three million gold crowns owed by France to England. The franc will as France's monetary unit for the next 638 years until it is phased out in favor of the [[euro]] by the [[European Community]] on December 31, 1998.<ref>{{cite book|author=L. Ciani|title=Les Monnaies Royales Françaises de Hugues Capet à Louis XVI avec indication de leur valeur actuelle |publisher=B. Hoffman's|year=1926|pages=77, 92}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Red Turban Rebellions]]: [[Chen Youliang]] murders [[Xu Shouhui]] and proclaims himself the emperor of [[Chen Han|Han]] in [[Wuchang]] before unsuccessfully attempting to capture [[Nanjing]] from [[Zhu Yuanzhang]].<ref name=Cambridge>{{cite book |last = Twitchett|first = Denis|title = The Cambridge History of China, Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1 |year = 1998 |publisher = [[Cambridge University Press]] |location = Cambridge |isbn = 9780521243322 |page=41}}</ref>
* [[Shah Shoja Mozaffari|Shah Shuja]] regains rule of the [[Muzaffarids (Iran)|Muzaffarid]] tribe in [[Persia]] after the death of his brother, Shah Mahmud.
* Earliest known [[Kırkpınar]] [[oil wrestling]] tournament in the [[Ottoman Empire]], which will still be staged into the 21st century.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/2018/07/13/historical-kirkpinar-oil-wrestling-festival-kicks-off-in-northwestern-turkey|title=Historical Kırkpınar oil wrestling festival kicks off in northwestern Turkey|website=DailySabah|date=2018-07-13|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>

1400.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 4]] – The [[Epiphany Rising]] begins in [[England]] against [[Henry IV of England|King Henry IV]] by nobles planning to restore [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] to the throne, and is quickly crushed.  [[Ralph Lumley, 1st Baron Lumley|Baron Lumley]] dies after attempting to seize [[Cirencester]]. The [[John Montacute, 3rd Earl of Salisbury|Earl of Salisbury]] and the [[Thomas Holland, 1st Duke of Surrey|Earl of Kent]] are captured and beheaded on January 7. [[Thomas Blount (died 1400)|Sir Thomas Blount]] is hanged, drawn and quartered at [[Oxford]] on January 12. [[Thomas le Despenser, 1st Earl of Gloucester]] is captured and executed by a mob in [[Bristol]] on January 13. The [[John Holland, 1st Duke of Exeter|Earl of Huntingdon]] is beheaded at [[Pleshey]] on January 16. 
* [[February 14]] – The deposed [[Richard II of England]] dies by means unknown in [[Pontefract Castle]]. It is likely that King [[Henry IV of England|Henry IV]] ordered his death by starvation, to prevent further uprisings.
* [[February]] – [[Henry Percy (Hotspur)]] leads English incursions into [[Kingdom of Scotland|Scotland]].
* [[March 23]] – Five-year-old [[Trần Thiếu Đế]] is forced to abdicate as ruler of [[Đại Việt]] (modern-day [[Vietnam]]), in favour of his maternal grandfather and court official [[Hồ Quý Ly]], ending the [[Trần dynasty]] after 175 years and starting the [[Hồ dynasty]]. Hồ Quý Ly subsequently changes the country's name to Đại Ngu.

=== April–June===
* [[April 21]] – Sir [[Thomas Percy, 1st Earl of Worcester]], resigns as [[England]]'s [[Admiral of the North and West]] to join the resistance against [[Henry IV of England|King Henry IV]]. The office will remain vacant for more than six years. Percy will be beheaded in 1403 after his defeat in the [[Battle of Shrewsbury]].
* [[April 23]] – In what is now [[Romania]], [[Alexander I of Moldavia|Alexandru cel Bun]] (Alexander the Good) is installed as the new [[List of monarchs of Moldavia|Prince (Voivode)]] of [[Moldavia]] by [[Mircea the Elder]], the Voivode of [[Wallachia]], after Mircea removes the reigning monarch, [[Iuga of Moldavia|Prince Iuga]].
* [[April 25]] – [[Jingnan campaign]]: In the [[Shandong]] province of Ming dynasty China, [[Zhu Di]], Prince of Yan, defeats the Imperial forces of General [[Li Jinglong]] in the two-day Battle of Baigou River, by taking advantage of the chaos that results when a gust of wind breaks the staff of General Li's flag of battle. The Yan forces capture 100,000 of the Imperial soldiers as prisoners and Li and the others retreat to [[Jinan]]. 
* [[April]] – King [[Swa Saw Ke]], of [[Ava Kingdom|Ava]], the largest kingdom in Burma, dies after a reign of 33 years and is succeeded by his son, [[Tarabya of Ava|King Tarabya]], who reigns less than seven months before being assassinated.
* [[May 22]] – Meeting in [[Frankfurt]], three of the prince-electors of the [[Holy Roman Empire]] ([[Rupert, King of Germany|Rupert, elector of the Palatinate]], [[Rudolf III, Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg]], elector of Saxony, and [[Jobst of Moravia]], elector of Brandenburg) meet in [[May 1400 imperial election|an attempt to replace the Emperor]], [[Wenceslaus, King of the Romans]] because of his failure to stamp out civil unrest or to resolve the Western Schism. They select [[Frederick I, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg]] as the replacement for Wenceslaus. 
* [[June 5]] – Duke Frederick I of Brunswick-Lüneburg is assassinated after being identified as a rival to Wenceslaus, Holy Roman Emperor. Frederick, on his way back from a May 22 meeting of the prince-electors, is ambushed by a party of men led by [[Henry VII, Count of Waldeck|Count Henry of Waldeck]] while passing through the village of [[Kleinenglis]] in the [[Principality of Waldeck and Pyrmont]] (now part of the German state of [[Hesse]], near [[Borken, Hesse|Borken]]).

=== July–September ===
* [[July 7]] – [[Sir John Swinton, 14th of that Ilk|Sir John Swinton]], an envoy of [[Robert III of Scotland|King Robert III of Scotland]], crosses the border into England along with 20 knights, after being given a [[safe conduct|writ of safe conduct]] by [[Henry IV of England|King Henry IV]] to allow their travel to negotiate during the standoff between the two British kingdoms between phases of the [[Hundred Years' War]]. 
* [[July 26]] – [[Jagiellonian University]] is re-established in [[Kraków]] by order of [[Władysław II Jagiełło|King Władysław II]], with the creation of the Faculty of Theology at what is then called the Kraków Academy. The restoration is partially financed by the sale of jewelry owned by the King's late wife, [[Jadwiga of Poland|Queen Jadwiga]], who had died in [[1399]].
* [[August 6]] – Writing from [[Newcastle upon Tyne]] to [[Scotland]]'s [[Robert III of Scotland|King Robert III]], England's [[Henry IV of England|King Henry IV]] sends a demand that King Robert meet him "on Monday the 23rd of this present month of August, at [[Edinburgh]], where, for this reason and for the peace of tranquility of the realms of England and Scotland, we intend to be," for Robert "to perform the obligation which you owe us" as "overlords of Scotland and of its kings in all temporal matters pertaining to them..."  King Henry warns that "considering the effusion of Christian blood and other dangers and losses which may occur if you do not comply with our wishes, you will be present to render us homage and take the oath of fealty."  <ref name=Flemming>Jessie H. Flemming, [https://books.google.com/books?id=kYLSAAAAMAAJ&dq=edinburgh+august+1400&pg=PA6 ''England Under the Lancastrians''] (Longman's, Green and Co., 1921) pp.5-6</ref>
* [[August 14]] – King Henry IV leads the English Army into [[Scotland]], after receiving no answer from Scotland's King Robert III to his August 6 demand. The troops reach [[Haddington, East Lothian]] the next day and at [[Leith]], on the outskirts of [[Edinburgh]], by August 18. As historian  [[James Hamilton Wylie]] will note almost 500 years later, "the walls of Edinburgh did not fall before this ram's-horn blast, and August 23rd came and went without the required homage or recognition."<ref>James Hamilton Wylie, ''History of England Under Henry the Fourth'' (Longmans, Green and Co., 1884) p.138</ref> 
* [[August 20]] – Meeting at the [[Lahneck Castle]] in what is now the German state [[Rhineland-Palatinate]], the princes of the German states vote to depose the Holy Roman Emperor, [[Wenceslaus, King of the Romans|Wenceslaus]], due to his weak leadership and mental illnesses.
* [[August 21]] – [[Rupert, King of Germany|Rupert, Count Palatine of the Rhine]], is elected as [[King of the Romans]].
* [[August 29]] – Having failed in his expedition to receive a pledge of [[fealty]] from the King of Scotland, King Henry IV crosses back into England.<ref name=Flemming/> 
* [[September 16]] – [[Owain Glyndŵr]] is proclaimed [[Prince of Wales]] by his followers, and begins attacking [[Kingdom of England|English]] strongholds in northeast [[Wales]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 7]] – [[Timur|Tamerlane]], the Mongol conqueror, stops between [[Malatya]] and [[Aleppo]] at the Turkish garrison in [[Besni|Behesna]]. According to author Peter Purton, the garrison "had the temerity to shoot a catapult ball at Timur which rolled into his tent. Setting up his own battery of 20 machines, it is said that the first shot hit and destroyed the offending weapon. Treating this as a good omen, the attack was launched, the towers mined... and the place surrendered."<ref>Peter Purton, ''A History of the Late Medieval Siege, 1200-1500'' (Boydell & Brewer, 2009) p.186</ref>
* [[October 29]] – [[Jingnan campaign]]: In China, Prince [[Zhu Di]] of Yan expands his conquests with the capture of [[Cangzhou]] in [[Heibei]] province.
* [[October 30]] – (11 [[Rabi' al-Awwal|Rabi' I]] 803 AH) Tamerlane begins the [[Sack of Aleppo (1400)|destruction of the Syrian city]] of [[Aleppo]]<ref>Alphonse de Lamartine, ''History of Turkey'' (translated from the French) (D. Appleton and Company, 1855) p.320</ref> overwhelming the [[Mamluk Sultanate]] defenders. 
* [[November 2]] – The Mamluk Sultanate surrenders the city of Aleppo and Tamerlane's Army massacres many of the inhabitants.<ref>Rebecca Joyce Frey, ''Genocide and International Justice'' (Facts On File, 2009) p.188</ref>
* [[November 25]] – (9th waxing of Nadaw, [[Burmese calendar|730 ME]]) [[Minkhaung I]] becomes the new King of Ava, the largest kingdom in what is now northern [[Myanmar]], after a battle for power that follows the assassination of the erratic [[Tarabya of Ava|King Tarabya]].
* [[December 21]] – [[Manuel II Palaiologos]] becomes the only [[Byzantine Emperor]] ever to visit England, and is greeted at [[Blackheath, London|Blackheath]] by [[Henry IV of England|King Henry IV]], who hosts the Emperor at [[Eltham Palace]] during the Christmas holiday.<ref>"Henry IV", by T. F. Tout, in ''Dictionary of National Biography'', ed. by Leslie Stephen and Sidney Lee (The Macmillan Company, 1908) p.488</ref>
* [[December 25]] – In China, the [[Jingnan campaign]] of Prince [[Zhu Di]] of Yan suffers a serious reversal at the Battle of Dongchang as Imperial General Sheng Yong, replacement of [[Li Jinglong]], encircles the Yan forces. Yan Army General [[Zhang Yu (general)|Zhang Yu]] is killed, but Zhu Di is able to escape to the northern capital at [[Beijing]] and regroups his forces for a second attack to take place in February.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Timur]] defeats both the [[Ottoman Empire]] and the [[Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo)|Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt]], to capture the city of [[Damascus]] in present-day [[Syria]]. Much of the city's inhabitants are subsequently massacred by Timur's troops.
* [[Timur]] conquers the [[Kara Koyunlu|Empire of The Black Sheep Turkomans]], in present-day [[Azerbaijan]], and the [[Jalayirids|Jalayirid dynasty]] in present-day [[Iraq]]. Black Sheep ruler [[Qara Yusuf]] and Jalayirid Sultan [[Ahmad (Jalayirids)|Ahmad]] flee, and take refuge with the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] Sultan [[Bayezid I]].
* In modern-day [[Korea]], King [[Jeongjong of Joseon]] abdicates in fear of an attack by his ambitious younger brother, [[Taejong of Joseon|Taejong]]. Taejong succeeds to the throne.
* Prince [[Parameswara (sultan)|Parameswara]] establishes the [[Malacca Sultanate]], in present-day western [[Malaysia]] and northern [[Sumatra]].
* Hananchi succeeds Min as King of [[Hokuzan]], in modern-day north [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]], [[Japan]].
* [[Wallachia]] (modern-day southern [[Romania]]) resists an invasion by the [[Ottoman Turks|Ottomans]].
* A Wallachian army captures [[Iuga of Moldavia|Iuga]], and makes [[Alexander I of Moldavia|Alexandru cel Bun]] the Prince of [[Moldavia]].
* The [[Kingdom of Kongo]] begins.
*  The [[Haast's eagle]] and [[Moa]] are both driven to extinction by [[Māori people|Māori]] hunters.
* The [[Mississippian culture]] starts to decline.
* Europe is reported to have around 52 million inhabitants.
* The [[House of Medici]] becomes powerful in [[Florence]].
* [[Newcastle upon Tyne]] is created a [[county corporate]], by [[Henry IV of England]].
* [[Jean Froissart]] completes his ''[[Froissart's Chronicles|Chronicles]]'', detailing the events of the 14th Century in France.</onlyinclude>

1398.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 6]] – In [[Amberg]], [[Rupert, King of the Romans|Ruprecht III "the Righteous"]] of the [[House of Wittelsbach]] becomes the new [[List of counts palatine of the Rhine|Elector of the Palatinate]] within the [[Holy Roman Empire]] upon the death of his father, [[Rupert II, Elector Palatine|Ruprecht II "the Hard"]].<ref>{{cite book |title=A House Divided: Wittelsbach Confessional Court Cultures in the Holy Roman Empire, c.1550-1650 |first=Andrew L. |last=Thomas |publisher=Brill |year=2010 }}</ref>
* [[January 31]] – The 24th English Parliament of [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] is dissolved after having met since September 17. The King gives royal assent to numerous laws, including the [[Treason Act 1397]], providing for new definitions of treason (compassing the death of the King, making war against the King within the realm, attempting to repeal any judgments made by parliament convicting "certain traitors", or attempting to repeal the Treason Act itself.<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=27}} |pages=27 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[January]] – The [[Dao Ganmeng rebellion]] in the Chinese vassal state of [[Möng Mao]],started in December by Dao Genmeng, is brought to an end in what is now [[Myanmar]] two months after [[:zh:刀干孟|Dao Ganmeng]]'s takeover. With the intervention of the Chinese Empire, led by the Ming dynasty [[Hongwu Emperor|Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang]], the deposed ruler [[:uk:Солонпа|Si Lunfa]] is restored to leadership.<ref>{{Citation|last=Fernquest|first=John|title=Crucible of War: Burma and the Ming in the Tai Frontier Zone (1382-1454)|year=2006|pages=46–49}}</ref>
* [[February 20]] – The vicar John de Aston of Colston Bassett is released from incarceration at [[Fleet Prison]] in England by order of King Richard II upon the payment of [[mainprise]] or bail.<ref>{{cite journal |first=H. M. |last=Colvin |author-link=Howard Colvin |editor-first=Frederick |editor-last=Williamson |title=The External History of Dale Abbey |url=https://archaeologydataservice.ac.uk/archiveDS/archiveDownload?t=arch-2300-1/dissemination/pdf/062/DAJ_v062_1941_058-087.pdf |journal=Journal of the Derbyshire Archaeological and Natural History Society |volume=62 |pages=81–82 |year=1941}}</ref>
* [[March 15]] – [[Trần Thuận Tông]] is forced to abdicate as ruler of the [[Trần dynasty]] in modern-day [[Vietnam]], in favour of his three-year-old son [[Trần Thiếu Đế]].
* [[March 17]] – The [[Teutonic Knights]] resume their attack on [[Lithuania]] as a fleet of 84 ships, 4,000 men and 400 horses departs from [[Danzig]] toward [[Gotland]], and arrive on March 21.<ref name=Schmandt>{{Cite journal |last=Schmandt |first=Raymond H. |date=December 1975 |title=The Gotland campaign of the Teutonic Knights, 1398–1408 |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01629777500000281 |journal=Journal of Baltic Studies |language=en |volume=6 |issue=4 |pages=247–258 |doi=10.1080/01629777500000281 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* [[March 19]] – [[Abu Said Uthman III]] succeeds his older brother [[Abdallah ibn Ahmad II]] as the ruler of the [[Marinid dynasty]] in modern-day [[Morocco]], reigning until his death in [[1420]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Abun Nasr |first=J.M. |year=1987 |title=A History of the Maghrib in the Islamic period |publisher=Cambridge University Press}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 5]] – The Teutonic Knights conquer the island of [[Gotland]], near [[Sweden]], which has previously been run by the piratical [[Victual Brothers]]. In the agreement of surrender, the city of [[Visby]] and the entire island are ceded to Johan of Mecklenburg, and merchants from the Hanseatic League are allowed free trade. In addition, the Knights receive the opportunity to clear all known pirates and other enemies from Gotland.<ref>{{Cite web |website=Medievalists.net |date=November 2, 2019 |title=The Occupation of Gotland by the Teutonic Knights, 1398-1408 |url=https://www.medievalists.net/2019/11/the-occupation-of-gotland-by-the-teutonic-knights-1398-1408/}}</ref> 
* [[May 10]] – [[Stephen (honorific)|Stephen]] [[Ostoja of Bosnia|Ostoja]] is enthroned as the new [[List of rulers of medieval Bosnia|King of Bosnia]] after [[Helen of Bosnia|Queen Helen]] is deposed.<ref>{{citation|title=Jelena|work=Kotromanići|last=Ćošković|first=Pejo|publisher=Miroslav Krleža Institute of Lexicography|year=2005|language=sh|url=https://hbl.lzmk.hr/clanak/137}}</ref>
* [[May 11]] – The Treaty of Pavia is signed between the [[Republic of Florence]] and the [[Duchy of Milan]] to end the [[Florentine–Milanese Wars#Second or Mantuan War (1397–1398)|Mantuan War]] after 14 months.<ref>{{cite book |last = Kohl |first = Benjamin G. |title = Padua under the Carrara, 1318–1405 |year = 1998 |publisher = Johns Hopkins University Press |location = Baltimore |pages=313–314 | isbn = 0-8018-5703-1| url=https://archive.org/details/paduaundercarrar0000kohl/}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last = Najemy |first = John M. |title = A History of Florence 1200–1575 |year = 2006 |publisher = Blackwell Publishing |location = Oxford |pages=193 |isbn = 978-1-4051-1954-2}}Najemy 2006, p. 193  Kohl 1998, pp. 313–314</ref>
* [[May 22]] – The Assembly of Paris begins, as Catholic clergy and bishops discuss whether withdraw obedience from the rival popes, [[Pope Boniface IX|Boniface IX]] in Rome and the [[antipope]] [[antipope Benedict XIII|Benedict XIII]] at [[Avignon]] withdrawing the right of either of the popes to bestow [[benefice]]s to officials in France in return for past or future services.
* [[June 25]] – [[Jianwen Emperor|Zhu Yunwen]] succeeds his grandfather, [[Hongwu Emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]], as [[List of emperors of the Ming dynasty|Emperor Ming dynasty China]], bringing an end to the Hongwu Era and beginning the Jianwen era.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Langlois |first=John D |title=The Cambridge History of China Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1988 |isbn=0521243327 |editor-last=Mote |editor-first=Frederick W. |location=Cambridge |chapter=The Hung-wu reign, 1368–1398 |page=181 |editor-last2=Twitchett |editor-first2=Denis C.}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 14]] – In what is now central [[Turkey]], [[Kadi Burhan al-Din]], the vizier of and regent for the [[Eretnid dynasty|Sultanate of Eretnia]], on a campaign to conquer the [[Emirate of Erzincan]] (eastern Turkey and western Armenia) and capture its Emir [[Mutahharten]], is killed in battle by [[Qara Yuluk Uthman Beg]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shukurov |first1=Rustam |title=Between Peace and Hostility: Trebizond and the Pontic Turkish Periphery in the Fourteenth Century |journal=Mediterranean Historical Review |date=June 1994 |volume=9 |pages=27–37|publisher=Routledge |doi=10.1080/09518969408569663}}</ref>
* [[July 22]] – The first ships to complete passage on the {{convert|60|mi}} long [[Stecknitz Canal]] in Germany arrive at [[Lübeck]], with 30 barges carrying salt from [[Lüneburg]]. The canal, completed after seven years between the rivers [[Elbe]] and [[Trave]], is one of the earliest navigable [[summit level canal]]s in the world.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Seas and Waterways of the World: An Encyclopedia of History, Uses, and Issues |first1=John |last1=Zumerchik |first2=Steven Laurence |last2=Danver |volume=1 |publisher=[[ABC-CLIO]] |year=2010 |isbn=9781851097111 |pages=118, 121 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IBKoUXrF5p0C&pg=PR132 |accessdate=27 May 2016}}</ref>
* [[July 27]] – Following the consensus of the Assembly of Paris of that had begun meeting on May 11, King [[Charles V of France]] signs an ordinance withdrawing obedience to both the French [[Antipope Benedict XIII|Avignon pope Benedict XIII]] and to Rome's [[Pope Boniface IX]] to issue [[benefice]]s to persons who offer services to the Catholic Church.<ref>{{cite book |last=Blumenfeld-Kosinski |first=Renate |year=2009 |chapter=The Conceptualization and Imagery of the Great Schism |editor-last1=Rollo-Koster |editor-first1=Joëlle |editor-link1=Joëlle Rollo-Koster |editor-last2=Izbicki |editor-first2=Thomas M. |title=A Companion to the Great Western Schism (1378–1417) |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mgnaIRVSx44C&pg=PA124 |location=Leiden |publisher=Brill Publishers |pages=124–125 |isbn=978-90-04-16277-8}}</ref> An army led by [[Geoffrey Boucicaut]] occupies [[Avignon]], and starts a five-year siege of the [[Palais des Papes|papal palace]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Sumption |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Sumption, Lord Sumption |year=2009 |title=The Hundred Years War, Volume III: Divided Houses |publisher=Faber and Faber |page=845 |isbn=978-0-571-24012-8}}</ref>
* [[August 21]] – [[Martin of Aragon|King Martin of Aragon]], and ruler of Valencia, Majorca and Barcelona, begins the [[Bona crusade]] of Christians against the Muslims of [[Tunisia]] and departs from the island of [[Menorca]] with 13 galleys, 77 warships and 7,500 crusaders toward the [[Hafsid dynasty|Harsid Kingdom]], ruled by the Caliph [[Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II]].<ref name=Paesi>{{Citation|chapter=Paesi Evoluti e Paesi |chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/j.ctt1vxm84x.9 |title=A che ora si mangia? |pages=45–61 |publisher=Quodlibet|doi=10.2307/j.ctt1vxm84x.9 | isbn=978-88-229-0906-0|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* [[September 2]] – The Bona crusaders from Spain sack the Algerian village of [[Crusade of Tedelis|Tedelis]] in the [[Kingdom of Tlemcen]], killing around 1,000 people, before abandoning the African crusade and returning to defend the siege of [[Avignon]] at France.<ref name=Paesi/>
* [[September 9]] – [[Janus, King of Cyprus|Janus of the House of Poitiers-Lusignan]] becomes the new [[Kingdom of Cyprus#List of monarchs of Cyprus|King of Cyprus]] upon the death of his father, [[James I of Cyprus|King Jacques I]], who had reigned since 1382.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=The Kingdom of Cyprus |first=Harry |last=Luke |title=A History of the Crusades: The fourteenth and fifteenth centuries |volume=III |editor-first=Kenneth Meyer |editor-last=Setton |publisher=University of Wisconsin Press |year=1975|pages=370–371}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cypnet.co.uk/ncyprus/history/lusignan/4janus.htm |title=Cyprus History: Lusignan Period - the Reign of Janus }}</ref>
* [[September 16]] – King [[Richard II of England]] exiles his cousin Henry Bolingbroke (the future [[Henry IV of England]]) for 10 years, in order to end Henry's feud with [[Thomas de Mowbray, 1st Duke of Norfolk]], who is also exiled.<ref>{{cite ODNB  |last= Horrox |date=2004 |first=Rosemary |title=Edward, second duke of York (c. 1373–1415) |url=http://www.oxforddnb.com/view/article/22356 |edition=online }}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 12]] – The [[Treaty of Salynas]] is signed by [[Vytautas]], [[Grand Duke of Lithuania]], and Konrad von Jungingen, [[Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights]], in an attempt to cede [[Samogitia]] to the Knights.
* [[October 14]] – King [[Taejo of Joseon]] abdicates the throne of the [[Joseon dynasty]] in modern-day [[Korea]], following the murder of his heir Yi Bangsuk, during a coup by Yi's older half-brother, [[Taejong of Joseon|Yi Bang-won]], in The First Strife Of Princes. Taejo's eldest son [[Jeongjong of Joseon|Jeongjong]] succeeds to the throne.
* [[November 11]] – [[Janus of Cyprus|Janus]] succeeds his father, [[James I of Cyprus|James I]], as King of [[Cyprus]] and claimant to the throne of [[Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia|Armenian Cilicia]].
* [[December 17]] – [[Timur]] defeats the last ruler of the [[Delhi Sultanate]], which has been weakened after four years of civil war. Following his victory, Timur's [[Islamic]] troops sack the city of [[Delhi]], and proceed to massacre hundreds of thousands of the state's [[Hindu]] inhabitants.

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Kingdom of Singapura]] falls, after being invaded by the [[Majapahit]] Empire.
* [[Bunei (Ryukyu)|Bunei]] succeeds his father, [[Satto]], as King of [[Chūzan]] (modern-day central [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]], [[Japan]]).
* [[Glendalough]] [[monastery]] in [[Wicklow]], [[Ireland]] is destroyed by [[England|English]] troops.
* [[Ferapontov Monastery]] is founded in modern-day northwest [[Russia]] by [[Therapont of Belozersk]].
* The [[Munmyo]] [[Confucian]] shrine and [[Sungkyunkwan University]] are founded in modern-day [[Seoul]].
* [[Mount Grace Priory]] is established in [[Yorkshire]], [[Kingdom of England|England]].
* According to [[fringe theory|fringe theorists]], the [[Scotland|Scottish]] explorer [[Henry I Sinclair, Earl of Orkney]], reaches [[North America]].</onlyinclude>

1351.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* [[January 14]] – [[Edward III of England]] institutes the [[Treason Act 1351]], defining treason in English law. It remains unrepealed into the 21st century.<ref>Blackstone, William; Stewart, James (1839). The Rights of Persons, According to the Text of Blackstone: Incorporating the Alterations Down to the Present Time. p. 77.</ref><ref>The Treason Act 1351 legislation.gov.uk.</ref>
* [[February]] – Enactments by the [[Parliament of England]]:
** The [[Statute of Labourers 1351|Statute of Labourers]] deals with a labour shortage caused by the [[Black Death]].
** [[Statute of Provisors]] prevents the Pope from appointing clergy to English [[benefice]]s.<ref name=CBH>{{cite book|last1=Palmer|first1=Alan|author2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=104–106|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[March 4]] – The [[Ayutthaya Kingdom]] is established by King [[Uthong]] (Ramathibodi I) in modern-day [[Thailand]].<ref>Baker, Chris; Phongpaichit, Pasuk (11 May 2017). A History of Ayutthaya: Siam in the Early Modern World (Kindle ed.). Cambridge University Press. p. 43.</ref> He begins to propagate [[Theravada Buddhism]] as the state religion.
* [[March 23]] – [[Firuz Shah Tughlaq]] succeeds Mohammad Tughlaq as ruler of the [[Delhi Sultanate]]. At this time, the [[Samma dynasty]] in [[Sindh]] (part of modern-day Pakistan) breaks away from the Sultanate.
* [[March 26]] – [[War of the Breton Succession]]: [[Combat of the Thirty]] – Thirty chosen [[knight]]s each, from the Kingdoms of France and [[Kingdom of England|England]], fight to determine who will rule the [[Duchy of Brittany]]; a Franco-Breton victory is assured by the [[squire]] Guillaume de Montauban.
*[[April 1]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: [[Battle of Saintes]]. – The French are defeated by the English.<ref>Wagner, John A. (2006). "Saintes, Battle of (1351)". Encyclopedia of the Hundred Years War. Woodbridge, Suffolk: Greenwood. ISBN 978-0313327360. p. 275.</ref>
* [[April 8]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: Battle of Taillebourg. – The French are defeated by the English.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last=Rickard|first=J.|date=2000-10-03|title=Battle of Taillebourg, 8 April 1351|url=http://www.historyofwar.org/articles/battles_taillebourg.html|encyclopedia=Military History Encyclopedia on the Web|access-date=2015-03-26}}</ref>
* [[May 1]] – [[Canton of Zürich|Zürich]] joins the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]].
* [[November 26]] – [[Emperor Sukō]] abdicates as 3rd Emperor of the [[Northern Court]] of Japan.

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Red Turban Rebellions]] break out in China, leading to permanent weakening of the [[Mongolia]]n-run [[Yuan dynasty]].
* King [[Gongmin of Goryeo|Gongmin]] ascends the throne in [[Goryeo]].
* The region of [[Vantaa]] in Finland is first mentioned (as ''Helsinge'').</onlyinclude>

1374.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 17]] – 
**In Italy, at [[Padua]], [[:it:Alvise Forzatè|Alvise Forzatè]] is arrested on charges of treason and conspiracy with his nephew Filippo Forzate, in [[1373]], to assassinate [[Francesco I da Carrara]], Lord of Padua.<ref>{{DBI |title=Forzatè, Alvise |author=Laura Gaffuri|year=1997 |volume=9}}</ref> The two men are beheaded one week later on January 24.
**[[Frederick the Simple|King Federico of Sicily]] swears his allegiance to [[Pope Gregory XI]] as part of the [[Treaty of Villeneuve]] after the Pope's recognition of him as the sovereign.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/federico-iv-d-aragona-re-di-sicilia-detto-il-semplice_(Dizionario-Biografico)/ |title=Federico IV d'Aragona, re di Sicilia, detto il Semplice |trans-title=Federico IV of Aragon, King of Sicily, called 'the Simple' |encyclopedia=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani |volume=45 |year=1995 |first=Salvatore |last=Fodale |location=Rome |publisher=Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana }}</ref>
* [[February 3]] –After invading [[Cyprus]], the [[Republic of Genoa]] bombards the city of [[Kyrenia]], but the Cypriots repel the invasion and force the Genoese to retreat to [[Nicosia]].<ref name=Purton>{{cite book|first=Peter|last=Purton|title=A History of the Late Medieval Siege, 1200-1500|publisher=Boydell & Brewer|year=2009|page=167|isbn=9781843834496}}</ref> 
* [[February 11]] – In Germany, the [[Rhine]] river rises high enough in the [[Mosel (wine region)|Mosel River Valley]] during a flood that horses reportedly drown in the streets at [[Cologne|Koln]]<ref>{{cite book|first=Kelina|last=Gotman|title=Choreomania: Dance and Disorder|publisher=Oxford University Press |date=2018|page=49|isbn=9780190840419}}</ref>
* [[February 16]] – [[Robert de Juilly]] becomes the new Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller upon the death of [[Raymond Berengar (Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller)|Raymond Berengar]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Gordon Ellyson |last=Abercrombie |title=The Hospitaller Knights of Saint John at Rhodes 1306-1522|publisher=Pen and Sword|date=2024|page=84|isbn=9781399048040}}</ref>
* [[February]] – In what is now [[Hanoi]] in [[Vietnam]], the Emperor [[Trần Duệ Tông]] of [[Đại Việt]] issues decrees establishing an imperial examination for civil servants.<ref>{{citation|last=Ngô |first=Sĩ Liên|title=[[Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư]]|trans-title=The Complete Book of the Historical Records of Đại Việt| year=1993 |language=Vietnamese|publisher=Social Science Publishing House|location=[[Hanoi]]}}</ref>
* [[March 3]] – Genoa makes a second assault on Kyrenia in Cypturs by land and sea and overcomes the defenders.<ref name=Purton/>
* [[March 20]] – In a meeting at [[Dax, Landes|Dax]] in what is now the [[département]] of [[Landes (department)|Landes]], [[Gaston III of Foix]], overlord in France of multiple territories in the [[Pyrenees]] as [[Count of Foix]] and [[Viscount of Béarn]] forms an alliance with England's [[John of Gaunt]]

=== April–June ===
* [[April 8]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] issues the [[papal bull]] ''Salvator humani generis'', condemning 14 articles of the ''[[Sachsenspiegel]]'', challenging canon law.<ref>{{cite book|first=Christopher|last=Ocker|title=Johannes Klenkok: A Friar's Life, c. 1310- 1374|publisher=American Philosophical Society|year=1993|page=62}}</ref>
* [[April 12]] – At [[Almazán]], now part of [[Spain]] but at the time a town in the Kingdom of [[Castile and León]], a peace agreement is executed by [[Henry II of Castile|King Enrique II of Castile]] and [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pedro IV of Aragon]], with the two monarchs agreeing to the wedding of Enrique's son and Pedro's daughter.
* [[April 15]] – The [[Councils of Narbonne#Council of 1374|Council of Narbonne]] is convened for the first time since [[1261]] by orders of Pope Gregory XI, and will publish 28 canons of Roman Catholic law.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title= Narbonne, Councils of |encyclopedia= Cyclopædia of Biblical, Theological and Ecclesiastical Literature |year= 1880 |editor1-last= Strong |editor1-first= James |editor2-last= McClintock |editor2-first= John |publisher= Harper and Brothers |location= New York |url= https://www.biblicalcyclopedia.com/N/narbonne-councils-of.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Du Pin |first1=Louis Ellies |title=A New History of Ecclesiastical Writers:: New ecclesiastical history, containing an account of the controversies in religion, the lives and writings of ecclesiastical authors |date=1699 |publisher=Swalle and Childe |page=110 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hr8sAAAAYAAJ }}</ref>
* [[April 23]] – 
**[[Casimir IV, Duke of Pomerania|Casimir IV]] becomes the new [[Duke of Pomerania]] upon the death of his father [[Bogislaw V, Duke of Pomerania|Bogislaw V]], while Bogislaw's nephew, [[Bogislaw VI, Duke of Pomerania|Bogislaw VI]] becomes [[Prince of Rügen]].<ref>{{cite dictionary |title=Kazimierz IV |first=George J. |last=Lerski |dictionary=Historical Dictionary of Poland, 966-1945 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |year=1996|page=250}}</ref>
**On [[Saint George's Day]], in recognition of services, King [[Edward III of England]] grants the English writer [[Geoffrey Chaucer]] a gallon of wine a day, for the rest of his life.<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Riverside Chaucer |edition=3rd |editor1-last=Benson|editor1-first=Larry D. |publisher=Houghton-Mifflin |date=1987 |isbn=978-0-395-29031-6}}</ref>
* [[May 20]] – [[Edward the Black Prince]], eldest son and heir apparent to [[England]]'s [[Edward III|King Edward III]], presides over a council of bishops and nobles at [[Westminster]] on [[Whitsunday]] to review a demand by [[Pope Gregory XI]] for a subsidy from England to help the Papal States in the war against the Republic of Florence. In his letter, the Pope asserts his right as Lord Spiritual and refers to himself as "Lord of all". The English nobles conclude, and the bishops agree, that the Kingdom of England will not be subject to the Pope's authority.<ref>{{cite book|first=James|last=Girdner|chapter =Edward, Prince of Wales (1330-1376)|title=The Dictionary of National Biography|editor1=Leslie Stephen|editor2=Sidney Lee|volume=6|publisher=Oxford University Press|
page=518}}</ref>
* [[June 24]] – The illness [[dancing mania]] begins in [[Aix-la-Chapelle]] ([[Aachen]]), possibly due to [[ergotism]].

=== July–September ===
* [[July 26]] – [[Leo V of Armenia|Levon of Lusignan]] arrives at [[Sis (ancient city)|Sis]], capital of the [[Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia]] and now a set of ruins near the town of [[Kozan, Adana]] in [[Turkey]], to take the Cilician throne left vacant by the death of [[Constantine IV of Armenia|King Constantine IV]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Boase |first=T. S. R. |title=The Cilician Kingdom of Armenia |year=1978 |publisher=[[Scottish Academic Press]] |location=Edinburgh |isbn=0-7073-0145-9}}</ref> [[Marie of Korikos]], Constantine's widow, has been ruling as the regent and supports Levon's the election by Cilician nobles.
* [[August 18]] – [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]] pledges his infant daughter, [[Jadwiga of Poland|Princess Hedwig]], to marriage to  [[William, Duke of Austria|Wilhelm of Habsburg]], the four-year-old son of [[Leopold III, Duke of Austria]], as part of an alliance between Austria and Hungary.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Halecki |first=Oscar |year=1991 |title=Jadwiga of Anjou and the Rise of East Central Europe |publisher=[[Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America]] |page=58|isbn=0-88033-206-9}}</ref>
* [[August 27]] – In France, after 14 years as territory of the Kingdom of England, the village of [[Martel, Lot]] is retaken by [[Bertrand du Guesclin]], "The Eagle of Brittany".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Fourgous |first=Jean |title=A Travers le Lot |year=1963 |location=Cahors |page=224}}</ref>
* [[September 12]] – [[Jayasthiti Malla|King Jayasthiti Malla of Nepal]] leads soldiers into battle against the [[Kingdom of Lalitpur|Kingdom of Patan]] and captures its capital, [[Bhaktapur|Bhadagon]], as well as imprisoning and killing 53 of the Patan leaders.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Petech |first=Luciano |url=https://ia902904.us.archive.org/29/items/mediaevalhistoryofnepallucianopetech_643_f/Mediaeval%20History%20of%20Nepal%20%20Luciano%20Petech.pdf |title=Medieval History of Nepal |publisher=Fondata Da Giuseppe Tucci |year=1984 |edition=2nd |page=133}}</ref>
* [[September 14]] – Levon of Lusignan is formally crowned as King Leo V of Cilicia.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mutafian |first=Claude |title=Le Royaume Arménien de Cilicie |year=2001 |publisher=[[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS Editions]] |location=Paris |language=fr|isbn=2-271-05105-3}}</ref>
* [[September 17]] – [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]], in his role as King Ludwik of Poland, promulgates the [[Privilege of Koszyce]], granting major concessions to the nobles of Poland in return for the nobles' pledge that they will recognize his daughter, [[Jadwiga of Poland|Jadwiga]], as the reigning monarch upon his death. The privileges granted are a release from paying a [[tribute]] to the King as a form of property tax, except for a token amount, limiting appointments to office to persons of Polish ethnicity, release from obligations to build and repair towns, bridges and castles, release from payment of the king's expenses, and a reimbursement by the King to the nobles to pay soldiers' wages.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://polskieradio24.pl/artykul/2369417,przywilej-koszycki-pierwszy-krok-ku-demokracji-szlacheckiej|title= Przywilej koszycki. Pierwszy krok ku demokracji szlacheckiej|trans-title= The Privilege of Koszyce. The First Step towards Gentry Democracy}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 8]] – [[Shaikh Hasan Jalayir]] became the ruler of the [[Jalayirid Sultanate]], in what is now [[Iraq]], as the eldest son of the late [[Shaykh Uways Jalayir]], who had been Sultan since 1356, but would reign for only one day.<ref name=Wing>{{Cite book |last=Wing |first=Patrick |title=The Jalayirids |date=2016 |publisher=Edinburgh Univ Press |isbn=978-1-4744-0226-2 |location=[[Edinburgh]] |page=126}}</ref>
* [[October 9]] – [[Shaikh Hussain Jalayir|Hussain Jalayir]] was installed as the new ruler of the [[Jalayirid Sultanate]] after he and the other [[emir]]s arrested and executed Hussain's older brother, the Sultan Hasan, who had reigned for only one day.<ref name=Wing/>
* [[October 27]] – King [[Gongmin of Goryeo]] is assassinated by several men who invade the royal palace at [[Songdo]], enter the King's private chamber and hack him to death with swords. King Gongmin is succeeded by [[U of Goryeo]] as ruler of [[Goryeo]] (now part of [[South Korea]]).<ref>{{cite news |title=King Gongmin, one of the most underrated kings of Goryeo |url=https://world.kbs.co.kr/service/contents_view.htm?lang=e&menu_cate=history&id=&board_seq=60330&page=25&board_code= |access-date=5 February 2024 |agency=[[KBS World]] |date=September 1, 2011}}</ref> 
* [[November 25]] – [[James of Baux]] succeeds his uncle, [[Philip II of Taranto|Philip II]], as Prince of [[Taranto]] (modern-day eastern [[Italy]]) and [[titular ruler]] of the [[Latin Empire]] (northern [[Greece]] and western [[Turkey]]).
* [[December 18]] – [[Alexander Neville (bishop)|Alexander Neville]] is installed in England as the new Roman Catholic [[Archbishop of York]].<ref>{{cite book |editor-last=Fryde |editor-first=E. B. |year=1986 |title=Handbook of British Chronology |edition=3rd, reprinted 2003 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page=282 |isbn=0-521-56350-X}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Rao Biram Dev succeeds Rao Kanhadev as ruler of [[Marwar]] (the modern-day [[Jodhpur]] district of [[India]]).
* [[Shaikh Hasan Jalayir]] succeeds his father, [[Shaykh Uways Jalayir]], as ruler of the [[Jalayirid Sultanate]] in modern-day [[Iraq]] and western [[Iran]]. Hasan proves to be an unpopular ruler and is executed on October 9 and succeeded by his brother, [[Shaikh Hussain Jalayir]].
* [[Musa II (mansa)|Musa II]] succeeds his father, [[Mari Djata II]], as [[Mansa (title)|Mansa]] of the [[Mali Empire]] (modern-day [[Mali]] and [[Senegal]]).
* [[Robert de Juilly]] succeeds Raymond Berenger as Grand Master of the [[Knights Hospitaller]].
* Princes from the [[Nasrid dynasty|Kingdom of Granada]] choose Abu al-Abbas Ahmad to succeed Muhammad as-Said, as Sultan of the [[Marinid dynasty|Marinid]] Empire in [[Morocco]]. The Empire is split into the [[Kingdom of Fez]] and the Kingdom of [[Marrakesh]].
* A form of the [[Great Plague]] returns to Europe.
* The [[Château de Compiègne]] royal residence is built in [[France]].</onlyinclude>

1371.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 5]] – Six days after his election to lead the Roman Catholic Church, Pierre Roger de Beaufort is crowned as [[Pope Gregory XI]]. The coronation is performed by the protodeacon Rinaldo Orsini at the [[Avignon Cathedral]].<ref>S. Miranda [https://cardinals.fiu.edu/bios1348.htm#Roger Cardinal Pierre Roger de Beaufort (Pope Gregory XI)]</ref>
* [[January 8]] – King Edward II summons the members of the House of Lords and House of Commons to assemble at Westminster for a one-month session of the [[English Parliament]].
* [[January]] – [[Edward the Black Prince]], gives up the administration of [[Aquitaine]] and returns to England, because of his poor health and heavy debts.
* [[February 1]] – [[War of the Lüneburg Succession]]: In what is now the state of [[Lower Saxony]] in north Germany, after the Duke of Brunswick, [[Magnus II, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg|Magnus Torquatus]], attempts to claim his inheritance to rule of the [[Principality of Lüneburg]], residents of the town of [[Lüneburg]] destroy the [[Lüneburg Kalkberg|ducal castle]] that had been owned by the late [[William II, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg|Prince Wilhelm]], and Brunswick relocates his residence to the town of [[Celle]].<ref name=Havemann>{{cite book|first=Wilhelm |last=Havemann|title=Geschichte der Lande Braunschweig und Lüneburg|trans-title= History of the Lands of Brunswick and Lüneburg|location=Hannover| publisher=Hirschheydt|year=1975|isbn=3-7777-0843-7}}</ref>
* [[February 17]] – Rival brothers [[Ivan Sratsimir of Bulgaria|Ivan Sratsimir]] and [[Ivan Shishman of Bulgaria|Ivan Shishman]] become co-Emperors of [[Bulgaria]] after the death of their father, [[Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria|Ivan Alexander]]. Bulgaria is weakened by the split.
* [[February 22]] – [[Robert II of Scotland|Robert II]] becomes the first [[House of Stuart|Stuart]] king of [[Kingdom of Scotland|Scotland]], after the death of his uncle, [[David II of Scotland|King David II]], prompting a rebellion by [[Archibald Douglas, 3rd Earl of Douglas|the Earl of Douglas]].<ref name=Boardman>{{citation |last=Boardman |first=Stephen |authorlink=Steve Boardman (historian) |title=The Early Stewart Kings: Robert II and Robert III, 1371–1406 |publisher=John Donald, an imprint of Birlinn Ltd |year=2007 |location=Edinburgh |series=The Stewart Dynasty in Scotland Series|pages=40-41|isbn=978-1-904607-68-7}}</ref>
* [[February 24]] – The English Parliament opens its session at Westminster.
* [[March 26]] – The coronation of Robert II as [[List of Scottish monarchs|King of Scotland]] takes place at [[Scone Abbey]].<ref name=Boardman/>
* [[March 28]] – The [[London Charterhouse]], a [[Carthusian]] [[monastery]], is founded in [[Aldersgate]].
* [[March 29]] – The English Parliament closes and King Edward II gives [[royal assent]] to laws passed during its session, including the confirmation of the Great Charter of the Forest, as well as defining "the penalty of him that setteth up or enhanceth wares" and a ban against enforcement, without consent, of the law of ''sylva caedua'', a tithe to the church of a portion of any timber of 20 years growth.<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |pages=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 9]] – [[Emperor Go-En'yu]] of Japan succeeds [[Emperor Go-Kōgon]] of the [[Northern Court]] of [[Japan]].
* [[May 17]] – The [[Lordship of Milan]] expands its holdings when [[Feltrino Gonzaga]] sells almost all of his holdings of [[Province of Reggio Emilia|Reggio di Lombardia]] to the Lords [[Bernabò Visconti|Galeazzo and Bernabo Visconti]], with the exception of Novellara and Bagnolo.
* [[May 30]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] names 12 new Roman Catholic cardinals to supplement the existing 20 living cardinals. The new cardinals at Avignon include [[Antipope Clement VII|Robert de Geneve]] who will become the first [[antipope]] of the [[Western Schism]].
* [[May]] – Under the direction of [[Hongwu Emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]], the Emperor Hongwu, the [[Ming conquest of Xia]] begins as troops from [[Ming dynasty|China]], led by Generals [[Fu Youde]] and [[Tang He]] invade what is now the [[Sichuan]] province from the north, while Admiral [[:zh:廖永忠|Liao Yongzhong]] leads an attack on Xia's east coast and along the [[Yangtze]] river.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Taylor |first=Romeyn |title=Basic Annals of Ming T'ai-tsu |pages=70-72 |publisher=Chinese Material and Research Aids Service Center, Inc |year=1975 |asin=B076VFSKS1}}</ref>
* [[June 24]] – In punishment for his malfeasance as regent during the reign of King David II, the property of [[William III, Earl of Ross]] at Inverness is confiscated by King Robert II.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Barrell |first=A. D. M. |title=Medieval Scotland |date=2000 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=0-521-58602-X}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 21]] – [[John of Gaunt]], Duke of Lancaster, resigns his command from the English Army and abandons the attempt to recapture the Duchy of Aquitaine, but remains in France.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last=Todd|first=Elizabeth Marion|title=John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster (1340-1399)|encyclopedia=The Dictionary of National Biography|volume=10|page=856|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=1973}}</ref>
* [[August 22]] – Brabant is unexpectedly defeated by the Duchy of [[Jülich]] at the [[Battle of Baesweiler]].
* [[September 21]] – [[John of Gaunt]], son of King [[Edward III]] of England, marries [[Constance of Castile, Duchess of Lancaster|Constance of Castile]], daughter of King [[Pedro of Castile]], giving John a claim to the throne of Castile.
* [[September 26]] – In the [[Battle of Maritsa]], troops led by [[Lala Shahin Pasha]] and [[Hacı İlbey]] from the [[Ottoman Empire]] overwhelm and kill most of the Serbian defenders, including [[Vukašin of Serbia|King Vukašin]], his brother Prince [[Jovan Uglješa]], and most of the lords of the [[Mrnjavčević family]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Nicol |first=Donald M. |title=The Last Centuries of Byzantium, 1261-1453 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1993 |pages=275-276|isbn=978-0-521-43991-6 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=y2d6OHLqwEsC}}</ref> The victory paves the way for the Ottoman Empire to expand into the [[Balkan Peninsula]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 21]] – An attempt on [[Saint Ursula|Saint Ursula's Day]] by the Duke of Brunswick, to defeat the uprising in the principality of Luneberg and to reclaim his title, is unsuccessful.<ref name=Havemann/>
* [[November 18]] – Shen-Chi and Chang-Jhing-Chi, diplomatic envoys from [[Ming dynasty|China]], land in [[Java]] to deliver a message from the Chinese Emperor to [[Muhammad Shah of Brunei]].<ref >{{cite book |author=Jatswan S. Sidhu |title=Historical Dictionary of Brunei Darussalam |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Bry0sOwstIMC&pg=PA20 |date=2009 |publisher=Scarecrow Press |isbn=978-0-8108-7078-9 |page=20}}</ref>
* [[November 26]] – In the Kingdom of [[Goryeo]] (now sections of North Korea and South Korea), [[Gongmin of Goryeo|King Gongmin]] names his [[Royal Consort Shin-Bi|Shin-Bi]] as his royal consort and primary wife.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://db.history.go.kr/KOREA|title=염제신의 딸을 신비로 삼다|trans-title= Take Yeomjesin's Daughter as Mystery|website=db.history.go.kr}}</ref>
* [[December 4]] – [[Stefan Uroš V]], the Tsar of Serbia and King of the Greeks since 1346, dies childless at the age of 35.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ćirković|first=Sima|year=2004|title=The Serbs|location=Malden|publisher=Blackwell Publishing|pages=79-80|isbn=9781405142915}}</ref> [[Prince Marko|Marko Mrnjavčević]], the young son of the late co-ruler of Serbia, King Vukasin, is designated as the nominal Emperor, although [[Lazar of Serbia|Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović]] controls most of the remaining territory of the Serbian Empire.

=== Date unknown ===
* The first widely accepted historical reference is made to [[playing cards]] (in [[Spain]]).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bodle |first1=Andy |title=Guide to games: Leaders of the pack: A short history of cards |url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2008/nov/22/history-of-playing-cards |website=The Guardian |access-date=24 April 2019 |date=22 November 2008}}</ref>
* Polish priest [[Andrzej Jastrzębiec]] becomes the first bishop of [[Siret]], thus bringing Catholicism to [[Moldavia]].
* Zhao Bing Fa becomes King of [[Mong Mao]] (in modern-day south China/north Myanmar) after the death of his father, [[Si Kefa]].
* Kalamegha claims the vacant title of King of [[Cambodia]] after the power of the [[Thailand|Thai]] invaders from [[Ayutthaya Kingdom|Ayutthaya]] begins to weaken. The Ayutthayans are finally expelled in [[1375]].
* [[Byzantine]] co-emperor [[John V Palaiologos]] pledges loyalty to the [[Ottoman Empire]], to prevent the Turks from invading [[Constantinople]].
* The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of the [[Ming dynasty]] in [[China]] introduces the [[census]] registration system of ''lijia'', or the hundreds-and-tithing system, throughout the [[Yangtze River|Yangzi]] Valley. This system groups households into units of ten and groups of one hundred, whereupon their capacities for paying taxes and providing the state with [[corvée]] labor service can be assessed. The system becomes fully operational in [[1381]], when it counts 59,873,305 people living in China (the historian [[Timothy Brook (historian)|Timothy Brook]] asserts that the number was much higher, somewhere between 65 million and 75 million).</onlyinclude>

1382.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 6]] – [[Basalawarmi]], the [[Yuan dynasty]] Prince of [[Wei (state)|Liang]] (now in the [[Henan]] province), commits suicide at his palace in [[Kaifeng]] after having been forced to retreat from the [[Ming dynasty]] armies.<ref>Denis Twitchett and John K. Fairbank, ''The Cambridge History of China'' (Cambridge University Press, 2004) vol. 7, pp. 143–146.</ref>
* [[January 20]] – Princess [[Anne of Bohemia]], a daughter of the late [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], becomes the Queen Consort of England by marrying [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]]; the marriage produces no heirs before her death in 1395.
* [[February 25]] – The English Parliament adjourns after a seession of almost four months that had started on 30-day session that began on November 3. Among the laws given [[royal assent]] by King Richard II are the [[Treason Act 1381]], the [[Forcible Entry Act 1381]] and the confirmations of the liberty of the church, prohibition of the exportation of gold or silver without permission, and setting of price ceilings on wine.<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=25}} |pages=25 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> 
* [[March 3]] – The [[Harelle|Mailottins massacre]] takes place in [[Paris]] when revenue agents for King Charles VI arrive at the [[Les Halles]] market to collect taxes. The agents are killed by a mob of almost 500 merchants, and the number of people involved increases to several thousand, with the rioters seizing a large store of iron mallets (mallots) at the [[Place de Greve]]. Armed with heavy weapons, the mallotins begin attacking and looting churches, businesses, government offices and homes of wealthy people and then attack the Jewish section of city. An estimated 30 people are killed by the mob.<ref name=Sumption>{{cite book|title= The Hundred Years War: Divided Houses|year=2009|author=Sumption, Jonathan|isbn=978-0-8122-4223-2|publisher=[[University of Pennsylvania Press]]|pages=445–447}}</ref>
* [[March 5]] – King Charles VI arrives at the gates of the walled city of Paris and, with the Duke of Burgundy as his intermediary, attempts to negotiate peace to end the rebellion in Paris. While their demands are not met, the mob opens the cells of the city's prisons and frees the persons incarcerated.<ref name=Sumption/>
* [[March 10]] – (24th day of Leap Month of [[Kōwa (Muromachi period)|Kōwa 2]]) [[Kusunoki Masanori]], fighting for Southern Japan, is defeated in a battle at Kawachi Hirao with Yamana Ujiyoshi and is forced to retreat to [[Tokyo]].
* [[March 29]] – Troops commanded by the King of France and the Duke of Burgundy liberate [[Rouen]] from rebel control, without resistance, and all  but 12 of the rebels are spared from execution.<ref name=Sumption/>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 9]] – [[Ming dynasty|Ming dyansty China]], ruled by the [[Hongwu Emperor|Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang]], completes the [[Ming conquest of Yunnan|conquerst of Yunnan]] the remaining portion of China still occupied by the [[Yuan dyansty]] in what is now the [[Yunnan]] province.<ref>John E. Herman, ''[https://www.google.com/books/edition/Amid_the_Clouds_and_Mist/kKTaDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22April+1382%22+Ming&pg=PA86&printsec=frontcover|Amid the Clouds and Mist: China’s Colonization of Guizhou, 1200–1700]'' (Brill, 2020) pp.85-86 ISBN  9781684174638</ref> General [[Fu Youde]] leads 250,000 Ming Chinese troops overwhelming the smaller Yunnan force of Mongol and Chinese Muslim troops.
* [[May 12]] – Charles of Durazzo executes the cimprisoned [[Joanna I of Naples]], and succeeds her as [[Charles III of Naples]].
* [[May 21]] – [[John Wycliffe]]'s teachings are condemned by the Synod of London, which becomes known as the "[[Earthquake Synod]]", after its meetings are disrupted by [[1382 Dover Straits earthquake|an earthquake]].<ref>*"Earthquake Synod." In Cross, F. L. and E. A. Livingstone, eds. ''The Oxford Dictionary of the Christian Church.'' London: Oxford UP, 1974. p. 437</ref>
* [[June 10]] – [[Michele Morosini]] is elected as the new [[Doge of Venice|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Venice]], five days after the death of [[Andrea Contarini]], but serves for only four months before dying in office.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 19]] – [[Joanna I of Naples|Joanna of Anjou]], who had been Queen of [[Kingdom of Naples|Naples]] until being deposed  on August 25, 1381, is murdered by strangulation after being transferred in May to the prison at the [[Castle of Muro Lucano]].<ref>{{cite book | first=Émile-G. |last=Léonard |title=Les Angevins de Naples |location=Paris |publisher=Presses universitaires de France |year=1954|page=468}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |first=Eugène |last=Jarry |url=http://www.persee.fr/web/revues/home/prescript/article/bec_0373-6237_1894_num_55_1_462767 |title=La mort de Jeanne I, reine de Jérusalem et de Sicile, en 1382 |encyclopedia=Bibliothèque de l'école des chartes |language=fr |year=1894 |volume=55 |issue=1 |pages=236–237}}</ref>
* [[August 9]] – King Richard II summons the English Parliament for the third time in the year, directing the Lords and members of Commons to assemble at Westminster on October 6.
* [[August 10]] – The [[Treaty of Elvas]] is signed between [[Fernando I of Portugal|King Fernando]] of [[Portugal]] and [[John I of Castile|King Juan]] of [[Crown of Castile|Castile]] to end the [[Third Fernandine War]]. Under the agreement, Portugal ends its alliance with England and joins Castile and France in the [[Hundred Years' War]], and recognizes the jurisdiction of the [[Clement VII (antipope)|antipope Clement VII]] over the Portuguese church. Castile returns all Portuguese prisoners of war and ships, and gives [[Almeida, Portugal|Almeida]] and [[Miranda do Douro|Miranda]] back to Portugal. Finally, King Fernando's daughter [[Beatrice of Portugal|Beatriz]] marries King Juan's son [[Ferdinand I of Aragon|Ferdinand]].<ref>H.V. Livermore, ''History of Portugal'' (Cambridge University Press, 1947) p.173</ref>
* [[August 15]] – [[Władysław II Jagiełło|Jogaila]] resumes his position as Grand Duke of Lithuania.
* [[August 23]] – [[Siege of Moscow (1382)|The Siege of Moscow]] begins as [[Tokhtamysh]], khan of the [[Golden Horde]] attacks the capital of the Principality of Muscovy while its ruler, Prince [[Dmitry Donskoy]], is away seeking assistance from other Russian princes.<ref name=MS/>
* [[August 26]] – 
**After three days, Tokhtamysh promises the highest ranking official in Moscow, [[:ru:Остей|Prince Ostei]], that if a peaceful surrender can be negotiated, the Tatars of the Golden Horde will spare the population. As Ostei opens the gate of the walled city and walks out with his team, Tokhtamysh kills the Russian group and his troops begin looting, raping and killing the Moscow residents.<ref name=MS>Marat Shaikhutdinov, ''Between East and West: The Formation of the Moscow State'' (Academic Studies Press, 2021) p. 106 ISBN 9781644697153</ref>
**The iconic painting the [[Black Madonna of Częstochowa]] is brought from [[Jerusalem]], to the [[Jasna Góra Monastery]] in Poland on her the day celebrated as the [[feast day]] in her honor.
* [[September 10]] – [[Louis I of Hungary|Lajos I]], [[List of Hungarian monarchs|King of Hungary and Croatia]] and [[List of Polish monarchs|Poland]], dies at the age of 56 after 40 years as the Hungarian monarch.<ref>{{Cite EB1911 |wstitle=Louis I. of Hungary |volume=17 |page=49 |last=Bain |first=Robert Nisbet |author-link=Robert Nisbet Bain}}</ref>
* [[September 17]] – Following the death of King Lajos, his daughter [[Mary, Queen of Hungary|Mary]] is crowned the "King" of Hungary in a ceremony at [[Székesfehérvár]], carried out by [[Demetrius of Esztergom|Cardinal Demeter]], [[Archbishop of Esztergom]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Engel |first=Pál |year=2001 |title=The Realm of St Stephen: A History of Medieval Hungary, 895–1526 |publisher= I.B. Tauris Publishers |page=195 |isbn=1-86064-061-3}}</ref>
* [[September 30]] – The inhabitants of [[Trieste]] (now in northern Italy) donate their city to [[Leopold III, Duke of Austria|Duke Leopold III of Austria]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 13]] – While being held as a prisoner in the [[Republic of Genoa]], [[James I of Cyprus|Jacques de Lusignan]] is elected by a parliament of Cypriot nobles to succeed his nephew, [[Peter II of Cyprus|Peter II]] (who died on September 9), as [[Kingdom of Cyprus#List of monarchs of Cyprus|King of Cyprus]].<ref>"The fourteenth and fifteenth centuries", by Harry W. Hazard, ''A History of The Crusades: Chapter XI, The Kingdom of Cyprus 1369-1489'', ed. by Kenneth Meyer Setton  (University of Pennsylvania Press, 1914), pp. 361-370</ref>
* [[October 16]] – [[Michele Morosini]], Doge of Venice, dies after contracting the bubonic plague. [[Antonio Venier]] is elected to succeed him. Vernier will be the chief executive of the republic for 18 years until his death in 1400.
* [[October 20]] – [[Winchester College]] is founded in [[Kingdom of England|England]].
