* [[November 25]] – The nobles of [[Greater Poland]] assemble at [[Radomsko]] and, not wishing to be ruled by Mary' of Hungarys fiancee, the future [[Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor|Sigismund of Luxembourg]], choose Mary's younger sister, [[Jadwiga of Poland|Jadwiga]], to become ruler of Poland.<ref name=Halecki>{{Cite book |last=Halecki |first=Oscar |author-link=Oscar Halecki |year=1991 |title=Jadwiga of Anjou and the Rise of East Central Europe |publisher=[[Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America]] |page=99 |isbn=0-88033-206-9}}</ref>
* [[November 27]] – 
**After a five-year revolt, [[Barquq]] deposes [[Al-Salih Hajji|Hajji II]] as [[Mamluk]] Sultan of Egypt, marking the end of the [[Bahri Mamluks|Bahri Dynasty]] and [[Qalawunid dynasty|Qalawunid Dynasty]], and the start of the [[Burji Mamluks|Burji Dynasty]].<ref>Holt, 2014, p. [https://books.google.com/books?id=TqasAgAAQBAJ 128]</ref>
**[[Battle of Roosebeke]]: A French army under [[Louis II, Count of Flanders]] defeats the Flemings, led by [[Philip van Artevelde]].
* [[December 12]] – The noblemen of [[Lesser Poland]] meet at [[Wiślica]] and, as with the November 25 decision of the nobles of [[Greater Poland]], vote to invite Jadwiga of Hungary to be their ruler.<ref name=Halecki/>

=== Date unknown ===
* Khan [[Tokhtamysh]] of the [[Golden Horde]] overruns [[Grand Duchy of Moscow|Muscovy]], as punishment for Grand Prince [[Dmitry Donskoy]]'s resistance to Khan [[Mamai]] of the [[Blue Horde]] in the 1370s. Dmitry Donskoy pledges his loyalty to Tokhtamysh, and is allowed to remain as ruler of Moscow and [[Vladimir, Russia|Vladimir]].
* The [[Ottoman Turks|Ottomans]] take [[Sofia]] from the [[Second Bulgarian Empire|Bulgarians]].
* [[Ibrahim I of Shirvan|Ibrahim I]] is selected to succeed Husheng, as Shah of [[Shirvanshah|Shirvan]] (now [[Azerbaijan]]).
* [[Kęstutis]], the [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania|Grand Duke of Lithuania]], is taken prisoner by former Grand Duke [[Jogaila]], whilst meeting him to hold negotiations. Kęstutis is subsequently murdered, and Jogaila regains the rule of Lithuania.
* [[Sultan Ahmed Jalayir|Ahmed]] deposes his brother, [[Shaikh Hussain Jalayir|Hussain]], as ruler of the [[Jalayirids|Jalayirid Dynasty]] in western [[Persia]].
* Rana Lakha succeeds Rana Kshetra Singh, as ruler of [[Mewar]] (now part of western India).
* Conrad Zöllner von Rothenstein succeeds [[Winrich von Kniprode]], as Grand Master of the [[Teutonic Knights]].
* [[Balša II]] of [[Principality of Zeta|Zeta]] conquers [[Albania]].
* [[Dawit I]] succeeds his brother [[Newaya Maryam]], as Emperor of [[Ethiopian Empire|Ethiopia]].
* [[Ignatius Abraham bar Garib|Abraham bar Garib]] becomes Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Mardin.<ref>{{cite book | last1 =Barsoum| first1=Ephrem |date=2003|title=The Scattered Pearls: A History of Syriac Literature and Sciences|edition=2nd|publisher=Gorgias Press|translator=Matti Moosa|author-link=Ignatius Aphrem I Barsoum|page=495}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

1352.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* [[February 13]] – [[War of the Straits]] – The [[Battle of the Bosporus]] is fought in a stormy sea into the night between the Genoese, Venetian, Aragonese, and Byzantine fleets.   The Genoese emerge victorious, as the other fleets withdraw. <ref>{{cite book | last = Musarra | first = Antonio | title = Il Grifo e il Leone: Genova e Venezia in lotta per il Mediterraneo | year = 2020 | publisher = Editori Laterza | location = Bari and Rome | isbn = 978-88-581-4072-7 | language = Italian | pages=235–236 }}</ref>
* [[June 4]] – [[Canton of Glarus|Glarus]] joins the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]].
* [[June 27]] – [[Canton of Zug|Zug]] joins the Old Swiss Confederacy.
* [[September 25]] – [[Emperor Go-Kōgon]] becomes 4th Emperor of the [[Northern Court]] of Japan.<ref>Titsingh, Isaac, ed. (1834). [Siyun-sai Rin-siyo/Hayashi Gahō, 1652], Nipon o daï itsi ran; ou, Annales des empereurs du Japon. Paris: Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland, pp. 302</ref>
* [[October]] – [[Byzantine civil war of 1352–1357]] – [[Battle of Demotika]]: Fighting as allies of [[John VI Kantakouzenos]], the [[Ottoman beylik]] scores its first victory on European soil, against the [[Serbian Empire|Serbs]].
* [[November 7]] – [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge|Corpus Christi College]] is founded as a College of the [[University of Cambridge]] in England, by the Guilds of Corpus Christi and the [[Blessed Virgin Mary]].<ref>University of Cambridge (6 March 2019). "Notice by the Editor". Cambridge University Reporter. 149 (Special No 5): 1. Retrieved 20 March 2019.</ref>
* [[December 18]] – [[Pope Innocent VI]] succeeds [[Pope Clement VI]] as the 199th pope.
* [[December 26]] – The [[Earl of Kent|Earldom of Kent]] of the 5th creation in England becomes extinct.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Süleyman Pasha (son of Orhan)]] is probably granted control of [[Çimpe Castle]] on the [[Gallipoli]] peninsula by Emperor [[John VI Kantakouzenos]], the first territory west of the [[Bosporus]] held by the [[Ottoman Empire]].<ref>Nicolle, David; Hook, Adam. ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=C9UVaLyo4UEC&pg=PA8 Ottoman Fortifications 1300-1710]{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}.'' Osprey Publishing, 2010. Accessed 3 Sept 2011.</ref></onlyinclude>
* The [[Bengal Sultanate]] is formed after the realms of [[Satgaon]], [[Gauḍa (city)|Lakhnauti]] and [[Sonargaon]] are united under [[Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah]].
* Coming from Hungary, the noble Vlach [[Dragoş]] becomes the first [[voivode]] of [[Moldova]], being seen as the founder of this principality (some scholars place this moment as early as [[1345]]).
* Following the death of his father [[Basarab I of Wallachia|Basarab]], [[Nicholas Alexander of Wallachia|Nicholas Alexander]] becomes voivode of [[Wallachia]], after being co-ruler for about eight years.
* The town of [[Biel/Bienne]], Switzerland, finalizes its alliance with the city of [[Bern]].
* [[Lionel of Antwerp]] marries Elizabeth, daughter of [[William de Burgh, 3rd Earl of Ulster]].
* [[Reginald de Cobham, 1st Baron Cobham]] becomes a Companion of the [[Order of the Garter|Most Noble Order of the Garter]] of England.
* The [[metropolitan bishop|Metropolitan]] of the [[Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church]]; the Metropolitan of Halych begins to relocate back to [[Kyiv]], after having moved to [[Halych]] in [[1299]]. Thereafter, the Metropolitan will hold the title of Metropolitan of Kiev-Halych and All Rus.
* After years of begging and being a [[Chinese Buddhism|Buddhist]] monk, the penniless [[China|Chinese]] peasant [[Zhu Yuanzhang]] joins the [[Red Turban Rebellions]] against the Mongol-led [[Yuan dynasty]] of China; he will later become the first emperor of the [[Ming dynasty]].<ref>Bowman, John Stewart, ed. (2000). Columbia chronologies of Asian history and culture. New York: Columbia University Press. pp. 39. ISBN 978-0231500043. OCLC 51542679.</ref>
* [[:File:Tommaso da modena, ritratti di domenicani (Ugo di Provenza) 1352 150cm, treviso, ex convento di san niccolò, sala del capitolo.jpg|Earliest surviving illustration of someone wearing spectacles]], a fresco in the chapter house of the Dominican convent of San Nicolò, [[Treviso]] by [[Tommaso da Modena]] (anachronistically{{dubious|date=September 2022|reason=There are reports a monk in northern Italy was making and giving away glasses about the time of Hugh of Siant-Cher about 50 years before the painting}}) depicting [[Hugh of Saint-Cher]].
* Moroccan traveller [[Ibn Battuta]] reports the existence of the [[Xalam|ngoni]] and [[balafon]] musical instruments, at the court of [[Mansa Musa]].

1353.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* [[March 3]] – [[Canton of Bern|Bern]] signs an alliance with the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]].
* [[August 27]] – [[War of the Straits]] and [[Sardinian–Aragonese war]] – [[Battle of Alghero]]: The allied Aragonese and Venetian fleets crush  the Genoese fleet, most of which is captured.<ref>{{cite book | last = Musarra | first = Antonio | title = Il Grifo e il Leone: Genova e Venezia in lotta per il Mediterraneo | year = 2020 | publisher = Editori Laterza | location = Bari and Rome | isbn = 978-88-581-4072-7 | language = Italian | pages=237–238 }}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Moroccan people|Moroccan]] traveler [[Ibn Battuta]] makes the first recorded visit to [[Timbuktu]] and [[Kabara, Mali|Kabara]], when returning from a stay in the capital of the [[Mali Empire]].<ref>{{cite book|editor1-link=Nehemia Levtzion|editor1-last=Levtzion|editor1-first=Nehemia|editor2-last=Hopkins|editor2-first=John F. P.|title=Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West Africa|publisher=Marcus Weiner Press|location=New York|year=2000|isbn=1-55876-241-8|page=299}}</ref>
* ''[[The Decameron]]'' is finished by [[Giovanni Boccaccio]].
* The [[Black Death]] ([[1331]]) subsides.
* The [[Lao people|Lao]] kingdom of [[Lan Xang]] is founded by [[Fa Ngum]].</onlyinclude>

1354.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* Early in the year – [[Ibn Battuta]] returns from his travels at the command of [[Abu Inan Faris]], [[sultan]] of [[Morocco]], who appoints a [[scribe]] to write an account of the adventures.<ref>[[Ibn Battuta#CITEREFDefrémerySanguinetti1858|Defrémery & Sanguinetti 1858]], pp. 444–445 Vol. 4; [[Ibn Battuta#CITEREFLevtzionHopkins2000|Levtzion & Hopkins 2000]], p. 303; [[Ibn Battuta#CITEREFDunn2005|Dunn 2005]], p. 306</ref>
* [[February 12]] –  The [[Treaty of Stralsund (1354)|Treaty of Stralsund]] settles border disputes between the [[duchies]] of [[Mecklenburg]] and [[Pomerania]].
* [[March 2]] –   During the night between 1 and 2 March, a strong earthquake destroyed the city of [[Gallipoli]] and its city walls, weakening its defenses, along with destroying the neighboring villages and towns in the area.<ref>[[George Ostrogorsky|Ostrogorsky, George]]. ''History of the Byzantine State,'' pp. 530–537. Rutgers University Press (New Jersey),</ref>
* [[March]] - Within a month after the devastating earthquake the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottomans]] [[Fall of Gallipoli|besieged and captured]] the town of Gallipoli, making it the first Ottoman stronghold in Europe and the staging area for Ottoman expansion across the [[Balkans]].<ref>Crowley, Roger. 1453: ''The Holy War for Constantinople and the Clash of Islam and the West''. New York: Hyperion, 2005. p 31 {{ISBN|1-4013-0850-3}}.</ref>
* [[October 8]] – [[Cola di Rienzo]], self-proclaimed "[[tribune]]" of [[Rome]], is killed by an [[angry mob]].<ref>Ronald G. Musto, ''Apocalypse in Rome. Cola di Rienzo and the politics of the New Age''(Berkeley & Los Angeles, University of California Press, 2003).</ref>
* [[August 16]] – [[War of the Straits]]: The [[Republic of Venice|Venetian]]-ruled town of [[Poreč]] is sacked by the [[Republic of Genoa|Genoese]] under [[Paganino Doria]], who carry off the relics of saints [[Eleutherius and Antia|Eleutherius]] and [[Maurus of Parentium]] to Genoa, where they were deposited at the church of [[San Matteo (Genoa)|San Matteo]].<ref>{{cite book | last = Musarra | first = Antonio | title = Il Grifo e il Leone: Genova e Venezia in lotta per il Mediterraneo | year = 2020 | publisher = Editori Laterza | location = Bari and Rome | isbn = 978-88-581-4072-7 | language = Italian | pages = 239–240}}</ref>
* [[November 4]] – [[War of the Straits]]: The Genoese fleet under Paganino Doria defeats and captures the entire Venetian fleet under [[Niccolò Pisani]] at the [[Battle of Sapienza]].<ref>{{cite book | last = Musarra | first = Antonio | title = Il Grifo e il Leone: Genova e Venezia in lotta per il Mediterraneo | year = 2020 | publisher = Editori Laterza | location = Bari and Rome | isbn = 978-88-581-4072-7 | language = Italian | pages = 240–241}}</ref>
* [[December 10]] – The reign of [[John VI Kantakouzenos]] as [[Byzantine Emperor]] is ended, after [[John V Palaiologos]] retakes [[Constantinople]] and is restored as sole emperor.<ref>Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1991</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* After 24 years of struggling for independence, since the [[Battle of Posada]], [[Nicholas Alexander of Wallachia]] becomes a vassal to Hungarian king [[Louis I of Hungary|Louis I]].<ref>(in Romanian) Constantin C. Giurescu, ''Istoria Românilor'', vol. I, Ed. ALL Educațional, București, 2003.</ref>
* [[Shihabu'd-Din Shah|Sahab-ud-Din]] becomes Sultan of [[Kashmir Sultanate|Kashmir]].</onlyinclude><ref>Retzlaff, Ralph H.; Hasan, Mohibbul. "Kashmir under the Sultans". ''Journal of the American Oriental Society'' (4): 46. [[Doi (identifier)|doi]]:10.2307/595144. [[ISSN (identifier)|ISSN]] 0003-0279. [[JSTOR (identifier)|JSTOR]] 595144.</ref>

1355.events:
<onlyinclude>
* [[January 6]] – [[Charles IV of Bohemia]] is crowned with the [[Iron Crown of Lombardy]] as King of Italy in Milan.
* [[January 7]] – King [[Afonso IV of Portugal]] sends three men who kill [[Inês de Castro]], mistress of his son [[Peter I of Portugal|Pedro]], who revolts and incites a civil war.
* [[February 10]] – [[St Scholastica Day riot]] in [[Oxford]], [[Kingdom of England|England]], breaks out, leaving 63 scholars and perhaps 30 locals dead in two days.<ref>Brockliss, L. W. B. (2016). The University of Oxford: A History. Oxford: Oxford University Press. ISBN 978-0-19-924356-3.</ref>
* [[March 16]] – [[Red Turban Rebellions]]: [[Han Lin'er]], a claimed descendant of [[Emperor Huizong of Song]], is proclaimed emperor of the restored [[Song dynasty]] in [[Bozhou]].<ref name=Twitchett>{{cite book|author=Denis Twitchett|title=The Cambridge History of China, Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tyhT9SZRLS8C|date=1988|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn= 978-0-521-24332-2|pages=42–45}}</ref>
* [[April]] – [[Philip II, Prince of Taranto]], marries [[Maria of Calabria]], daughter of [[Charles, Duke of Calabria]], and [[Marie of Valois, Duchess of Calabria|Marie of Valois]].
* [[April 5]] – [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor|Charles IV]] is crowned Holy Roman Emperor in [[Rome]].
* [[April 18]] – In [[Venice]], the [[Council of Ten]] beheads [[Doge of Venice|Doge]] [[Marin Falier]], for conspiring to kill them.<ref>Villari, Luigi (1911). "Faliero, Marino" . In Chisholm, Hugh (ed.). Encyclopædia Britannica. Vol. 10 (11th ed.). Cambridge University Press. p. 148.</ref>
* [[May]] – [[Red Turban Rebellions]]: [[Guo Zixing]] dies, leaving his forces to the command of his son-in-law, [[Zhu Yuanzhang]]. Guo's successors are later killed in battle while trying to capture [[Nanjing]].<ref name=Twitchett/></onlyinclude>
* [[August]] – [[Battle of Nesbit Moor (1355)|Battle of Nesbit Moor]]: The Scottish army decisively defeats the English.<ref>Dalrymple, Sir David (1819). Annals of Scotland. Edinburgh, Scotland: Archibald Constable & Co. p. 182-183.</ref>
* [[September 1]] – The [[old town of Visoki]] is first mentioned in [[Tvrtko I of Bosnia]]'s charter ''in castro nostro Vizoka vocatum''.<ref>Commission to Preserve National Monuments of Bosnia and Herzegovina (3 April 2009). "Povijesno područje – Stari grad Visoki". Commission to Preserve National Monuments of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Archived from the original on 30 March 2012. Retrieved 15 June 2023.</ref>
* [[October 5]]–[[December 2]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: [[Black Prince's chevauchée of 1355|Black Prince's ''chevauchée'' of 1355]] – A large mounted Anglo-Gascon force under the command of [[Edward the Black Prince]] marches from [[Bordeaux]] in English-held [[Gascony]] 300 miles (480 km) south to [[Narbonne]] and back, devastating a wide swathe of French territory.<ref>Madden, Mollie Marie (2014). The Black Prince at War: The Anatomy of a Chevauchée (PDF) (PhD thesis). Minnesota: University of Minnesota.</ref>
* Date unknown – [[Battle of Ihtiman]]: The [[Ottoman Turks]] defeat the [[Second Bulgarian Empire|Bulgarian Empire]] but suffer heavy losses and do not return to Bulgarian territory for around 15 years.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Asenov|first=Veselin|title=Michael Asen IV and Ivan Asen IV - the forgotten heroes|language=Bulgarian|url=https://bulgarianhistory.org/mihail-asen-ivan-asen-zabraveni-geroi/|journal=Bulgarian History|date=2018-03-19}}</ref>

1356.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–December ===
* [[January 20]] – [[Edward Balliol]] surrenders his title as King of Scotland, to [[Edward III]] of England.<ref>Hammond, Matthew (2019). "The Acts of Edward Balliol, king of Scots (1332–56)". The community of the realm in Scotland, 1249–1424. Retrieved June 15, 2023.</ref>
* ca. [[February]] – [[Burnt Candlemas]]: [[Edward III]] of England burns down every town and village in [[Lothian]], Scotland.
*[[June 17]] – The city of [[Lwów]] is granted [[Magdeburg rights]] by [[Casimir III the Great]], King of Poland. The advantages of the rights are not only economic, but also political.<ref>Oskar Halecki; W: F. Reddaway; J. H. Penson. The Law of Magdeburg used in Poland. The Cambridge History of Poland. CUP (Cambridge University Press) Archive. pp. 133–136. {{ISBN|1-001-28802-5}}. Retrieved June 16, 2023.</ref>
* [[September 19]] – [[Hundred Years' War]] – [[Battle of Poitiers]]: The English, commanded by [[Edward the Black Prince]], defeat the French. The greatly outnumbered English forces not only rout the French, but capture the French king [[John II of France]] and his youngest son, the future [[Philip the Bold]] of Burgundy.<ref>McKisack 1959, p. 139.</ref>
* [[October 17]] – [[Erik Magnusson, King of Sweden|Erik XII]] proclaims himself king of Sweden, in opposition to his father, King [[Magnus Eriksson|Magnus IV]]. Thus begins a civil war in Sweden between father and son, which will last until Erik's death in [[1359]].<ref>"Erik Magnusson". Svenskt biografiskt lexikon. Retrieved June 15, 2023.</ref>
* [[October 18]] (St Luke's Day) – The [[1356 Basel earthquake|Basel earthquake]] affects northern [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Switzerland]], with a maximum [[Medvedev–Sponheuer–Karnik scale|MSK]] intensity of IX–X (''Destructive–Devastating''), leaving around 1,000 dead. It is the most damaging intraplate earthquake known to have occurred in central Europe.<ref>1356 Basel Earthquake: A 650-Year Retrospective" (PDF). Risk Management Solutions. 2006. Archived from the original (PDF) on 29 February 2012. Retrieved 16 June 2023. The most damaging intraplate earthquake known to have occurred in central Europe.</ref>
* [[December 25]] – [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], promulgates the [[Golden Bull of 1356|Golden Bull]], a [[constitution]] for [[Holy Roman Empire|his empire]].<ref>Luxembourg, Charles IV (2 November 2019). The Golden Bull of 1356 AD. {{ISBN|978-1-9870-2740-2}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Hanseatic League]], a trading alliance between many cities in northern Europe, first meets.
* Sweden's first [[guild privileges]] (for tailors) are issued in [[Stockholm]].<ref>Lindström, Dag. 1991. Skrå, stad och stat. Stockholm, Malmö och Bergen ca 1350-1622. Acta Universitatis Upsaliensis: Uppsala.</ref>
* Ghazan II replaces [[Anushirwan]] as ruler of the [[Ilkhanate]] in [[Persia]].
* [[Zhu Yuanzhang]], one of the leaders in the [[Red Turban Rebellion]], captures the city of [[Nanjing]] from the [[Mongol]]-led [[Yuan dynasty]] in China; from then on it becomes his base of power, and the capital of a new dynasty he would establish in [[1368]], the [[Ming dynasty]].<ref>Ebrey (1999), 191.</ref>
* The majority of the [[Great Pyramid of Giza]]'s limestone casing stones are removed by [[Bahri dynasty|Bahri Sultan]] [[An-Nasir Hasan]], to build [[fortress]]es and [[mosque]]s in the nearby city of [[Cairo]], leaving the first of the [[Seven Wonders of the Ancient World]] in the step-stone condition in which it remains into modern times.
* The [[Castelvecchio Bridge]] in [[Verona]] is probably completed this year; its main span of {{convert|48.7|m|ft|abbr=on}} is the world's longest arch at this time.</onlyinclude>

1357.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–June ===
* [[January 7]] – The [[Diet of Metz (1356/57)|Diet of Metz]], which had been convened in the French city by the Holy Roman Emperor Charles Von November 17, is closed after two months.
* [[February 3]] – The [[Estates General (France)|Estates General]] in [[Kingdom of France|France]] meets and passes [[Étienne Marcel]]'s [[Great Ordinance of 1357|Great Ordinance]] in an attempt to impose limits on the [[French monarchy|monarchy]], in particular in fiscal and monetary matters.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Michelet|first1=Jules|last2=Smith|first2=G. H.|title=History of France: from the earliest period to the present time|year=1845|publisher=D. Appleton & Co.|page=442|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t2Je9tWfiZgC&q=Great+Ordinance+of+1357&pg=PA442|volume=1}}</ref>
* [[April 6]] – King Jean II of France, acting from his imprisonment at [[Bordeaux]], overules the Great Ordinance that had been approved on February 3 by the Estates General.<ref>{{cite book|first=Serge|last=Savisky|title=Les Valois dans la tourmente : l'ordonnance du 3 mars 1357|trans-title=The Valois in Turmoil  : The Ordinance of 3 March 1357|publisher=Canope|location=Chamalières|date=2001}}</ref>
* [[April 28]] – [[Eric XII of Sweden|Erik Magnusson]] is recognized as king of most of Sweden, in opposition to his father, King [[Magnus IV of Sweden|Magnus]]. The action takes place at a meeting of the Swedish nobility at [[Jönköping]], and Erik is granted control of Finland, Scania, the southern half of [[Halland]], and other parts of the Kingdom of Sweden.<ref>{{cite book|last=Schybergson|first=Magnus Gottfrid|title=Finlands historia|year=1903|publisher=G. W. Edlund|page=90|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ju4KAAAAIAAJ&q=28+april+1357|language=sv|volume=2}}</ref>
* [[May 28]] – [[Peter I of Portugal|Peter I]] becomes King of [[Kingdom of Portugal|Portugal]], after the death of his father, [[Afonso IV of Portugal|Alfonso IV]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia Americana|title=Oporto to Photoengraving|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eflGAAAAMAAJ&q=strengthened+royal+authority+by+vigorously|year=2004|publisher=Scholastic Library Publishing|volume=21|isbn=978-0-7172-0138-9|page=803}}</ref>
* [[June 4]] – The [[War of the Brabantian Succession]], a conflict over the successor to the late [[John III, Duke of Brabant|Jan III]] of the [[Duchy of Brabant]], comes to an end almost a year after it began on June 15, 1356, when the Peace of Ath is signed between the belligerents after being brokered by [[William I, Duke of Bavaria|Willem III, Count of Hainaut]].

=== July–December ===
* [[July 9]] – Construction formally begins on [[Charles Bridge]] in [[Prague]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Burton|first=Richard|title=Prague: a cultural and literary history|year=2003|publisher=Signal Books|isbn=978-1-902669-63-2|page=24|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=G0uaU8M2bosC&q=charles+bridge+9+July+1357&pg=PA24}}</ref>
* [[July 22]] – On the death of [[Jani Beg]], he is succeeded as Khan of the [[Blue Horde]] by his son [[Berdi Beg]]<ref>{{cite book|last1=Perrie|first1=Maureen|last2=Lieven|first2=D. C. B.|last3=Suny|first3=Ronald Grigor|title=The Cambridge History of Russia: From early Rus' to 1689|year=2006|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-81227-6|page=154|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GQcviLmjNm0C&q=Berdibek+1357&pg=PA154}}</ref> who orders the death of at least 12 of his close kinsmen to secure his position.
* [[July 26]] – (8 [[Sha'ban]] [[Islamic calendar|758 AH]]) A Mamluk assassin attacks [[Shaykhu|Sheikh Al-Omari Al-Nasiri]], the chief minister of the Sultan [[Al-Nasir Hasan]] of Egypt, and severely injures him with a sword.<ref>{{cite book|first=Howyda|last=Al-Harithy|title=The Encyclopaedia of Islam|publisher=BRILL|year=1996|isbn=9789004106338}}</ref>
* [[October 3]] – The [[Treaty of Berwick (1357)|Treaty of Berwick]] ends the [[Second War of Scottish Independence]] and King [[David II of Scotland]] is released by the English in return for a ransom of 100,000 [[mark (currency)|marks]] at a rate of 10,000 marks per year for ten years.<ref>{{cite book|last=Brown|first=Keith M.|editor-last=Tanner|editor-first=Roland|title=Parliament and politics in Scotland, 1235–1560|year=2004|publisher=Edinburgh University Press|isbn=978-0-7486-1485-1|page=16|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7SMfrAIkWksC&q=David+-+after+his+release+in+1357&pg=PA74}}</ref>
* [[November 6]] – Meeting at Scone, the Scottish Parliament votes to ratify the Treaty of Berwick and King David II returns home after 11 years.
* [[November 21]] – (26 [[Dhu'l-Qa'da]] [[Islamic calendar|758 AH]]) Sheikh Al-Omari Al-Nasiri dies from his injuries four months after being wounded by an assassin.

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Blue Horde]] unseats Ghazan II as the ruler of the [[Il-Khanate]], and appoints their own governor.
* [[Battle of Bubat]]: The [[Sunda Kingdom|Sundanese]] royal family is massacred by the Majapahit Army on the orders of [[Gajah Mada]]; the death toll includes Sundanese King Lingga Buana and Princess [[Dyah Pitaloka Citraresmi]], who commits suicide.
* Rao Kanhadev becomes [[Rathore dynasty|Rathore]] ruler of [[Marwar]] (part of modern-day [[India]]).<ref>{{cite book|last=Bunce|first=Frederick W.|title=Royal palaces, residences, and pavilions of India|year=2006|publisher=D.K. Printworld|isbn=978-81-246-0356-7|page=303|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VfjVAAAAMAAJ&q=Kanha+Dev+1357}}</ref>
* [[Influenza]] is first identified as a [[disease]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Raoult|first1=Didier|last2=Drancourt|first2=Michel|title=Paleomicrobiology: past human infections|year=2008|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-540-75854-9|page=200|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9P_4EwsZuC0C&q=In+1357%2C+an+epidemic+was+described+in+Florence&pg=PA200}}</ref>
* The first public exhibition of the [[Shroud of Turin]] is recorded.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Remarkable Metrological History of Radiocarbon Dating|publisher=DIANE Publishing|isbn=978-1-4223-1857-7|page=200|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bKoL_vPa47EC&q=Shroud+of+Turin+1357&pg=PA200|volume=2}}</ref>
* The [[Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat]] (Famous Wat Yai) Temple is constructed in [[Phitsanulok]], Thailand.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Eliot|first1=Joshua|last2=Bickersteth|first2=Jane|title=Thailand handbook|year=2003|publisher=Footprint Travel Guides|isbn=978-1-903471-54-8|page=214|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lg1t7IhJwsEC&q=Wat+Phra+Sri+Rattana+Mahathat+1357&pg=PA214|edition=2nd}}</ref></onlyinclude>

1358.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 10]] – [[Abu Inan Faris]], Sultan of Morocco of the [[Marinid dynasty]] is assassinated in a conspiracy by his [[vizier]], Faris bin Maymum, who has the Sultan strangled to death. [[Muhammad II ibn Faris]] becomes the new Sultan briefly before being replaced by [[Abu Bakr ibn Faris]]<ref>.{{cite book|last=Bosworth |first=Clifford E. |title=The New Islamic Dynasties|publisher=Edinburgh University Press |date=1996 |page=141 |isbn=978-0-231-10714-3}}</ref> 
* [[February 11]] – At [[Kalaburagi]] (now located in the [[Karnataka]] state of India), [[Mohammed Shah I]] becomes [[Bahmani Sultan]] of [[Deccan Plateau|Deccan]] after the death of Sultan [[Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.68551/page/76/mode/1up|first=Harroon Khan|last=Sherwani|title=The Bahmanis Of The Deccan|year=1946|page=76}}</ref><ref name="sen2">{{Cite book |last=Sen |first=Sailendra |title=A Textbook of Medieval Indian History |publisher=Primus Books |year=2013 |isbn=978-9-38060-734-4 |pages=106–108}}</ref>
* [[February 18]] – The [[Treaty of Zadar]] is signed between the [[Kingdom of Croatia (1102–1526)|Kingdom of Croatia]] and the [[Republic of Venice]]: The Venetians lose influence over their former Dalmatian holdings.
* [[February 23]] – [[Albert I of Bavaria|Albert of Wittelsbach, Duke of Bavaria]], is appointed as the Holy Roman Empire's [[regent]] for [[County of Holland|Holland]], and soon given control of [[County of Hainaut|Hainaut]], and [[County of Zeeland|Zeeland]], and assigned to suppress rebellions within what is now the [[Netherlands]] during the ongoing [[Hook and Cod wars]].<ref name=Waggenaar>{{citation |last=Wagenaar |first=Jan |title=Vaderlandsche historie |volume=III |publisher=Isaak Tirion|location=Amsterdam |year=1770|pages=293-296 }}</ref>
* [[March 16]] – King [[Haakon VI of Norway]] designates the city of [[Skien (town)|Skien]] as a city with trading privileges, making it the sixth town with city status in [[Norway]].

=== April–June ===
* [[April 6]] – A peace conference opens in [[Milan]] with participation by nearly all of the Italian kingdoms, republics and city states to discuss a war between a league of cites nadd Milan.<ref name=storia>{{Cite web |title=Storia di Milano ::: dal 1351 al 1375 |url=https://www.storiadimilano.it/cron/dal1351al1375.htm |website=www.storiadimilano.it}}</ref>
* [[May 8]] – The [[First Treaty of London]] is signed at [[Windsor Castle]] between [[Edward III|King Edward III]] of England and [[John II of France|King Jean II]] of France, who has been held prisoner of war in England since 1356. Under the terms of the treaty, the ransom for King Jean II and other prisoners of war retained as hostages is set at four million [[écu]]s, to be paid in six annual installments. France also agrees to cede one-fourth of its territory to England, and King Edward III renounces his claims to the throne of France. The amount of 4,000,000 écus represents most of France's income and payment proves to be financially impossible, leading to a renegotiation of the terms after France is unable to make its first payment on November 1. 
* [[May 28]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: The [[Jacquerie]] – A peasant rebellion begins in France, which consumes the [[Beauvais]], and allies with [[Étienne Marcel]]'s seizure of Paris. Over the three weeks that follow, the angry peasants, angry about the devastation caused in the and around Paris by the Kingdom of Navarre, murder members of the French nobility, destroy castles, and commit numerous atrocities.<ref name=Firnhaberbaker>Justine Firnhaber-Baker, The Jacquerie of 1358: A French Peasants' Revolt. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2021.</ref>
* [[June 8]] – After two months of negotiations, the treaty of Sant'Ambrogio is signed in Milan with Novara and Alba returned to the Visconti family and Asti and Pavia being kept by the Marquis of Montferrat.<ref name=storia/>
* [[June 10]] – The [[Jacquerie]] rebellion is brutally suppressed by French troops.<ref name=Firnhaberbaker/>
* [[June 17]] – [[Androin de la Roche]] abandons his two-month siege of the city of [[Forli]].<ref name=Roche>{{cite encyclopedia |first=Guillaume |last=Mollat |title=Androin de La Roche |editor1=[[Alfred Baudrillart]] |editor2=P. Richard |editor3=Albert Vogt |editor4=Urbain Rouziès |encyclopedia=[[Dictionnaire d'histoire et de géographie ecclésiastiques]] |volume=2 |location=Paris |publisher=Letouzey et Ané |year=1914 |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k6561037d/f909 |at=cols. 1770–1773}}</ref>
* [[June 27]] – The [[Republic of Ragusa]] is founded in what is now [[Croatia]], after being freed from the [[Republic of Venice]] by the Treaty of Zadar.<ref>Kenneth Meyer Setton (1978). The Papacy and the Levant, 1204–1571 Vol. 2, (Diane Publishing), ISBN 0-87169-127-2.</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 10]] – [[Battle of Mello]]: The [[Jacquerie]] rebellion is defeated by a coalition of nobles, led by [[Charles II of Navarre]].<ref>Firnhaber-Baker, Justine (2021). The Jacquerie of 1358 : a French peasants' revolt (First ed.). Oxford. ISBN 978-0-19-259835-6. OCLC 1255709650.</ref>
* [[July 25]] – De la Roche captures [[Meldola]] after a 24-day siege.<ref name=Roche/>
* [[August 22]] – [[Pietro Badoer]] of the Republic of Venice is named as the [[List of rulers of Crete#Dukes of Crete, 1209–1669|Duke of Crete]], Venice's governor over the nominally independent [[Kingdom of Candia]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Duca di Candia: Quaternus Consiliorum, 1340–1350 |editor-first=Paola |editor-last=Ratti Vidulich |publisher=Comitato per la pubblicazione delle fonti relative alla storia di Venezia |location=Venice |year=1976}}</ref>
* [[September 1]] – A [[Teutonic Knights|Teutonic knight]], Bonifacius Rotarius of Asti, becomes the first person known to have climbed to the top of the {{convert|11608|ft}} high  mountain [[Rocciamelone]], in the Italian Alps, bringing with him a small image of the Virgin Mary as a gesture of gratitude for having survived captivity in the [[Holy Land]] during a crusade against the Muslims.<ref name=lastampa>{{Cite news |title= L'alpinismo? È nato sul Rocciamelone  |work=[[La Stampa]]|location=Turin|date=July 30, 2008
|language=it |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080916195420/http://www.lastampa.it/Torino/cmsSezioni/viaggi/200807articoli/7758girata.asp}}</ref>, and begin an annual tradition of Catholics making a pilgrimage to the summit of Rocciamelone every August 5. 
* [[September 21]] – Badoer, Duke of Crete, meets with an ambassador sent from the Emirate of Menteshe to discuss trade between the two nations.<ref name=Thiriet/>
* [[September 29]] – [[Przemyslaus I Noszak]] become the new [[Duchy of Teschen|Duke of Teschen]] (now in Poland) upon the death of his father, [[Casimir I of Cieszyn]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 12]] – [[Hook and Cod wars]]: On orders of Albert, Duke of Holland, [[Dirk Loef of Horne]] provides 30 archers to aid in Albert's siege of Heusden, a rebellious city in the Netherlands, and the city surrenders in January.<ref>{{citation |last=Klaversma |first=Taede |year=1991 |work=Weert in woord en beeld: jaarboek voor Weert |volume=V  |title=De heren van Horne, Altena en Kortessem (1345 -1433) (vervolg) |publisher=Stichting Weerter Publikaties, Weert | url=http://www.showeert.nl/artikelen/1.1%20hornes;%20weert-wessem-horn//klaversma%20horne-weert%20jbw4,5,6.pdf |pages=29}}</ref>
* [[October 13]] – Badoer, on behalf of Crete, signs a treaty of peace and trade with the [[Menteshe|Emirate of Menteshe]], located in western Turkey and ruled by the Emir Musa.<ref name=Thiriet>{{cite book |editor-first=Freddy |editor-last=Thiriet |publisher=Mouton |location=Paris |year=1966 |volume=1: 1160–1363 |title=Délibérations des assemblées vénitiennes concernant la Romanie|page=241}}</ref>
* [[November 1]] – France defaults on its obligation to pay 600,000 [[écu]]s as the first installment on the 4,000,000 écus owed to England under the First Treaty of London.<ref>{{cite book |last=Rogers |date=2014 |orig-year=2000 |first=Clifford J. |title=War Cruel and Sharp: English Strategy under Edward III, 1327–1360 |publisher=Boydell Press |place=Woodbridge, Suffolk |pages=388-389|isbn=978-0-85115-804-4}}</ref>
* [[November 24]] – [[Hugh IV of Cyprus|Hugh IV]], King of Cyprus since 1324, abdicates and his son [[Peter I of Cyprus|Peter I]] becomes the new monarch.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Kingdom of Cyprus and the Crusades, 1191–1374 |first=Peter W. |last=Edbury |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1991 |pages=147-148}}</ref>
* [[December 4]] – [[Hook and Cod wars]]: Albert, Duke of Bavaria, begins the siege of [[Heemskerk Castle]] after an unsuccessful ambush against [[Reinoud I van Brederode]] by rebels. Heemskerk surrenders after almost four months, on March 24, 1359.<ref name=Waggenaar/>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Mubariz al-Din Muhammad]], leader of the Arab [[Muzaffarids of Iran|Muzaffarid]] tribe, expels the [[Blue Horde]] from [[Ilkhanate]] territory in [[Persia]]. The Muzaffarid then release control of the Il-Khanate, after being marched on by the [[Mongol]] [[Jalayirid]] tribe, ruled by [[Shaikh Uvais]]. Shaikh Uvais becomes the new Il-Khan. The Ilkhanate is effectively now disbanded, and replaced by the Jalayirid dynasty of Persia.
* Shah Shuja overthrows his father, Mubarazuddin Muhammad, as leader of the Muzaffarid tribe.
* Estimation: [[Nanjing]] in [[Yuan China]] becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from [[Hangzhou]] in [[Yuan China]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm |title=Geography at about.com |access-date=February 27, 2006 |archive-date=July 14, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070714185311/http://geography.about.com/library/weekly/aa011201a.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref></onlyinclude>

1361.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 24]] – The English Parliament is opened at Westminster by King [[Edward III]] for a 25-day session. 
* [[February 16]] – In what is now Spain, the Muslim Sultan [[Muhammad VI of Granada]] concludes a six-year treaty of alliance with the Christian [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pedro IV of Aragon]].<ref>{{EI2|last1=Latham|first1=John D.|last2=Fernández-Puertas|first2=Antonio|title=Naṣrids|volume=7|pages=1024|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/1573-3912_islam_COM_0855}}</ref>
* [[February 18]] – The English Parliament closes after a 25-day session. Among the acts passed and given royal assent are the [[Justices of the Peace Act 1361]], defining, for the first time, the duties and powers of a [[justice of the peace]] and setting for the qualifications required.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://statutes.org.uk/site/the-statutes/fourteenth-century/1361-34-edward-3-1-justices-of-peace/|title=1360: 34 Edward 3 c.1: Justices of the Peace|date=28 November 2017|work=The Statutes Project|access-date=26 May 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref>, as well as acts governing weights and measres, the limitation of purveyances to "the King, the Queen and the King's eldest son", several acts for punishment of labourers and servants for "departing from their service into another county," and directing that if they "If a labourer or servant do flee to a city or borough, do flee to a city or borough, the chief officer upon request shall deliver him up."<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |pages=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[March 17]] – [[An-Nasir Hasan]], [[Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo)|Mamluk Sultan]] of Egypt, is killed by one of his own [[mamluk]]s, [[Yalbugha al-Umari]], who, with the senior Mamluk emirs, has [[Al-Mansur Muhammad, Sultan of Egypt|al-Mansur Muhammad]] installed as the new sultan.<ref>Bauden, Frédéric. "The Qalawunids: A Pedigree" http://mamluk.uchicago.edu/qalawunids/qalawunid-pedigree.pdf  (PDF). University of Chicago. Retrieved 2023-06-21.</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 13]] – The [[University of Pavia]] is founded, on the [[Italian Peninsula]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.unipv.eu/site/en/home/about-us/history.html|title=History|website=www.unipv.eu|language=it|access-date=2017-10-10|archive-date=2017-12-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215221758/http://www.unipv.eu/site/en/home/about-us/history.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[May 1]] – King [[Magnus Eriksson]] of Sweden and Norway sends a letter to the citizens of [[Visby]], with a warning of an upcoming [[Battle of Visby|Danish invasion]].
* [[May 18]] – With the mediation of Cardinal [[Guy of Boulogne]], the legate of [[Pope Innocent VI]], the [[Terrer|Peace of Terrer]] is agreed upon in Spain by representatives of [[Peter of Castile|King Pedro of Castile]] and [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pedro IV of Aragon]] to end the [[War of the Two Pedros]] between Castile and Aragon. Boulogne returns to Avignon on November 8, but the treaty he negotiated is not ratified by either kingdom.<ref>{{cite book|first=Guillaume |last=Mollat |title=The Popes of Avignon: (1305-1378)|edition=2d|location=Paris |publisher=LeCoffre |year=1912|pages=288-299}}</ref> 
* [[June 24]] – Thirteen years after the [[Black Death]] disease came to England, a two-day spike in deaths occurs in [[London]] with 1,200 people dying from the bubonic plague on June 24 and June 25.<ref>{{cite book|last=Shrewsbury|first=J. F. D. |title=A History of Bubonic Plague in the British Isles|year=1970|publisher=Cambridge University Press|page=129|isbn=978-0-52102-247-7}}</ref>
* [[June]] – [[Ahi Ayna]], monarch of the [[Emirate of Erzincan]] in what is now eastern [[Turkey]] leads an expedition of conquest into the [[Kingdom of Georgia]], capturing [[Akhaltsikhe]], [[Samtskhe–Javakheti|Samstskhe]], and [[Atsquri Fortress|Atsquri]], taking 12,000 people captive and collecting the ''jizya'', a special tax on non-Muslims.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yücel |first1=Yaşar |title=Mutahharten ve Erzincan Emirliği |trans-title=Mutahharten and the Emirate of Erzincan |journal=Belleten |date=October 1971 |volume=35 |issue=140 |page=669 |url=https://belleten.gov.tr/tam-metin-pdf/3032/tur |language=tr}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 27]] – [[Battle of Visby]]: King [[Valdemar IV of Denmark]] conquers the city of  [[Visby]] by defeating the defending [[Gutnish]] country yeomen, killing 1,200 of their number, and takes [[Gotland]]. To avert being sacked and looted, the leaders of Visby pay a large ransom to King Valdemar, which is collected in payments by sheriffs sent regularly to the city for tribute.<ref>Lihammer, Anna (2011). "Slaget om Visby". Arkeologiska upptäckter i Sverige. Lund: Historiska Media ISBN 978-91-85873-96-8</ref>
* [[August 3]] – (24th day of 6th month of [[Shōhei|Shōhei 16]]) The [[1361 Shōhei earthquake|Shōhei earthquake]], estimated centuries later as being at least 8.4 magnitude, strikes off of the eastern coast of Japan and causes a [[tsunami]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Earthquake Information|url=https://www.waterdamagedefense.com/pages/emergency-preparedness-earthquakes-information|access-date=2021-06-28|website=Water Damage Defense|language=en}}</ref> which sweeps 1,700 houses and their thousands of inhabitants around Yukinominato Bay out to sea.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.histeq.jp/kaishi/HE31/HE31_075_079_Ishibashi.pdf|title=Did the top of the nine-ringed finial of the Horyu-ji Temple's five-story pagoda really burn during the 1361 Kōan Nankai Earthquake?|first=Katsuhiko |last=Ishibashi |year=2016 |journal=Historical Earthquakes|language=jp|issue=31|pages=75-79}}</ref>
* [[August 6]] – The Emir Ahi Ayna guides his army into the Empire of Trebizond and besieges the cities of Lazica, Golacha and Koukos.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shukurov |first1=Rustam |title=Between Peace and Hostility: Trebizond and the Pontic Turkish Periphery in the Fourteenth Century |journal=Mediterranean Historical Review |date=June 1994 |volume=9 |issue=1 |page=33 |publisher=Routledge}}</ref> 
* [[August 23]] – King [[Peter I of Cyprus]] lands 10 ships at [[Antalya]] in what is now Turkey and, after a one-day siege, conquers the city<ref>.{{cite book |first=D'Arcy Jonathan Dacre |last=Boulton |title=The Knights of the Crown: The Monarchical Orders of Knighthood in Later Medieval Europe, 1325–1520 |year=1987 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Pv1RUpw5ss4C&pg=PA241 |publisher=The Boydell Press |pages=241-249}}</ref> 
* [[September 22]] – King Peter and his fleet arrive back in Cyprus after bringing back spoils of war and tributes from various regions of Asia Minor.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Armenian Kingdom in Cilicia During the Crusades |first=Jacob G. |last=Ghazarian |publisher=Routledge |year=2000|pages=166-168}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 10]] – [[Edward the Black Prince]] marries [[Joan of Kent]] at [[Windsor Castle]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=Palmer, Alan|last2=Palmer |first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|isbn= 0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[October]] – A force of 200,000 soldiers of the [[Red Turban Rebellions|Red Turbans]] of [[Yuan dynasty]] China, unable to retreat to China's [[Heibei]] region, cross the [[Yalu|Yalu River]] and invade northern Korea, ruled by the kingdom of Goryeo. Led by Pan Cheng, Sha Liu, Guan Xiansheng, and Zhu Yuanshu, they capture Sakju and Iseong, and then assemble at Muju (now [[Yeongbyeon]] by early November.
* [[November 11]] – China's Red Turbans break through the Korean defense line at Jeoryeong, and King [[Gongmin of Goryeo]] is forced to evacuate his capital at [[Gaegyeong]] (now [[Kaesong]], North Korea) and to flee to Bokju (now [[Andong]], [[North Gyeongsang Province]], [[South Korea]]).<ref name=Jeong/>
* [[November 21]] – [[Philip of Rouvres]], the 15-year old [[Duke of Burgundy]], dies from the plague has no heirs, bringing an end to rule by the House of Capet and leaving the Duchy open to conquest by King Jean II of France.
* [[November 24]] – China's Red Turbans, already occupying much of the Goryeo Kingdom (now North Korea), invade the capital city of Gaegyeong and burn down the royal palace.<ref name=Jeong>{{cite book|editor=Jeong Hae-eun|title=고려시대 군사전략|trans-title=Military Strategy of the Goryeo Dynasty |publisher=Military History Compilation Institute, Ministry of National Defense|page=294|language=ko}}</ref>
* [[December 21]] – The [[Battle of Linuesa]] is fought between invaders from the [[Emirate of Granada]] and defenders from the [[Kingdom of Castile]] at the city of [[Huesa]] in Castile's autonomous [[Kingdom of Jaén]] (now the Jaén Province of Spain). The Castilian Army, led by the Christian [[Diego García de Padilla]], is able to defeat the Muslim troops of Granada. Most of the 600 Granadan troops are slaughtered before they can retreat.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_BswWAAAAQAAJ |last=López de Ayala |first=Pero |author2=Pero López de Ayala |title=Cronicas de los reyes de Castilla: Don Pedro, Don Enrique II, Don Juan I, Don Enrique III| chapter=8 |publisher=Imprenta de Don Antonio de Sancha |year=1779 |location=Madrid |pages=335-336}}</ref>
* [[December 28]] – [[John II of France|King Jean II of France]], nicknamed "John the Good" in English accounts, invades and takes control of the Duchy of Burgundy.<ref name=Schnerb1999-2>{{Cite book | last = Schnerb | first = Bertrand | title = L'État bourguignon (1363-1477) | publisher = Perrin | year = 1999 | location = Paris |chapter=Chapter 2 |language=fr |quote = Five days later, on December 28, the king had the Estates of the Duchy of Burgundy, that is, the representatives of the Church, the nobles, and the townspeople, assembled before him at Saint-Bénigne.}}</ref> He chooses to keep the Duchy as a separate state with himself as Duke, rather than to annex it to the Kingdom of France.<ref>{{cite book |last=Vaughan |first=Richard |title=Philip the Bold: The Formation of the Burgundian State |publisher=Boydell Press |year=2002 |chapter = Chapter 1 |quote=King John at once laid claim to and took possession of this important fief which, if it could have been incorporated into the royal domain, would have greatly increased the power and the income of the crown. But the local particularism of the inhabitants, coupled with King John's generous feelings towards his youngest son, made this impossible.}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* In the [[Marinid]] Empire in modern-day [[Morocco]], [[Abu Salim Ibrahim]] is overthrown by Abu Umar, who is in turn overthrown by Abu Zayyan.
* [[Great Troubles]]: the [[Blue Horde]] descends into anarchy. Between 1361 and [[1378]], over 20 khans succeed each other in different parts of the Blue Horde's territory.
* [[Ottoman Emirate]] conquered [[Didymoteicho]]
* [[China|Chinese]] rebels capture the [[Goryeo]] capital.
* The earliest known [[musical keyboard]] instrument is built, with the layout of black and white keys that becomes standard.</onlyinclude><ref>[[File:Syntagma_musicum025.gif|left|thumb|Keyboards of [[Halberstadt organ|Nicholas Faber's organ]] for [[Halberstadt]], built in 1361 and enlarged 1495. The illustration is from [[Michael Praetorius|Praetorius]]' ''[[Syntagma Musicum]]'' (1619). At the top is the earliest example of the "seven plus five" layout. The bottom two illustrate the earlier "eight plus four" arrangement]]
.</ref>

1362.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 1]] – The [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] switches [[New Year]] to January 1, before any other country does.
* [[January 16]] – The "[[Saint Marcellus's flood|Grote Mandrenke]]" [[storm tide]] kills more than 25,000 people after striking the [[Netherlands]], England, Germany and [[Denmark]] on the feast day of Saint Marcellus, and destroying the Danish settlement of [[Rungholt]] in the [[Duchy of Schleswig]], and the [[Humber]] estuary port of [[Ravenser Odd]] in England.<ref>{{cite web|first=Stephen |last=Moss |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2011/jan/20/weatherwatch-grote-mandrenke |title=Weatherwatch: The Grote Mandrenke|work=The Guardian |date=January 20, 2011}}</ref> The [[East Frisian Islands|East Frisian island]] of [[Buise]] is broken into two islands by [[North Sea]] floods.
* [[February 7]] – General [[Hu Dahai]], the chief military adviser to the Chinese warlord [[Hongwu Emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]], the future Emperor of China and the ruler of most of the Anhui and Jiangsu provinces, is assassinated by General Jiang Ying after being lured to the city of [[Jinhua]] in the [[Zhejiang]] on the pretext of reviewing the troops. Distracting Hu, Jiang kills him with an iron hammer, as well as killing two other visitors, Hu Guanzhu and Geng Zaicheng.
* [[February 15]] – King [[Haakon VI]] of Norway, son of King [[Magnus Eriksson]] of [[Sweden]], proclaims himself king of Sweden in opposition to his father.<ref name=Nordberg>{{cite book|last=Nordberg|first=Michael|title=I kung Magnus tid: Norden under Magnus Eriksson (1317–1374)|publisher=Norstedt|page=77 |isbn=9789119521224}}</ref> However, later in the year, father and son are reconciled and rule Sweden together.
* [[March 13]] – Sultan [[Muhammad V of Granada]], returns to the throne after the usurper [[Muhammad VI of Granada|Muhammed VI]] flees the Alhambra and seeks asylum from King Pedro I of Castile.<ref name=Fernandez>{{cite journal |title=The Three Great Sultans of al-Dawla al-Ismā'īliyya al-Naṣriyya Who Built the Fourteenth-Century Alhambra: Ismā'īl I, Yūsuf I, Muḥammad V (713–793/1314–1391) |first=Antonio |last=Fernández-Puertas |journal=Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society |volume=7 |number=1 |page=18 |date=1997|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]}}</ref>
* [[March 20]] – [[Simon Sudbury]] is consecrated as the [[Bishop of London]], serving in the office until becoming the [[Archbishop of Canterbury]] in 1375.<ref>{{cite book |author1=Fryde, E. B. |author2=Greenway, D. E. |author3=Porter, S. |author4=Roy, I. |title=Handbook of British Chronology|publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |year=1996 |page=258|isbn=0-521-56350-X }}</ref>
* [[March]] –
**[[Murad I]] succeeds his father [[Orhan]] as sultan of the [[Ottoman Empire]].
**The nation of [[Champa]] (now in southern Vietnam), ruled by King [[Po Binasuor]], raids the Hóa Châu prefecture of [[Đại Việt]] (now in northern Vietnam), then withdraws.<ref>Ngô Sĩ Liên (1993), [[Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư]], page 257, Volume VII, "Dụ Tông hoàng đế"</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 6]]
** [[Battle of Brignais]]: The [[Free Companies]] defeat a French army.
** A fire destroys much of [[St Patrick's Cathedral, Dublin|St Patrick's Cathedral]] in [[Dublin]].<ref name=Fires>"Fires, Great", in ''The Insurance Cyclopeadia: Being an Historical Treasury of Events and Circumstances Connected with the Origin and Progress of Insurance'', Cornelius Walford, ed. (C. and E. Layton, 1876) p27</ref>
* [[April 17]] – [[Kaunas Castle]] in Lithuania falls to the [[Teutonic Order]], after a [[Siege of Kaunas (1362)|month-long siege]].
* [[April 25]] – After the former Sultan [[Muhammad VI of Granada]] arrives in the Crown of Castile, King Pedro I not only denies him asylum, but has him executed.<ref name=Fernandez/>
* [[May 1]] – [[Ulrich IV of Württemberg|Ulrich IV]], co-ruler with his brother [[Eberhard II, Count of Württemberg|Eberhard II]] as [[Count of Württemberg]] in Germany, is forced by the Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV to resign after his insistence that Württemberg be divided between the two counts. As compensation, Ulrich receives [[Hohenneuffen Castle]] and several towns and castles.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Schöntag |first=Wilfried |title=Neue Deutsche Biographie |title-link=Neue Deutsche Biographie |year=2016 |edition=Online |volume=26 |pages=596–597 |language=de |chapter=Ulrich III. |access-date=6 March 2024 |chapter-url=https://www.deutsche-biographie.de/pnd135931231.html#ndbcontent}}</ref> 
* [[May 26]] – [[Joanna I of Naples|Giovanna I di Napoli]] becomes the sole ruler of the [[Kingdom of Naples]] after the death, from bubonic plague, of her husband, [[Louis I of Naples|King Ludovico di Napoli]], with whom she had allowed the sharing of power since their marriage in 1347.<ref>{{cite book |last=Boulton|first=D'Arcy Jonathan Dacre|title=The Knights of the Crown: The Monarchical Orders of Knighthood in Later Medieval Europe, 1325–1520 |publisher=Boydell Press |year=2000 |isbn=0851157955 |page=214}}</ref>
* [[June 8]] – [[Pir Husayn]], ruler of Karahisar, invades the Emirate of Erzincan to confront the Emir Ahi Ayna.
* [[June 22]] – An alliance is formed between the [[Kingdom of England]] and the [[Crown of Castile]].<ref name=CBH>{{cite book|last=Palmer|first=Alan |last2=Palmer |first2=Veronica |year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=106–108|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[June]] – Under the terms of the will of Sir [[John de Wingfield]] (died 1361), the church of St. Andrew and a college of priests are founded in [[Wingfield, Suffolk]], England.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 3]] – [[Ahi Ayna]], the Emir of Erzincan and conqueror of much of eastern Turkey, the Kingdom of Georgia and the Kingdom of Trebizond and reportedly dies as a [[martyr]] after Pir Husayn's invasion of the emirate.<ref name=Shukurov>{{cite journal |last1=Shukurov |first1=Rustam |title=Between Peace and Hostility: Trebizond and the Pontic Turkish Periphery in the Fourteenth Century |journal=Mediterranean Historical Review |date=June 1994 |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=35–36 |publisher=Routledge}}</ref> 
* [[July 8]] – [[Valdemar IV of Denmark]] defeats the [[Hanseatic League]] in the naval [[Battle of Helsingborg (1362)|Battle of Helsingborg]].
* [[July 10]] – [[Pir Husayn]] becomes the new Emir of Erzincan.<ref name=Shukurov/>
* [[August 14]] – King Edward III summons the English Parliament members to assemble at Westminster on October 13.
* [[August 22]] – In what is now [[Croatia]], peace is concluded at [[Nikšić|Onogoste]] (now Nikšić in [[Montenegro]])  between he [[Republic of Ragusa]] and Prince [[Vojislav Vojinović]] of the Republic of [[Dubrovnik]].<ref>{{citation| last=Blagojević |first=Miloš |title= Državna uprava u srpskim srednjovekovnim zemljama |trans-title= State Administration in Serbian Medieval Countries |edition= 2nd |year= 2001 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=srAVAQAAIAAJ | publisher= Službeni list SRJ |place=Belgrade |page=178|isbn=86-355-0497-6 |language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{citation |last= Mihaljčić |first= Rade |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=V3FpAAAAMAAJ |title= Kraj srpskog carstva |trans-title=The End of the Serbian Empire |publisher= Beogradski izdavačko-grafički zavod| place=Belgrade |year=1989 |pages=37–39|isbn= 978-86-13-00346-5 |orig-date=1975 |language=sr}}</ref>
* [[September 7]] – [[Joan of the Tower|Joan, Queen of Scots]], the Queen consort of Scotland, wife of [[David II of Scotland|King David II]] and sister of [[Edward III|King Edward III of England]], dies at Hertfordshire in England at the age of 41 after having been separated from David for many years.<ref>{{cite book |last=Warner |first=Kathryn |title=Philippa of Hainault: Mother of the English Nation |year=2020 |publisher=Amberley Publishing |page=310|isbn=978-1-4456-6280-0}}</ref>
* [[September 22]] – A [[1362 conclave|papal concave]] begins at the [[Palais des Papes]] in [[Avignon]] as 20 of the Roman Catholic cardinals meet to elect a successor to [[Pope Innocent VI]], who had died on September 12.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/papalconclavesa01trolgoo |first=Thomas Adolphus |last=Trollope|title=The Papal Conclaves, as They Were and as They Are |publisher=Chapman and Hall |year= 1876 |page=98}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 13]] – The [[English Parliament]] is opened for the first time with a speech in [[English language|English]], as delivered by the Lord Chancellor, after having been opened for centuries with a speech in [[Latin language|Latin]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/history/11156904/The-slang-words-that-defined-the-First-World-War.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018004128/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/history/11156904/The-slang-words-that-defined-the-First-World-War.html|archive-date=October 18, 2014|title=The slang words that defined the First World War|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=Oct 13, 2014|access-date=October 24, 2014}}</ref> Under [[Edward III]], the [[Pleading in English Act 1362|Pleading in English Act]] makes [[English language|English]] rather than [[Law French]] the official language in English law courts.<ref name=CBH/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://languageandlaw.org/TEXTS/STATS/PLEADING.HTM|title=Statute of Pleading|year=1362|publisher=Language and Law.org|access-date=2014-02-03}}</ref> [[Henry Green (English judge)|Sir Henry Green]], Chief Justice of the King's Speech, is elected as the Speaker of the House of Lords.
* [[October 28]] – [[Pope Urban V|Guillaume de Grimoard]], the apostolic legate to the [[Kingdom of Naples]], is selected ''[[Election in absentia|in absentia]]'' as the new Pope of the Roman Catholic Church after 30 days of disagreements in Avignon on a successor, in that none of the proposed candidates receives the require two-thirds (14 of 20) necessary votes. Rather than informing Grimoard of his election, the cardinals send a message to Florence, stating that they wish to consult with him at Avignon, in that Grimoard (who wishes to keep the papacy at Avignon rather than returning it to Rome) might be detained by authorities in Italy. Grimoard reaches Avignon after nine days of travel from Florence, and takes the papal name of [[Pope Urban V]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Baumgartner|first=Frederic J.|title= Behind Locked Doors: A History of the Papal Elections |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |year=2003|page=54 |isbn=0-312-29463-8}}</ref>
* [[October 30]] – The English Parliament ends its session after 17 days, and [[royal assent]] is given by King Edward III to laws passed therein, including the Purveyance Acts 1363, limiting government purchases to the King and Queen (or authorized representatives), and penalties for purveyors who violate the law, as well as the Parliament Act 1363 ("A parliament shall be holden once in the year.")<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of and Index to the Statutes |edition=13th |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1896 |volume=1: To the End of the Session 59 Vict. Sess. 2 (1895) |url={{GBurl|EfcZAAAAYAAJ|page=28}} |pages=28 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[November 6]] – [[Pope Urban V]] is crowned after his arrival in [[Avignon]] and his consecration as a bishop of the Roman Catholic Church, after having been elected on October 28.
* [[November 13]] – [[Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence|Lionel of Antwerp]], the second son of King [[Edward III]] of England, is created [[Duke of Clarence]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Lionel-of-Antwerp-duke-of-Clarence|title=Lionel of Antwerp, duke of Clarence {{!}} English noble|work=Encyclopædia Britannica|access-date=2018-01-24|language=en}}</ref> and [[John of Gaunt]], King Edward's third son, is created [[Duke of Lancaster]]<ref>{{Cite EB1911 |wstitle= Lancaster, John of Gaunt, duke of |volume= 16 |last= Kingsford |first= Charles Lethbridge |pages = 146–147}}</ref> 
* [[December 5]] – The [[Battle of Launac]] is fought in France between [[John II of Armagnac|Jean II, Count of Armagnac]] and [[Gaston III of Foix|Gaston III Febus, Count of Foix]]. Not only does Febus triumph in battle, supported by a archers for Foix who fire a volley of arrows into the Armagnac cavalry, Count Jean II and most of the Armagnac leaders are captured as prisoners of war and held for a total ransom of 600,000 gold [[florin]]s, each with 3.5g of pure gold, equal to 2,100 kilograms (more than 74,000 ounces) of gold. Of this, 300,000 florins are paid for the release of Count Jean.<ref>{{cite book |title=Lord of the Pyrenees: Gaston Fébus, Count of Foix |last=Vernier |first=Richard |year=2008 |publisher=Boydell Press |location=Woodbridge |isbn= 978-1-84383-356-7|pages=58 }}</ref>
* [[December 21]] – [[Constantine IV of Armenia|Constantine IV]] succeeds his cousin, [[Constantine III of Armenia|Constantine III]], as [[King of Armenia]].

=== Date unknown ===
* Autumn 1362 or [[1363]] – [[Battle of Blue Waters]]: [[Grand Duke of Lithuania]] [[Algirdas]] defeats the [[Golden Horde|Tatars]], and takes over [[Kyiv]].
* [[Red Turban Rebellions]]: [[Hu Dahai]], aide to [[Zhu Yuanzhang]], is killed by [[Miao people|Miao]] chieftains in Yanzhou (part of modern-day [[Jinhua]] and [[Hangzhou]]).<ref name=Ming>''[[History of Ming]]'', ''[https://zh.wikisource.org/zh-hans/%E6%98%8E%E5%8F%B2_(%E5%9B%9B%E5%BA%AB%E5%85%A8%E6%9B%B8%E6%9C%AC)/%E5%8D%B7133 Vol.133]''</ref> [[Chaghan Temur]] is killed and succeeded by his nephew [[Köke Temür]].
* The [[Ottoman Turks|Ottomans]] capture [[Plovdiv|Philippopolis]] (or in 1364, 1371) and [[Adrianopole]] (the modern-day city of [[Edirne]], or in 1369) from the [[Byzantine Empire]], reducing its territory to the city of [[Constantinople]], part of the [[Peloponessus]], and some islands.
* The [[Öræfajökull]] volcano erupts in Iceland, resulting in the destruction of the district of [[Litlahérað]] by flood and [[tephra]] fall.
* The [[English College, Rome|English Hospice]] of the Most Holy Trinity and St Thomas is founded in [[Rome]]. It goes on to become the [[English College, Rome|English College]], a centre for training English priests in Rome.</onlyinclude>

1363.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 4]] – The Lombardy towns of [[Magenta, Lombardy|Magenta]] and [[Corbetta, Lombardy|Corbetta]] are captured from the control of Galeazzo Visconti by British mercenaries hired by the Marquis of Monferrato, [[William VII of Montferrat|Guglielmo VII Aleramici]].
* [[February 21]] – [[Simon Langham]] is appointed by King Edward III as the new [[List of lord chancellors and lord keepers|Lord Chancellor of England]] after the retirement of the Chancellor [[William Edington]].<ref>{{cite book |author1=Fryde, E. B. |author2=Greenway, D. E. |author3=Porter, S. |author4=Roy, I. |title=Handbook of British Chronology|edition=Third revised |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |year=1996 |page=86|isbn=0-521-56350-X}}</ref>
* [[March 14]] – [[Gabriele Adorno]] is elected as the new [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Genoa]] following the sudden death of the Doge [[Simone Boccanegra]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/gabriele-adorno_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29|author=Giuseppe Oreste|title=Adorno, Gabriele|encyclopedia=[[Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani]]|publisher= Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana|volume=1|year=1960}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 9]] – King [[Haakon VI of Norway]] marries  [[Margaret I of Denmark|Princess Margrethe of Estridsen]], the daughter of King [[Valdemar IV of Denmark]] in a ceremony at the [[Copenhagen Cathedral]].<ref>{{citation |last=Etting|first=Vivian|year=2009 |title=Margrete den første |publisher=Nordisk Forlag A/S |page=16 |isbn=978-8702071771}}</ref> Margrethe will become Queen of Denmark in 1387 after Haakon's death.
* [[May 7]] – (12 [[Pashons]] [[Coptic calendar|1080 AM]]) In Egypt, the bishop Youhanna of Damascus is elected as the new [[List of popes of the Coptic Orthodox Church|Pope of the Coptic Orthodox Christians]] and takes the regnal name of [[Pope John X of Alexandria]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Meinardus |first=Otto F.A. |author-link=Otto Friedrich August Meinardus |title=Two Thousand Years of Coptic Christianity |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Cmey73GtfuUC&pg=PA273 |year=2002 |publisher=American University in Cairo Press |isbn=978-977-424-757-6 }}</ref>. He serves until his death on July 13, 1369.
* [[May 8]] – [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]] and his former son-in-law, [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]] meet at [[Uherské Hradiště]] (now in the Czech Republic) to conclude a peace agreement to avoid a battle over control of Bohemia.<ref>{{cite book |last=Udvardy |first=József |year=1991 |title=A kalocsai érsekek életrajza (1000–1526)|trans-title=Biographies of Archbishops of Kalocsa, 1000–1526|publisher=[[Görres Society|Görres Gesellschaft]]|page=229|language=hu}}</ref>
* [[May 29]] – [[Al-Ashraf Sha'ban]] is installed as the Sultan of Egypt at the age after the Emir [[Yalbugha al-Umari]] leads a coup d'etat against the Sultan [[Al-Mansur Muhammad, Sultan of Egypt|Al-Mansur Muhammad]], who had reigned for two years.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Steenbergen|first1=Jo Van|title=The Amir Yalbughā al-Khāṣṣakī, the Qalāwūnid Sultanate, and the Cultural Matrix of Mamlūk Society: A Reassessment of Mamlūk Politics in the 1360s|journal=Journal of the American Oriental Society|date=September 2011|volume=131|issue=3|jstor=41380710|publisher=American Oriental Society|pages=437}}</ref>
* [[June 1]] – [[Edward III|King Edward III]] of England summons the English Parliament, directing the members to assemble at Westminster on October 6.
* [[June 15]] – at the age of 2, [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Prince Wenceslaus of Luxembourg]], the son of [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], is crowned at [[St. Vitus Cathedral]] in [[Prague]] as Vaclav IV, [[King of Bohemia]], the position formerly held by his father. The Archbishop of Prague, [[Arnošt of Pardubice]], places the crown on the head of the child, despite his protest that crowning an infant is a mockery of the coronation ceremony.<ref>{{cite book|first=Jiri|last=Spéváček|title=Václav IV. 1361–1419. K předpokladům husitské revoluce |trans-title=Wenceslas IV (1361–1419): On the Presuppositions of the Hussite Revolution |location=Prague |publisher=Nakladatelsvi Svoboda |year=1986|pages=45–47}}</ref> 
* [[June 29]] – [[Edward, the Black Prince]], son of King Edward III of England and heir to the English throne, arrives in [[Bordeaux]] to become the new administrator of the [[Duchy of Aquitaine]], a principality that had been ceded by France to England under the [[Treaty of Bretigny]].<ref>{{cite book |first=Pierre |last=Tucoo-Chala |title=Gaston Fébus, prince des Pyrénées |publisher= Ėditions Deucalion |year= 1991|page=117|isbn= 2-906483-43-5|language=fr}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 1]] – [[Louis I of Anjou|Louis, Duke of Anjou]], the son of the French King [[John II of France|John the Good]], arrives in France after having been held a hostage in London since 1360 in exchange for King John's release from captivity as a prisoner of war. The escape leads to a crisis that ends with King John's voluntary return to imprisonment in England six months later.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HbTTn3C3GtYC&pg=PA163 |last1=Kosto |first1=Adam J. |title=Hostages in the Middle Ages |date=2012 |publisher=Oxford University Press  |page=163  |isbn=9780199651702}}</ref>  
* [[July 2]] – An envoy of Pope Urban V, [[Jean de la Grange]], arranges the signing of the [[:es:Paz de Murviedro|Peace of Morvedre]] (now [[Sagunto]] in Spain) to end the "[[War of the Two Pedros]]  between [[Peter of Castile|King Pedro of Castile]] (aided by England and other nations) and [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pedro IV of Aragon]] (aided by France), but neither side attempts to ratify the accords. Fighting continues until 1369 when Pedro of Castile is overthrown and replaced by [[Henry II of Castile|Enrique de Trastámara]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Mario|last=Lafuente Gomez|title=La guerra de los Dos Pedros en Aragón (1356-1366): Impacto y trascendencia de un conflicto bajomedieval |trans-title=The War of the Two Peters in Aragon (1356-1366): Impact and Transcendence of a Late Medieval Conflict |publisher=University of Zaragoza|year=2009|pages=93-95|isbn=}}</ref>
* [[July 8]] – [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos I of Hungary]] leads an attack on [[Sokograd]] in [[Bosnia]] and begins a three-day siege that is defended by [[Vukac Hrvatinić]], whose son [[Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić]] will later become the Grand Duke of Bosnia. The Bosnian defense saves the city and King Lajos is forced to retreat with his troops back to Hungary after three days.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Fine |first=John Van Antwerp Jr. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y0NBxG9Id58C |title=The Early Medieval Balkans: A Critical Survey from the Sixth to the Late Twelfth Century |publisher=University of Michigan Press |year=1994 |page=369|isbn=0472081497}}</ref>
* [[August 8]] – The [[Revolt of Saint Titus]], against the rule of the [[Republic of Venice]] in the [[Kingdom of Candia]] (island of [[Crete]]), begins.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=McKee |first=Sally |title=The Revolt of St Tito in fourteenth-century Venetian Crete: A reassessment |journal=Mediterranean Historical Review |volume=9 | number=2|date=December 1994 |pages= 173–204 }}</ref>
* [[August 15]] – The Army of China's rebel leader [[Zhu Wenzheng]] marches from [[Nanjing]] with 100,000 troops toward the Han State to  confront [[Zhang Shicheng]]. 
* [[August 30]]– The [[Battle of Lake Poyang]], one of the [[Largest naval battle in history|largest naval battles in history]] begins in [[Yuan dynasty]] [[China]] between multiple ships and 650,000 rebels led by [[Chen Youliang]], against a smaller force of 200,000 troops led by the [[Red Turban Rebellion|Red Turban Rebel]] [[Zhu Yuanzhang]] and continues for five weeks.
* [[September 6]] – [[Philip the Bold]] (''Philippe II le Hardi''), son of King [[John II of France|John the Good]] (''Jean le Bon'') is secretly designated as the new [[Duke of Burgundy]] by the King after the death of the previous Duke, [[Philip of Rouvres]]. <ref>{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Philip the Bold |volume=21 |page=386 |first=René |last=Poupardin}}</ref> Previously, [[Guillaume IV de Melun]], [[:fr:Comté de Tancarville|Count of Tancarville]], had been administrator of Burgundy since the death in 1361 of the prior Duke, [[Philip of Rouvres]], until King John had become dissatisfied with him.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 4]] – The [[Battle of Lake Poyang]] ends as [[Zhu Yuanzhang]] and his Red Turban Rebels defeat the rebels led by [[Chen Youliang]].
* [[October 6]] – The English Parliament is opened at Westminster for a 24-day session.
* [[October 30]] – King Edward III gives [[royal assent]] to laws passed by the Parliament as its session closes, including the ''[[Statute Concerning Diet and Apparel 1363]]'', a [[sumptuary law]] limiting the style of clothing that people of different classes were allowed to wear, aimed at halting a trend by lower class and middle class to wear fashions similar to more wealthy English citizens, as well as requiring higher prices for "hen, capon, pullet and goose". The new law has 19 chapters setting the dress code for "handicraftsmen and yeomen" (c. 9), "gentlemen under the estate of knights" (c.10), merchants (c.11), knights with lands of a value of 200 marks and knights with lands of 400 marks (c.12), clerks (c.13), and ploughmen (c.14).<ref>{{cite book | last=Emberley |first=Julia V. |title=Venus and furs: the cultural politics of fur |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hRFpheymYZ0C |publisher=[[I.B. Tauris]] | year=1998 | location=London | page=46 | isbn=978-1-86064-227-2}}</ref>
* [[November 26]] – [[Pope Urban V]] selects Cardinal [[Androin de la Roche]] to replace Cardinal [[Gil Álvarez Carrillo de Albornoz]] as the papal negotiator to establish peace with the Lord of Milan, [[Bernabò Visconti]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |first=Guillaume |last=Mollat |title=Androin de La Roche |editor1=[[Alfred Baudrillart]] |editor2=P. Richard |editor3=Albert Vogt |editor4=Urbain Rouziès |encyclopedia=[[Dictionnaire d'histoire et de géographie ecclésiastiques]] |volume=2 |location=Paris |publisher=Letouzey et Ané |year=1914 |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k6561037d/f909 |pages=1770–1773}}</ref>
* [[December 20]] – [[John de Coupland]], the ruthless [[Sheriff of Northumberland]] in [[England]] who had taken King [[David II of Scotland]] as a [[prisoner of war]] for 11 years following the 1346 [[Battle of Neville's Cross]], is assassinated by a group of his enemies as he is trying to cross through [[Bolton le Moors]] in [[Lancashire]]. A contemporary account notes that later that "nine of the attackers wielded lances and eleven were archers," and that they all fled across the border to Scotland after the murder.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Rollason|first1=David|last2=Prestwich|first2=Michael|title=The Battle of Neville's Cross, 146|location=Stamford, Lincolnshire|publisher=Shaun Tyas|year=1998}}</ref> 

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Ottoman Turks]] seize [[Plovdiv|Filibe]] (Philippopolis) in Thrace in the [[Byzantine–Ottoman wars]].<ref>{{cite book |last=İnalcık |first=Halil |author-link=Halil İnalcık |title=Kuruluş Dönemi Osmanlı Sultanları |publisher=İSAM |year=1994 |isbn=978-605-5586-06-5 |pages=69–71 |language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Fine |first=John V. A. Jr. |author-link=John Van Antwerp Fine Jr. |title=The Late Medieval Balkans: A Critical Survey from the Late Twelfth Century to the Ottoman Conquest |publisher=University of Michigan Press |year=1994 |isbn=0472082604 |location=Ann Arbor, Michigan |pages=377–378 |orig-date=1987}}</ref>
* [[Dmitry Donskoy]], Prince of the [[Grand Duchy of Moscow]], dethrones [[Dmitry of Suzdal]] to become Grand Prince of [[Vladimir Oblast|Vladimir]].
* [[Al-Afdal al-Abbas]] succeeds Al-Mujahid Ali as [[Rasulid]] Sultan of [[Yemen]].
* The [[Mosque-Madrassa of Sultan Hassan]] is completed in [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]].</onlyinclude>

1366.events:
=== January – March=== 
* [[January 3]] – Count [[Amadeus VI of Savoy]], preparing to lead the [[Savoyard crusade|a Christian crusade against the Muslim Turks]] in the Balkans, names [[Bonne de Bourbon]], his wife, as the regent to govern Savoy during his absence.
* [[January 6]] – As the members of the [[Savoyard crusade]] are preparing to depart from [[Le Bourget-du-Lac]] in [[France]] to fight the Turks in the Balkans, [[Pope Urban V]] announces from [[Avignon]] that all funding from the Vatican will be discontinued, and revokes two papal bulls that had been issued on April 1, 1364 for a crusade to the Holy Land.<ref name="Cox66">{{cite book |last1=Cox |first1=Eugene L. |title=The Green Count of Savoy: Amadeus VI and Transalpine Savoy in the Fourteenth Century |publisher=Princeton University Press |location=Princeton |date=1967|pages=206-224}}</ref> While Amadeus persuades Pope Urban to give a papal blessing, no funding is made and Count Amadeus issues a tax on the citizens of Savoy to pay for the crusade.
* [[January 18]] – [[Dmitry Donskoy]], the [[Grand Prince of Moscow]] and ruler of much of Russia, marries [[Eudoxia of Moscow|Eudoxia Dmitriyevna]], daughter of [[Dmitry of Suzdal]], [[Grand Prince of Vladimir]], who had taken the office from Donskoy in 1360.<ref name=oca>[https://oca.org/saints/lives/2015/05/17/101407-st-euphrosyne-the-princess-eudocia-of-moscow "St. Euphrosyne the Princess, (Eudocia) of Moscow", Orthodox Church in America]</ref>
* [[January 28]] – [[Adam de Bury]] is removed from the office of [[Lord Mayor of London]] by the city's [[alderman|aldermen]], and replaced by [[John Lovekyn]].<ref>{{cite DNB|wstitle=Lovekyn, John|volume=34}}</ref>
* [[January 20]] – [[Edward III|King Edward III of England]] sends a summons directing the members of the English Parliament to assemble at Westminster on May 4 for an eight-day session.
* [[February 8]] – [[Savoyard crusade]]: Amadeus of Savoy departs from France with a fleet of ships toward Venice, and arrives at [[Rivoli, Piedmont|Rivoli]] by February 15.<ref name="Cox66"/>
* [[February 18]] – The [[Statutes of Kilkenny]] are passed by the Irish Parliament, which had been summoned by [[Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence|Lionel, Duke of Clarence]], [[Lord Lieutenant of Ireland]] and son of King Edward III of England, to curb the decline of the [[Norman Irish|Hiberno-Norman]] [[Lordship of Ireland]].<ref>{{cite book|title=This Day in Irish History|first=Padraic |last=Coffey |publisher=O'Brien Press|year=2021|isbn=9781788493116}}</ref><ref>{{Cite ODNB |last=Ormrod |first=W. M.|title=Lionel, duke of Clarence (1338–1368)|orig-year=2004|date=January 2008b|id=16750}}</ref>
* [[March 13]] – [[Henry II of Castile|Enrique of Trastámara]] deposes his half-brother, King [[Pedro of Castile]], to become the new [[Crown of Castile|King of Castile]].<ref name=Lopez>{{cite web|last=López de Ayala|first=Pero|title=Crónica de don Enrique II|trans-title=The Chronicle of Don Enrique II|url=https://liburutegibiltegi.bizkaia.eus/bitstream/handle/20.500.11938/75771/b11102408.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y|series=Cronicas de los Reyes de Castilla (Chronicles of the Kings of Castille)|volume=2|date=1780}}</ref>
* [[March 19]] – [[Otto V, Duke of Bavaria|Otto VII of Wittelsbach]], [[Elector of Brandenburg]], marries [[Catherine of Bohemia|Katharine of Luxembourg]], daughter of the reigning monarch, [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], and widow of the late [[Rudolf IV of Austria|Rudolf IV, Duke of Austria]].Urban 1989, p. 244 On the same day, Katharine's sister [[Elisabeth of Bohemia (1358–1373)|Elisabeth]] marries the new Duke of Austria, [[Albert III of Austria|Albrecht III]].<ref>{{cite book |first=C.W. |last=Previte-Orton |title=The Shorter Cambridge Medieval History: The Twelfth Century to the Renaissance |volume=2 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1952|pages=795-796}}</ref>
* [[March 29]] – The coronation of Enrique of Trastamara as King Enrique II of Castile takes place at the [[Abbey of Santa María la Real de Las Huelgas]] in [[Burgos]], now in Spain.<ref name=Lopez/>

=== April – June===
* [[April 17]] – [[Paul, Latin Patriarch of Constantinople|Paul of Thebes]] is appointed by [[Pope Urban V]] as the new [[Latin Patriarch of Constantinople]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.catholic-hierarchy.org/bishop/bpaolosm.html |title=Patriarch Paolo de Tebe |website=Catholic-Hierarchy.org}}</ref>
* [[April 26]] – [[Simon Islip]], the [[Archbishop of Canterbury]] since 1349, dies at [[Mayfield, Sussex]], three years after having suffered a stroke that deprived him of the power of speech, beginning a vacancy that lasts for a year and a half after Bishop William Edington, declines to become the leader of the English Roman Catholic Church.<ref>{{cite book |author1=Fryde, E. B. |author2=Greenway, D. E. |author3=Porter, S. |author4=Roy, I. |title=Handbook of British Chronology|edition=Third revised |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |year=1996 |isbn=0-521-56350-X }}</ref>
* [[May 4]] – The English Parliament assembles at Westminster, but the session adjourns on May 11 without any accomplishments, and does not meet again until 1368.
* [[May 10]] – King Edward III elects William Edgington, Bishop of Winchester, as the new [[Archbishop of Canterbury]], but Edgington declines the office for reasons of health.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Edginton, William|first=R.
