L.|last=Poole|encyclopedia=Dictionary of National Biography|volume=16|editor=Leslie Stephen|location=London|publisher=Smith, Elder, & Co.|year=1888|pages=386-387}}</ref>
* [[May 25]] – [[Arnaud de Cervole]], who had assembled a group of mercenaries to join a crusade against the Turks in Hungary, is murdered by his own men while they are encamped on the [[Rhône]] river in France near [[Mâcon]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Françoise |last=Autrand|title=Charles V, le Sage |publisher=Fayard|year=1994|page=501 |isbn=9782213027692 |language=fr}}</ref>
* [[May 29]] – After the city councilmen of [[Bremen]] refuse to comply with the orders of Bremen's [[Albert II of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel|Archbishop-Prince Albert II of Brunswick]], troops sent by Albert invade the city, drive out the existing council, and burn the symbol of Bremen's autonomy, the [[Bremen Roland]].<ref name=Krause>{{de-ADB|1|180|181|Albert II., Erzbischof von Bremen|Karl Ernst Hermann Krause|ADB:Albert II. (Erzbischof von Bremen-Hamburg)}}</ref>
* [[June 8]] – Having raised funding in [[Pavia]] and stopped in Padua on June 1 with his fleet, Amadeus of Savoy and his troops arrive at the [[Republic of Venice]], where the Republic provides him additional support.<ref name="Cox66"/>
* [[June 21]] – The [[Savoyard crusade]] reaches its next phase as Amadeus and his troops depart from Venice toward Bulgaria.<ref name="Cox66"/>
* [[June 27]] – Count Conrad II of [[County of Oldenburg|Oldenburg]] captures the city of [[Bremen]] and drives out troops that had been sent by Albert II of Brunswick to end the city's autonomy. Members of the city council, who had been installed temporarily by Albert to replace the existing council members, are beheaded and the autonomy of Bremen and neighboring [[Stade]] is restored.<ref name=Krause/>
* [[June 28]] – [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]] issues the [[Decree of Turda]] in what is now [[Romania]], granting special privileges to nobles of the province of [[Transylvania]] "in order to remove, from this country, malefactors belonging to any nation, especially Romanians," including the power to take measures against non-resident Romanian landowners.<ref>{{cite book |last=Pop |first=Ioan-Aurel |editor1-last=Lévai |editor1-first=Csaba |editor2-last=Vese |editor2-first=Vasile |title=Tolerance and Intolerance in Historical Perspective |publisher=Plus |year=2003 |page=122 |chapter=Nations and Denominations in Transylvania (13th-14th Century) |isbn=88-8492-139-2}}</ref>

=== July – September===
* [[July 22]] – [[Pope Urban V]] suspends aid to the [[Greek Orthodox Church]] for a year, and conditions further aid to the return of the Orthodox clergy to Roman Catholicism. In response, the Emperor of Byzantium, [[John V Palaiologos]] declines to assist the Savoyard Crusade.<ref name="Cox66"/><ref name=Setton>{{cite book |last1=Setton |first1=Kenneth M. |title=The Papacy and the Levant, 1204–1571 |volume=I |publisher=American Philosophical Society |location=Philadelphia |date=1976|page=289}}</ref>
* [[July 23]] – [[Bahmani–Vijayanagara War (1362–1367)]]: The [[Battle of Kauthal]] takes place in what is now the [[Andhra Pradesh]] state of [[India]] as troops of the [[Bahmani Kingdom]] (led by the Sultan [[Mohammed Shah I]] defeat a larger force from the [[Vijayanagara Empire]], ruled by the Emperor [[Bukka Raya I]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Jaques |first=Tony |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EbLOEAAAQBAJ |title=Dictionary of Battles and Sieges: A Guide to 8,500 Battles from Antiquity through the Twenty-first Century |year=2006 |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing USA |isbn=978-0-313-02799-4 |pages=516 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Sherwani |first=Haroon Khan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3kIeAAAAMAAJ |title=The Bahmanis of the Deccan |date=1985 |publisher=Munshiram Manoharlal|language=en}}</ref>
* [[August 11]] – [[Tvrtko I of Bosnia|Tvrtko Kotromanić]], ruler of [[Banate of Bosnia|Bosnia]], grants his general, [[Vukac Hrvatinić]], the [[Pliva (river)|Pliva Valley]] župa and the [[Sokograd (Pliva)|town of Sokol]] for his loyalty during Bosnia's war against Hungary.<ref>{{cite book|last=Vego|first=Marko|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7sFpAAAAMAAJ|title=Postanak srednjovjekovne bosanske države|publisher=Svjetlost|year=1982|location=Sarajevo|page=41}}</ref>
* [[August 22]] – [[Savoyard crusade]]: The crusaders under Amadeus launch a naval attack and invasion, led by [[Francesco I Gattilusio]], Prince of [[Lesbos]], against the Turkish-held city of [[Gelibolu]] (Gallipoli). The Turks abandon the city and Gelibolu falls to the Crusaders on August 26.<ref name="Cox66"/>
* [[September 4]] – [[Savoyard crusade]]: The crusaders' ships arrive off of the coast of Constantinople.<ref name="Cox66"/>
* [[September 23]] – The [[Treaty of Libourne]] is signed at the city of [[Libourne]] in [[Aquitaine]] (now in France) between the recently-deposed [[Peter I of Castile|King Pedro of Castile]], [[Edward the Black Prince]], son of King Edward III of England and heir to the throne; and [[Charles II of Navarre|King Carlos II of Navarre]] as Prince Edward commits English troops to aid the Spanish troops in fighting invaders from the [[Kingdom of France]] and Castile's [[Henry II of Castile|King Enrique II]] during the [[Castilian Civil War of 1351–1369|Castilian Civil War]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Peter|last=Linehan|chapter=Castille, Navarre and Portugal|title=The New Cambridge Medieval History|volume=6|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2005|page=640|isbn=978-0521362900}}</ref>

=== October – December===
* [[October 4]] – [[Savoyard crusade]]: After leaving a contingent of troops to protect Constantinople and the Chrisitan community, Amadeus and his fleet arrive at the coast of Turkish-held [[Bulgaria]], after crossing the [[Black Sea]]. By October 20, the crusaders capture [[Nesebar]].<ref name="Cox66"/>
* [[October 12]] – [[Frederick the Simple]], [[King of Sicily]], promulgates a law prohibiting the external decoration of Jewish [[synagogues]], and directs that any existing decorating be taken down.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Jewish_Encyclopedia/J94xAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=synagogues+sicily+1366&pg=PA324&printsec=frontcover|author=Schulim Ochser|title=Sicily|encyclopedia=The Jewish Encyclopedia|volume=11|page=324|publisher=Ktav Publishing House, Inc.|quote=The external decoration of synagogues was prohibited by Frederick III on Oct. 12, 1366; in consequence of this law old synagogues that had already been decorated were pulled down.}}</ref> 
* [[October 26]] – Comet [[55P/Tempel–Tuttle]] passes within {{convert|0.0229|AU|km mi|abbr=on|lk=on}} from Earth.<ref name="closest">{{cite web |title=Closest Approaches to the Earth by Comets |publisher=Minor Planet Center |url=https://minorplanetcenter.net//iau/lists/ClosestComets.html}}</ref>
* [[November 6]] – In the city of [[Amber, India|Amer]] in what is now the [[Rajasthan]] state of India, the Raja Udaikaran becomes the new ruler of the [[Kingdom of Amber]] in India as the Raja Johnsi Dev dies after a reign of almost 50 years.
* [[November 7]] – [[Gerald FitzGerald, 3rd Earl of Desmond]] replaces Prince Lionel as the [[Lord Lieutenant of Ireland]] and Lionel, who had served since 1361, leaves Ireland, vowing never to return.<ref>{{EB1911 |wstitle=Clarence, Dukes of |display=Clarence, Dukes of s.v. Lionel of Antwerp|volume=6 |pages=428}}</ref>
* [[December 9]] – At the urging of the Mamluk nobles, the Mamluk Sultan [[Al-Ashraf Sha'ban]] arrests the Emir [[Yalbugha al-Umari]], who is then taken from prison and dismembered by his attackers.<ref>{{cite journal |first= Ayaz |last= Fatih Yahya |year= 2007 |title= Türk Memlükler Döneminin Büyük Emîrlerinden Yelboğa El-Ömerî (Ö. 768/1366) ve İdaredeki Nüfuzu |trans-title=Yelboğa El-Ömerî (d. 768/1366), One of the Great Emirs of the Turkish Mamluk Period, and His Influence in Administration |journal=Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü Dergisi (Journal of the Institute of Social Sciences |volume= 16 |issue= 1 |pages=92-94 |publisher= Çukurova Üniversity |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325123919/https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/50339 |language=tr }}</ref>
* [[December 27]] – [[Red Turban Rebellions]]: [[Zhu Yuanzhang]] begins the 10-month siege of the Chinese city of [[Suzhou]], controlled by the rebel warlord [[Zhang Shicheng]] who has plundered the cities of the [[Jiangsu]] province and the [[Zhejiang]] province for the past 13 years.<ref name=Mote>{{Cite book |title=The Cambridge History of China |volume=7 |last=Mote |first=Frederick W. |chapter=The rise of the Ming dynasty, 1330–1367|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1988|pages=30-35|isbn=9780521243322}}</ref> Zhang is able to resist until the fall of Suzhuou on October 1, 1367, when he is captured and imprisoned at the Ming dynasty center at [[Nanjing]], where Zhu declares himself as the [[Hongwu Emperor]] and becomes ruler of China.<ref name=Mote/>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz I of Morocco]] succeeds assassinated Abu Zayyan as [[Sultan]] of the [[Marinid]] Empire in [[Morocco]].
* The Den Hoorn brewery is founded at Leuven in the [[Low Countries]]. In 1717 this will be renamed the ''Brouwerij Artois'', and later releases a beer in 1926 named [[Stella Artois]].
* [[Hongwu Emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]], leader of the [[Red Turban Rebellion]] that will overthrow the [[Yuan dynasty]] and establish the [[Ming dynasty]] two years later, begins building the walls for a new capital city at [[Nanjing]].
* [[Fraser of Muchalls|Thomas Fraser]] obtains lands in [[Aberdeenshire]] (Scotland) on which he starts the building of a towerhouse, that will later be known as [[Muchalls Castle]].

1367.events:
=== January–March ===

* [[January 18]] – [[Ferdinand I of Portugal|Fernando the Handsome]] becomes King of [[Kingdom of Portugal|Portugal]] after the death of his father, [[Peter I of Portugal|King Pedro the Avenger]].<ref>{{EB1911|inline=y|wstitle=Ferdinand I. of Portugal|volume=10|page=265}}</ref>
* [[January 29]] – At [[Chur]] in what is now the Swiss [[Canton of Raetia]], the [[League of God's House]] is founded in the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]] as an agreement between nine communities to come to each other's aid in the event of a crisis.<ref>{{HDS|17154|League of God's House|rm=1432}}</ref>
* [[February 28]] – [[Henry II of Castile|King Enrique II of Castile]] sends a letter of challenge to [[Edward, the Black Prince]] of England, who has already crossed the Pyrenees into Spain with 27,000 troops, daring him to help King Pedro to reclaim the Castilian throne, prompting Edward to organize an army and invade Spain.<ref>{{cite book|first=Michael|last=Jones|title=The Black Prince|publisher=Pegasus Books|year=2018|page=1292|isbn=9781784972936}}</ref>
* [[March 19]] – The [[:es:Combate de Inglesmendi|Battle of Inglesmendi]] is fought in the Crown of Castile (now in Spain) by English troops led by Edward the Black Prince and supporters of the recently deposed King Pedro of Castile who are seeking to restore Pedro to the Castilian throne, against the supporters of the reigning King Enrique II. The knight [[William Felton (died 1367)|William Felton]] is killed and his brother Thomas Felton is taken prisoner of war.<ref>{{DNB |mode=cs2 |last=Fotheringham |first=James Gainsborough |wstitle=Felton, William (d.1367)|volume=18 |page=311}}</ref>
* [[March 29]] – (14th waning of [[Tagu]] [[Burmese calendar|728 ME]]) In what is now [[Myanmar]], [[Pyanchi I of Toungoo|Pyanchi]] becomes the [[List of rulers of Toungoo|King of Toungoo]] upon the death of his father, [[Theingaba of Toungoo|King Theingaba]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Sein Lwin Lay |first=Kahtika U |title=Mintaya Shwe Hti and Bayinnaung: Ketumadi Taungoo Yazawin |language=my |location=Yangon |publisher=Yan Aung Sarpay |orig-year=1968 |year=2006 |pages=22–23}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 3]] – [[Battle of Nájera]]: [[Pedro of Castile]] is restored as King of [[Crown of Castile|Castile]] (in modern-day Spain) after defeating his half-brother, [[Henry II of Castile|King Enrique the Fratricidal]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Sir John Froissart's Chronicles of England, France, Spain, and the Adjoining Countries, from the Latter Part of the Reign of Edward II. to the Coronation of Henry IV. |last=Froissart |first=Jean |date=1808 |publisher=Longman, Hurst, Rees, and Orme |page=302 |language=en}}</ref> Pedro is aided in the battle by the [[Kingdom of England|English]] under [[Edward the Black Prince]], and Henry by the [[Kingdom of France|French]].
* [[April 24]] – [[Otto I, Duke of Brunswick-Göttingen|Otto I, "the Evil"]], becomes Duke of the independent city of [[Göttingen]] (in modern-day [[Germany]]) on the death of his father, [[Ernest I, Duke of Brunswick-Göttingen|Ernst I]].
* [[May 2]] – At [[Burgos]] in Spain, [[Edward the Black Prince]] of England attempts to get himself and his soldiers paid by King Pedro of Castile for their services at the battle of Najera, but receives instead a renewal of a bond to secure the debt owed.<ref>{{DNB|mode=cs2 |last=Hunt |first=William |wstitle=Edward the Black Prince |volume=17 |page=98}}</ref>
* [[May 20]] – John of Ashwell becomes the new [[Attorney General for England and Wales]] upon the departure of Thomas of Shardelow.<ref>The Chronological Historian:Volume 1. p. 59.
</ref>
* [[May 31]] – King [[Robert III of Scotland]] names his son [[James I of Scotland|Prince James of Stewart]] as the [[Earl of Atholl]], a title traditionally given to the heir of the Scottish throne.<ref>{{Cite ODNB |last=Boardman |first=S. I. |year=2004 |title=Robert III |edition=online |series=Oxford Dictionary of National Biography (ODNB) |doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/23714 |url=http://www.oxforddnb.com/view/article/23714}}</ref>
* [[June 20]] – The author [[Geoffrey Chaucer]] is appointed by King Edward III of England as a [[valet de chambre]] as a means of receiving a regular income while pursuing his writing. By 1372, Chaucer delivers his first epic poem, ''[[The Book of the Duchess]]'', in honor of Duchess Blanche of Lancaster<ref>{{cite book|first=Kylene|last=Beers|title=Holt Literature and Language Arts|publisher=Holt, Rinehart, and Winston|year=2003|page=113|isbn=978-0030573743}}</ref>.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 9]] – [[Guy II, Count of Blois|Guy de Blois, Count of Sissons]], held hostage by [[Enguerrand VII de Coucy]], [[Earl of Bedford]], is forced to surrender [[Counts of Soissons|Soissons to Bedford]] in return for his freedom.<ref>{{cite book|first=George Edward|last=Cokayne|chapter=Bedford (County)|title=The Complete Peerage of England, Scotland, Ireland, Great Britain and the United Kingdom: Bass to Canning|volume= |publisher=St. Catherine Press|year=1912|page=69}}</ref>
* [[July 19]] – King [[Charles V of France]] issues a royal edict ordering the ''bonne villes'' (defined as "the French town that enjoyed especial royal favour") to improve their defenses by improving town walls, towers and gateways.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Rosamond McKitterick|title=The New Cambridge Medieval History: Volume 6, C.1300-c.1415|publisher= Cambridge University Press|year=1995|page=113}}</ref>
* [[July 26]] – At [[Avignon]], [[Pope Urban V]] learns of a possible invasion of France by [[John of Gaunt]] and his intention to capture [[Provence]], and writes to England's King Edward III to take steps to prevent it.<ref>{{cite book|first=Kathryn|last=Warner|title=John of Gaunt: Son of One King, Father of Another|publisher=Amberley Publishing|year=2022|isbn=9781445670324}}</ref>
* [[August 31]] – In Switzerland, [[Amadeus IV of Geneva|Amadeus IV, Count of Geneva]] become the new Count of Geneva when his brother, [[Aymon III of Geneva|Aymon III]], dies of battle wounds after only seven months after taking office on January 18.<ref>{{cite book|first=Eugene L.|last=Cox|title=The Eagles of Savoy: The House of Savoy in Thirteenth-Century Europe|location=Princeton, New Jersey|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=1974|page=240}}</ref>
* [[September 5]] – In what is now [[Myanmar]], [[Swa Saw Ke]] becomes the new [[List of Burmese monarchs#Ava (1364–1555)|King of Ava]] two days after the death of his brother-in-law, King [[Thado Minbya]], and following the decision of [[Thilawa of Yamethin]] to reject the offer of the throne.<ref>{{cite journal | author=Than Tun | author-link=Than Tun | title=History of Burma: A.D. 1300–1400 |journal=Journal of Burma Research Society | date=December 1959 | volume=XLII | number=II|page=128}}</ref>
* [[September 17]] – One month before his appointment as Bishop of Winchester, [[William of Wykeham]] is confirmed as the [[Lord Chancellor|Chancellor of England]] following his appointment by King Edward III.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_History_and_Antiquities_of_the_Count/c8lOAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wykeham+Chancellor+1367+lipscomb&pg=RA1-PA361&printsec=frontcover|first=George|last=Lipscomb|chapter=Hardwick, with Weedon|title=The History and Antiquities of the County of Buckingham|volume=3|publisher=J. & W. Robins |year=1847|page=361|quote=Being now qualified, by his ecclesiastical promotion, for further advancement in the State, he was constituted Chancellor of England, and confirmed in that high office, 17 September 1367.}}</ref>
* [[September 28]] – The [[Battle of Tripoli (1367)|Battle of Tripoli]] is fought in [[Tripoli, Lebanon|Lebanon]] as the Muslim [[Mamluk Sultanate|Mamluk Syrian]] army, led by the Emir Idmor, repels Christian invaders led by [[Peter I of Cyprus|King Peter of Cyprus]]<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/GeorgeHillAHistoryOfCyprus.Volume2.TheFrankishPeriod11921432finalOcr/page/n401/mode/1up|first=George |last=Hill |year=1948|title= A History Of Cyprus, Volume II, The Frankish Period, 1192-1432|publisher=Cambridge University Press |pages=352-353}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 1]] – [[Red Turban Rebellions]]: [[Zhu Yuanzhang]] takes [[Suzhou, Jiangsu|Suzhou]] from [[Zhang Shicheng]], who unsuccessfully attempts suicide before being captured and taken to [[Nanjing]], where he dies.<ref>{{sfn|Twitchett|1998|p=34-35}}</ref>
* [[October 16]] – [[Pope Urban V]] makes the first attempt to move the [[Papacy]] back to Rome from [[Avignon]]. This move is reversed in [[1370]], when he is forced to return to Avignon, and shortly afterwards dies.
* [[November 19]] – In Germany, the [[Confederation of Cologne|Kölner Konföderation]] is founded by eight German members of the [[Hanseatic League]] ([[Lübeck]], [[Rostock]], [[Stralsund]], [[Wismar]], [[Chełmno|Kulm]] and [[Toruń|Thorn]], and five non-League Dutch cities ([[Amsterdam]], [[Brielle]], [[Harderwijk]],[[Elbląg|Elbing]] and [[Kampen, Overijssel|Kampen]]) to fight against the [[Kingdom of Denmark]], whose ruler [[Valdemar IV of Denmark|King Valdemar IV]], has been seizing land to expand the territory owned by the [[crown land|Danish crown]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Dollinger |first=Philippe |url=http://archive.org/details/germanhansa0000doll |title=The German Hansa |date=1970 |publisher=Stanford University Press |location=Stanford, California|isbn=978-0-8047-0742-8}}</ref>
* [[December 28]] – During the [[Red Turban Rebellions]],  [[Hu Mei (Ming dynasty)|Hu Mei]] captures [[Shaowu]], while [[Xu Da]] and [[Chang Yuchun]] capture [[Jinan]], bringing both under the Hongwu Emperor [[Zhu Yuanzhang]]'s control.{{sfn|Twitchett|1998|p=97}}

=== Date unknown ===
* Winter – Construction of a stone [[Moscow Kremlin Wall]] around the city is begun to resist invasion by the [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania]].
* [[Petru I of Moldavia|Petru I]] succeeds his grandfather [[Bogdan I of Moldavia|Bogdan I]] as [[voivode]] (ruler) of [[Moldavia]].
* The first [[university]] in [[Pécs]], [[Hungary]], is founded by [[Louis I of Hungary|King Louis I]].

1368.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 12]] – Zhu Yuanzhang declares himself as Emperor of China and forces [[Toghon Temür|Emperor Huizong]] of the [[Yuan dynasty]] to flee the capital, [[Nanjing|Yingtian]] (now Nanjing).<ref>{{cite book|author=Frederick Mote|chapter= The rise of the Ming dynasty, 1330–1367|title=The Cambridge History of China|volume=7|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1988|pages=51–57|isbn=9780521243322}}</ref> 
* [[January 23]] – Zhu Yuanzhang establishes the [[Ming dynasty]] with himself as the Emperor [[Hongwu Emperor|Hongwu]]. The new dynasty will last until [[1644]]. The Emperor immediately orders every county magistrate to set up four [[Granary|granaries]], and halts government taxation on books.<ref name=Langlois>{{cite book|last=Langlois|first=John D.|chapter=The Hung-wu reign, 1368–1398|title=The Cambridge History of China|editor1=[[Frederick W. Mote]]|editor2=Denis C. Twitchett|volume=7|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1988|pages=111–113|isbn=0521243327}}</ref> Work begins later year on restoring the surviving [[Great Wall of China]].<ref>{{cite book|author=[[Frederick Mote]]|year=1999|title=Imperial China: 900-1800|publisher=[[Harvard University Press]]|location=Cambridge MA|isbn=978-0-674-01212-7|page=563}}</ref>
* [[February 13]] – [[Otto V, Duke of Bavaria|Otto VII]], [[Elector of Brandenburg]] signs the Treaty of [[Drawsko Pomorskie|Dramburg]] a treaty with King [[Casimir III of Poland]], returning the town of [[Wałcz|Wôłcz]] (no Walcz) to Poland's control. 
* [[February 24]] – King [[Edward III]] of England summons the English Parliament to meet at Westminster on May 1.
* [[March 4]] – On behalf of [[Louis I of Anjou|Louis of Anjou]], brother of France's [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]], [[Bertrand Du Guesclin]] and 2,000 troops began a siege of the city of [[Tarascon]], which surrenders to him on March 22.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Masson |first1=Paul |title=Encyclopédie départementale des Bouches-du-Rhône, Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône |date=1937 |location=Marseille |page=405}}</ref> 
* [[March 7]] – 
**[[Mamluk raid on Cyprus (1368)]]: Acting at the orders of Egypt's Mamluk Sultan [[al-Ashraf Sha'ban]], General Ibrahim al-Tazi lands with 500 troops at Cyprus and begins a 23-day raid.<ref name=Onimus>Clément Onimus, "Peter I of Lusignan's Crusade and the Reaction of the Mamluk Sultanate", in Alexander D. Beihammer and Angel Nicolaou-Konnari, eds., ''Crusading, Society, and Politics in the Eastern Mediterranean in the Age of King Peter I of Cyprus'' (Brepols, 2022), pp. 251–271, at 258–259.</ref>
**The new [[Ōan]] era is proclaimed in Japan, ending the [[Jōji]] era because of problems in 1367 with an epidemic and natural disasters.
* [[March 16]] – 12th waning of [[Tabaung]], [[Burmese calendar|729 ME]]. In what is now [[Myanmar]], the coronation of [[Swa Saw Ke]] as [[Kingdom of Ava|King of Ava]] is held. Swa Saw Ke had taken power on six months earlier on September 5, but waited for the court astrologers to determine the ideal date for the coronation ceremony.<ref>{{cite book |last=Sandalinka |first=Shin |title=Mani Yadanabon |edition=2009, 4th printing |year=1781 |location=Yangon |language=Burmese | publisher=Seit-Ku Cho Cho|page=35}}</ref>
* [[March 29]] – [[Emperor Chōkei]] accedes to the throne of [[Japan]].<ref>Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' p. 158.</ref>
* [[March 30]] – [[Mamluk raid on Cyprus (1368)]]: Ibrahim al-Tazi completes raid by Egypt's [[Mamluk Sultanate]] on the [[Kingdom of Cyprus]] and begins sending back captured treasure.<ref name=Onimus/>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 4]] – The [[Siege of Copenhagen (1368)|siege of Copenhagen]], capital of the [[Kingdom of Denmark]], is started by the [[Hanseatic League]] as 37 ships and 2,000 soldiers arrive at the city after sailing from the German city of [[Lübeck]] under the leadership of the city's leader, [[Bruno von Warendorp]]. The invaders bring with them 400 horses and eight [[trebuchet]]s (long range catapults) and four regular [[catapult]]s.<ref name=Reisnert>{{Cite book |last=Reisnert |first=Anders |url=https://pure.au.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/162355026/Castles_At_War.pdf |title=The Siege and Storm of Lindholmen during the Second Hanseatic War (1368-1369) |publisher=Rudolf Habelt GMBH|location=Bonn|year=2015 |pages=206–208}}</ref> While the city falls in four weeks, the [[Absalon's Castle|Absalon fortress]] on [[Slotsholmen]] island holds out for two months.
* [[April 30]] – [[Henry II of Castile|Henry of Trastámara]], deposed a year earlier from his position as King of Castile and Leon, captures the city of [[León, Spain|León]] after a [[Siege of León (1368)|siege of more than three months]].
* [[May 1]] – The English Parliament is opened for a 21-day session by King Edward III.
* [[May 2]] – Copenhagen, capital of Denmark, falls to the Hanseatic League four weeks after the April 4 invasion of the kingdom and [[Waldemar IV of Denmark|King Valdemar IV]] is forced to flee while the city is pillaged and looted by troops led by Bruno von Warendorp.<ref name=Reisnert/>
* [[May 10]] – Forces of the [[Republic of Venice]] suppress the [[Revolt of Saint Titus]] against Venetian rule in the [[Kingdom of Candia]] on the island of [[Crete]]).<ref>McKee, Sally (December 1994), "The Revolt of St Tito in fourteenth-century Venetian Crete: A reassessment", ''Mediterranean Historical Review'', '''9'''(2): 173–204, [[Doi (identifier)|doi]]:10.1080/09518969408569670</ref>
* [[May 21]] – The English Parliament adjourns and King Edward III gives royal assent multiple new laws, including the landmark Observance of Due Process of Law, "declaring that none shall be put to answer an accusation made to the King without presentment", still in effect more than 650 years later. The King also approves the Naturalisation Act (" Children born beyond sea in the King's dominions shall be inheritable in England".<ref>{{cite web |title=Acts of the English Parliament from 1368 |url=https://www.legislation.gov.uk/aep/1368 |website=[[legislation.gov.uk]] |publisher=[[The National Archives (United Kingdom)|The National Archives]]}}</ref>
* [[May 25]] – The [[Pomerania-Wolgast|Duchy of Wolgast]], created more than 200 years earlier in [[1160]] as part of the division of the [[Duchy of Pomerania]], is divided among the heirs of the late [[Barnim IV, Duke of Pomerania|Barnim IV]], who had been co-ruler with his brothers Wartislaw V and Bogislaw V.<ref>{{cite book|title=Rodowód książąt pomorskich|trans-title=Genealogy of the Dukes of Pomerania |author=Edward Rymar|publisher=[[Pomeranian Library]]|date=2005|pages=315–316}}</ref> 
* [[June 10]] – [[Michele Morosini]] becomes the new [[Doge of Venice|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Venice]] and replaces the late Doge [[Andrea Contarini]], but he serves for only four months before dying in office at the age of 74.
* [[June 16]] – The [[Siege of Copenhagen (1368)|siege of Copenhagen]] by the Hanseatic League ends as the remaining defenders of Absalon Castle surrender and the building is destroyed.<ref name=Reisnert/>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 28]] – With the death of [[Bolko II the Small]], one of the Dukes of Silesia, his widow [[Agnes of Austria (1322–1392)|Agnes of Austria]] receives control of the [[Duchy of Świdnica]], the duchies of [[Jawor]], [[Lwówek Śląski]] and [[Lusatia]], and half of five other Polish duchies ([[Brzeg]], [[Oława]] from, [[Siewierz]], [[Głogów]] and [[Ścinawa]]. Upon her death 14 years later, the duchies are all incorporated into the [[Crown of Bohemia]] and its ruler, [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Wenceslaus IV]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://miasta.gazeta.pl/katowice/1,35022,1814747.html |title=Sylwetki ważniejszych książąt śląskich |access-date=2006-09-29 |archive-date=2006-09-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060907015102/http://miasta.gazeta.pl/katowice/1,35022,1814747.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[August 15]] – The Ming General [[Xu Da]] sets off from [[Kaifeng]] at the direction of the Chinese Emperor Hongwu, with plans to rid China of the former Yuan dyansty Emperor Huizong.<ref name=Langlois/>
* [[August 25]] – [[:de:Gottfried IV (Arnsberg)|Count Gottfried IV of Ambsbe]], who has no children, sells [[Arnsberg]] to the [[Duchy of Westphalia]] by way of the Archbishop of [[Cologne|Köln]], for 30,000 guilders, allowing Westphalia to complete its reunification.
* [[September 10]] – Xu Da captures the city of Tongzhou after defeating a Yuan army, forcing Huizong to flee to [[Shangdu]].<ref name=Langlois/>
* [[September 14]] – General Xu Da captures the Yuan city of Khanbaliq and renames it [[Names of Beijing|Beiping]] ("northern peace"), a forerunner to the current name of [[Beijing]] ("northern capital").<ref name=Langlois/>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 11]] – [[Pope Urban V]] issues a [[papal bull]] appointing William Whittlesey as [[Archbishop of Canterbury]], and "primate of all England".<ref>{{cite journal|title=Prince's 'Worthies of Devon' and the 'Dictionary of National Biography'|author=W. Pengelly|journal=Report and Transactions of the Devonshire Association of Science, Literature, and Art|volume=XVIII|year=1886|page=349}}</ref>
* [[October 16]] – [[Michele Morosini]] dies in office from the bubonic plague, only four months after becoming Doge of Venice, and is replaced by [[Antonio Venier]] as the Republic's chief executive.<ref name=Crowley>{{cite book |last= Crowley |first = Roger |title= City of Fortune - How Venice Won and lost a Naval Empire |location= London |publisher= Faber and Faber |date=2011 |type= Hardback |isbn= 978-0-571-24594-9}}</ref>
* [[October 17]] – 
**[[Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence|Lionel, Duke of Clarence]], second only to [[Edward the Black Prince]] as heir to the throne of England, dies in Italy at the age of 29, less than five months after her May 28 marriage to [[Violante Visconti]], daughter of [[Galeazzo II Visconti]] Lord of Milan. Lionel's death, suspected to have been from accidental food poisoning, ends any chance for an alliance between England and Milan.<ref>{{Cite ODNB |last=Ormrod |first=W. M.|title=Lionel, duke of Clarence (1338–1368)|orig-year=2004|date=January 2008b|id=16750}}</ref>
**[[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]] and [[Pope Urban V]] meet at [[Viterbo]] in Italy and make plans to enter [[Rome]] together after the Pope's travel from [[Avignon]].<ref name=AlexLee>{{cite book|first=Alexander|last=Lee|title=
Humanism and Empire: The Imperial Ideal in Fourteenth-Century Italy|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2018|page=141|isbn=9780191662645}}</ref>
* [[October 21]] – Charles greets Pope Urban at [[Monte Mario]], and the two ride together to a welcome in [[Rome]].<ref name=AlexLee/>
* [[November 1]] – [[Elizabeth of Pomerania]], wife of the Charles IV, is crowned as the [[List of Holy Roman empresses|Empress of the Holy Roman Empire]] by Pope Urban V.<ref>{{cite book |title=Richard II: A True King's Fall |first=Kathryn |last=Warner |publisher=Amberley Publishing |year=2017 }}</ref>
* [[November 21]] – King [[Algirdas of Lithuania]] and the Grand Duke [[Mikhail II of Tver]] defeat troops of the [[Grand Duchy of Moscow]] in the [[:ru:Тросненская битва (1368|Battle of the Trosna River]], and reach the outside of the [[Moscow Kremlin Wall]] that surrounds the capital, but find it to be insurmountable and are unable to mount a siege.
* [[December 3]] – [[Joanna of Bourbon]], [[Queen consort of France]] as wife of [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]], gives birth to his first child, the [[Dauphin of France|Dauphin]] [[Charles VI of France|Charles of Valois]]. The Dauphin will become King Charles VI in 1380 upon the death of his father.
* [[December 7]] – The Treaty of Plüschow is signed, allowing [[Albert II of Mecklenburg|Albrecht II]], Duke of Mecklenburg, to purchase neighboring [[County of Schwerin|Schwerin]] for 20,000 silver [[Mark (currency)|Marks]] to create Mecklenburg-Schwerin, jointly ruled by his wife, [[Richardis of Schwerin, Queen of Sweden|Richardis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Von den Grafen zu Schwerin (1166-1359) |url=http://www.lexikus.de/bibliothek/Geographisch-statistisch-historisches-Handbuch-des-Mecklenburger-Landes-Band-1/Abriss-der-Geschichte/Das-Mittelalter-(von-1227-1662)/Von-den-Grafen-zu-Schwerin-(1166-1359) |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=lexikus.de |language=de}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Durrës]], the second-largest city in modern-day Albania (at this time known as Dyrrhachium), is captured from the [[Capetian House of Anjou|Angevins]] by [[Karl Thopia]], a powerful feudal prince and warlord.<ref>[[Karl Thopia#CITEREFFine1994|Fine 1994]], pp. 372–373: "Karlo entered into close relations with Venice, which granted him Venetian citizenship and called him Prince of Albania."</ref>
* [[Lațcu of Moldavia|Lațcu]], son of [[Bogdan I of Moldavia|Bogdan I]], deposes his nephew [[Petru I of Moldavia|Petru I]], and becomes voivode of [[Moldavia]]. (Other sources state that Lațcu had succeeded his father Bogdan in 1367).<ref>{{cite book|last=Sălăgean|first=Tudor|editor-first=Pop|editor-last=Ioan-Aurel|title=History of Romania: Compendium|publisher= Romanian Cultural Institute (Center for Transylvanian Studies)|year=2006|page=201|chapter=Romanian society in the early Middle Ages|isbn=978-973-7784-12-4}}</ref>
* [[Timur]] ascends the throne of [[Samarkand]] (in modern-day [[Uzbekistan]]).<ref>Shahane, Girish (28 December 2016). "Counterview: Taimur's actions were uniquely horrific in Indian history". ''Scroll.in''. Archived from the original on 9 November 2017. Retrieved 28 December 2016.</ref>
* [[Maha Thammaracha II]] becomes ruler of the [[Sukhothai Kingdom]] (in modern-day northern [[Thailand]]) after the death of [[Maha Thammaracha I]].<ref>[[George Coedès|Coedès, George]] (1968). Walter F. Vella (ed.). ''The Indianized States of Southeast Asia''. trans.Susan Brown Cowing. University of Hawaii Press, pp.  219–220 .  {{ISBN|978-0-8248-0368-1}}</ref>
* [[Mikhail II of Tver|Mikhail Aleksandrovich]] becomes the sole ruler of [[Tver]] (in modern-day western Russia), after the death of co-ruler and rival Vasiliy Mikhailovich of Kashin.<ref>[[Janet L. B. Martin|Martin, Janet]] (2007). ''Medieval Russia: 980–1584. Second Edition. E-book''. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-511-36800-4}}</ref>
* [[Moscow]] attacks [[Tver]], which counter-attacks with the aid of [[Lithuania]] and the [[Blue Horde]].<ref>Batūra, Romas (2013). "Algirdo žygiai į Maskvą 1368 1370, 1372". In Zikaras, Karolis (ed.). ''Žymiausi Lietuvos mūšiai ir karinės operacijos'' (in Lithuanian) (2nd ed.). Vilnius: Alio. pp. 46–49. {{ISBN|978-9986-827-05-4}}.</ref>
* The King of [[Norway]] sends the last Royal Ship from Norway to the [[Greenland]] [[Eastern Settlement]]. This event is part of both the [[Norse colonization of the Americas]], and of the [[History of Greenland]].
* A peace treaty is signed between [[Norway]] and the [[Hanseatic League]].
* The [[Bibliothèque nationale de France]] (National Library of France) is founded as the Royal Library at the [[Louvre Palace]] in Paris, by [[Charles V of France]].<ref>David A. Hanser (2006). ''Architecture of France''. Greenwood Publishing Group. p. 115.</ref>
* [[Petrarch]] concludes writing the sequence of [[Italian poetry|Italian]] [[sonnet]]s and other poems known as ''[[Il Canzoniere]]''.<ref>'Introduction' to ''Canzoniere'', translated by Anthony Mortimer (London: Penguin, 2002), xiv.</ref></onlyinclude>

1369.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 17]] – [[Peter II of Cyprus|Peter the Fat]] becomes the new [[King of Cyprus]] when his father, [[Peter I of Cyprus|King Peter I]], is stabbed to death while in bed at the Palace of La Cava in [[Nicosia]]. The murder is carried out by a group of noblemen, led by Philip of Ibelin, Henry of Jubail, John of Gaurelle, and James of Nores, along with some outlaws freed from imprisonment earlier in the evening.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Edbury |first=Peter |date=1980 |title=The murder of King Peter I of Cyprus (1359–1369) |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1016/0304-4181(80)90018-4 |journal=Journal of Medieval History |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=219–233}}</ref> 
* [[January 25]] – King Charles of France sends a summons to [[Edward the Black Prince]], who is residing at [[Bordeaux]], demanding that Edward appear before the King in [[Paris]] to answer for Edward's assessment of taxes on the people of [[Aquitaine]]. The Black Prince reportedly responds with the threat "We will willingly attend at Paris on the day appointed since the King of France sends for us, but it shall be with our helmet on our head and 60,000 men in our company".<ref>{{DNB|mode=cs2 |last=Hunt |first=William |wstitle=Edward the Black Prince |volume=17 |page=99}}</ref>
* [[February 19]] – [[Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II]], the Muslim Caliph of Tunis, is killed in a shipwreck at the age of 32 and is succeeded by his 12-year-old son [[:fr:Abû al-Baqâ' Khâlid|Abu-al-Baqa Khalid II]].<ref >{{cite book |last1=Brunschwig |first1=Robert |title=La Berberie Orientale sous les Hafsides |trans-title=The Eastern Berbers under the Hafsids |date=1940 |publisher=Adrienne-Maisonneuve |url=https://archive.org/details/LBERBBRIEORIENTALESousLesHafsidesT.1/mode/2up |pages=185-187}}</ref>
* [[February]] – [[Vladislav I of Wallachia]] liberates [[Vidin]] from the Hungarians, resulting in the restoration of [[Ivan Sratsimir of Bulgaria|Ivan Sratsimir]] on the throne of [[Bulgaria]], in the autumn.
* [[March 14]] – King [[Pedro of Castile]] loses the [[Battle of Montiel]] to [[Kingdom of France|French]] soldiers led by [[Bertrand du Guesclin]] and Castilians led by his half-brother, [[Henry II of Castile|Enrique]]. Pedro takes refuge in a fortress and offers du Guesclin 200,000 gold coins and a promise of several towns in Castile, in return for betraying Enrique. Afterwards, du Guesclin informs Enrique of the offer.<ref name="Diaz Martin">{{cite book|first=Luis Vicente |last=Díaz Martín |title= Pedro I the Cruel |publisher= Ediciones Trea S.L.|edition=2nd|year=2007 | location= Gijón |page=275|isbn=978-84-9704-274-1}}</ref>
* [[March 18]] – In a period of a few days, more than 800 communities in the [[Duchy of Aquitaine]] send requests to King Charles V of France for aid in escaping England's rule.
* [[March 23]] – Enrique of Castile assassinates King Pedro of Castile after Pedro is betrayed by Bertrand du Guesclin.<ref name="Diaz Martin"/> 

=== April–June ===
* [[April 6]] – 
**The city of [[Lucca]] in [[Italy]] pays the [[Holy Roman Emperor Charles V]] for the right for self-government, and Cardinal Guy de Montfort is appointed the imperial vicar to secure the debt.
**King Edward III summons the members of the House of Lords and House of Commons to assemble on June 3 for a session of the [[English Parliament]]. 
* [[April 13]] – [[Joanna I of Naples]], in her capacity as [[List of rulers of Provence|Countess of Provence]], signs a treaty with [[Louis I of Anjou|Louis, Duke of Anjou]] to end the war between Anjou and Provence.<ref>{{cite book |first=Raoul |last=Busquet |title=Histoire de Provence |publisher=Imprimerie nationale de Monaco |year=1954 | edition=1997|page=198|language=fr}}</ref>
* [[April 15]] – Saint [[Elzéar of Sabran]] (1285-1323) is canonized by [[Pope Urban V]] as a saint of the Roman Catholic Church.<ref name=Carr>[https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/05397a.htm Carr, Gregory. "St. Elzéar of Sabran." The Catholic Encyclopedia] Vol. 5. New York: Robert Appleton Company, 1909. 30 September 2021{{PD-notice}}</ref>
* [[May 7]] – [[Košice]], in [[Slovakia]], becomes the first town in Europe to be granted its own [[coat of arms of Košice|coat of arms]] as King Louis of Hungary grants the right in a charter in recognition of the city's assistance in the Battle of Rozhanovice.<ref>{{cite book|first=Ladislav |last=Vrtel |title=Osem storočí slovenskej heraldiky|trans-title=Eight Centuries of Slovak Heraldry|quote=Privy pripad udelenia erbu listinou predstavuje listina Ludovita I, so. 7. maja 139, korou Kosciciam udeluje mestsky erb. |year=2003 |page=94|isbn=9788070906910}}</ref>
* [[May 9]] – At a meeting of the [[Estates General (France)|Estates General]] in [[Paris]], the delegates approve the resumption of hostilities between France and England.
* [[May 21]] – The Yuan dynasty Chinese warlord of [[Shaanxi]] province, [[Li Siqi (warlord)|Li Siqi]], surrenders to the Ming dynasty Emperor Hongwu.<ref name="L117"/> 
* [[May 25]] – [[Dương Nhật Lễ]] becomes the new Emperor of Vietnam (Dai Viet) upon the death of the Emperor [[Trần Dụ Tông]].<ref>{{citation|last=Ngô |first=Sĩ Liên |title=[[Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư]]|trans-title=Annals of Dai Viet |year=1993|language=Vietnamese|publisher=Social Science Publishing House|location=[[Hanoi]]|page=259}}</ref>
* [[May]] – King [[Charles V of France]] renounces the [[Treaty of Brétigny]], and war is declared between France and [[Kingdom of England|England]].
* [[June 3]] – At the opening of the English Parliament at Westminster, King [[Edward III of England]] proclaims himself to the rightful heir to the throne of France after the [[Hundred Years' War]] is resumed by France's [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Jean|last=Favier|title=La guerre de Cent Ans|trans-title=The Hundred Years War|location=Paris|publisher=Fayard |year=1980|page =324|isbn=2-213-00898-1|language=fr}}</ref>
* [[June 5]] – [[John of Lusignan|Jean de Lusignan]], regent for the King of Cyprus, uses his navy to attack [[Sidon]] in what is now [[Lebanon]], but is then forced to retreat because of a storm.
* [[June 11]] – The Parliament of England adjourns after eight days, as King Edward III gives [[royal assent]] to acts passed, removing the [[Merchants of the Staple#The staple at Calais|wool staple of Calais]], as well as specifying limits to the import of wine from [[Gascoigne]], and prohibiting the king's butler and lieutenants from taking "more wines than is commanded."<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |pages=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[June 19]] – At [[Ghent]], [[Philip the Bold]], [[Duke of Burgundy]] and ruler of a realm that includes much of [[Burgundian Netherlands|present-day Netherlands and Belgium]], marries [[Margaret III of Flanders|Margaret]], daughter of [[Louis II of Flanders]].<ref>{{cite book |first=Richard |last=Vaughan |title=Philip the Bold: The Formation of the Burgundian state |publisher=The Boydell Press |year=2009|page=16}}</ref>
* [[June 27]] – [[Thomas de Brantingham]] succeeds [[John Barnet]] as the [[Lord High Treasurer]] of England.<ref>{{cite book |first=Kenneth Meyer |last=Setton |title=The Papacy and the Levant, 1204-1571: The thirteenth and fourteenth centuries |year=1976 |publisher=American Philosophical Society |page=282|isbn=9780871691149 }}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 9]] – Lusignan of Cyprus leads the Cypriots in an unsuccessful attack on [[Alexandria]] in [[Egypt]], then retreats, attacks Sidon again on July 19 and then is force by the weather to return to Cyprus, landing back at [[Famagusta]] on July 22.
* [[July 20]] – 
**In the continued conquest of [[Yuan dynasty]] China by the [[Ming dynasty]], General [[Chang Yuchun]] captures the Yuan capital, [[Shangdu]], forcing the Yuan [[Toghon Temür|Emperor Huizong]] to flee further northward.<ref name="L117">{{Cite book|title=The Cambridge History of China|volume=7|last=Langlois, Jr.|first=John D.|chapter=The Hung-wu Reign, 1368–1398|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1988|page=117}}</ref>
**The kingdoms of [[England]] and [[Scotland]] sign a 14-year-truce.{{cite book|first=John |last=Dowden|title=The Bishops of Scotland|publisher=J. Maitland Thomson|location=Glasgow|year=1912}}
* [[August 15]] – [[Philippa of Hainault]], wife of King [[Edward III]],  dies after 39 years as Queen consort of England.<ref>{{Cite ODNB|id=22110|title=Philippa [Philippa of Hainault] (1310x15?–1369)|last=Vale|first=Juliet|year=2010|orig-year=2004|doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/22110}}</ref>
* [[August 23]] – [[John of Gaunt]], [[Duke of Lancaster]], lands with English troops at [[Calais]] to begin a raid in [[France]] while [[Philip the Bold]], Duke of Burgundy, assembles troops to confront the English invasion. The standoff continues while Lancaster waits for additional troops from the Earl of Warwick. 
* [[August 24]] – [[Danish–Hanseatic War (1361–1370)]]: After an [[Siege of Lindholmen|18-month siege]] by the armies of the Hanseatic League and the Kingdom of Sweden, Denmark recaptures [[Lindholmen Castle]] and forces a retreat by [[Albert, King of Sweden|King Albert of Sweden]] along with the Hansa and Swedish forces.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Reisnert |first=Anders |url=https://pure.au.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/162355026/Castles_At_War.pdf |title=The Siege and Storm of Lindholmen during the Second Hanseatic War (1368-1369) |publisher=Rudolf Habelt GMBH|location=Bonn |year=2015 |pages=206-213}}</ref>
* [[August 29]] – [[Vladislav I of Wallachia]] obtains, by permission from the King of Hungary, control of the Transylvanian duchies of Almas and [[Făgăraș|Fagaras]]
* [[September 2]] – [[Philip the Bold]], [[Duke of Burgundy]], is forced to disband the army that he had assembled to capture Normandy from the control of England, after being ordered by King Charles V of France.
* [[September 22]] – [[Ludovico II Gonzaga]] becomes the new [[Duchy of Mantua|Lord of Mantua]] upon the death of his father, [[Guido Gonzaga]].<ref>{{cite book |title=A Short History of the Italian Renaissance |first=Kenneth R. |last=Bartlett |publisher=University of Toronto Press |year=2013|page=190}}</ref>
* [[September 29]] – The [[:de:Frieden von Schärding|Treaty of Scharding]] is signed between Duke Albrecht III of Austria and Duke Stephen II of Bavaria to end the dispute over control of [[Tyrol]].<ref>{{cite book |first=Johann Jacob |last=Staffler |title=Tirol und Vorarlberg |volume=1 |publisher=Verlag Rauch |year=1839 |page=17}}</ref>
* [[September]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: The French burn [[Portsmouth]], England;<ref>{{cite web|title=Dockyard Timeline|url=https://portsmouthdockyard.org.uk/timeline/time/romans|publisher=Portsmouth Royal Dockyard Historical Trust|access-date=2018-09-21}}</ref> the English raid [[Picardy]] and [[Normandy]].<ref name=CBH7>{{cite book|author1=Palmer, Alan|last2=Palmer |first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages= 06–108|isbn= 0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 18]] – [[John V Palaiologos]], partiarch of Constantinople and leader of the Eastern Orthodox Christian faith, meets in Rome with the Roman Catholic Pope Urban V and agrees to recognize the Pope as the leader of all Christendom, after negotiation between Rome and Constantinople had been made by [[Demetrios Chrysoloras]].<ref>{{cite book|author =[[Edward Gibbon]]|title=[[The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire]]|chapter=66. Visit of John Palaeologus to Urban V. at Rome, A.D. 1369, 13 October|publisher=Strahan & Cadell|year=1789}}</ref>
* [[November 30]] – Hundred Years' War: Charles V of France recaptures most of [[Aquitaine]] from the English.<ref name=CBH7/>
* [[December 7]] – The [[Estates General (France)|Estates General]] in France approves the request by King Charles V to raise taxes in order to finance the renewed war with England.
* [[December 25]] – [[Frederick the Simple]], [[King of Sicily]], issues an order on Christmas Day directing all [[Judaism|Jews]] on the island to wear a red badge identifying their heritage.{{cite encyclopedia|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Jewish_Encyclopedia/J94xAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=synagogues+sicily+1366&pg=PA324&printsec=frontcover|author=S. O.|title=Sicily|encyclopedia=The Jewish Encyclopedia|page=324|quote=The wearing of a special badge was ordered by the same monarch on Dec. 25, 1369. The badge consisted of piece of red material, not smaller than the largest royal seal; men were required to wear it, under the chin, and women on the breast.}} 
* [[December]] – Financed by Charles V of France, Welshman [[Owain Lawgoch]] launches an invasion fleet against the English, in an attempt to claim the throne of [[Wales]].A storm causes Owain to abandon the invasion. <ref>{{cite DWB|title=Owain ap Thomas ap Rhodri (' Owain Lawgoch '; died 1378), a soldier of fortune and pretender to the principality of Wales|first=Thomas Jones|last=Pierce|year=1959}}</ref>

=== Dates unknown ===
* The [[Ottoman Empire]] invades [[Bulgaria]].<ref>{{cite book|author=James C. Bradford|title=International Encyclopedia of Military History|publisher=Routledge|year=2004|isbn=0-415-93661-6}}</ref>
* [[Venice]] repels a [[Kingdom of Hungary|Hungarian]] invasion.
* The [[Thailand|Thai]] [[Ayutthaya Kingdom]] conquers [[Cambodia]] for a second time.<ref>{{cite book|author=
Kalman A. Dubov|title=Journey to the Kingdom of Cambodia}}</ref>
* Charles V of France orders [[Hugues Aubriot]] to construct the fortress of the [[Bastille]] in [[Paris]].
* [[Timur]] names the city of [[Samarkand]] as the capital of his empire.<ref>{{cite book|author=Ahmed Rashid|title=The Resurgence of Central Asia: Islam or Nationalism?|year=2017|publisher=New York Revie Books|page=254}}</ref>
* The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of the [[China|Chinese]] [[Ming dynasty]] issues a decree ordering every country magistrate in the empire to open a [[Confucianism|Confucian]] school of learning.
* The official production of [[Jingdezhen porcelain]] in Ming dynasty China is on record.</onlyinclude>

1370.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
*[[January 2]] – In France, the war over the autonomous state of [[County of Provence|Provence]], launched by King Charles V's brother, the [[Louis I of Anjou|Duke of Anjou]], against the ruling countess, [[Queen Joanna I of Naples]], is halted by a truce forced by the invention of [[Pope Urban V]] and King Charles.<ref>{{cite book |first=Raoul |last=Busquet |title=Histoire de Provence |publisher=Imprimerie nationale de Monaco |date=1954 |edition=1997 |page=198}}</ref>
*[[January 6]] – 11 ([[Tobi (month)|Tubah]] [[Coptic calendar|1086 AM]]) [[Pope Gabriel IV of Alexandria|Pope Gabriel IV]] is consecrated as the new [[List of popes of the Coptic Orthodox Church|leader of the Coptic Orthodox Church]] for the Coptic Christians of Egypt, and assumes the title of Bishop of Alexandria, succeeding the late [[Pope John X of Alexandria|Pope Yoannis X]], who had died eight months earlier.<ref>{{cite book |author=Youhanna Nessim Youssef |chapter=Athanasius of Qus and His Time |editor1=Gawdat Gabra |editor2=Hany N. Takla |title=Christianity and Monasticism in Upper Egypt |volume=2 |publisher=The American University in Cairo Press |year=2010 |pages=174–175}}</ref>
*[[January 9]] – The funeral of the late [[Philippa of Hainault|Queen Philippa]], who had served as Queen consort of England for 61 years as the wife of King Edward III, is held at [[Westminster Abbey]].<ref>{{cite book |last= St. John|first= Lisa Benz|date= 2012|title= Three Medieval Queens: Queenship and the Crown in Fourteenth-Century England|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=lTDHAAAAQBAJ&pg=PA4|location= New York|publisher= Palgrave MacMillan|page= 4|isbn= 978-1-349-29483-1}}</ref>
*[[February 18]] – The [[Battle of Rudau]] is fought between [[State of the Teutonic Order|the Teutonic Knights]] and the [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] near Rudau village, north of Königsberg (now Melnikovo village in the [[Kaliningrad oblast]]). According to the Teutonic chronicler Wigand of Marburg and the Livonian chronicle of Hermann de Wartberge, the Lithuanians suffer a great defeat.<ref>Rowell, S. C. (1994). Lithuania Ascending: A Pagan Empire Within East-Central Europe, 1295-1345. Cambridge Studies in Medieval Life and Thought: Fourth Series. Cambridge University Press. p. 243. ISBN 978-0-521-45011-9.</ref>
* [[March 20]] – King [[David II of Scotland]] divorces his wife and queen consort of six years, [[Margaret Drummond, Queen of Scotland|Margaret Drummond]]. Queen Margaret then travels to [[Avignon]] and persuades Pope Urban V to rescind the divorce before King David dies the next year.<ref>{{cite book|first=Archibald H.|last=Dunbar|title=Scottish Kings – A Revised Chronology of Scottish History 1005–1625|location=Edinburgh|publisher=D. Douglas|year=1899| pages=154-156}}</ref>
* [[March 27]] – [[Antonio Ballester]] of Catalonia is appointed as the [[Latin Archbishop of Athens]] by [[Pope Urban VI]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Kenneth M. |last=Setton|title=Catalan Domination of Athens 1311—1380|publisher=Variorum|year=2013|isbn=978-1258669010}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 9]] – [[Timur]] becomes first [[Amir]] of the [[Timurid Empire]], following the [[Siege of Balkh (1370)|Siege of Balkh]] which establishes his rule over the [[Chagatai Khanate]], completing his conquest of [[Central Asia]] and parts of [[Persia]].<ref>Marozzi, Justin (2004). Tamerlane: Sword of Islam, conqueror of the world. HarperCollins.</ref>
* [[May 23]] – [[Toghon Temür|Emperor Huizong]], who was the last Chinese ruler of the [[Yuan dynasty]] (from 1333 to 1368) and ruler of a portion of Inner Mongolia after his defeat in 1368, dies at the age of 49.<ref>{{cite book |last=Mote |first=Frederick W. |year=1999 |title=Imperial China 900–1800 |publisher=Harvard University Press |location=Cambridge MA |isbn=978-0-674-01212-7}}</ref>
* [[May 24]] – The [[Treaty of Stralsund (1370)|Treaty of Stralsund]] ends the [[Second Danish-Hanseatic War|second war]] between [[Denmark]] and the [[Hanseatic League]], an alliance of market towns across northern Europe along the [[North Sea]] and the [[Baltic Sea]].<ref>{{cite book|first1=Phillip|last1=Pulsiano|first2=Kirsten|last2= Wolf|title=Medieval Scandinavia: An Encyclopedia|publisher=Taylor & Francis|year=1993|page=265|isbn=0-8240-4787-7}}</ref>
* [[June 6]] – At [[Yingchang]], now part of the [[Hexigten Banner|Hexigten]] province of China's [[Inner Mongolia]] autonomous region, [[Biligtü Khan Ayushiridara]] is crowned as Emperor of the [[Northern Yuan]], the remaining portion of the Chinese territory that had been ruled by the [[Yuan dynasty]] prior its overthrow in [[1368]] by the rulers of the [[Ming dynasty]]. Prince Ayushiridara is the son of the late [[Toghon Temür|Emperor Huizong of Yuan]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=明初徐達築城與元大內宮殿的拆毀|trans-title=
Xu Da's Construction of the City Wall in the Early Ming Dynasty and the Demolition of the Yuan Dynasty's Inner Palace|author=Li Xieping|journal=Palace Museum Journal|year=1997|language=zh}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 16]] – An agreement is signed between Spain's [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pedro IV of Aragon]] and King [[Charles V of France]] for the marriage of [[John I of Aragon|Juan, Duke of Girona]], heir to King Pedro, and [[Joan of France (1351–1371)|Princess Jeanne de Valois]], the aunt of King Charles. However, before the marriage can take place, Jeanne dies in 1371 while traveling to meet Prince Juan.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Pastrnak |first=Patrik |title=Dynasty in Motion: Wedding Journeys in Late Medieval and Early Modern Europe |year=2023|publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=978-1-000-91707-9 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[August 16]] – (24th day of 7th month, [[Shōhei |Shōhei 25]]) The Japanese era [[Kentoku]] begins to reflect the reign of the southern [[Emperor Chōkei]]
* [[September 9]] – [[Casimir III the Great|King Casimir III of Poland]] sustains a complicated fracture of his left leg when he is thrown from a horse while deer hunting outside the village of [[Żeleźnica, Łódź Voivodeship|Zeleznica]].' When he ignores medical advice, his injury becomes infected and he dies of sepsis less than two months later.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=O śmierci Kazimierza, króla polskiego [About the Death of Casimir, King of Poland]|title=Kronika Jana z Czarnkowa|trans-title=The Chronicle of Jan of Czarnków}}</ref>
* [[September 19]] – The [[Siege of Limoges]] takes place in the course of the [[Hundred Years' War]] as the [[Kingdom of England|English Army]], led by [[Edward the Black Prince]], retakes the of Limoges from the [[Kingdom of France|French]]<ref name="Cassell's Chronology">{{cite book|last=Williams|first=Hywel|title=Cassell's Chronology of World History|url=https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/168|url-access=registration|location=London|publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson|year=2005|isbn=0-304-35730-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/168 168–169]}}</ref> by storm with wide destruction, effectively ending the [[Limoges enamel]] industry.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 20]] – [[Philip II, Prince of Taranto|Philip]] of [[Duchy of Anjou|Anjou]], [[Latin Empire|Titular Emperor of Constantinople]], marries  his second wife [[Elizabeth of Slavonia]] (daughter of Stephen of Anjou and Margaret of Bavaria).
* [[November 5]] – [[Casimir III the Great]], king of [[Poland]], dies two months after being injured in an accident while hunting, and is succeeded jointly by his sister, [[Elizabeth of Poland, Queen of Hungary|Elizabeth of Kujavia]], and her son, [[Louis I of Hungary]], beginning the rule of the country by the [[Capet-Anjou]] family.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Wyrozumski |first=Jerzy |author-link=Jerzy Wyrozumski |title=Kazimierz Wielki |date=1982 |publisher=[[Ossolineum]] |page=217|isbn=83-04-01041-0}}</ref>
* [[November 15]] – [[Trần Nghệ Tông]] deposes [[Dương Nhật Lễ]] as emperor of [[Đại Việt]], modern-day [[Vietnam]].<ref>{{citation|last=Ngo |first=Si Lien|title=[[Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư]]|trans-title= Complete Annals of Đại Việt|edition=Nội các quan bản|year=1993|language=Vietnamese|publisher=Social Science Publishing House|location=[[Hanoi]]|page=266}}</ref>
* [[November 26]] – [[Lithuanian–Muscovite War (1368–1372)|Lithuanian–Muscovite War]]: In retaliation for the attack by the Grand Principality of Moscow on Tver and Bryansk, the [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] and the [[Principality of Tver]] begin a two-day siege of the Muscovite city of [[Volokolamsk]]. While the leader of Volokolamsk's defenses, Prince Vasily Ivanovich Berezuysky, is killed, the attackers end the siege without capturing the city, and then march toward Moscow.<ref name=Batura/> 
* [[December 4]] – In the [[Battle of Pontvallain]], fought in the Hundred Years' War, a French army under [[Bertrand du Guesclin]] heavily defeats an English force in surprise attacks in northwest France.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Dictionary of Battles and Sieges: A Guide to 8,500 Battles from Antiquity through the Twenty-first Century: P-Z|last=Jaques|first=T.|publisher=Greenwood|year=2006|isbn=978-0-313-33539-6|volume=III|location=Westport CT|page=809}}</ref>
* [[December 6]] – [[Algirdas]], [[Grand Duke of Lithuania]], leads a siege of [[Moscow]] itself, the capital of the Grand Principality, and his forces burn and pillage the city as Moscow's Grand Prince [[Dmitry Donskoy]] retreats to the safety of the [[Moscow Kremlin|Kremlin]]. Donskoy's allies, his cousin [[Vladimir the Bold]] of [[Serpukhov]] and [[:ru:Владимир Дмитриевич|Prince Vladimir Dmitrievich Yaroslavich]] of [[Pronsk, Pronsky District, Ryazan Oblast|Pronsk]], come to Moscow's aid.<ref name=Batura>{{cite book |first=Romas |last=Batūra |chapter=Algirdo žygiai į Maskvą 1368 1370, 1372 ("Algirdas' campaigns to Moscow 1368 1370, 1372")|title= Žymiausi Lietuvos mūšiai ir karinės operacijos |trans-title=The most famous Lithuanian battles and military operations |language=lt |editor-first=Karolis |editor-last=Zikaras |edition=2nd |year=2013 |publisher=Alio |location=Vilnius |isbn=978-9986-827-05-4 |pages=46–49}}</ref>
* [[December 14]] – Moscow and Lithuania reach a truce to end the Lithuanian siege and Grand Duke Algirdas and his Lithuanian forces withdraw.<ref name=Batura/>
* [[December 20]] – The 200th Roman Catholic pontiff, [[Pope Urban V]], dies in [[Avignon]] after eight years, the first five of which were in [[Rome]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Chaillan|first=Marius |title=La vieille Église de Saint-Victor de Marseille et le Pape Urbain V: Documents des Archives Vaticanes|trans-title=The Old Church of Saint-Victor in Marseille and Pope Urban V: Documents from the Vatican Archives|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=K-viNAAACAAJ|year=1929|publisher=Tacussel|location=Marseille|pages=202-204|language=fr}}</ref>
* [[December 30]] – Cardinal Pierre de Beaufort, nephew of the late Pope [[Clement VI]], is [[1370 conclave|unanimously elected]] as the new Pope by 18 of the 20 Roman Catholic cardinals at Avignon. Beaufort takes the name [[Pope Gregory XI]] and is crowned six days later.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cardinals.fiu.edu/conclave-xiv.htm#1370 |last=Miranda |first=Salvador |title=Conclave of December 29-30, 1370 (Gregory XI) |work=The Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church |publisher=[[Florida International University]]}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Khun Luang Pa-Ngua, ruler of Suphanburi, marches and usurps the throne of the [[Ayutthaya Kingdom]].
* The city of [[Xi'an]] in [[Ming dynasty]] China is given a new defensive city wall.
* [[Hugues Aubriot]] begins construction of the fortress of the [[Bastille]] in [[Paris]].
* The steel [[crossbow]] is first used as a weapon of war.</onlyinclude>

1372.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 6]] – The coronation of [[Peter II of Cyprus|Peter the Fat]] as King Peter II of Cyprus takes place in [[Nicosia]] at the Greek Orthodox [[Selimiye Mosque, Nicosia|Cathedral of Saint Sophia]] (now the Selimiye Mosque).<ref name=Edbury>{{cite book|first=Peter W.|last=Edbury|title=The Kingdom of Cyprus and the Crusades 1191–1374|publisher=Cambridge University Press|date=1994|isbn=0521458374}}</ref> Peter had become the ruler of Cyprus at age 14 upon the death of his father, King Peter I.
* [[January 17]] – [[Frederick the Simple]], [[King of Sicily]], agrees to marry [[Antonia of Baux]], as part of negotiations for a peace treaty between Sicily and the [[Kingdom of Naples]] and Neapolitan and Papal recognition of his right to the throne. The marriage will take place the next year on November 26, 1373.
* [[January 29]] – [[John of Gaunt]], Duke of Lancaster and the third son of England's King [[Edward III]], [[John of Gaunt's claims to the Castilian throne|begins a claim to the throne]] of Spain's [[Crown of Castile]] after his September 21 marriage to [[Constance of Castile, Duchess of Lancaster|Princess Constance of Castile]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Wagner |first=John A. |chapter=John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster (1340–1399)|title=Encyclopedia of the Hundred Years War |date=2006 |publisher=Greenwood Press |page=183|isbn=978-0-3133-2736-0}}</ref> [[Peter of Castile|King Pedro of Castile]], who was killed by his brother, who took control as [[Henry II of Castile|King Enrique II]], in [[1369]]. 
* [[February 21]] – [[John IV of Brittany|Jean, County of Montfort]], [[Duchy of Brittany|Duke of Brittany]] makes a secret agreement with the [[Kingdom of England]] to allow English troops to pass through the lands he owns during the English war with France, event though he had previously allied with King Charles V of France in the same war.<ref>{{cite book|first1=Jean-Pierre|last1=Leguay|first2=Hervé|last2=Martin|title=Fastes et malheurs de la Bretagne ducale 1213-1532|trans-title=The Glory and Tragedy of Ducal Brittany (1213–1532)|publisher=Ouest France|year=1997|pages=124-125|isbn=978-2858823093}}</ref>
* [[March 8]] – In the [[Holy Roman Empire]], the Archbishop-Elector of Trier, [[Kuno II von Falkenstein]] and the Archbishop-Elector of Köln, [[Friedrich III. von Saarwerden]], become co-founders of their own [[Mint (facility)|mint]] abd begin production of being the minting of coins, including the "Weisspfennig" (the "white penny").<ref>{{citation|last=Suhle|first=Arthur|year=1974|chapter=Die Groschen- und Goldmünzprägung im 14. und 15. Jahrhundert (The Minting of Groschen and Gold Coins in the 14th and 15th Centuries)|title=Deutsche Münz- und Geldgeschichte von den Anfängen bis zum 15. Jahrhundert|trans-title=German Coinage and Monetary History from the Beginnings to the 15th Century|publisher=VEB Deutscher Verlag der Wissenschaften|page=174|language=de}}</ref>
* [[March 12]] – [[Bridget of Sweden|Saint Bridget]] sets out on a [[pilgrimage]] to the [[Holy Land]], staying in Cyprus until May 12. In August, she is in [[Bethlehem]] where she sees a vision of Jesus' birth. In September, she sets sail for [[Naples]], where she arrives in December.<ref>Fr. Paolo O. Pirlo, SHMI (1997). "St. Bridget". My First Book of Saints. Sons of Holy Mary Immaculate – Quality Catholic Publications. pp. 158–159. ISBN 971-91595-4-5.</ref>
*[[March 14]] – [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], signs a deed in [[Wrocław]], acknowledging the sovereignty of King [[Louis I of Hungary]] as ruler of Hungary, Croatia and Poland.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Deletant |first=Dennis |title=Moldavia between Hungary and Poland, 1347-1412 |journal=The Slavonic and East European Review |volume=64 |issue=2 |page=195 |year=1986}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 8]] – King [[Robert II of Scotland]] issues a [[Royal Charter]] granting [[royal burgh]] status to the town of [[Irvine, North Ayrshire]],<ref>{{cite book|first=James D.|last=Marwick|title=The River Clyde and The Clyde Burghs|location=Glasgow|publisher=The Scottish Burgh Records Society|year=1909|page=7}}</ref> a status that lasts for 603 years until royal burghs are abolished in 1975.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.visionofbritain.org.uk/unit/10360134  |title=Irvine Burgh|publisher=Vision of Britain}}</ref> 
* [[April 13]] – Saint Bridget and her fellow pilgrims arrive at [[Famagusta]] in [[Cyprus]], after their ship has survived a five-day storm that they had encountered after departing from Asia Minor.<ref name=ACQR>{{cite journal|author=Sven Magnus Gronberger|title=St. Bridget of Sweden— A Chapter of Mediaeval History|journal=The American Catholic Quarterly Review|date=January 1917|page=139}}</ref>
* [[May 10]] – [[Owain Lawgoch]] makes a second attempt to take the throne of [[Wales]], sailing with French support from [[Harfleur]], and issues a declaration of war against England for "having treacherously and covetously... slain my ancestors, kings of Wales," as well as having "by force and power appropriated" the country and submitted its people to divers services, the which country is, and should be, mine by right of succession, by kindred, by heritage, and by right of descent from my ancestors the kings of that country."<ref>{{cite journal|first=Owen|last=Edwards|url=https://archive.org/details/transactionsofho00hono/page/n5/mode/2up|title=Owain Lawgoch - Yeuain de Galles: Some Facts and Suggestions |journal=Transactions of the Honourable Society of Cymmrodorion|date=1900|pages=61-62}}</ref> After attacking the island of [[Guernsey]], Lawgoch will abandon the invasion in order to fight for France at [[La Rochelle]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Davies|first=Rees. R|title=The Revolt of Owain Glyndwr|date=1997|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=Oxford|page=436|isbn=978-0198205081}}</ref>
* [[May 13]] – St. Bridget and her fellow pilgrims finally arrive at [[Jerusalem]] on [[Ascension Day]] after a two-month journey.<ref name=ACQR/>
* [[June 22]] – The [[Kingdom of France]] and the [[Crown of Castile]] defeat the [[Kingdom of England]] in the [[Battle of La Rochelle]], and France gains control of the [[English Channel]] for the first time since [[1340]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sherborne |first=J. W. |date=1969 |title=The Battle of La Rochelle and the War at Sea, 1372-5 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1468-2281.1969.tb02322.x |journal=Historical Research |language=en |volume=42 |issue=105 |pages=17–29 |doi=10.1111/j.1468-2281.1969.tb02322.x |issn=1468-2281|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 10]] – The [[Treaty of Tagilde]] is signed between [[Ferdinand I of Portugal]] and representatives of [[John of Gaunt]] of England, marking the beginning of the [[Anglo-Portuguese Alliance]], which remains in effect into the 21st century.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Benham |first1=Jenny |title=The Treaty of Tagilde |url=https://www.bhsportugal.org/library/articles/the-treaty-of-tagilde |access-date=31 May 2022 |website=British Historical Society of Portugal}}</ref>
* [[August 20]] – Peace is declared between the [[Kingdom of Sicily]] and the [[Kingdom of Naples]] with the signing of the [[Treaty of Villeneuve]] between Joanna of Anjou (ruler of Naples) and King Frederick IV of Aragon (ruler of Sicily).<ref>{{Britannica|event/Sicilian-Vespers|Sicilian Vespers}}</ref>
* [[September 15]] – [[Jayasthiti Malla]] becomes the new [[List of Malla kings of Nepal|King of Nepal]] when he overthrows King [[Jayarjunadeva]], who had ruled since [[1360]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Petech |first=Luciano |url=https://ia902904.us.archive.org/29/items/mediaevalhistoryofnepallucianopetech_643_f/Mediaeval%20History%20of%20Nepal%20%20Luciano%20Petech.pdf |title=Medieval History of Nepal |publisher=Fondata Da Giuseppe Tucci |year=1984 |edition=2nd |location=Italy |page=133}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 10]] – King Peter II of Cyrpus is crowned as [[King of Jerusalem]] at a ceremony in [[Famagusta]],<ref name=Edbury/> although the Christian kingdom in Jerusalem had been dissolved 80 years earlier after the "[[Holy Land]]" fell to Muslim control in 1291. Although leaders of the Genoese and Venetian communities at Famagusta appear together at symbolic ceremonies to hold the two [[rein]]s of the King's horse, an argument over which leader would hold the rein on the right and who would hold the remaining rein on the left leads to a fight between the two communities after the Venetian leader is allowed to hold the rein on the right.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k110089k/f3.image|title=Chroniques d'Amadi et de Strambaldi|trans-title=Chronicles of Amadi and of Strambaldi|volume=1|pages=432-435}}</ref> With the Venetian winning the privilege, the [[Republic of Genoa]] organizes an expedition to invade and conquer Cyprus.
* [[October 24]] – (22 Rabi’ al-Thani [[Islamic calendar|774 AH]]) ; Four-year-old [[Muhammad III ibn Abd al-Aziz]] succeeds his father, [[Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz I]], as [[Marinids|Marinid]] [[List of rulers of Morocco|Sultan of Morocco]].
* [[November 9]] – [[Trần Duệ Tông]] succeeds his brother [[Trần Nghệ Tông]] as King of [[Vietnam]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Ngô |first=Sĩ Liên|title=[[Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư]]|trans-title=Complete Annals of Dai Viet|year=1993|language=vi|publisher=Social Science Publishing House|location=[[Hanoi]]|page=266}}</ref>
* [[December 2]] – [[Rupert I of Legnica|Ruprecht]] and his brothers [[Wenceslaus II of Legnica|Waclaw]], [[Bolesław IV of Legnica|Boleslaw]] and [[Henry VIII of Legnica|Henryk]] sign an agreement that they will not divide the [[Duchy of Legnica]] (in Poland) for at least 10 years, having jointly inherited from their father, Waclaw the First.
* [[December 30]] – ( 4th waxing of [[Pyatho]], [[Burmese calendar|734 ME]]. A major earthquake strikes what is now Myanmar during the reign of King [[Swa Saw Ke]] over the [[Kingdom of Ava]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Than Tun |title=History of Burma: A.D. 1300–1400 |journal=Journal of the Burma Research Society |date=December 1959|page=129}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Encounter of [[Sintra]]: Twenty [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] knights rout four hundred Castilian infantrymen of the country.
* The Kingdom of [[Chūzan]], ruled by King [[Satto]] on the island of [[Okinawa Island|Okinawa]], in [[Japan]]) enters [[Tribute|tributary relations]] with [[Ming dynasty]] [[China]] by way of an envoy, [[:ja:楊載 (明)|Yang Zai]], sent by the [[Hongwu Emperor|Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang]].
* [[Newaya Maryam]] succeeds his father, [[Newaya Krestos]], as ruler of [[Ethiopian Empire|Ethiopia]].
* The city of [[Aachen]], Germany, begins adding a [[Roman numeral]] [[Anno Domini]] date to a few of its [[coin]]s, the first city in the world to do so.</onlyinclude>

1373.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 13]] – King [[Charles VI of France]] issues an ordinance to reform the kingdom's defense forces, with a goal of improving efficiency and discipline. For the first time, captains of regiments of soldiers are required to pay their men directly and report the accounting to their superiors, who are required to audit the reports. Previously, the captains pocketed the wages and allowed their men "to pay themselves by pillage."<ref>{{cite book|first=James|last=Mackinnon|title=The Growth and Decline of the French Monarchy|publisher=Longmans, Green and Company |year=1902|page=57}}</ref>
* [[January 15]] – [[Majorie Castle]] in [[Switzerland]] becomes the official residence of the Roman Catholic [[List of bishops of Sion|Prince-bishop of Sion]], [[:fr:Guichard Tavelli|Guichard Tavelli]], and the bishops that follow.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Elsig |first1=Patrick |title=The Castles of Sion |date=2019 |publisher=Society for the History of Swiss Art SHSA |isbn=978-3-03797-600-5 |pages=30–34}}</ref>
* [[February 16]] – King Edward III of England appoints [[William Montagu, 2nd Earl of Salisbury|Lord Salisbury]] to command a fleet of English and [[Republic of Genoa|Genoese]] galleys and 1,700 soldiers to fight in the [[Duchy of Brittany]].<ref>{{cite book|first=J. W.|last=Sherborne|year=1994|title=
War, Politics and Culture in 14th Century England|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic|pages=49–50|isbn=9781852850869}}</ref><ref name=ED3>"Edward III", in ''Dictionary of National Biography''), volume 18, (Oxford University Press, 1899) p.68</ref> 
* [[March 7]] – [[Second Ferdinand War]]: The [[Battle of Lisbon (1373)|Battle of Lisbon]] is fought off the coast of the capital of the Kingdom of Portugal. The attack by the [[Crown of Castile]], by 12 galleys led by [[Ambrosio Boccanegra]], disperses the 21 ships of the defending Portuguese navy (led by [[:es:Lanzarote Pessanha|Lanzarote Pessanha]], and leaves [[Lisbon]] open to capture and pillaging by the Castilian invaders.
* [[March 21]] – The [[Battle of Chiset]] is fought between France and England near what is now [[Chizé]] in [[Deux-Sèvres]] [[département]] in France.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2, 2020|title=La Bataille et le Siege de Chize, 21 March 1373|url=https://la-guerre-de-cent-ans-et-nous.com/la-bataille-et-le-siege-de-chize-21-mars-1373/ |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=LA GUERRE DE CENT ANS ET NOUS |language=fr}}</ref> The French force of 1,500 defenders, led by [[Bertrand du Guesclin]] overwhelms 700-man English force led by [[John Devereux, 1st Baron Devereux|Baron Devereux]], who is taken prisoner of war.
* [[March 24]] – The [[:pt:Tratado de Santarém|Treaty]] of [[Santarém, Portugal|Santarém]] is signed between [[Ferdinand I of Portugal]] and [[Henry II of Castile]], ending the second war between the two countries.<ref>Chisholm, Hugh, ed. (1911). "Ferdinand I. of Portugal". Encyclopædia Britannica. Vol. 10 (11th ed.). Cambridge University Press. p. 265.</ref> 
* [[March 31]] – The [[Treaty of Villeneuve]], signed on August 20, 1372 to settle the dispute between the [[Capetian House of Anjou]] and the [[House of Barcelona]] over rule of the [[Kingdom of Sicily]], is ratified by [[Joanna I of Naples|Queen Giovanna of Naples]] (for Anjou), acknowledging the loss of Sicily to King [[Frederick the Simple]] of Sicily of the House of Barcelona.<ref>{{cite book |title=Medieval European Coinage, Volume 14: Italy (III) (South Italy, Sicily, Sardinia) |first1=Philip |last1=Grierson |author-link1=Philip Grierson |first2=Lucia |last2=Travaini |year=1998 |location=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press|page=270}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 28]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: The French re-capture most of [[Brittany]] from the English, but are unable to take [[Brest, France|Brest]], and [[John IV of Brittany|John IV, Duke of Brittany]], is forced into exile.<ref name=CBH>{{cite book|last=Palmer|first=Alan|last2=Palmer|first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=108–110|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[May 6]] – [[Byzantine]] co-emperor [[Andronikos IV Palaiologos]] allies with [[Savcı Bey]], the son of the Ottoman Sultan [[Murad I]], rebels against his father, [[John V Palaiologos]], for agreeing to let [[Constantinople]] become a [[vassal]] of the [[Ottoman Empire]], but the rebellion fails.<ref name=ODB>"Andronikos IV Palaiologos", by A. M. Talbot, in ''Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium'' (Oxford University Press), pp. 95–96</ref>
* [[May 7]] – The troops of the Papal States and of the [[county of Savoy]] and the French mercenary [[Enguerrand VII de Coucy]], defeat the [[Visconti of Milan|Visconti]], rulers of the [[Lordship of Milan]] in the [[Battle of Montichiari]] and stop Milan's attempts to expand its empire within Italy.<ref>{{cite book|first=Gianni|last=Oliva|title=I Savoia. Novecento anni di una dinastia|trans-title=The Savoys: Nine Hundred Years of a Dynasty|language=it|publisher=Mondadori|year=1999|page=113|isbn= 9788804464310}}</ref>
* [[May 13]] – The English [[anchoress]], Dame [[Julian of Norwich]] receives the 16 ''[[Revelations of Divine Love]]'' from God while seriously ill.<ref>{{cite book |date=2015 |editor1-last=Windeatt |editor1-first=Barry |title=Revelations of Divine Love |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yoQSBwAAQBAJ |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |page=ix|isbn=978-0-19-811206-8}}</ref>
* [[May 17]] – The dukes of the various duchies of Pomerania, enter into an alliance in a meeting at [[Karsibór|Kaseburg]] (now Karsibor in Poland) to resist the expansion of the neighboring state of [[Margraviate of Brandenburg|Brandenburg]].<ref name=Bucholz>{{cite book |editor1-last= Buchholz |editor1-first= Werner |title= Pommern |year=2002 |publisher= Siedler |language=de|isbn= 3886807800}}</ref> 
* [[May 30]] – Andronikos IV is arrested, imprisoned, and blinded in one eye on orders of his father, the Emperor John V Palaiologos, who was directed by Sultan Murad to carry out the punishment.<ref name=ODB/>Savci, who was completely blinded, is executed on orders of Murad, his father.<ref>Lord Kinross: ''The Ottoman Centuries'', (Trans. by Nilifer Epçeli) Altın Kitaplar, Istanbul, 2008, {{ISBN|978-975-21-0955-1}} p. 49</ref> After the rebellion fails, Ottoman Emperor [[Murad I]] commands to blind his son.<ref>Kazhdan, Alexander, ed. (1991). The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium. Oxford and New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN 0-19-504652-8, pp. 95–96.</ref>
* [[June 12]] – [[John of Gaunt's chevauchée of 1373]]: King Edward III appoints [[John of Gaunt]], Duke of Lancaster as his captain-general in the war in France and sends him with a large army across the English Channel to [[Calais]].<ref name=ED3/>
* [[June 16]] – The [[Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 1373|Anglo-Portuguese Treaty]] is signed in London, and is the oldest active treaty in the world.<ref name="Cassell's Chronology"/><ref>{{cite book|title=The New Guinness Book of Records 1996|year=1995|publisher=Guinness Publishing|page=183}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 1]] – [[Marquard of Randeck]], [[Prince-Bishop of Augsburg]], who had joined an alliance in a war against the [[Republic of Venice]], is defeated in the Battle of Fossa Nuova, near [[Treviso]], after the [[Doge of Venice]], [[Andrea Contarini]], hired Turkish mercenaries.
