Randeck is forced to negotiate surrender terms and sign a peace treaty.<ref name=DBIMDR>{{DBI|title= Marquardo di Randeck|first=Gerard |last=Schwedler|year= 2008|volume = 70}}</ref>
* [[August 4]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: [[John of Gaunt]] launches [[John of Gaunt's chevauchée of 1373|a new invasion of France]], setting out with 15,000 men from [[Calais]] and marching through Picardy, Champagne and Burgundy, "burning and destroying as he advanced<ref>".{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/John_Wyclif_A_Study_of_the_English_Medie/oRevCwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22John+of+Gaunt%22+August+1373&pg=PA255&printsec=frontcover|first=Herbert B.|last=Workman|title=John Wyclif; A Study of the English Medieval Church|publisher=Wipf & Stock|date=2012|page=255|isbn= 9781620325698}}</ref><ref name="Cassell's Chronology">{{cite book|last=Williams|first=Hywel|title=Cassell's Chronology of World History|url=https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/168|url-access=registration|location=London|publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson|year=2005|isbn=0-304-35730-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/168 168–169]}}</ref>
*[[August 8]] – [[Bristol perambulation]]: [[Bristol]] is made a [[county corporate]], the first town in he [[Kingdom of England]] outside London to be granted this status.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/bristol-record-society-01/page/118/mode/2up Norah Dermott Harding (ed.), ''Bristol Charters, 1155-1373'' (Bristol Record Society publications, Vol. I, Bristol, 1930), pp. 118-141.]</ref>
* [[August 18]] – The [[:de:Vertrag von Fürstenwalde|Treaty of Fürstenwalde]] is concluded between the Holy Roman Empire and the Margravate of Brandenburg, as the [[List of margraves and electors of Brandenburg|Margrave]] [[Otto V, Duke of Bavaria|Otto V]] abdicates the throne and sells Brandenburg to the Holy Roman Emperor in return for several castles and towns in the [[Upper Palatinate]] 500,000 [[Rhenish gulden|imperial guilders]] (1,900 kg or almost 68,000 ounces of gold) as [[Margrave of Brandenburg]]<ref>{{cite book|first=Jan |last=Winkelmann|title=Die Mark Brandenburg des 14. Jahrhunderts|trans-title=The March of Brandenburg in the 14th Century|publisher=|year=2011|page=81|isbn=9783867321129}}</ref>
* [[September 9]] – [[Władysław the White]] (Władysław Biały), formerly the [[Duchy of Gniewkowo|Duke of Gniewkowo]] begins [[Władysław the White's Rebellion|a rebellion]] against the [[Kingdom of Poland]] in an attempt to become the kingdom's monarch rather than the King of Hungary. He begins an attempt to reestablish his [[duchy]], capturing [[Gniewkowo]], [[Włocławek]], [[Inowrocław]] and [[Złotoria, Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship|Złotoria]], but ultimately fails after he flees to Zlotoria in 1376 and is besieged there, surrendering in [[1377]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Józef|last=Śliwiński |title=Władysław Biały|trans-title=Wladyslaw the White|publisher=Ostatni Książę Kujawski|location=Kraków|year=2017|pages=69-97|isbn=9788377302507}}</ref>
* [[September 12]] – , The German prince-bishop Marquard of Randeck signs a peace treaty with the [[Republic of Venice]], forfeiting all territory recaptured during the war, with the exception of [[Feltre]] and [[Belluno]].<ref name=DBIMDR/>
* [[September 25]] – At [[Constantinople]], [[Manuel II Palaiologos]] is proclaimed as [[List of Byzantine emperors|co-Emperor]] of [[Byzantium]] by his father, the Emperor [[John V Palaiologos]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Manuel II Palaiologos (1350–1425) |last=Çelik |first=Siren |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2021 |page=63|isbn=9781108836593}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 2]] – [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Wenzel of Luxembourg]], son of [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], is installed by the Empire as the new Margrave of Brandenburg, ending the war with Pomerania and entering into an alliance with the Pomeranian dukes.Buchholz (1999), p.161
* [[November 21]] – King Edward III opens the English Parliament at [[Westminster]] and demands more money to be raised to continue the war with France.<ref name=ED3/>
* [[November 25]] – [[Philip II, Prince of Taranto]] hands over the rule of Achaea (modern-day southern [[Greece]]) to his cousin, [[Joanna I of Naples]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/A_Companion_to_Latin_Greece/z3ajBQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=November+1373+Taranto+Achaea&pg=PA429&printsec=frontcover|title=A Companion to Latin Greece|editor1=Nickiphoros I. Tsougarakis|editor2=Peter Lock|publisher=Brill|year=2014|page=429|isbn=9789004284104}}</ref>
* [[December 21]] – The Parliament of England ends its session after 20 days and royal assent is given to measures passed therein, including an act setting "the length and breadth of cloth of ray,<ref>"ray" was a term for a form of striped cloth popular in the Middle Ages [http://lexissearch.arts.manchester.ac.uk/entry.aspx?id=3971|ray] in The Lexis of Cloth and Clothing Project, the [[University of Manchester]]</ref> and cloth of colour", and setting the exchange rate for a [[Scottish coinage#List of Scottish coins|Scottish groat]] as three English pence.<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |page=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Louis I of Hungary]] takes Severin again, but the Vlachs will recover it in [[1376]]–[[1377]].
* [[Constantine IV, King of Armenia|Constantine IV]], ruler of the [[Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia]] (modern-day southern Turkey), is assassinated; he is succeeded by his distant cousin [[Leo V, King of Armenia|Leo V]].
* <!-- The death of Sultan [[Muhammad III ibn Abd al-Aziz]] begins a period of political instability in [[Morocco]].(The death of Muhammad III is listed as 1374 in the article about him) -->
* <!-- The city of [[Phnom Penh]] (modern-day capital city of [[Cambodia]]) is founded.(The article says that Phnom Penh was founded in 1372)-->
* A city wall is built around [[Lisbon]], Portugal to resist invasion by [[Crown of Castile|Castile]].
* [[Merton College Library]] is built in [[Oxford]], England.
* The [[Adina Mosque]] is built in [[Bengal]].
* The [[Emperor of China|Chinese emperor]] of the [[Ming dynasty]], the [[Hongwu Emperor]], suspends the traditional [[Imperial examination|civil service examination system]] after complaining that the 120 new ''jinshi'' degree-holders are too incompetent to hold office; he instead relies solely upon a system of recommendations, until the [[civil service]] exams are reinstated in [[1384]].</onlyinclude>

1375.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 30]] – (28th day of 12th month of [[Bunchū|Bunchu 3]]) [[Emperor Go-En'yū]] is enthroned in [[Kyoto]] as Emperor of Northern Japan, after having succeeded his father, [[Emperor Go-Kōgon]], in [[1374]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=18oNAAAAIAAJ&q=nipon+o+dai+itsi+ran|first=Isaac |last=Titsingh |title=Nipon o daï itsi ran: Annales des empereurs du Japon|trans-title=Nipon o daï itsi ran: Annals of the Emperors of Japan|location=Paris|publisher=Royal Asiatic Society|year=1834|language=fr}}</ref>
* [[February 7]] – In what is [[Myanmar]], King [[Swa Saw Ke]] of [[Kingdom of Ava|Ava]] declares that occupiers from the neighboring [[Shan State]] of [[Möng Mao]] have been driven out of the kingdom, and a monument is inscribed at the capital, [[Inwa]]. <ref>{{cite journal |author=Than Tun |title=History of Burma: A.D. 1300–1400 |journal=Journal of Burma Research Society |date=December 1959|page=131}}</ref>
* [[February 13]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] issues the bull ''Debitum pastoralis offici'', establishing a second ecclesiastical province in the [[Kingdom of Poland]], the [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Halych]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Krętosz |first=Józef |date=2012 |title=Powstanie w 1412 roku metropolii lwowskiej obrządku łacińskiego oraz jego historyczny i kulturowy kontekst |trans-title=The establishment of the Latin-rite metropolis of Lviv in 1412 and its historical and cultural context|journal=Śląskie Studia Historyczno-Teologiczne |volume=45 |issue=2 |pages=316-330}}</ref>
* [[March 4]] – Under an agreement between [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]] and [[Leopold III, Duke of Austria]], Ludvik's one-year-old daughter, [[Jadwiga of Poland|Princess Jadwiga]], is [[betrothal|betrothed]] to Leopold's  four-year-old son [[William, Duke of Austria|Wilhelm of Habsburg]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Halecki |first=Oscar |author-link=Oscar Halecki |year=1991 |title=Jadwiga of Anjou and the Rise of East Central Europe |publisher=[[Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America]] |page=58|isbn=0-88033-206-9}}</ref>
* [[March 31]] – In the [[Principality of Nizhny Novgorod-Suzdal]] (now part of [[Russia]]), the Grand Prince [[Dmitry of Suzdal]] oversees the massacre of the [[Tatars|Tatar]] prisoners of war who had been captured during the [[Blue Horde]]'s unsuccessful [[Sary-Aka's embassy|attempt by Sary-Aka to incite a rebellion]] against the principality's domination by Moscow.<ref>{{cite book|author=Vladimir Volʹfovich Boguslavskiĭ|chapter=Nizhny-Novgorod|title=Славянская энциклопедия|trans-title=The Slavic Encyclopedia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5w2aelUEB_UC&pg=PA314|year=2001|publisher=ОLMA Media Group|isbn=978-5-224-02251-9|volume=2|page=314}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 14]] – The [[Mamluks]] from [[Egypt]] complete their [[Fall of Sis|conquest]] of the [[Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia]]. [[Leo V of Armenia|King Levon V]] is imprisoned for several years in [[Cairo]], until a ransom is paid by King [[John I of Castile]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Dadoyan |first=Seta B. |authorlink=Seta Dadoyan |title=The Armenians in the Medieval Islamic World: Armenian Realpolitik in the Islamic World and Diverging Paradigms: Case of Cilicia Eleventh to Fourteenth Centuries |volume=2 |publisher=[[Transaction Publishers]] |location=New Brunswick, New Jersey |year=2013 |page=191 |isbn=978-1-4128-4782-7}}</ref>
* [[April 21]] – At [[Kalaburagi]] (now apart of the Indian state of [[Karnataka]], [[Mujahid Shah]] succeeds his father, [[Mohammed Shah I]], as ruler of the [[Bahmani Sultanate]] in the [[Deccan Plateau]] of southern [[India]].<ref>{{cite journal|author= N Venkataramayya|title=Mujahid Shah Bahmani and Vijayanagar|journal=Proceedings of the Indian History Congress|year=1941 |volume=5 |pages=572–583}}</ref> A war begins two months later when the Sulatn Mujahid begins a fight against the neighboring [[Vijayanagara Empire]]<ref>{{cite web |first=M. H. |last=Rama Sharma |title=The History of the Vijayanagar Empire| website=Internet Archive |date=October 2016 | url=https://archive.org/stream/dli.bengal.10689.12385/10689.12385_djvu.txt}}</ref>
* [[May 1]] – [[Hungarian–Ottoman War (1375–1377)|The third war]] between the [[Kingdom of Hungary]] and the [[Ottoman Empire]] as the 40,000 Hungarian troops, led by [[Louis I of Hungary|King Lajos of Hungary]] depart from [[Oradea|Várad]] (now Oradea in Romania) and march into the [[Wallachia|Principality of Wallachia]], whose ruler, [[Vladislav I of Wallachia|Vladislav]], has recently changed his alliance from Hungary to the Ottoman sultanate.<ref>{{cite book|first=Gyula|last=Kristó|title=Az Anjou-kor háborúi|trans-title= The Wars of the Angevin Era|location=Budapest|publisher=Zrínyi Katonai Kiadó|isbn=978-963-326-905-3}}</ref>
* [[May 4]] – [[Simon Sudbury]], the Catholic Bishop of London becomes the new [[List of archbishops of Canterbury|Archbishop of Canterbury]], leader of the Roman Catholic Church in the Kingdom of England, upon his appointment by [[Pope Gregory XI]] following the death almost a year earlier of the Archbishop [[William Whittlesey]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fryde|first1=E. B. |last2=Greenway|first2=D. E. |last3=Porter|first3=S. |last4=Roy|first4=I. |title=Handbook of British Chronology|edition=Third revised |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |year=1996 |isbn=0-521-56350-X}}</ref> Sudbury will preside for six years until his assassination in [[1381]].
* [[June 18]] – In Spain, the eldest son of [[Henry II of Castile]], [[John I of Castile|Prince Juan of Trastámara]] marries the daughter of [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pedro of Aragon]], [[Eleanor of Aragon, Queen of Castile|Princess Leonor of Aragon]] as part of a peace agreement between the [[Kingdom of Castile]] and the [[Kingdom of Aragon]]. The marriage takes place at [[Soria]], a town on the [[Douro]] river, the border between the two kingdoms. Juan will become King of Aragon in 1379 and Leonor the Queen consort.<ref>{{cite book |first=Charles William |last=Previté-Orton |title=The Shorter Cambridge Medieval History |volume=2 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1960|page=767}}</ref>
* [[June 26]] – Shortly after an earthquake in [[Japan]], the Southern Court, ruled by [[Emperor Chōkei]], changes the name of the [[Bunchū]] era, and the [[Tenju]] era begins.
* [[June 27]] – [[Hundred Years' War]]: The [[England|English]], weakened by the plague, lose so much ground to the [[France|French]] that they agree to sign the [[Treaty of Bruges (1375)|Treaty of Bruges]], leaving them with only the coastal towns of [[Calais]], [[Bordeaux]] and [[Bayonne]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.maisonstclaire.org/timeline/1371.html |title=Timeline of the Hundred Years War. |access-date=October 13, 2012 |archive-date=May 9, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170509235653/http://www.maisonstclaire.org/timeline/1371.html |url-status=usurped }}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 3]] – The fortress of St. Sauveur le Viconte surrenders to a French fleet commanded by Jean de Vienne after a siege of more than six months.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|chapter=Owen of Wales|title=The Dictionary of National Biography |volume=42|publisher=Macmillan|year=1895|pages=396-398}}</ref>
* [[July 15]] – During a plague in England, Simon Sudbury, Archbishop of Canterbury, sends a call for prayers to all churches, asking that believers "pour out unceasing prayers to The Most High for the cessation of this pestilence or epidemic and for the tranquility of peace, and to entreat mercy of Him with a humble heart," and adds "For prayer is an immediate defence, an immolation of the enemy, a solace to angels and a pleasing sacrifice to God, and assiduous appeals for mercy made by a just man very often carry great power."<ref>{{cite book|title=The Black Death|editor=Rosemary Horrox|publisher=Manchester University Press|year=2013|page=120|isbn= 9781526112712}}</ref>
* [[July 24]] – Despite an appeal by [[Pope Gregory XI]] to cities in Tuscany to remain allied to the Catholic Church in a war with the [[Republic of Florence]], the city of [[Pisa]] enters a defensive alliance with the Visconti family of Florence and supplies are sent by Florence for lance-bearing soldiers, as well as archers and infantry as part of a federation of Tuscan communes.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Florentine_Politics_and_Society_1343_137/pwPWCgAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%2222+July+1375%22&pg=PA294&printsec=frontcover|title=Florentine Politics and Society: 1343-1378|first=Gene A. |last=Brucker|publisher=Princeton University Press|date=1962|pages=293-294}}</ref>
* [[August 8]] – In Switzerland, the Roman Catholic bishop [[:fr:Guichard Tavelli|Guichard Tavel]] becomes a victim of the long-standing feud between the Tavel family and the de la Tour family. Antoine de la Tour and a group of soldiers enter the [[Soie Castle]] (now in the Canton of Valais), ostensibly to arrest Bishop Tavel. The la Tour gang drags the Bishop up to the top of the castle walls and throws him off to his death.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.swisscastles.ch/valais/chateau/soie_d.html |title=Schloss de la Soie bei Savièse |trans-title=The Castle of la Soie in Saviese|website=www.swisscastles.ch}}</ref>
* [[September 4]] – In the [[Duchy of Aquitaine]], now part of [[France]] but at the time ruled by the King of England, the civic leaders of the town of [[Soule]] sign an agreement with [[Gaston III of Foix]], popularly known as "Fébus", for his protection against raids from [[John of Gaunt]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Tucoo-Chala |first=Pierre |url=http://archive.org/details/gastonfebusungra0000tuco |title=Gaston Fébus: Un grand prince d'Occident au XIVe siècle |trans-title=Gaston Febus: A Great Prince of the West in the 14th Century|date=1976 |location=Pau |publisher=Marrimpouey|page=142}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 24]] – [[Margaret I of Denmark]] becomes Regent of [[Denmark]] after the death of her father, [[Valdemar IV of Denmark|Valdemar IV]].
* [[November 12]] – At [[Brno]], now in the Czech Republic, [[Jobst of Moravia|Jobst of Luxembourg]] (Jošt Lucemburský) becomes the new [[margrave]] of [[Margraviate of Moravia|Moravia]], succeeding his father [[John Henry, Margrave of Moravia|Jan Jindřich Lucemburský]].<ref>{{Cite EB1911|wstitle=Jobst |volume=15 |page=427}}</ref>
* [[December 2]] – With the threat of the Russian Orthodox believers of the [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] being converted to the Roman Catholic Church, the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, [[Philotheos Kokkinos]], creates the Orthodox metropolis of Lithuania with the approval of the other bishops at the Council of Constantinople. Philotheos consecrates [[Cyprian, Metropolitan of Kiev|Cyprian]] as the first Orthodox Metropolitan of Lithuania and designates Cyprian will be the successor to [[Alexius, Metropolitan of Kiev|Alexius II]], Metropolitan of Kiev and all Russia.<ref>{{cite book|author=F. Shabuldo|url=http://resource.history.org.ua/cgi-bin/eiu/history.exe?Z21ID=&I21DBN=EIU&P21DBN=EIU&S21STN=1&S21REF=10&S21FMT=eiu_all&C21COM=S&S21CNR=20&S21P01=0&S21P02=0&S21P03=TRN=&S21COLORTERMS=0&S21STR=Kypriyan_mytropolyt |chapter=Kyprian, Metropolitan|title=Encyclopedia of History of Ukraine|year=2007}}</ref>
* [[December 20]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] designates nine new cardinals at Avignon, having appointed 21 new cardinals to supplement the 20 who had been living when he became Pope. Among those selected are [[Antipope Benedict XIII|Pedro Martínez de Luna y Pérez de Gotor]], who becomes the second [[antipope]] at Avignon during the [[Western Schism]] between Avignon and Rome.<ref>{{cite web|authorlink=Salvador Miranda (historian) |last=Miranda |first=Salvador |title=Consistories for the creation of Cardinals 14th Century (1303-1404): Gregory XI (1370-1378) |url=https://cardinals.fiu.edu/consistories-xiv.htm#GregoryXI|work=The Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church |publisher=[[Florida International University]]}}</ref>
* [[December 25]] – [[Joanna I of Naples|Queen Joanna]] of [[Kingdom of Naples|Naples]] signs a marriage contract for the fourth time, agreeing to be married to [[Otto, Duke of Brunswick-Grubenhagen]].<ref>{{cite book |first=Dominique |last=Paladilhe |title=La reine Jeanne: Comtesse de Provence |publisher=Librairie Académique Perrin |year=1997 |page=149|isbn=978-2-262-00699-0|language=fr}}</ref> Queen Joanna's first three husbands (Andrew of Calabria, King Louis I of Naples and the Margrave James IV of Majorca) had all died, in 1345, 1362 and 1375, respectively.
* [[December 28]] – [[Edward III of England|King Edward III]] summons the [[Good Parliament|English Parliament]] to assemble at [[Westminster]] on April 28, [[1376]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://historyofparliament.com/2019/06/18/dramatic-parliaments-of-the-late-14th-century-part-one/ |title=The Good, the Bad and the Wonderful: The dramatic Parliaments of the late 14th century (Part One)|website=historyofparliament.com|first=Hannes |last=Kleineke|date=June 18, 2019}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Grand Duchy of Moscow]] and [[Tver]] sign a truce. Tver agrees to help Moscow fight the [[Blue Horde]].
* Presumed death of [[Tenoch]], ruler of the [[Mexica]]; he is succeeded by [[Acamapichtli]] who becomes first ''[[tlatoani]]'' (ruler) of the [[Aztecs]] of [[Tenochtitlan]] and founder of the Aztec imperial dynasty.<ref>{{cite book|last=Aguilar-Moreno|first=Manuel|title=Handbook to Life in the Aztec World|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2007|isbn=978-0-19-533083-0}}</ref>
* [[Petru II of Moldavia|Petru]] succeeds as [[Voivode]] (ruler) of [[Moldavia]] (modern-day [[Moldova]] & eastern [[Romania]]). He is the first ruler from the dynastic [[House of Bogdan]].
* [[Coluccio Salutati]] is appointed [[Chancellor of Florence]].
* The [[Russia]]n town of [[Kostroma]] is destroyed by the [[Ushkuyniks|ushkuynik]] pirates from [[Novgorod]].
* [[Heirin-ji]] Temple is founded near [[Tokyo]].
* In [[Nanjing]], capital of [[Ming dynasty]] [[China]], a bureau secretary of the Ministry of Justice, Ru Taisu, sends a 17,000 [[Chinese characters|character]]-long [[memorial to the throne]], to be read aloud to the [[Hongwu Emperor]]. By the 16,370th character, the emperor has been offended by several passages, and has Ru Taisu summoned to court and flogged for the perceived insult. The next day, having had the remaining characters read to him, he likes four of Ru's recommendations, and instates these in reforms. Ru is nevertheless castigated for having forced the emperor to hear thousands of characters before getting to the part with true substance. The last 500 characters are elevated in court as the model-type memorial that all officials should aspire to create while writing their own.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Confusions of Pleasure: Commerce and Culture in Ming China|first=Timothy|last=Brook|publisher=University of California Press|year=1999|isbn=978-0-520-22154-3|page=32}}</ref>
* Approximate date – [[Battle of Gardiki]]: The [[Principality of Achaea]] defeats the [[Despotate of the Morea]].</onlyinclude>

1376.events:
===January–March===
* [[January 23]] – In the [[Holy Roman Empire]], [[Wenceslaus I, Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg]] and [[List of rulers of Saxony|Elector of Saxony]], marries Cecilia da Carrara, daughter of [[Francesco I da Carrara]], Lord of Padua.<ref>{{Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie|41|735|736|Wenceslas|W. of Sommerfeld|ADB:Wenceslas (Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg)}}</ref>
* [[January]] – In what is now [[Myanmar]] [[Ma Sein of Toungoo]], the Viceroy of Taungoo who had been appointed by the King of [[Binnya U]] of [[Hanthawaddy kingdom|Hanthawaddy]] to replace the assassinated Viceroy [[Pyanchi I of Toungoo|Pyanchi]], is murdered near [[Pyay]] while trying to forment a rebellion against the [[Kingdom of Ava]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Sein Lwin Lay |first=Kahtika U |title=Mintaya Shwe Hti and Bayinnaung: Ketumadi Taungoo Yazawin |language=Burmese |location=Yangon |publisher=Yan Aung Sarpay |orig-year=1968 |year=2006 |pages=23-24}}</ref>
* [[February 12]] – English mercenary [[John Hawkwood]], [[condottiere|condottiero]] for [[Pope Gregory XI]] in the [[War of the Eight Saints]] against the [[Republic of Florence]], arrives at [[Faenza]] to suppress a potential revolt against the papal governor. He and his soldiers, who were not paid by the Pope, go on to loot the town instead of protecting it.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Caferro |first1=William |authorlink1=William Caferro |year=2006 |title=John Hawkwood: An English Mercenary in Fourteenth-century Italy |publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press |location=[[Baltimore]]|pages=189-190|isbn=978-0-8018-8323-1}}</ref>
* [[February 19]] – [[Jan III of Oświęcim|Jan III]] becomes the new Duke of Oświęcim in Poland upon the death of his father, [[Jan II of Oświęcim]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Jasiński |first=Kazimierz |title=Rodowód Piastów śląskich |trans-title=Genealogy of the Silesian Piasts |date=2007 |publisher=Avalon |location=Kraków |page=621 |edition=2nd}}</ref>
* [[February 26]] – The ''[[:de:Böse Fasnacht|Böse Fasnacht]]'', a riot in the Swiss city of [[Basel]], breaks out during a tournament at a carnival and numerous people are killed, including several of the soldiers of the Duke of Austria, Leopold III.<ref name=Wenger>{{cite book|author=Lukas Wenger |url=https://stadtgeschichtebasel.ch/blog/adel-in-haft-die-boese-fasnacht-von-1376 |chapter=Adel in Haft – Die “böse Fasnacht” von 1376 |trans-title=Nobility Imprisoned – The “Evil Carnival” of 1376 |editor=Robert Labhardt|title=Im Kleinen das Grosse entdecken – Kurzgeschichten aus der Basler Stadtgeschichte (Discovering the Big in the Small— Short Stories from Basel’s City History) |publisher=Friedrich Reinhardt Verlag |location=Basel |date=2022 |ISBN=978-3-7245-2586-8 |pages=63–65|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Roger Jean Rebmann |url=https://altbasel.ch/fragen/fasnacht_1376.html |title=Die Böse Fasnacht von 1376 |trans-title=The Evil Carnival of 1376|work=altbasel.ch |date=January 25, 2024}}</ref> The city council arrests and executes 12 perpetrators, but Duke Leopold proceeds with placing the city under stricter control.
* [[March 12]] – The [[Treaty of Bruges (1375)|Treaty of Bruges]], signed on June 27, 1375 between [[Kingdom of England|England]] and [[Kingdom of France|France]] to end hostilities in the [[Hundred Years' War]] for a year, is extended by agreement to June 24, 1377.<ref>{{cite book|first=Françoise|last=Autrand|title=Charles V: le Sage|publisher=Fayard|year=1994|pages=617-618|isbn=978-2-213-02769-2}}</ref> 
* [[March 31]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] excommunicates all members of the government of the Republic of Florence, and places the city under an interdict.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Williman |first1=Daniel |first2=Karen |last2=Corsano |title=The Interdict of Florence (31 March 1376): New Documents |series=Rivista Di Storia Della Chiesa in Italia |volume=56 |issue=2 |date=2002|pages=427-481}}</ref>

===April–June===
* [[April 28]] – The [[Good Parliament]], so called because its members attempt to reform the corrupt Royal Council, begins in England .
* [[May 3]] – [[Olaf II of Denmark|Olav IV Haakonsson]] is elected King Oluf II of Denmark, following the death of his grandfather, [[Valdemar IV]], in [[1375]].
* [[June 7]] – The day before his death, [[Edward the Black Prince|Prince Edward of Wales]], heir to the English throne and known as "The Black Prince" summons his father, [[Edward III|King Edward III]], and brother, [[John of Gaunt]], and makes them swear to uphold the claim to the throne of his son [[Richard II of England|Richard]]. Edward is the first "[[England|English]]" Prince of Wales (as opposed to [[Wales|Welsh]]) not to become King of England.
* [[June 10]] – [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Wenceslaus the Idle]], son of [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], is [[1376 imperial election|elected]] [[King of the Romans]] by the prince-electors.<ref name=Wenceslaus>{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Wenceslaus |volume=28 |pages=517}}</ref>
* [[June 18]] – [[Catherine of Siena|Saint Catherine of Siena]], now the Roman Catholic [[patron saint]] of [[Italy]], visits [[Pope Gregory XI]] in [[Avignon]] in [[France]], to attempt to persuade him to make peace with [[Florence]], and move the Papacy back to [[Rome]].<ref>{{DBI|chapter= CATERINA da Siena, santa|author= Eugenio Dupré Theseider|year= 1979}}
</ref> 

===July–September===
* [[July 6]] –
**The Swiss city of [[Basel]] is placed under an imperial ban by the Habsburg dynasty's [[Leopold III, Duke of Austria]] because of the February 26 riot.<ref name=Wenger/>
**Wenceslaus the Idle is crowned King of the Romans at a ceremony in the [[Aachen Cathedral]].<ref name=Wenceslaus/>
* [[July 10]] – The [[Good Parliament]] is dissolved (at this time, it is the longest Parliament to have sat in England).
* [[August 12]] – With the help of the [[Republic of Genoa|Genoese]], [[Byzantine]] co-emperor [[Andronicus IV Palaeologus]] invades [[Constantinople]] and dethrones his father, [[John V Palaeologus]], as co-emperor. [[John V Palaeologus]] is taken prisoner.
* [[September 13]] – Pope Gregory XI departs from Avignon in France to begin his journey to Rome in an attempt to make peace between the Republic of Florence and the Papal States. 
* [[September]] – John of Gaunt summons religious reformer [[John Wyclif]] to appear before the Royal Council.

===October–December===
* [[October 7]] – King Edward III of England makes out his Last Will and Testament, formally declaring his grandson [[Richard II of England|Prince Richard]] as his successor, describing him as "Next we give and leave to our future heir, on whom may God confer his saving Grace, Richard, namely the son of Edward of honoured memory lately prince of Wales our firstborn son".<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_reign_of_Richard_II/HW8CEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22October+1376%22&pg=PR6&printsec=frontcover|first=Alison|last=McHardy|title=The Reign of Richard II: From Minority to Tyranny 1377–97 |publisher=Manchester University Press|year=2015|page=20 |isbn= 9781526112651}}</ref>
* [[October 12]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] and several cardinals of the Roman Catholic Church depart on a ship from the port of [[Marseille]] in [[France]], and encounter severe storms before arriving in [[Genoa]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Tombs_of_the_Popes/NZVDAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22October+1376%22&pg=PA96&printsec=frontcover|first=Ferdinand |last= Gregorovius|title=The Tombs of the Popes: Landmarks in the History of the Papacy |publisher=Victoria Home |date=1895| page=96}}</ref> He will finally arrive in Rome on January 17, 1377.
* [[October 28]] – Pope Gregory XI and his cardinals sail out of the Bay of Genoa toward Corneto. Several cardinals become seriously ill, including Cardinal de Narbonne, who disembarks at Pisa and dies there.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Irish_Monthly/kT6plmIzR1EC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22October+1376%22&pg=PA193&printsec=frontcover|title=A Citizen Saint|journal=The Irish Monthly Magazine|date=December 1874|publisher=McGlashan & Gill|page=193}}</ref>
* [[November 20]] – [[Richard II of England|Richard of Bordeaux]], son of the Black Prince, is created [[Prince of Wales]] in succession to his father.
* [[December 25]] – John of Gaunt presents his nephew, Richard of Bordeaux, to the feudatories of the realm and swears to uphold Richard's right to succeed Edward III.

1377.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 17]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] moves the papacy back from [[Avignon]] to [[Rome]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Rollo-Koster |first=Joëlle |year=2008 | title=Raiding Saint Peter: Empty Sees, Violence, and the Initiation of the Great Western Schism (1378) |publisher=Brill |page=182 |isbn=978-9004165601}}</ref>
* [[January 27]] – The "[[Bad Parliament]]", the 48th and last to be convened during the reign of King Edward III of England, begins its session with the goal of repealing most of the acts of the 1376 Parliament.<ref name=Omrod44>{{cite book |title= The Reign of Edward III |last= Ormod |first= W. M.  |year=2000 |publisher=Tempus |location=Stroud |isbn=0-7524-1773-8 |edition=Updated |pages=44–45}}</ref> Influenced by [[John of Gaunt]], 1st Duke of Lancaster and son of King Edward, it undoes the work done by the [[Good Parliament]], the previous year, to reduce corruption in the Royal Council.<ref>Wedgewood, J. C. (1930) "John of Gaunt and the packing of parliament", ''English Historical Review'' 45, pp. 623–5.</ref> For the first time, the leader of the members of the House of Commons has a title, as [[Thomas Hungerford (speaker)|Sir Thomas Hungerford]], Gaunt's steward, is selected as the first "[[Speaker of the House of Commons (United Kingdom)|Speaker of the House of Commons]]".<ref name=DNBHungerford>{{cite ODNB |author=Kightly, Charles |title=Hungerford, Sir Thomas |year=2004 |doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/14179}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author=Fryde, E. B. |author2=Greenway, D. E.|author3= Porter, S.|author4= Roy, I. |title=Handbook of British Chronology|edition=Third revised |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |year=1996 |isbn=0-521-56350-X |page=564}}</ref> 
* [[January]] – On the 24th day of the first lunar month of the year [[:vi:Đinh Tỵ|Dinh Ty]],  [[Trần Duệ Tông|Tran Due Tong]], [[List of monarchs of Vietnam|Emperor of Đại Việt]] ([[Vietnam]]), is killed in the [[:vi:Trận Đồ Bàn (1377)|Battle of Đồ Bàn]].<ref name=Ngo/>
* [[February 3]] – The Pope's representative in northern Italy, Robert de Geneve (the future [[antipope Clement VII]]), and mercenaries commanded by English soldier of fortune [[John Hawkwood]], complete the three-day pillaging of [[Cesena]] in the [[Papal States]], and [[:it:Massacro dei Bretoni|4,000 antipapal rebels are massacred]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cesenatoday.it/eventi/john-hawkwood-il-condottiero-inglese-che-segno-la-storia-di-cesena.html|title=John Hawkwood, il condottiero inglese che segnò la storia di Cesena|trans-title=John Hawkwood, the English leader who marked the history of Cesena|date=April 10, 2018}}</ref>
* [[February 24]] – In southern India, [[Harihara II]] succeeds [[Bukka Raya I]], as ruler of the [[Vijayanagara Empire]] at its capital, Vijayanagara (now [[Hampi]] in [[Karnataka]] state).<ref>{{Cite journal |url= https://www.jstor.org/stable/44145214|last=Lakshmi|first=Kumari Jhansi|journal=Proceedings of the Indian History Congress |date=1958|volume=21 |pages=290–297 |title=The Chronology of the Sangama Dynasty|jstor=44145214 }}</ref>
* [[March 2]] – The [[Bad Parliament]] dissolves and King Edward III gives royal assent to measures that roll back the 1376 legislation that he had been forced to agree to. He also approves the Bad Parliament's passage of a [[poll tax]] of four [[English penny|pennies]] for every male voter at least 14 years old, an attempt by the House of Commons to expand voting to the lower economic classes in return for expanding the tax burden from property owners to include those citizens who did not own property.
* [[March 13]] – At [[Hanoi|Thang Long]], capital of [[Dai Viet]] (now Hanoi, capital of the Republic of Vietnam), [[Trần Phế Đế|Tran Phe De]] succeeds his late father, [[Trần Duệ Tông|Tran Due Tong]] as the Emperor of Dai Viet. However, the real power remains with Nghe Tong, the regent for Phe De.<ref name=Ngo>{{cite book|author=Ngo Si Lien|authorlink=Ngô Sĩ Liên|title=[[Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư]]|trans-title=The Complete Annals of Dai Viet|year=1993|language=Vietnamese|publisher=Social Science Publishing House|location=[[Hanoi]]|pages=267–272}}</ref> 
* [[March 15]] – [[Al-Ashraf Sha'ban]], the [[Sultan of Egypt#Bahri Dynasty|Sultan of Egypt]] since [[1363]], is assassinated in [[Cairo]] and his 9-year-old son, [[Al-Mansur Ali II, Sultan of Egypt|Al-Mansur Ali II]] is installed as the new Sultan by the rebel leader Emir Aynabak al-Yalbughawi, who serves as the sultanate's actual leader.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Levanoni|first1=Amalia|title=A Turning Point in Mamluk History: The Third Reign of Al-Nāṣir Muḥammad Ibn Qalāwūn (1310-1341)|date=1995|publisher=Brill|page=104|isbn=9789004101821|url=https://www.academia.edu/12312607}}</ref>
* [[March 21]] – [[John Minsterworth]], who had plotted a French invasion of the Kingdom of England in conjunction with France's [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]], is arrested in [[Pamplona]], and letters to him regarding the proposed invasion are discovered. Minsterworth is taken first to [[Bordeaux]] in France and then returned for imprisonment in the Tower of London, where he reveals plans for a May 1378 invasion by the French Navy. Convicted of treason, he is executed on April 12 and his body is drawn and quartered.<ref>{{cite book|first=James H.|last=Ramsay|title=Genesis of Lancaster, or the Three Reigns of Edward II, Edward III and Richard II, 1307-1399|publisher=Clarendon Press|location=Oxford|year=1913|page=12}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 23]] – King [[Edward III of England]] formally confers [[knighthood]] upon two of his grandsons, both aged 10, [[Richard II of England|Prince Richard of Woodstock]] (son of King Edward's deceased son [[Edward the Black Prince]]), and upon [[Henry IV of England|Henry Bolingbroke]] (son of [[John of Gaunt]]), as well as his 13-year-old illegitimate son [[John de Southeray]], and 11-year-old [[John de Mowbray, 1st Earl of Nottingham|John de Mowbray]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Cokayne |first=G.E. |year=1936 |title=[[The Complete Peerage]] |volume=IX |edition=2nd |editor=H.A. Doubleday |editor2=Lord Howard de Walden |place=London |publisher=St. Catherine Press |author-link=George Edward Cokayne |page=780}}</ref> Two months later, Prince Richard will become King Richard II upon Edward's death, and in [[1399]], Bolingbroke will overthrow Richard and becomes King Henry IV. 
* [[May 22]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] issues five [[papal bulls]] condemning the opinion of [[John Wycliffe]], who has argued that Catholic priests should live in poverty, like the twelve disciples of [[Jesus]].
* [[May 24]] – [[Władysław II Jagiełło]] succeeds his father, [[Algirdas]], as [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania|Grand Duke of Lithuania]].<ref>{{cite book|first1= Jadwiga|last1=Krzyżaniakowa |first2=Jerzy|last2=Ochmański |title= Władysław II Jagiełło |date=1990 |isbn=9788304033177 |location= Wrocław |publisher=[[Zakład Narodowy im. Ossolińskich|Ossolineum]]|page= 362}}</ref> Jagiello initially shares power with his uncle, [[Kęstutis|Kestutis Giedyminowicz]], until [[1381]]. 
* [[June 21]] – After a reign of more than 50 years, [[Edward III|King Edward III of England]] dies at [[Sheen Palace]] in Richmond at the age of 64. His 10-year-old grandson, [[Richard II of England|Prince Richard of Woodstock]], succeeds to the throne as King Richard II. Richard is the son of King Edward's oldest son, [[Edward the Black Prince]], who had died a year earlier.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ormrod |first=W. Mark |title=The Reign of Edward III |date=2000 |publisher=Tempus |isbn=978-0-7524-1434-8 |edition=repr. |location=Stroud |page=45}}</ref>
* [[June 24]] – The [[Caroline War]], which had been fought for six years from 1369 until the [[Treaty of Bruges (1375)|Treaty of Bruges]] on June 27, 1375, resumes between the kingdoms of England and France as the treaty expires. The war, a dispute over the control of Aquitaine, will last until 1389.<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia|last=Wagner|first=John A|title=Encyclopedia of the Hundred Years War|publisher=Greenwood Press|location=Westport CT|year=2006|pages=63–64|isbn=0-313-32736-X }}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 16]] – [[Richard II of England|Richard II]], the 10-year-old grandson of [[Edward III]], is crowned king of England at [[Westminster Abbey]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Saul |first=Nigel |title=Richard II |date=1997 |publisher=[[Yale University Press]] |location=New Haven |isbn=0-3000-7003-9 |page=24}}</ref> A minority government is established, and a series of continual councils rule on his behalf until [[1381]].
* [[July 27]] –  [[Frederick the Simple]], who has reigned as King Federico III of Sicily since [[1355]], dies in [[Messina]] at the age of 35<ref>Setton, Kenneth M. (1975) "[[iarchive:AHistoryOfTheCrusades14th15thC|Volume III: The fourteenth and fifteenth centuries]]", Edited by Harry W. Hazzard, page 214.</ref> and is succeeded by his 14-year-old daughter, [[Maria, Queen of Sicily|Maria of Aragon]], who becomes the [[List of Sicilian monarchs|Queen of Sicily]]. The kingdom is administered by a regency of four "vicars", led by [[:it:Artale I Alagona|Artale I d'Alagona]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Giunta |first=Francesco |title=Alagona, Artale |encyclopedia=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani |publisher=Istituto dell’Enciclopedia Italiana |volume=1 |year=1960 |url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/alagona-artale_(Dizionario-Biografico) |language=it}}</ref>
* [[August 2]] – In the [[Battle on Pyana River]], part of the [[Great Troubles|Golden Horde Dynastic War]], an alliance of five Russian principalities is defeated by the Mongol [[Blue Horde]] (a part of the [[Golden Horde]]), led by [[Arab Shah|Arapsha Khan]]. According to a later Russian account, ''Chronicle On The Slaughter at Pyana River'', the Russian troops had been drinking [[mead]] and [[beer]] while waiting at the river for the Golden Horde attack and are intoxicated when Arapsha's troops attacked from five directions.<ref name=Pokhlebkin>{{cite book |last1=Pokhlebkin |first1=William |author-link = William Pokhlyobkin |title = [[A History of Vodka]]|date= 1992| publisher = Verso|pages=66–67| isbn= 0-86091-359-7}}</ref> The Russian commander, [[:ru:Иван Дмитриевич (суздальско-нижегородский княжич)|Prince Ivan Dmitriyevich]] of [[Nizhny Novgorod]] and staff attempt to retreat across the [[Pyana|Pyana River]] and drown, and the river itself,  Arapsha Khan and his troops then take over Nizhny-Novgorod with no opposition.<ref>{{cite book |last=Solovyov |first=Sergey |author-link = Sergey Solovyov (historian) |title = A History of Russia |volume=3 |chapter=7|year=1851–1879}}</ref> The name of the river itself derives from the [[Russian language]] word for "drunk", ''пьяный'' (''pyanyy'').
* [[August 4]] – The members of England's House of Commons and House of Lords are directed, in the name of the new King Richard II, to assemble at Westminster on October 13.<ref name=Dasent>{{Cite book |last=Dasent |first=W. I. |url=https://archive.org/details/speakersofhouseo00dase |title=The Speakers of the House of Commons from the earliest times to the present day |date=1911}}</ref> 
* [[August 21]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] agrees to acknowledge the right of existence of the [[Bologna|Bolognese Republic]] as autonomous within, and separate from, the other Papal States.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mAZBAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22August+1377%22&pg=PA161|title=A History of the Italian Republics: Being a View of the Origin, Progress & Fall of Italian Freedom |first=J. C. L.|last= Sismondi ·|publisher=J. M. Dent|year=1910|page=161}}</ref>
* [[August]] – The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of the [[Ming dynasty]] of China scraps the Office of Reports Inspection (established in [[1370]]) for a new Office of Transmission, in his efforts to create a more efficient communicatory system in the empire. A month before this he noted that anyone could send [[memorials to the throne]]; commoners often did, although the only times their petitions were read aloud to the emperor were when they called for the [[impeachment]] of local officials who were not up to par with their official duties.Wilkinson, 534–535.
* [[September 24]] – The Spanish Aragonese knight [[Juan Fernández de Heredia]] becomes the new [[Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller]], who control the island of [[Rhodes]], one of the [[Dodecanese]] islands of [[Greece]] and the island of [[Cyprus]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Luttrell|first=Anthony|title=Juan Fernandez de Heredia, Castellan of Amposta (1346–1377), Master of the Order of St. John at Rhodes (1377–1396)|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=1959}}</ref> Fernandez is elected by his fellow Knights to replace the late Grand Master [[Robert de Juilly]], who had died on July 29.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 13]] – Richard II of England's first parliament assembles for a session of almost two months. The House of Commons members elect [[Peter de la Mare]] as the Speaker of the House.<ref name=Dasent/> 
* [[October 26]] – [[Tvrtko I of Bosnia|Stefan Tvrtko]] is crowned as the first [[King of Bosnia]] at a monastery in [[Mileševa]] on the feast day of Saint Demetrius.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lovrenović |first1=Dubravko | title=Proglašenje Bosne Kraljevstvom 1377 |trans-title=The proclamation of Bosnia as the kingdom in 1377 |journal=Forum Bosnae |date=1999 |issue=3–04 |pages=227–287 |url=https://www.ceeol.com/search/article-detail?id=225841 |publisher=Međunarodni forum Bosna |language=bs}}</ref>
* [[November 16]] – The village of [[List of settlements lost to floods in the Netherlands#Drowned villages and places in Zeeland and West-Brabant|Westkerke]] in the Netherlands, on the island of [[Wolphaartsdijk]] is entirely washed away by a flood. Three centuries later, the Dutch will reclaim the land from sea by the building of dikes, Wolphaartsdijk will no longer be an island and the area where Westkerke had existed will be resettled. The remains of the lost village will be found in 1975, almost six centuries after its destruction.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orisant.com:80/verdronken/lijst.htm|last=De Schipper |first=Paul|title=Hele lijst met verdronken dorpen|trans-title=Full list of drowned villages|website=Orisant.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151127044001/http://www.orisant.com:80/verdronken/lijst.htm |archive-date=27 November 2015 }}</ref>
* [[November 30]] – The [[:it:Battaglia della Fornarina|Battle of Fornarina]] is fought in [[Italy]] when the independent village of [[San Ginesio]] (now in Italy's Macerata province) is invaded by mercenaries from the larger city of [[Fermo]] from a neighboring province. As the mercenaires cross through an unguarded and open gate, a baker in the middle of baking bread hears the troops approach, throws hot ashes into the first line of soldiers, and alerts the Ginosan troops who drive the invaders up a hill and over the side of a steep cliff.<ref>{{cite book|first1=Giovanni|last1=Salvi|title=Memorie storiche di Sanginesio (Marche) in relazione con le terre circonvicine|trans-title= Historical Memories of Sanginesio (Marche) in Relation to the Surrounding Lands|publisher= Tipografia Savini|location=Camerino|year=1889}}</ref>
* [[December 5]] – The English Parliament adjourns and laws passed therein are given royal assent by Queen Joan of Kent, regent for King Richard II. Among the laws enactted are the Purveyance Act ("Prelants shall have their action of trespass against purveyors offending"), the Arrest of Clergy Act (setting "the penalty for arresting of priests during divine service.") and the Villanies Act ("Commissions shall be awarded to enquire of and punish the misbehaviour of villains and land-tenants to their lords").<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |pages=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref><ref name=Dasent/>

=== Date unknown ===
* A rebellion against the [[Majapahit Empire]] is quashed in [[Sumatra]] in what is now Indonesia.
* Informed that [[Urus Khan|Khan Urus]] of the [[White Horde]] has died, [[Timur]] of the [[Timurid Empire]] sends [[Tokhtamysh]] to take the Horde throne, but is defeated by Urus' son, [[Timur-Malik|Timur Malik]].
* [[Radu I of Wallachia|Radu I]] succeeds [[Vladislav I of Wallachia|Vladislav I]] as [[Prince of Wallachia]] in what is now southern [[Romania]].
* King [[U of Goryeo]] adopts the [[Ming dynasty|Ming]] calendar and begs to be invested by the [[Hongwu Emperor]].
* The [[Trezzo sull'Adda Bridge]] is completed in Lombardy, and becomes the longest single-[[arch bridge]] in the world to be built for four centuries.
* A sermon by a German monk states "the game of [[card game|card]]s has come to us this year", and prohibitions against cards are issued by Prince [[John I of Castile|John of Castile]], and the cities of [[Florence]] and [[Basel]].</onlyinclude>

1378.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
[[File:Karel4 Karel5 Vaclav4.jpg|250px|thumb|[[January 6]]: The Banquet of the Three Kings is hosted in Paris.]] 
* [[January 6]] – At the Great Hall of the [[Conciergerie]] in [[Paris]], King [[Charles V of France]] hosts the Banquet of the Three Kings with his uncle, [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]] and the Emperor's son, [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Wenzel the Idle, King of the Romans]] as his guests (along with 800 German and French knights), to celebrate the friendship between the nations. The banquet, held on the day of the Feast of the Epiphany, has three courses, with 10 dishes in each course.<ref>{{cite book|last1=de Parseval |first1=Béatrice |last2=Mazeau |first2=Guillaume |title=La Conciergerie - Palais de la Cité |language=fr |publisher=Editions du Patrimoine- Centre des Monuments historiques |year=2019 |location=Paris |pages=14-15 |isbn=978-2-7577-0667-1}}</ref>
* [[January 13]] – [[Balša II]] succeeds his brother, [[Đurađ I of Zeta|Durađ I]], as ruler of [[Zeta under the Balšići|Lower Zeta]] in what is now [[Montenegro]].<ref>{{cite book|last=E. Jacques|first= Edwin |title=The Albanians: An Ethnic History from Prehistoric Times to the Present - Volume 1 |date=2009 |publisher=McFarland & Company|isbn=978-0-7864-4238-6 |page=169}}</ref>
* [[January 14]] – [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] opens the [[List of parliaments of Ireland|Irish Parliament]] for the first time since the death of his father, [[Edward III of England|King Edward III]], a year earlier.
* [[February 6]] – King [[Charles V of France]] is widowed when his queen consort, [[Joanna of Bourbon|Joanna]] dies at age 40, two days after giving birth to their last child, [[Catherine of France, Countess of Montpensier|Catherine]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Women, Manuscripts and Identity in Northern Europe, 1350-1550 |first=Joni M. |last=Hand |publisher=Ashgate Publishing |year=2013|page=16}}</ref> Against medical advice, Queen Joanna had taken a hot bath in order to induce labor.<ref>J. A. Buchon, ''Collection des Chroniques nationales françaises écrites en langue vulgaire du treizième au seizième siècle, Chroniques de Froissart'', Tome VII, Verdière, Libraire, Paris, 1824, p. 61</ref>
* [[February 12]] – [[Alexius, Metropolitan of Kiev]] and spiritual leader of the [[Russian Orthodox Church]] since 1354, dies of old age and his designated successor, [[Cyprian, Metropolitan of Kiev|Cyprian, Metropolitan of Lithuania]], attempts to become the new leader. However, Grand Prince [[Dmitry Donskoy]] of Moscow denies Cyprian permission and appoints [[Pimen, Metropolitan of Kiev|Pimen]] as successor to Alexius.<ref>John Meyendorff, ''Byzantium and the Rise of Russia'' (Crestwood, NY: St. Vladimir's Seminary, 1989), pp. 214–221.</ref>
* [[February 19]] – In [[Kingdom of England|England]], [[John Wycliffe]], who has been trying to promote ideas for Catholic reform and has published a [[Tract (literature)|tract]] outlining his theses, appears at the Church of St. Paul before a group of bishops headed by the [[Archbishop of Canterbury]], [[Simon of Sudbury]], to defend his actions. With a citation having directed him to appear "on the thirtieth court-day" after receipt, Wycliffe arrives before the bishops to proceed with trial, but proceedings are halted when Sir Lewis Clifford, dispatched by Joan of Kent,  Princess of Wales, acting as the regent for her son, King Richard II the Kingdom, directs that the bishops are "not to presume to determine anything against John Wycliffe. According to a chronicler, "Struck with terror, they at once abandoned the business of their meeting," but they subsequently order Wycliffe to appear at [[Lambeth]] in March.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/A_History_of_the_English_Church_596_1509/pX3ZAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wycliffe+February+1378&pg=PA425&printsec=frontcover|title=A History of the English: From Its First Planting to the Accession of Henry VIII. (596-1509) |volume=1|last=Perry|first=G. G.|publisher=John Murray |location=London|year=1903|page=425}}</ref>
* [[March 27]] – [[Pope Gregory XI]] dies at the Vatican in [[Rome]] after a little more than seven years as leader of the Roman Catholic Church, and shortly after moving the church leadership back to Rome from the French city of [[Avignon]]. Officials of Rome begin a campaign of intimidation to prevent the Roman Catholic cardinals, a majority of whom are French, from electing a French cardinal as Gregory's successor.<ref>{{cite book|first=Mandell |last=Creighton|title=The Great Schism. The Council of Constance, 1378–1418 |year=2012|publisher=Houghton, Mifflin & Company|page=50}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 9]] – Following the death of [[Pope Gregory XI]], and riots in [[Rome]] calling for a Roman pope, the cardinals, who are mostly French, meet in [[1378 conclave|a papal conclave]] and elect an Italian from [[Naples]], Bartolomeo Prignano, [[Archbishop of Bari]], as the 202nd [[Pope]].<ref>{{cite web |date=2002|last=Miranda|first= Salvador |author-link=Salvador Miranda (historian) |url=https://cardinals.fiu.edu/conclave-xiv.htm#1378 |website=The Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church | title=Conclaves of the 14th Century (1303-1394) |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303183708/http://www2.fiu.edu/~mirandas/conclave-xiv.htm#1378 |archive-date=3 March 2016}}</ref> Prignano takes the regnal name [[Pope Urban VI]], and is the last Pope of the Roman Catholic Church to have been elected from outside of the College of Cardinals. The French cardinals then flee from Rome before the populace learns that a non-Roman was picked, and return to [[Avignon]], beginning the [[Western Schism]], a 39-year period where rival popes are selected at Avignon and Rome.<ref>{{Cite CE1913|wstitle=Pope Urban VI}}</ref>
* [[April 16]] – [[Mujahid Shah]], ruler of the [[Bahmani Sultanate]] in what is now the [[Karnataka]] state in southern [[India]], is assassinated by his uncle, Da'ud Shah, while traveling between Adoni and Kulbarga. Da'ud and three accomplices enter Mujahid's tent and stab him to death, after which Da'ud declares himself to be the new Sultan of Bahmani.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last=Sherwani |first=Haroon Khan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3kIeAAAAMAAJ&q=The+Bahmanis+Of+The+Deccan+by+Sherwani,haroon+Khan |title=The Bahmanis of the Deccan |date=1985 |publisher=Munshiram Manoharlal |pages=119–123 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[April 18]] – The coronation of [[Pope Urban VI]] takes place in Rome on Easter Sunday.<ref>Bernhard Schimmelpfennig (translated by James Sievert), ''[https://archive.org/details/papacy0000schi_x5t1 The Papacy]'' ({{ISBN|0-231-07515-4}}), p. 220. Quote: "The next day, after Prignano had called upon them to do so, most of the cardinals came back to the palace and enthroned him. Prignano gave himself the name of Urban VI. The cardinals presented him with the customary petitions, and then took part in worship services being held not for the new pope but in celebration of Holy Week, before the new pontiff was crowned on Easter Sunday, April 18. The cardinals stayed at his court for the next three months, assisting him with liturgical functions. The curia that had remained in Rome likewise seemed to have acknowledged him."</ref>
* [[May 21]] – After only five weeks as Sultan of Bahmani in India, [[Daud Shah Bahmani|Da'ud Shah]] is assassinated while praying in the grand mosque at the capital, [[Kalaburagi]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Haig |first=Wolseley |url=http://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.46989 |title=Cambridge History Of India Vol. 2 |date=1925 |pages=383–384}}</ref> Da'ud Shah is succeeded by one of his nephews, Mahmud Shah. 
* [[May 26]] – [[Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür]] succeeds his father, [[Biligtü Khan Ayushiridara]], as ruler of the Northern [[Yuan dynasty]] in [[Mongolia]].
* [[May 30]] – The [[War of Chioggia]] begins on the Italian peninsula between the navies of the [[Republic of Venice]] and the [[Republic of Genoa]], with a surprise attack on 11 Genoese galleys at Capo d'Anzio by a 10-galley fleet led by Venetian Admiral [[Vettor Pisani]]. Venice captures five of the Genoese ships and takes their crews as prisoners of war, including the Genoese admiral, Luigi de' Fieschi.<ref>{{EB1911 |wstitle=Chioggia |volume=6 |page=235 |first1=Thomas |last1=Ashby |first2=David McDowall |last2=Hannay|authorlink2=David Hannay (historian)}}</ref>
* [[June 17]] – In the wake of the recent defeat of the Genoese Navy at the battle of [[Anzio|Capo d'Anzio]], [[Domenico di Campofregoso]], [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Genoa]], is removed from office by the Genoese Senate and replaced by [[Nicolò Guarco]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Musso|first=Riccardo|title=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nicolo-guarco_(Dizionario-Biografico)/|access-date=4 March 2012|year=2003}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 21]] – The [[Ciompi Revolt]] becomes violent in the [[Republic of Florence]] as a group of 64 discontented wool carders, led by [[Salvestro de' Medici]], briefly take over the government of Florence and place [[Michele di Lando]] in the executive office.<ref>Winter, Yves. "Plebeian Politics: Machiavelli and the Ciompi Uprising." ''Political Theory'' 40.6 (2012): 736–766.</ref>
* [[August 4]] – [[Gian Galeazzo Visconti]] succeeds his father, [[Galeazzo II Visconti]], as ruler of [[Milan]].
* [[August 11]] – [[Battle of the Vozha River]]: [[Dmitry Donskoy|Prince Dmitri Ivanovich of Moscow]] resists a small invasion by the [[Mongol]] [[Blue Horde]] under [[Mamai]].
* [[September 3]] – As regent for the 11-year-old King Richard II of England, his mother [[Joan of Kent]] summons the [[English Parliament]], directing the members of the House of Commons and the House of Lords to assemble at [[Gloucester]] on October 20.
* [[September 20]] – Unhappy with Pope Urban's critical attitude towards them, the majority of the cardinals meet at [[Fondi]], elect [[Antipope Clement VII|Clement VII]] as [[antipope]], and establish a rival papal court at [[Avignon]]. This split within the Catholic Church becomes known as the [[Western Schism]], also known as the Great Schism.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Western Schism {{!}} History, Background, Popes, & Resolution {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/Western-Schism |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref> France, [[Aragon]], [[Castile and León]], [[Cyprus]], [[Duchy of Burgundy|Burgundy]], [[Savoy]], [[Naples]] and [[Scotland]] choose to recognise [[Antipope Clement VII]]. [[Denmark]], England, [[Flanders]], the [[Holy Roman Empire]], [[Hungary]], northern [[Italy]], [[Ireland]], [[Norway]], [[Poland]] and [[Sweden]] continue to recognise [[Pope Urban VI]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 22]] – Sir [[James Pickering]] is elected as Speaker of the English House of Commons.
* [[October 31]] – The coronation of Count Onorato Caetani as the [[antipope Clement VII]] takes place in [[Italy]] at [[Fondi]] at the cathedral of San Pietro adjacent to the Caetani palace.<ref>Kelly, J.N.D. [1986] (2006) ''Oxford Dictionary of Popes'', Updated Ed. with new material by M. Walsh, Oxford University Press, {{ISBN|0-19-861433-0}} p. 566</ref>  Clement operates as a rival leader of the Roman Catholic Church for about a year before he and his cardinals relocate to Avignon.<ref>Giovanni Pesiri, ''Una inedita memoria dello Scisma d’occidente a Fondi: la cappella dell’antipapa Clemente VII nella cattedrale di S. Pietro'' ("An unpublished memory of the Western Schism in Fondi: the chapel of the antipope Clement VII in the cathedral of San Pietro"), in ''Annali del Lazio meridionale'', 10/1 (2010), pp. 7-13.</ref>
* [[November 10]] – The first observation of [[Halley's Comet]] from Earth is made, based on an estimate from orbital calculations.<ref>''Annales Mediolanenses''.</ref>
* [[November 16]] – The English Parliament concludes its session after four weeks, and [[royal assent]] is given to new laws passed during the session, including the [[Scandalum Magnatum Act 1378]], prescribing penalties for "telling slanderous lies of the great men of the realm", the Pope Urban VI Act 1378 (declaring that Urban "was duly chosen pope, and so ought to be accepted and obeyed," and the Riots Act 1378 granting authority to award commissions to persons to arrest rioters }and other persons offensive to the peace."<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |pages=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[November 29]] – [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], dies in [[Prague]]. He is succeeded by his son, [[Wenceslaus, King of the Romans|Wenceslaus]], as [[List of rulers of Bohemia|King of Bohemia]], but the office of [[Holy Roman Emperor]] falls into abeyance, until Charles's son [[Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor|Sigismund]] is crowned in [[1433]].
* [[December 16]] – The [[antipope Clement VII]] declares nine clerics to be added as cardinals of the Roman Catholic Church, joining those already allied with him as part of the [[Avignon Obedience]] against the cardinals of [[Pope Urban VI]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The Great Schism of the West|first=Louis|last=Salembier|publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co.|year=1907|pages=83-84}}</ref> Among the new "pseudo-cardinals", assigned to secure allegiance to the Antipope Clement from other European nations are [[Niccolò Brancaccio]], Nicolas de Saint-Saturnin,  Pierre Raimundi de Barrière Mirepoix, and Giacomo d'Itri.

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Raseborg Castle]] is mentioned for the first time in documents,<ref>[https://travel.sygic.com/en/poi/raseborg-castle-poi:19241478 Raseborg Castle - Sygic Travel]</ref> but its actual date of foundation is unknown.
* [[Tokhtamysh]] dethrones [[Temur-Malik (White Horde)|Temur-Malik]] to become Khan of the [[White Horde]].
* [[Uthman Beg]] establishes the [[Aq Qoyunlu]] (Turkomans of the White Sheep) dynasty at [[Diyarbakır]], in modern-day southeast [[Turkey]].
* [[Ottoman Turks]] capture the town of [[Ihtiman]] in west [[Bulgaria]].
* Tai Bian succeeds Zhao Bing Fa as King of [[Mong Mao]] (modern-day northern [[Myanmar]]).
* Sa'im al-Dahr is hanged for blowing the nose off the [[Great Sphinx of Giza]].<ref>According to [[Al-Maqrizi]].</ref></onlyinclude>

1379.events:
=== January–March===
* [[January 23]] – [[Maria, Queen of Sicily]] since 1377, is kidnapped from her home at the Ursino Castle in [[Catania]] by [[:it:Guglielmo Raimondo III Moncada|Guglielmo Raimondo III]] of the rival [[House of Moncada]] claimants to the throne held by the [[House of Barcelona|House of Aragon]]. The action takes place with the support of [[Peter IV of Aragon|King Pero IV of Aragon]], who installs his son [[Martin of Aragon]] as the Viceroy of Sicily.<ref>{{Cite web|language=es|url=https://www.enciclopedia.cat/gran-enciclopedia-catalana/maria-i-de-sicilia|title=Maria I de Sicília|work=Gran Enciclopèdia Catalana}}</ref> 
* [[February 16]] – King [[Richard II of England]] issues an order directing the [[List of parliaments of England#Parliaments of Richard II|English Parliament]] to assemble on April 24 in London. 
* [[February 18]] – [[Henry III, Duke of Mecklenburg|Heinrich III]] is installed as the new [[Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin|Duke of Mecklenburg]] at [[Schwerin]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wigger |first=Friedrich |year=1885 |title=Stammtafeln des Großherzoglichen Hauses von Meklenburg |url=https://mvdok.lbmv.de/mjbrenderer?id=mvdok_document_00002930 |journal=Jahrbücher des Vereins für Mecklenburgische Geschichte und Altertumskunde |chapter= |volume=50 |pages=111–326}}</ref> (now part of Germany) upon the death of his father, [[Albert II, Duke of Mecklenburg|Albrecht II]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia| first=Oliver |last=Auge |editor-last=Röpcke |editor-first=Andreas |title=Biographisches Lexikon für Mecklenburg. Band 6 |publisher=Schmidt-Römhild | publication-place=Rostock |date=2011 |isbn=978-3-7950-3750-5 |language=de | entry=Albrecht II. |url=https://purl.uni-rostock.de/rosdok/ppn1890621528}}</ref>  
* [[February 28]] – In what is now part of [[Kazakhstan]] and [[Russia]], [[Tulak (Golden Horde)|Tulak Khan of Borjigin]] is confirmed by the [[Beylerbey]] [[Mamai]] of the [[Golden Horde]], with the approval of the ruler [[Tokhtamysh]], after Mamai arranges the assassination of Tulak's cousin, the former khan.<ref>Safargaliev, M. G., ''Raspad Zolotoj Ordy.'' (Saransk: 1960) p.133</ref><ref>Grigor'ev, A. P., "Zolotoordynskie hany 60-70-h godov XIV v.: Chronologija pravlenii," ''Istriografija i istočnikovedenie stran Azii i Afriki'' 7 (1983), pp.9-54</ref>
* [[March 24]] – The [[First War of the Guelderian Succession]] ends after eight years of fighting in what is now the German state of [[North Rhine-Westphalia]], between [[William I of Guelders and Jülich|Wilhelm of Jülich]] and the Duchess [[Mechteld of Guelders]]. Duchess Mechteld, wife of [[John II, Count of Blois]], who renounces all claims to further rule after a defeat at the Battle of Hönnepel. In return for her surrender of claims to Guelders, she receives an annual pension of 33,000 gold pieces.<ref>Aleid W. van de Bunt: ''Mechteld, Hertogin van Gelre'', in: Gelders Oudheidkundig Contactbericht 33 (April 1967), pp. 1–6.</ref><ref>''Mechtild von Geldern (um 1320–1384). Vom begehrten Heiratsobjekt zur selbstbewussten Landesherrin des Spätmittelalters'' ("Mechtild of Geldern (c. 1320–1384). From sought-after marriage prospect to self-confident ruler of the late Middle Ages"), by Brigitte Sternberg, in ''Starke Frauen vom Niederrhein'' (''Strong Women of the Lower Rhine''), (Duisburg: Arbeitsgruppe »Gleichstellung der Region NiederRhein, 2000)</ref>
* [[March 31]] – The [[:es:Tratado de Briones|Treaty of Briones]] is signed between King Carlos of Navarre and King Enrique of Castile, ending a war that started the previous year. The Kingdom of Navarre ends its alliance with the Kingdom of England, whose troops it had allowed passage during the [[Hundred Years War]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lacarra|first=José María |title=Historia política del Reino de Navarra: Desde sus orígenes hasta su incorporación a Castilla|trans-title=The Political History of the Kingdom of Navarre: From its origins until its incorporation by Castile|volume=3|year=1973 |publisher=Aranzadi |location=Pamplona |isbn=84-500-5700-0|chapter=Tratado de Briones (1379)|page=196}}</ref>

=== April–June===
* [[April 9]] – (22nd day of third month of [[Eiwa|Eiwa 5]]) The [[Kōryaku]] era begins in the [[Northern Court]] of Japan at [[Kyoto]] on decree of the northern  [[Emperor Go-En'yū]] because of a disastrous time of plague and war.   
* [[April 24]] – The English Parliament opens for a five-week session under the direction of King Richard II. 
* [[May 7]] – The [[War of Chioggia#Battle of Pola (7 May 1379)|Battle of Pola]] is fought in the [[Adriatic Sea]] between the navies of the [[Republic of Genoa]] and the [[Republic of Venice]].<ref name="EB1911">{{EB1911 |wstitle=Chioggia |volume=6 |page=235 |first1=Thomas |last1=Ashby |first2=David McDowall |last2=Hannay|authorlink2=David Hannay (historian)}}</ref> The Venetian fleet, commanded by Admiral [[Vettor Pisani]]  loses 19 of its 25 galleys in the battle, but Genoese Admiral [[:it:Luciano Doria|Luciano Doria]] is killed in the battle. One of Doria's lieutenants conceals the admiral's death from the rest of the sailors by donning the admiral's clothes.<ref>{{DBI|title= Luciano Doria|author=Giovanni Nuti|year= 1992|volume = 41}}</ref> Admiral Pisani is put in prison upon his return to Venice, but later released when Genoa invades in the Battle of Chioggia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.veneto.org/history/serenissima2.htm|title=The voyage of Domenico Michiel|series=Venice Republic: the Middle Ages|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010828210513/http://www.veneto.org/history/serenissima2.htm|archive-date=August 28, 2001|work=Veneto}}</ref>
* [[May 27]] – The English Parliament closes after a short session, and King Richard II issues royal assent to legislation passed, including the Riots Act 1379, a prohibition against "fraudulent deeds made by debtors to avoid their creditors", and a confirmation of liberties of the Church.<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=24}} |page=24 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[May 29]] – [[John I of Castile|John I]] succeeds his father, [[Henry II of Castile|Henry II]], as King of [[Kingdom of Castile|Castile]] and [[Kingdom of León|King of León]].<ref>Elorza, Juan C.; Vaquero, Lourdes; Castillo, Belén; Negro, Marta (1990). Junta de Castilla y León. Consejería de Cultura y Bienestar Social (ed.). ''El Panteón Real de las Huelgas de Burgos. Los enterramientos de los reyes de León y de Castilla'' [''The Royal Pantheon of the Huelgas de Burgos. The graves of the monarchs of León and Castile''] (in Spanish) (2nd ed.). Editorial Evergráficas S.A. {{ISBN|84-241-9999-5}}.</ref>
* [[June 30]] – [[New College, Oxford]], is founded in [[Kingdom of England|England]] by [[William of Wykeham]], Bishop of Winchester.<ref>"The History of New College". New College. Retrieved 14 January 2025.</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 1]] – Forces of the [[Republic of Venice]] and [[Ottoman Turks]], having invaded [[Constantinople]], restore [[John V Palaiologos]] as [[Byzantine]] co-emperor. [[Andronikos IV Palaiologos]] is allowed to remain as co-emperor, but is confined to the city of [[Silivri]] for the remainder of his life.<ref>[[Andronikos IV Palaiologos#CITEREFPLP|PLP]], 21438. Παλαιολόγος, Ἀνδρόνικος IV. [Κομνηνός].</ref>
* [[August 16]] – The [[Republic of Genoa]], led by the [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] [[Nicolò Guarco]] and its allies from Hungary and Padua, captures Venice's port of [[Chioggia]] and [[Battle of Chioggia|seize the Venetian Army garrison there]] and soon threaten to take Venice and the Venetian Republic. An attempt by the Venetian Senate to apply for peace is rejected as Genoa demands a full surrender, and the Venetians resolve to fight, releasing Admiral Pisani from prison.<ref name="EB1911"/>
* [[September 9]] – The [[Treaty of Neuberg]] is signed, splitting the [[Austria]]n [[Habsburg]] lands between brothers [[Albert III of Austria|Albert III]] and [[Leopold III of Austria (Habsburg)|Leopold III]]. [[Albert III of Austria|Albert III]] retains the title of Duke of Austria.<ref>"Austria | Facts, People, and Points of Interest - Early Middle Ages". ''Encyclopedia Britannica''. Retrieved 14 January 2025.</ref>
* [[September 14]] – Andrea Contarini, Doge of Venice, announces to the besieged Venetians that the Republic will fight Genoa rather than surrender their nation.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 20]] – King Richard II issues a summons directing the English Parliament to assemble on January 16.
* [[November 28]] – From [[Avignon]] in [[France]], the [[antipope Clement VII]] issues his own a papal bull confirming the foundation of the [[University of Perpignan Via Domitia|University of Perpignan]].<ref>{{CathEncy|wstitle=Diocese of Perpignan}}</ref>
* [[December 22]] – [[Andrea Contarini]], the [[Doge of Venice|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Venice]], directs Admiral Pisani to blockade the port of Genoa, effectively trapping the Genoese fleet and preventing the occupation of Venice.<ref name="EB1911"/>

=== Date unknown ===
* Bairam Khawaja establishes the independent principality of the [[Kara Koyunlu]] (Turkomans of the Black Sheep Empire), in modern-day [[Armenia]].
* [[Dmitry Donskoy]] of [[Moscow]] raids [[Estonia]].
* In the [[Hundred Years' War]], the [[Kingdom of France|French]] lose control of most of [[Brittany]] to the English.<ref>{{cite book|last=Palmer|first=Alan|last2=Palmer|first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[Wisbech Grammar School]] is founded in England.<ref>"Schools". ''Cambridgeshire Archives and Local Studies''. Cambridgeshire County Council. Retrieved 14 January 2025.</ref>
* [[Timur]] conquers the [[Sufid]] Dynasty of Khwarazm.<ref>Bosworth, Clifford Edmund (1978). "Khwarazm". ''The Encyclopedia of Islam''. Vol. IV. Leiden: E. J. Brill.</ref>

1381.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
*[[January 14]] – [[Thomas of Woodstock, Duke of Gloucester]] and son of the late King Edward III of England, ends his [[:fr:Siège de Nantes (1380-1381)|siege]] of the French city of [[Nantes]] after two months, having started on 8 November 1380.
*[[January 25]] – [[Charles VI of France|King Charles VI the Beloved]] re-confirms the 1315 [[Charter to the Normans]] (''Charte aux Normands''), recognizing the rights and privileges of the residents of the  [[Duchy of Normandy]] to self-government within France. The Charter had lapsed in 1364 when [[Charles V of France|King Charles V the Wise]] declined to confirm it after ascending the throne.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Contamine |first=Philippe |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_2ydotlxKeUC&pg=PA215 |title=England and Normandy in the Middle Ages |date=1994 |publisher=[[The Hambledon Press]] |page=225 |isbn=1-85285-083-3 |editor-last=Bates |editor-first=David |editor-last2=Curry |editor-first2=Anne|volume=1 |chapter=Chapter 16: The Norman "Nation" and the French "Nation" in the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries: Proceedings of the conference held at the University of Reading in September 1992}}</ref>
*[[January 26]] – Japan's [[Kōwa (Muromachi period)|Kōwa era]] begins.
*[[February 1]] – Sir [[Robert Hales (knight)|Robert Hales]] is appointed by King [[Richard II of England]] as the new [[Lord High Treasurer]], replacing [[Thomas de Brantingham]] in an office that will eventually cost him his life. Because Hales administers the collection of taxes, including the new [[poll tax]] passed into law by Brantingham, 
*[[March 14]] – The Italian town of [[Chioggia]] concludes an alliance with the Croatian towns of [[Zadar]] and [[Trogir]] against the [[Republic of Venice]], which lsts until 1412.

=== April–June ===
*[[April 14]] – The second Treaty of [[Guérande]] is concluded in France between [[John I, Count of Penthièvre|Jean, Count of Penthièvre]] and [[John IV of Brittany|Yann IV, Duke of Brittany]] as Penthièvre drops his claim to rulership of the Duchy in return for being released from Gloucester Castle in England and being paid a substantial indemnity.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |encyclopedia=Medieval France: An Encyclopedia |title=Brittany |first=Julia H.M. |last=Smith |editor-first1=William W. |editor-last1=Kibler |editor-first2=Grover A. |editor-last2=Zinn |publisher=Garland Publishing Inc. |year=1995 }}</ref> Penthièvre had been the eldest son of [[Charles, Duke of Brittany|Charles of Blois-Châtillon]], who had been Duke of Brittany until his death in 1364.
*[[April]] – ([[Muharram]] [[Islamic calendar|783 AH]]) In what is now [[Afghanistan]], the [[Siege of Herat (1381)|Siege of Herat]] by the Mongol conqueror Timur ends with the Persian city surrendering to the Mongols, in return for the populace being spared.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Jalali |first1=Ali Ahmad |title=Afghanistan: A Military History from the Ancient Empires to the Great Game |date=15 December 2021 |publisher=University Press of Kansas |isbn=978-0-7006-3263-3 |page=221 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Afghanistan/NBGrEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&pg=PA221&printsec=frontcover |language=en}}</ref>
*[[May 21]] –  [[Al-Salih Hajji]] succeeds his older brother, [[Al-Mansur Ali II, Sultan of Egypt|Al-Mansur Ali II]] as the [[Mamluk Sultanate|Mamluk]] Sultan of [[Egypt]]. The Egyptian government continues to be controlled by rebel leader [[Barquq]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Steenbergen|first1=Jo Van|title=Order Out of Chaos: Patronage, Conflict and Mamluk Socio-political Culture, 1341-1382|date=2006|publisher=Brill|page=33|isbn=9789004152618}}</ref> 
* [[June 2]] – Due to the support by Queen [[Joanna I of Naples]] for the [[antipope Clement VII]], [[Pope Urban VI]] declares her cousin, [[Charles III of Naples|Carlo di Durazzo]] to be the new ruler of the [[Kingdom of Naples]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Tuchman |first=Barbara W. |author-link=Barbara W. Tuchman |year=1978 |title=A Distant Mirror: The Calamitous 14th Century |publisher=Ballantine Books |page=399|isbn=0-345-34957-1 }}</ref> Afterward, with the help of the [[Hungarians]], Charles advances on Naples and captures Joanna. [[James of Baux]], the ruler of [[History of Taranto|Taranto]] and the [[Latin Empire]], claims the [[Principality of Achaea]] after Joanna's imprisonment.
* [[June 12]] – [[Peasants' Revolt]]: In [[Kingdom of England|England]], rebels from [[Kent]] and [[Essex]], led by [[Wat Tyler]] and [[Jack Straw (rebel leader)|Jack Straw]], meet at [[Blackheath, London|Blackheath]]. There the rebels are encouraged by a sermon, by renegade priest [[John Ball (priest)|John Ball]].
* [[June 14]] – [[Peasants' Revolt]]: The [[Archbishop of Canterbury]], [[Simon Sudbury]] (who also serves as [[Lord Chancellor]] of England is assassinated along with England's [[Lord High Treasurer]] [[Robert Hales (knight)|Robert Hales]] by rebels who storm the [[Tower of London]], residence of King Richard II. The rebels, who also destroy [[John of Gaunt]]'s [[Savoy Palace]] in London take Sudbury and Hales to the execution grounds at [[Tower Hill, London|Tower Hill]] and behead both of them. King Richard then meets with Wat tyler and other leaders of the revolt and agrees to reforms such as fair rents and the abolition of [[serfdom]].
* [[June 15]] – 
**[[Peasants' Revolt]]: During further negotiations, [[Wat Tyler]] is murdered by the King's entourage. Noble forces subsequently overpower the rebel army. The rebel leaders are eventually captured and executed and [[Richard II of England|Richard II]] revokes his concessions. The revolt is discussed in [[John Gower]]'s ''[[Vox Clamantis]]'' and ''[[Froissart's Chronicles]]''.
**(23rd day of 6th month of Kowa) – In [[Japan]]'s [[Higo Province]], [[Imagawa Sadayo]] and [[:jp:今川仲秋|Imagawa Nakaaki]] capture [[:jp:菊池城|Kikuchi Castle]] and Somedo Castle. <ref>Shoji Kawazoe, "Imagawa Ryōshun," (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 1964) pp. 286-287 (in Japanese).</ref>

=== July–September ===
*[[July 16]] – King Richard II of England summons the members of the English Parliament to assemble at Westminster on November 3.
*[[July 17]] – The [[Battle of Saltes Island]] is fought off of the coast of Spain between the navies of the Kingdom of Portugal and the Crown of Castile, with all but one of the Portuguese fleet of 23 galleys being captured, and their crews taken prisoner, by a smaller force of 17 galleys commanded by [[Fernando Sánchez de Tovar]].
*[[July 21]] – [[Gaston III of Foix]], commonly known as Gaston Fébus, launches an attack against the regents for King [[Charles V of France]], defeating a brigade of 2,500 mercenaries enlisted by one of the regents, the [[John, Duke of Berry|Duke of Berry]].<ref name=PTC>{{cite book|last=Tucoo-Chala|first=Pierre|year=1991|title=Gaston Fébus, prince des Pyrénées|language=fr|publisher=Ėditions Deucalion| pages=239-244 |isbn=2-906483-43-5}}</ref>
*[[August 8]] – The [[Treaty of Turin (1381)|Treaty of Turin]] is signed between the [[Republic of Venice]] and the [[Republic of Genoa]] to end the three-year [[War of Chioggia]] against [[Genoa]], on terms favorable to Venice. The settlement comes more than a year after Venice's triumph in the [[Battle of Chioggia]] on June 24, 1380.<ref>{{cite book |last= Crowley |first = Roger |title= City of Fortune - How Venice Won and lost a Naval Empire|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cJuZ-NBod98C |location= London |publisher= Faber and Faber |date=2011 |page=|isbn= 978-0-571-24594-9}}</ref>
* [[August 25]] – Queen [[Joanna I of Naples]] surrenders the kingdom to [[Charles III of Naples|Carlo di Durazzo]], Duke of Slavonia, Croatia and Dalmatia, who had been able to start an invasion of Naples after the excommunication and order of deposition of Joanna by order of [[Pope Urban VI]]].
