The Duke then takes the throne as King Carlo III.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Goldstone |first=Nancy |year=2009 |title=The Lady Queen: The Notorious Reign of Joanna I, Queen of Naples, Jerusalem, and Sicily |url=https://archive.org/details/ladyqueennoto00gold |publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing|Walker & Company]] |pages=290-291 |isbn=978-0-8027-7770-6}}</ref>
* [[August]] – [[Kęstutis]] overthrows his nephew, [[Jogaila]], as [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania|Grand Duke of Lithuania]]. Jogaila is allowed to remain as governor of eastern [[Lithuania]]. This marks the beginning of the [[Lithuanian Civil War (1381–84)]].
*[[September 25]] – King [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia]] grants Count Bernhard of Wurttemberg permission to rebuild fortresses that had been destroyed during the war with  the Swabian League, despite an order by the Holy Roman Emperor Karl that forbids rearmament within the Empire.<ref>{{cite book|title=Verhandlungen des Historischen Vereins für Oberpfalz und Regensburg|trans-title=Proceedings of the Historical Society for the Upper Palatinate and Regensburg |publisher=Historical Society for the Upper Palatinate and Regensburg|year=1898|page=207|language=de}}</ref>
*[[September 27]] – [[John IV of Brittany|John IV]], [[Duke of Brittany]], executes the [[Guerande#Second Treaty_of Guérande|Second Treaty of Guérande]] with [[Charles VI of France]], pledging the Duchy's neutrality in any war between France and England.<ref>{{cite book|first=John Bell |last=Henneman |title=Olivier de Clisson and Political Society in France Under Charles V and Charles VI|publisher=University of Pennsylvania Press|year=2018|page=101|isbn=9781512802573}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
*[[October 10]] – The [[St. Mary's Syro-Malabar Catholic Church, Koratty|Church of Koratty Muthy]] is established by Roman Catholic missionaries and local Christians on the Indian subcontinent at [[Koratty]] in the [[Venadu kingdom]], now part of the [[Kerala]] state in [[India]].<ref>''Kerala District Gazetteers: Alleppey'' (Kerala Superintendent of Government Presses, 1980) p.41</ref>
*[[October 14]] – Fishmonger [[John Northampton]] is elected as [[Lord Mayor of London]] to succeed Sir [[William Walworth]], who had retired after suppressing Wat Tyler's rebellion.
*[[November 3]] – The [[List of Parliaments of England#Parliaments of Richard II|English Parliament]] assembles at Westminster on orders of King Richard II. The House of Commons elects [[Richard Waldegrave (politician)|Sir Richard Waldegrave]] as the Speaker of the House.<ref>{{cite DNB|wstitle=Waldegrave, Richard}}</ref> The Parliament meets for almost four months before being adjourned on February 25.
*[[December 26]] – Count Febus of Foix and the Duke of Berry meet at [[Capestang]] and work out an agreement to end their war, with the Duke agreeing to cease support of Febus's enemies, the Armagnacs, and Febus agreeing to recognize the Duke's authority over [[Languedoc]].<ref name=PTC/>

=== Date not known ===
* [[Timur]] conquers east [[Persia]], ending the rule of the [[Sarbadars|Sarbadar]] dynasty.
* Sonam Drakpa deposes Drakpa Changchub as ruler of [[Tibet]].
* The [[Ming dynasty]] of China annexes the areas of the old [[Kingdom of Dali]], in modern-day [[Yunnan]] and [[Guizhou]] provinces, inhabited by the [[Miao people|Miao]] and [[Yao people (Asia)|Yao]] peoples. Hundreds of thousands of Chinese (including military colonists) will migrate there from the rest of China.
* In [[Ming dynasty]] China, the ''lijia'' census registration system begun in [[1371]] is now universally imposed, during the reign of the [[Hongwu Emperor]]. The census counts 59,873,305 people living in China in this year. This depicts a drastic drop in population since the [[Song dynasty]], which counted 100 million people at its height in the early 12th century. A modern historian states that the Ming census is inaccurate, as China at around this time has at least 65,000,000 inhabitants, if not 75,000,000.<ref name="brook 28">[[Timothy Brook|Brook, Timothy]] (1998). ''[[The Confusions of Pleasure: Commerce and Culture in Ming China]]''. Berkeley: University of California Press. {{ISBN|978-0-520-22154-3}}.</ref></onlyinclude>

1383.events:
<onlyinclude>
=== January–March ===
* [[January 7]] – [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] issues a summons for the Lords and members of the House of Commons to assemble for the [[English Parliament]], to convene on February 23.
* [[January 13]] – At [[Heian-kyō]] (now [[Kyoto]]),  [[Emperor Go-Komatsu|Go-Komatsu]] is enthroned as the Emperor of the [[Northern Court]] of [[Japan]], after having succeeded to the throne on the abdication of [[Emperor Go-En'yū]] on November 19.<ref>[[Isaac Titsingh]], [https://books.google.com/books?id=18oNAAAAIAAJ&pg=PA25 ''Annales des Empereurs du Japon''],  pp. 317–327 (1834).</ref>
* [[February 11]] – [[Charles II of Naples|King Carlo III]] of [[Kingdom of Naples|Naples]] confiscates the property of [[Peter of Enghien|Pietro d'Enghien]] and Luigi d'Enghien (both of whom are in Venice) and declares them both to be rebels against the Neapolitan crown.<ref>{{cite journal |title=The Latins of Argos and Nauplia: 1311–1394 |first=Anthony |last=Luttrell |journal=Papers of the British School at Rome |volume = 34 |year = 1966 |publisher = British School at Rome |page=45}}</ref>
* [[February 2]] – The Doge of Genoa agrees to release King [[James I of Cyprus]] from captivity in return for an agreement that the King's son, [[Janus, King of Cyprus|Janus]], will become the new prisoner.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Kingdom of Cyprus and the Crusades, 1191-1374 |first=Peter W. |last=Edbury |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1994 |pages=174-175}}</ref> 
* [[February 23]] – The English Parliament opens at Westminster for its 9th session under the rule of King Richard II, and Sir [[James Pickering]] is elected as the Speaker of the House of Commons.
* [[March 10]] – The English Parliament adjourns. Among the laws given royal assent by King Richard are the pardon of most "offenders in the last insurrection, with few exceptions" and a statute of limitations on actions for trespass.<ref name=Statutes>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of and Index to the Statutes |edition=13th |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1896 |volume=1: To the End of the Session 59 Vict. Sess. 2 (1895) |url={{GBurl|EfcZAAAAYAAJ|page=29}} |pages=29 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[March 13]] – [[Michael de la Pole, 1st Earl of Suffolk|Michael de la Pole]] becomes the new [[Lord Chancellor]] of the England for King Richard II. 
* [[March 16]] – In [[France]], [[Évrart de Trémaugon]], an adviser to [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]], interrupts the King's dinner at the [[Louvre Palace]] and accuses Guillaume de Chamborant, the King's [[equerry]], of the murder of Evrart's brother Yvon.Famiglietti 2015, vol.1, p.279. Charges are eventually dropped against Chamborant 16 months later and Evrart is ordered on July 30, 1484, to pay 500 [[Livres tournois]], equivalent to more than 404 kilograms of fine silver, to Chamborant.<ref>{{cite book |last=Morice |first=Hyacinthe |title=Mémoires Pour Servir De Preuves A L'Histoire Ecclesiastique Et Civile De Bretagne |volume=2 |publisher=Osmont |date=1744 | page=477}}</ref>
* [[March 28]] – In a proclamation made by her envoys to Poland, [[Elizabeth of Bosnia|Elizabeth]], the former Queen consort of Hungary and regent for her 10-year-old daughter [[Mary, Queen of Hungary]], formally releases the Kingdom of Poland from an oath of loyalty to Mary and announces that she will send her 9-year-old daughter [[Jadwiga of Poland|Hedwig]] to be the queen of Poland.<ref>{{cite book |last=Halecki |first=Oscar |author-link=Oscar Halecki |year=1991 |title=Jadwiga of Anjou and the Rise of East Central Europe |publisher=Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America |page=101|isbn=0-88033-206-9 }}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 7]] – [[Nicolò Guarco]] is deposed as [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Genoa]] and is replaced by [[Federico di Pagana]], who in is forced to resign at the end of the day in favor of [[Leonardo Montaldo]].<ref>[https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nicolo-guarco_(Dizionario-Biografico) "Guarco, Nicolò"] in ''Dizionario Biografico d'Italia''</ref>
* [[May 5]] – (3rd waxing of [[Nayon]] [[Burmese calendar|745 ME]]) In what is now [[Myanmar]], [[Razadarit|Prince Binnya Nwe]] begins a rebellion against his aunt, the regent [[Maha Dewi of Hanthawaddy]], as he and 30 of his men seize the governor's residence at [[Dagon Township|Dagon]], near [[Yangon]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Fernquest |first=Jon |title=Rajadhirat's Mask of Command: Military Leadership in Burma (c. 1348–1421) |journal=SBBR |volume=4 |issue=1 |date=Spring 2006 |url=https://www.soas.ac.uk/sbbr/editions/file64410.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801053519/https://www.soas.ac.uk/sbbr/editions/file64410.pdf |archive-date=2019-08-01 }}</ref>
* [[May 17]] – King [[John I of Castile]] and [[Kingdom of León|Leon]] marries [[Beatrice of Portugal]].
* [[June 16]] – At a meeting of the Polish nobles at [[Sieradz]], [[Siemowit IV, Duke of Masovia]] announces that he will claim the crown as King of Poland. Queen Elizabeth of Hungary sends an army of 12,000 soldiers two months later to devastate the [[Duchy of Masovia]] and its capital, [[Warsaw]], forcing Siemowit to give up his claims to the throne<ref>.{{Cite book|last=Przybyszewski|first=Bolesław|title=Saint Jadwiga, Queen of Poland 1374–1399|publisher=Veritas Foundation Publication Centre|year=1997|page=8 |isbn=0-948202-69-6}}
</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 7]] – [[James of Baux]], ruler of [[Taranto]] and [[Principality of Achaea|Achaea]], and last titular [[Latin Emperor]], dies childless.<ref>{{cite book | last = Lock | first = Peter | title = The Routledge Companion to the Crusades | publisher = Routledge | year = 2013 | isbn = 9781135131371 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=AkCKZ9Hs4-QC | page = 130}}</ref> As a result, [[Charles III of Naples]] becomes ruler of [[Principality of Achaea|Achaea]] (modern-day southern Greece); [[Otto, Duke of Brunswick-Grubenhagen]], the widower of [[Joanna I of Naples]], becomes ruler of [[Taranto]] (eastern Italy); and [[Louis I, Duke of Anjou]] inherits the claim to the [[Latin Empire]] (western [[Turkey]]), but never uses the title of Emperor.
* [[August 20]] – King Richard II summons the English Parliament five months after the adjournment of the last session, and directs the members to assemble at Westminster on October 26.
* [[August 27]] – (End of [[Tawthalin]] 745 ME) Queen Maha Devi gives word to the army of Hanthawaddy that she will suppress the rebellion by  Prince Binnya Nwe, with an attack to be launched at the end of Burma's rainy season.<ref name=Pan1>{{cite book |last=Pan Hla |first=Nai | title=[[Razadarit Ayedawbon]] | language=my | orig-year=1968 | edition=8th printing | year=2005 |pages=125-129 | location=Yangon | publisher=Armanthit Sarpay}}</ref>
* [[September 12]] – Shortly before his death, [[Ferdinand I of Portugal|King Fernando I]] of [[Portugal]] creates the kingdom's first police force, the [[:pt:Quadrilheiros|Quadrilheiros]], initially consisting of 20 of the strongest men in [[Lisbon]], and gives them the authority to arrest criminals.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.psp.pt/Pages/apsp/historia.aspx?menu=1&submenu=4 |title=A História |location=Lisbon, Portugal | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100316064650/http://www.psp.pt/Pages/apsp/historia.aspx?menu=1&submenu=4 | archive-date=16 March 2010 | publisher=Policia de Segurança Pública |editor=PSP |language=Portuguese |year=2012}}</ref>  The concept of a city police force is expanded to other communities and becomes the basis for the [[Polícia de Segurança Pública]].
* [[September 19]] – In Macedonia in Greece, the city of [[Serres]] is conquered and occupied by forces of the Ottoman Empire and renamed Siroz. Under the terms of surrender, the Greek population keeps control of the churches and most homes inside the walled city, while the Ottoman Turks settle outside the walls, which are eventually torn down.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title = Serres |encyclopedia = Brill's First Encyclopaedia of Islam, 1913–1936, Volume VII: S–Ṭaiba |first=Martijn Theodoor |last=Houtsma |publisher=BRILL |location=Leiden |year= 1987 |isbn=90-04-08265-4 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=VJM3AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA234 |page=234}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 22]] – King [[Fernando I of Portugal]] dies, and is succeeded by his 10-year-old daughter, [[Beatrice of Portugal|Beatriz]]. Her mother, Fernando's widow [[Leonor Teles]], proclaims herself the regent <ref>{{cite book |last=Livermore |first=H.V. |year=1969 |title=A New History of Portugal |url=https://archive.org/details/newhistoryofport0000unse_y9g3/page/n9/mode/2up |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page=99 |isbn=9780521095716}}</ref> A period of civil war and anarchy, known as the [[1383–1385 Portuguese interregnum]], begins in Portugal, due to Beatriz being married to [[John I of Castile|Juan]] King of [[Kingdom of León|Leon and Castile]].
* [[October 26]] – The English Parliament is opened at Westminster for a one-month session. The House of Commons re-elects Sir James Pickering as Speaker of the House.
* [[October 28]] – (3rd waxing of [[Nadaw]], 745 ME) With the rainy season over in Burma, Queen Maha Dewi of Hanthawaddy dispatches armies from [[Bago, Myanmar|Pegu]], [[Mottama|Martaban]] and [[Myaungmya]] to attack her rebel nephew, Binnya Nwe, at Dagon.<ref name=Pan1/>
* [[November 19]] – (10th waning of [[Nadaw]] 745 ME) The Pegu army of [[Smin Maru]] is driven back by the rebel Nwe, while General [[Zeik-Bye]] declines to intervene.<ref name=Pan>{{cite book |last=Pan Hla |first=Nai | title=[[Razadarit Ayedawbon]] | language=my | orig-year=1968 | edition=8th printing | year=2005 |pages=154-156 |location=Yangon | publisher=Armanthit Sarpay}}</ref>
* [[November 26]] – The English Parliament adjourns and King Richard II gives royal assent to multiple laws, including "a confirmation of the liberties of the church", a prohibition of exports of weapons or food to the Kingdom of Scotland without royal approval, and the Vagabonds Act.<ref name=Statutes/>
* [[December 6]] – In a coup d'etat, [[:pt:João Fernandes Andeiro|Count João Fernandes Andeiro]], the brother of the regent Leonor Teles and uncle of Queen Beatriz of Portugal, is assassinated by [[John I of Portugal|João, Master of Aviz]]. 
* [[December 7]] – [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Wenceslaus II the Lazy]], who is also King of Bohemia, becomes the new [[List of monarchs of Luxembourg|Duke of Luxembourg]] upon the death of his uncle, [[Wenceslaus I, Duke of Luxembourg|Duke Wenceslaus I]].<ref>{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Wenceslaus |volume=28 |pages=517–518 }}</ref>
* [[December 10]] – (12th waning of [[Pyatho]] 745 ME) After breaking through Queen Maha Dewi's last defenses, Binnya Nwe's troops reach the walls of Pegu and forces a stalemate between Queen Maha and Prince Nwe.<ref name=Pan/>
* [[December 16]] – As Queen Beatriz of Portugal flees Lisbon toward [[Alenquer, Portugal|Alenquer]]. João, Master of Aviz is declared to be the new regent.<ref>{{cite book |last= Schäffer |first= Heinrich |title= Histoire de Portugal: depuis sa séparation de la Castille jusqu'à nos jours |trans-title=History of Portugal: from its separation from Castile to the present day |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=aVILAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA311 | publisher= Parent-Desbarres |year=1840 |volume= 1 |pages=324-325 |language=french}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Teutonic Knights]] recommence war against pagan [[Lithuania]].
* [[Dan I of Wallachia|Dan I]] succeeds his father Radu as [[Prince of Wallachia]]. He is the ancestor of the [[House of Dăneşti]].
* Rao Chanda succeeds Rao Biram Dev as [[Rathore dynasty|Rathore]] ruler of [[Marwar]] (in modern-day western India).
* [[Löwenbräu]] beer is first brewed.
* Completion of the original inner courtyard of [[Farleigh Hungerford Castle]] in [[Somersetshire]], England.
* The [[Wat Phra That Doi Suthep]] Temple is built in modern-day [[Thailand]], by King Kuena of [[Lanna]].
* Construction of the [[Bastille]] fortress is completed in [[Paris]], [[Kingdom of France|France]].</onlyinclude>

1384.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 2]] (10th waxing of [[Tabodwe]], [[Burmese calendar|745 ME]]) – King [[Binnya U]] of Burma's [[Hanthawaddy kingdom]] is killed in a rebellion at the capital, [[Bago, Myanmar|Bago]]. His 16-year-old son, Pasoom-Paing-Cek, is installed by the rebels as King [[Razadarit]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Pan Hla |first=Nai |author-link=Nai Pan Hla |title=[[Razadarit Ayedawbon]] |language=my |orig-year=1968 |edition=8th printing |year=2005 |location=Yangon |publisher=Armanthit Sarpay|pages=157–158}}</ref>
* [[January 26]] – England and France agree to a truce and ceasefire in the ongoing [[Revolt of Ghent (1379–1385)|Revolt of Ghent]]. The Kingdom of Scotland goes to war to retake Scottish territory occupied by the English Army.<ref name=Boardman>{{citation |last=Boardman |first=Stephen |authorlink=Steve Boardman (historian) |title=The Early Stewart Kings: Robert II and Robert III, 1371–1406 |publisher=John Donald, an imprint of Birlinn Ltd |year=2007 |location=Edinburgh |series=The Stewart Dynasty in Scotland Series |page=118 |isbn=978-1-904607-68-7}}</ref>
* [[January 30]] – [[Margaret III, Countess of Flanders|Margaret III]] becomes the [[Count of Flanders#House of Dampierre|Countess of Flanders]] upon the death of her 53-year-old father, [[Louis II, Count of Flanders|Count Louis II]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Louis II, count of Flanders |website=Encyclopædia Britannica |publisher=Encyclopædia Britannica, Inc. |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Louis-II-count-of-Flanders}}</ref> Margaret and her husband [[Philip the Bold]], [[Duke of Burgundy#House of Valois-Burgundy|Duke of Burgundy]], become co-rulers of both Flanders and Burgundy.
* [[February 4]] –  Scottish forces make an attack against English occupation forces in Scotland and recapture [[Lochmaben Castle]] and Teviotdale.<ref>Sir Herbert Maxwell, ''A History of the House of Douglas: From the Earliest Times Down to the Legislative Union of England and Scotland'', Volume 1 (Freemantle & Company, 1902) pp.92-93</ref>
* [[February 7]] – [[Nicholas Brembre]], [[Lord Mayor of London]] after defeating [[John Northampton]]'s bid for re-election, arranges to have Northampton arrested on charges of [[sedition]].
* [[February 11]] – In protest of former mayor Northampton's arrest in London, local businessman and shoe manufacturer [[John Constantine (cordwainer)|John Constantine]] incites other business owners [[London guild conflicts|to close their shops and to disrupt commerce]]. Constantine is then arrested and beheaded at [[Cheapside]] for leading an insurrection, and his severed head is placed on the [[Newgate]] entrance to the [[London Wall]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Cohn|first1=S. K.|title=Popular Protest in Late Medieval English Towns|year=2013|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge|page=42|isbn=978-1-10702-780-0}}</ref>
* [[March 3]] – King Richard II of England summons the members of the House of Commons and the House of Lords to assemble at [[Salisbury]] on April 29. 

=== April–June ===
* [[April 29]] – The Parliament of England opens a four-week session at Salisbury at the palace of the Bishop of Salisbury. [[Sir James Pickering]] is elected as Speaker of the House of Commons for the third consecutive time of his career.
* [[May 27]] – The English Parliament adjourns and King Richard II gives royal assent to laws passed during the session.
* [[May 29]] – The army of the [[Crown of Castile]] army begins the [[Siege of Lisbon (1384)|siege of Lisbon]], capital of the [[Kingdom of Portugal]].<ref>Miguel Duarte, Luís, Batalhas da História de Portugal – Guerra pela Independência, Academia Portuguesa de História, Lisboa, 2006, Vol. IV, pp. 88-92</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Rogers |first=Clifford J. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mzwpq6bLHhMC |title=The Oxford Encyclopedia of Medieval Warfare and Military Technology |date=2010 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-533403-6 |pages=511–513 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[June 15]] – [[Antoniotto I Adorno]] is elected as [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Genoa]] following the death of the Doge [[Leonardo Montaldo]] from [[bubonic plague]] the day before.<ref>{{cite web|last=Oreste|first=Giuseppe|title=Dizionario biografico degli Italiano|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/antoniotto-adorno_(Dizionario_Biografico)/|access-date=March 1, 2012|year=1960}}</ref> Adorno serves as the Republic's chief executive until 1390.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 19]] – Portugal's Navy, with 34 ships, breaks the Castilian blockade of bhe besieged city of [[Lisbon]], defeating a force of 53 Castilian ships in the [[Naval Battle of the Tejo|Battle of Tejo]].<ref>Tancredo de Morais, ''História da Marinha Portuguesa'' (''History of the Portuguese Navy'') (Lisbon: Clube Militar Naval, 1940) p.185</ref>
* [[July 26]] – The Treaty of Heidelberg ends a fight between the [[Swabian League of Cities#Merger|Süddeutscher Städtebund]] (South German League of Cities, with 28 member cities) and the allies of [[Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia|Wenceslaus IV, King of Germany]].<ref>Friedrich Ebrard, ''Der erste Annäherungsversuch König Wenzels an den schwäbisch-rheinischen Städtebund 1384-1385. Eine historische Untersuchung.'' (''King Wenceslaus's First Attempt at Rapprochement with the Swabian-Rhenish League of Cities, 1384–1385. A Historical Investigation'') (Strasbourg, 1877) [https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_uazCgIuEdykC online im Internet Archive]</ref>
* [[August 5]] – An earthquake strikes the island of [[Lesbos]] in [[Greece]], killing numerous people including the [[Republic of Genoa|Genoa]]n Lord of [[Lesbos]], [[Francesco I Gattilusio]], along with his two eldest sons, Andronico and Domenico. His son [[Francesco II Gattilusio|Jacopo Gattiliuso]] survives and rules the island under the name Francesco II.<ref>{{cite book |last=Wright |first=Christopher |title=The Gattilusio Lordships and the Aegean World 1355-1462 |page=46 |publisher=Brill |year=2014 }}</ref> 
* [[August 16]] – The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of [[Ming dynasty|Ming China]] hears a case of a couple who tore [[Banknote|paper money notes]], while fighting over them. Under the law, this is considered an act of destroying stamped government documents, which is to be punished by a [[caning|caning with a bamboo rod]] of 100 strokes. However, the Emperor decides to pardon them, on the grounds that it was unintentional.<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=《大明太祖高皇帝實錄卷之一百六十三》 |url=https://ctext.org/wiki.pl?if=en&chapter=116515 |trans-title=[[Ming Veritable Records]] |website=ctext.org |language=zh |location= |publisher=Chinese Text Project |access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>
* [[September 3]] – The [[Siege of Lisbon (1384)|siege of Lisbon]] by the Castilian Army ends as the Portuguese defenders protect the capital of the kingdom of Portugal. 
* [[September 28]] – King Richard II summons the English Parliament to meet on November 12.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 16]] – At the age of 10, [[Jadwiga of Poland|Jadwiga]] is crowned "King" of [[Poland]] in [[Kraków]] following the [[1382]] death of her father, [[Louis I of Hungary|King Louis of Hungary]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Halecki |first=Oscar |author-link=Oscar Halecki |year=1991 |title=Jadwiga of Anjou and the Rise of East Central Europe |publisher=[[Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America]] |page=109|isbn=0-88033-206-9}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last = Wyrozumski |first = Jerzy |title = Królowa Jadwiga. Między epoką piastowską i jagiellońską |publisher = Universitas |trans-title=Queen Jadwiga: Between the Piast and Jagiellonian Eras |location= Kraków |year = 1997 |pages = 83–84 |isbn = 83-7052-934-8 }}</ref>
* [[November 12]] – The 12th parliament of King Richard II assembles and elects James Pickering as Speaker of the House for the fourth consecutive time.
* [[December 14]] – The second assembly in 1384 of the English Parliament is adjourned.
* [[December 25]] – Use of the [[Spanish era]] dating system in the [[Crown of Castile]] is suppressed.

=== Unknown Date ===
* The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of [[Ming China]] reinstates the [[Imperial examination]] system for drafting [[scholar-official]]s to the civil service, after suspending the system since [[1373]], in favor of a recommendation system to office.
* The [[Nasrid dynasty|Nasrid]] princes of [[Al-Andalus]] replace Abu al-Abbas with Abu Faris Musa ibn Faris, as ruler of the [[Marinid dynasty]] in modern-day [[Morocco]].
* Zain Al-Abidin succeeds his father, Shah Shuja, as ruler of the [[Muzaffarids (Iran)|Muzaffarids]] in central [[Persia]].
* Shortly before his death on the last day of the year, [[John Wycliffe]] sends out [[Tract (literature)|tract]]s against [[Pope Urban VI]], who has not turned out to be the reformist Wycliffe had hoped.
* Qara Muhammad succeeds Bairam Khawaja, as ruler of the [[Kara Koyunlu]] ("Black Sheep Turkomans"), in modern-day [[Armenia]] and northern [[Iraq]].
* [[Timur]] conquers the northern territories of the [[Jalayirid]] Empire, in western [[Persia]].
* [[Katharine Lady Berkeley's School]] is founded in [[Gloucestershire]], England.<ref>{{Cite ODNB |title=Berkeley [née Clivedon], Katherine, Lady Berkeley (d. 1385), benefactor |url=https://www.oxforddnb.com/view/10.1093/ref:odnb/9780198614128.001.0001/odnb-9780198614128-e-54435 |access-date=2021-03-25 | year=2004 |language=en |doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/54435| isbn=978-0-19-861412-8 }}</ref></onlyinclude>

1385.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 11]] – After learning that several of his cardinals had been debating whether to depose him on grounds that he is insane, [[Pope Urban VI]] orders the arrest of all of the cardinals within his reach. [[:it:Giovanni da Amelia|Giovanni da Amelia]], [[:it:Gentile di Sangro|Gentile di Sangro]], [[Adam Eston]], [[Ludovico Donato]], [[:it:Bartolomeo da Cogorno|Bartolomeo da Cogorno]], and [[:it:Marino del Giudice|Marino del Giudice]] are all arrested and imprisoned and tortured at the castle of Nocera.<ref>{{cite book|author=Dietrich (von Nieheim)|editor=Georg Erler|title=Theoderici de Nyem De scismate libri tres|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tFVhAAAAMAAJ|year=1890|publisher=Veit|location=Leipzig|language=Latin|pages=77–79}}</ref> Except for Eston, the cardinals arrested are put to death in [[Genoa]] by the end of 1386.<ref>{{cite book|editor-last1=Eubel|editor-first1=Conradus |title=Hierarchia catholica|volume= Tomus I|date=1913|publisher=Libreria Regensbergiana|pages=23–24|location=Münster|edition=second|language=Latin|url=https://archive.org/details/hierarchiacathol01eubeuoft}}</ref> 
* [[February 3]] – (2 [[Muharram]] [[Islamic calendar|787 AH]]) The [[Sultan Isa Medrese|madrasa]] (a religious school) of the Emir of [[Artuqids|Artuqid Empire]], [[Majd al-Din Isa Al-Zahir]], is dedicated and the date is placed on an inscription on the wall.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Beyazit |first=Deniz |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=94gxEAAAQBAJ&dq=mardin+zinciriye+muqarnas&pg=PA206 |title=Le décor architectural artuqide en pierre de Mardin placé dans son contexte regional: Contribution à l'histoire du décor géométrique et végétal du Proche-Orient des XIIe-XVe siècles |trans-title=Artuqid Architectural Stone Decoration in Mardin Placed within its Regional Context: A Contribution to the History of Geometric and Vegetal Decoration in the Near East (12th–15th Centuries) |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |year=2016 |isbn=978-1-78491-123-2 |pages=80–86 |language=fr}}</ref> The building is now a historic landmark in the city of [[Mardin]], now located in Turkey. 
* [[February 14]] – [[John of Gaunt]], Duke of Lancaster, son of the late King Edward III of England and uncle of King Richard II, flees London after learning during a [[joust]] that he has been targeted for assassination by the King's advisors [[Thomas Mowbray, 1st Duke of Norfolk]] and [[Robert de Vere, 9th Earl of Oxford]]; and [[John Montagu, 3rd Earl of Salisbury|John de Montacute, Earl of Salisbury]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Goodman |first=Anthony|title=John of Gaunt: The Exercise of Princely Power in Fourteenth-Century Europe |date=2013|publisher=Routledge|page=102|isbn=978-1-31789-480-3 |location=London}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Walsingham|first=Thomas|title=The Chronica Maiora of Thomas Walsingham, 1376–1422|translator-last1=Preest|translator-first1=D.|orig-year=1863–1864|editor-first=J. G.|editor-last=Clark|date=2005|publisher=Boydell Press|page=140|isbn=978-1-84383-144-0|location=Woodbridge}}</ref>
* [[February]] – [[List of rulers of Kano#Sultanate of Kano|Bugaya]] becomes the new [[Sultanate of Kano|Sultan of Kano]] in what is now northern [[Nigeria]], upon the death of his brother [[Yaji I]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hiskett|first=M.|date=1957|title=The Kano Chronicle|journal=Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland|issue=1/2|pages=79–81|issn=0035-869X|jstor=25201990}}</ref>
* [[March 13]] – Officials in the Kingdom of Scotland discover that 700 pounds sterling of [[bullion]] has been taken from the customs collectors of [[Edinburgh]] by [[Robert III of Scotland|John Stewart, the Earl of Carrick]], who diverted the funds while acting as [[Guardian of Scotland]].<ref>{{citation |last=Boardman |first=Stephen |title=The Early Stewart Kings: Robert II and Robert III, 1371–1406 |publisher=John Donald, an imprint of Birlinn Ltd |year=2007 |location=Edinburgh |pages=135–136|series=The Stewart Dynasty in Scotland Series |isbn=978-1-904607-68-7}}</ref>
* [[March 22]] – From the port of [[Sluis]] (now in the Netherlands), the Kingdom of France dispatches a fleet of ships, carrying an army of 1,315 soldiers, 300 crossbowmen and 200 assistants, to aid the Kingdom of Scotland in defense of an invasion by the Kingdom of England.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Sadler|first1=J.|title=Border Fury: England and Scotland at War, 1296–1598|date=2005|publisher=Routledge|location=Harlow|page=271|isbn=978-1-13814-343-2}}</ref> The fleet arrives at the Scottish port of [[Leith]], near Scotland's capital, [[Edinburgh]], on March 25.

=== April–June ===
* [[April 6]] – At [[Coimbra]], [[John I of Portugal|João, Master of Aviz]], son of the late [[Peter I of Portugal|King Pedro I]] of Portugal, is declared by the [[:pt:Cortes de Coimbra de 1385|Cortes of Coimbra]] to be the new King of Portugal.<ref>G. Mercer Adam ed., ''The History of Nations: Spain and Portugal'' (Philadelphia: John D. Morris and Company, 1906) p.174</ref>
* [[May 6]] – [[Gian Galeazzo Visconti]] leads a coup d'etat against his uncle, [[Bernabò Visconti]], [[Lord of Milan]] and begins conquests to transform Milan into a [[Duchy of Milan|Duchy]], with himself as the Duke of Milan.<ref>{{cite book |last=Black|first=Jane |title= Absolutism in Renaissance Milan. Plenitude of power under the Visconti and the Sforza 1329–1535 |publisher= Oxford University Press |location= Oxford |year=2009 |pages=52–53 |isbn= 9780199565290}}</ref> 
* [[May 14]] – The two-day [[:fr:Bataille de LÉcluse (1385)|Battle of Sluys]] concludes on the [[North Sea]] off of the coast of the Netherlands as England's Royal Navy, led by the [[Admiral of the North|Admiral]], [[Thomas Percy, 1st Earl of Worcester]] attempts to blockade the Flemish port of [[Sluis]] and more than 100 ships stationed there. [[Jean de Vienne]], Admiral of France, makes a successful counter-attack and the Royal Navy ships sail back to England to defend [[London]].<ref>Jean-Claude Castex, ''Répertoire Des Combats Franco-anglais de la Guerre de Cent Ans (1337-1453)'' [Directory of Franco-English Battles of the Hundred Years' War (1337–1453)](Vancouver: Les Éditions du Phare-Ouest, 2012) p.167</ref>
* [[May 29]] – The [[Battle of Trancoso]] is fought between the Kingdom of Portugal and the [[Crown of Castile]] after a Castilian army pillages and burns the city of [[Viseu]]. As the Castilians are marching back with their plundered loot and prisoners, they are met by the Portuguese Army, which kills more than 400 soldiers along with six of the seven Castilian officers, then recovers the stolen treasure and releases all of the Portuguese citizens taken prisoner.<ref>Pereira Felix, John ''Abridgement of the History of Portugal'' (BiblioBazaar, 2009) p.116 ISBN  978-1-1103-3516-9</ref>
* [[June 10]] – [[English invasion of Scotland (1385)]]: Preparing to lead invade [[Scotland]] as soon as the truce between England and Scotland expires on July 15, King [[Richard II of England]] assembles an army at [[Nottingham]].<ref name="hyw">{{Cite book|title=The Hundred Years' War: Divided Houses|last=Sumption|first=J.|publisher=Faber & Faber|year=2009|pages=545–548|isbn=978-0-57124-012-8|volume=III|location=London}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 8]] – [[English invasion of Scotland (1385)]]: King [[Robert II of Scotland]] sends two armies of Scottish soldiers and French mercenaries south from Edinburgh and raids the English county of [[Northumberland]].<ref name="hyw"/>
* [[July 16]] – King Richard II directs suppliers in Durham, Yorkshire, Northumberland, Cumberland and Westmorland to be prepared to supply food to the English Army, to be purchased "at a reasonable price for ready payment."<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sharp |first=B.|title=Famine and Scarcity in Late Medieval and Early Modern England: The Regulation of Grain Marketing, 1256–1631 |date=2016|publisher=Cambridge University Press |pages=126–127|isbn=978-1-10712-182-9|location=Cambridge}}</ref>
* [[July 17]] – [[Charles VI of France]] marries [[Isabeau of Bavaria]]; the wedding is celebrated with France's first court ball.
* [[July 21]] – [[John I of Castile|King Juan of Castile]] asserts in his will that he is the King of Portugal by virtue of his marriage in 1383 to [[Beatrice of Portugal|Queen Beatriz of Portugal]]<ref>{{cite book|author=J. P. Oliveira Martins|title=The Golden Age of Prince Henry the Navigator |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3nBI7I_cxtAC&pg=PA2 |date=2001|publisher=Simon Publications LLC|isbn=978-1-931313-99-5|page=3}}</ref> 
* [[August 6]] – 
**[[English invasion of Scotland (1385)]]: After setting off from [[Berwick-upon-Tweed]], the English Army invades Scotland.<ref name=Macdonald>{{cite book|last=Macdonald|first=A. J.|title=Border Bloodshed: Scotland and England at War, 1369–1403|year=2000|publisher=Tuckwell Press|location=East Linton|pages=89–90|isbn=978-1-86232-106-9}}</ref>  The English soldiers quickly run out of food, since to supply lines have been created and the residents of the border towns in Scotland have fled, taking their food with them.<ref name="hyw"/>
**[[Edmund of Langley]] is elevated to become the first [[Duke of York]] in England.
* [[August 11]] – [[English invasion of Scotland (1385)]]: The English Army reaches [[Edinburgh]], capital of Scotland, and finds it deserted as its civilian residents have fled and the Scottish and French soldiers have retreated to [[Ettrick Forest]].<ref name="hyw"/> The frustrated English soldiers burn and loot the city.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rait |first=R. S.|title=An Outline of the Relations between England and Scotland, 500–1707|date=1901 |publisher=Blackie|page=78|oclc=746293364|location=London}}</ref>|
* [[August 14]]
** [[Battle of Aljubarrota]]: John of Aviz defeats [[John I of Castile]] in the decisive battle of the [[1383–85 Crisis]] in Portugal. John of Aviz is crowned King [[John I of Portugal]], ending [[Beatrice of Portugal|Queen Beatrice]]'s rule, and Portugal's independence from the [[Kingdom of Castile]] is secured.
** The [[Union of Krewo]] establishes the [[Jagiellonian dynasty]] in Poland and [[Lithuania]], through the proposed marriage of Queen regnant [[Jadwiga of Poland]] and Grand Duke [[Jogaila]] of Lithuania, and sees the acceptance of [[Roman Catholic Church|Roman Catholicism]] by the Lithuanian elite, and an end to the [[Greater Poland Civil War]].
* [[August 15]] – [[English invasion of Scotland (1385)]]: With England's Army having left its borders undefended, Scottish and French troops invade England and plunder [[Cumberland]] in retaliation for the burning of Edinburgh.<ref name="hyw"/>
* [[August 17]] – [[English invasion of Scotland (1385)]]: Having accomplished nothing but destruction of property, the English Army begins its withdrawal from Scotland and returns to England.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Richard II|last=Saul|first=N.|publisher=Yale University Press|year=1997|page=145|isbn=978-0-300-07003-3|location=Bury St Edmunds}}</ref> 
* [[August 23]] – In celebration of the marriage of [[William, Duke of Austria|Wilhelm the Courteous]], [[List of rulers of Austria|Duke of Austria]], to [[Jadwiga of Poland|Jadwiga]], [[List of Polish monarchs|Queen of Poland]], the leaders of the city of [[Kraków]] grant amnesty to the prisoners in the city jail.<ref>{{cite book |last=Halecki |first=Oscar |author-link=Oscar Halecki |year=1991 |title=Jadwiga of Anjou and the Rise of East Central Europe |publisher=Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America |pages=132–133|isbn=0-88033-206-9}}</ref>
* [[August 31]] – King [[Richard II of England]] begins [[English invasion of Scotland (1385)|an invasion of Scotland]]. The English burn [[Holyrood, Edinburgh|Holyrood]] and [[Edinburgh]], but return home without a decisive battle.<ref>{{cite book|last=Palmer|first=Alan|last2=Palmer|first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=109–113|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[September 7]] – Scottish and French troops unsuccessfully try to besiege the walled city of [[Carlisle]] in England,<ref name=Macdonald/> but [[Henry Percy (Hotspur)|Sir Henry Percy]], nicknamed "Hotspur" breaks the siege and the attackers withdraw to Scotland, ending the war between the two kingdoms.<ref>{{cite book|last=Bevan|first=B.|title=King Richard II|year=1990|publisher=Rubicon Press|location=London|page=45|isbn=978-0-94869-517-9}}</ref>
* [[September 18]] – [[Battle of Savra]]: [[Serbian Empire|Serbian]] forces under [[Balša II]] and [[Mrnjavčević family|Ivaniš Mrnjavčević]] are defeated by [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] commander Hayreddin Pasha, near [[Berat]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 15]] – [[Battle of Valverde (1385)|Battle of Valverde]]: The armies of [[Kingdom of Portugal|Portugal]] defeat [[Crown of Castile|Castile]].
* [[November 1]] – [[Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor|Sigismund of Luxembourg]], [[List of margraves and electors of Brandenburg|Margrave of Brandenburg]] and son of the late [[Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor]], enforces a 1373 agreement of betrothal and marries [[Mary, Queen of Hungary]], citing an agreement that had been made by King [[Louis I of Hungary]].
* [[December 31]] – [[Charles III of Naples|King Carlo III]], ruler of the [[Kingdom of Naples]], is crowned as [[List of Hungarian monarchs|King Károly II of Hungary]] by the [[Archdiocese of Esztergom–Budapest|Archbishop]] [[Demetrius of Esztergom|Demeter]] of [[Esztergom]] at [[Székesfehérvár]] after a group of Hungarian nobles helps him overthrow [[Mary, Queen of Hungary|Queen Maria]].

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Tokhtamysh]] of the [[Golden Horde]] conquers parts of the [[Jalayirid Sultanate]] in western [[Persia]], causing a rift between himself and [[Timur]] of the Timurid Empire, who had also wanted to conquer Persia.
* [[Olav IV of Norway]] is elected as titular King of [[Sweden]], in opposition to the unpopular [[Albert of Sweden|King Albert]].
* The [[Hongwu Emperor]] of China's [[Ming dynasty]] relents after eighteen tribute missions over the previous eight years, and agrees to invest King [[U of Goryeo]].
* Construction is completed on 
** [[Castello Estense]] in [[Ferrara]] (now in Italy)
** [[Bodiam Castle]] ([[East Sussex]], England)</onlyinclude>

1386.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 6]] – Officials from the Swiss [[Canton of Lucerne]], arrive in the village of [[Sempach]], at the time under control of Austria and the Habsburg family, and offer Swiss citizenship and rights. Lucerne's representatives enter into similar pacts with other Austrian-controlled towns, including Meienberg, and bring with them soldiers from the [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]].<ref name=Steffen>{{Cite journal |last=Steffen |first=Walter |date=2013 |title=Luzerns Befreiungsschlag |url=https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=zen-001:2013:0::317 |journal=Zenit |pages=30 |via=[[E-Periodica]]}}</ref>
* [[January 11]] – [[Union of Krewo]]: A delegation of Poland's nobles visits the [[Władysław II Jagiełło|Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania]] at [[Vawkavysk|Valkaviskas]] (now Vawkavysk in [[Belarus]] and informs him that they will elect him as the new King of Poland on the condition that he convert from Lithuania's polytheistic religion to Christianity, and that he marry the Queen of [[Jadwiga of Poland]]. Jogaila agrees to the terms.<ref>{{citation |first=Mecislovas |last=Jucas |title=Lietuvos ir Lenkijos unija |trans-title=The Union of Lithuania and Poland| publisher=Aidai |year=2000 |page=114 |language=lt |isbn=9986-590-95-7 }}</ref> 
* [[January 14]] – The Austrian garrison at [[:de:Meienberg (Sins)|Meienberg]] responds to the overtures from the Swiss canton of Lucerne and kills over 140 of the Swiss Confederacy troops, starting a war between the two nations.<ref name=Steffen/>
* [[February 1]] – Meeting at [[Lublin]], the nobles of Poland elect Grand Duke Jogaila as King of Poland.<ref name=Davies>{{citation |first=Norman |last=Davies | title=[[God's Playground]]: A History of Poland. The Origins to 1795 |volume=I |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2005|page=95|isbn=978-0-19-925339-5}}</ref>
* [[February 13]] – The [[Republic of Venice]] takes control of the island of [[Corfu]].<ref>{{Cite book| first=Lawrence| last=Durrell| title=Prospero's cell: a guide to the landscape and manners of the island of Corcyra| publisher=Olympia Press| year=1967| page=95 |isbn=1-60872-097-7}}</ref>
* [[February 15]] – Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania is baptized by the Roman Catholic Bishop [[Bodzanta]] of [[Gniezno]] at [[Wawel Cathedral]], [[Kraków]] after converting to Christianity, and takes the name Wladyslaw II.<ref name=Davies/>
* [[February 18]] – Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania marries Queen [[Jadwiga of Poland]], unifying the two nations.
* [[February 24]] – [[Elizabeth of Bosnia]], the mother of the overthrown Queen [[Mary of Hungary]] and [[Croatia in the union with Hungary|Croatia]], arranges the assassination of [[Charles III of Naples]], the ruler of [[Kingdom of Hungary|Hungary]], [[Kingdom of Naples|Naples]], [[Principality of Achaea|Achaea]] and Croatia, with the result that Mary is reinstated as Queen of Hungary and Croatia; Charles' son, [[Ladislaus of Naples|Ladislaus]], becomes King of Naples; and a period of [[interregnum]] begins in Achaea, lasting until [[1396]]. The rule of Achaea is sought by numerous pretenders, none of whom can be considered to have reigned.
* [[March 4]] – Jogaila, [[Grand Duchy of Lithuania|Grand Duke of Lithuania]] is crowned [[Władysław II Jagiełło]], [[King of Poland]], beginning the [[Jagiellonian dynasty]].

=== April–June === 
* [[April 29]] – The Lithuanian Army, led by [[Skirgaila]], conquers the [[Principality of Smolensk]] in the [[Battle of the Vikhra River]].[[:ru:Святослав Иванович|Prince Sviatoslav IV]], who had supported a rebellion by Grand Duke Jolaila's younger brother [[Andrei of Polotsk]], is killed in combat and Smolensk becomes a vassal state of Lithuania.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Inga |last=Baranauskienė |title=Onos Vytautienės kilmė ir giminė |trans-title=The origin and family of Ona Vytautienė|journal=Kultūros barai (Cultural Barriers)|date=February 2012 |volume=2 |issn=0134-3106 |pages=65–66 |url=http://www.lmka.lt/onos-vytautienes-kilme-ir-gimine/ |language=lt}}</ref>
* [[May 9]] – King [[John I of Portugal]] and King [[Richard II of England]] ratify the [[Treaty of Windsor (1386)|Treaty of Windsor]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Mayson|first1=Richard|title=Port and the Douro|date=2012|publisher=Infinite Ideas|isbn=9781908474711|page=4|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0udEAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA4|language=en}}</ref>
* [[June 9]] – Queen [[Elizabeth of Hungary]] pledges to assist King Wladyslaw II of Poland against his enemies, the Teutonic Knights, who question the legitimacy of the King's marriage to Queen Jadigwa.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Deletant |first=Dennis |title=Moldavia between Hungary and Poland, 1347–1412 |journal=The Slavonic and East European Review |volume=64 |issue=2 |page=202 |year=1986 }}</ref>
* [[June 26]] – [[Heidelberg University]] is opened by [[Rupert II, Elector Palatine|Ruprecht I]], [[List of counts palatine of the Rhine|Count Palatine of the Rhine]] seven months after he received permission from [[Pope Urban V]] to create a school ''studium generale''. Formal establishment will take place on October 19.<ref>{{cite book |last=Wolgast  |first=Eike |title=Die Universität Heidelberg: 1386–1986 |publisher=Springer Verlag |location=Berlin |year=1986 |page=3 |isbn=978-3-540-16829-4 |language=de}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 9]] – 
**[[Battle of Sempach]]: Soldiers from cantons of the [[Old Swiss Confederacy]] defeat the Austrian Habsburg Army in a battle that leads to the unification of the cantons into the nation of Switzerland.
**[[John of Gaunt]], Duke of Lancaster and oldest surviving son of the late King [[Edward II of England]], departs from England with 5,000 men and a fleet of English and Portuguese ships to make good [[John of Gaunt's claims to the Castilian throne|his claim]] to the [[throne of Castile]]. John, whose nephew became King Richard II upon Edward's death, claims the Castilian throne by right of his  marriage to [[Constance of Castile, Duchess of Lancaster|Constanza of Castile]] in [[1371]].<ref>{{cite DNB|wstitle=John of Gaunt|year=1892|first=Edward Maunde |last=Thompson|page=425}}</ref>
* [[July 25]] –  [[Elizabeth of Bosnia]], mother of Queen [[Jadwiga of Poland]] is kidnapped by Croatian rebels at [[Gorjani, Croatia|Gorjani]], along with Jadwiga's sister, [[Mary, Queen of Hungary|Queen consort Mary of Hungary]] Mary, when they are ambushed by John Horvat and his men while traviling to Dakovo.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Van Antwerp Fine |first=John |title=The Late Medieval Balkans: A Critical Survey from the Late Twelfth Century to the Ottoman Conquest |publisher=University of Michigan Press |year=1994 |pages=396-397 |isbn=0-472-08260-4 }}</ref> [[Nicholas I Garai]], who had accompanied Elizabeth and Mary, is murdered and his severed head is sent by the rebels to [[Margaret of Durazzo]], the former Queen consort of Hungary and Naples, as proof that the murderers of her husband [[Charles III of Naples|King Charles III]], have been captured.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Engel|first=Pal|editor-last=Ayton|editor-first=Andrew|title=The realm of St. Stephen: a history of medieval Hungary, 895–1526 Volume 19 of International Library of Historical Studies |publisher=Penn State Press |year=1999 |page=198 |isbn=0-271-01758-9 }}</ref>
* [[August 8]] – King Richard II of England summons the members of the House of Commons and the House of Lords to assemble at [[Westminster Abbey]] on October 1 for his 14th Parliament, dubbed by historians as the "[[Wonderful Parliament]]".<ref name=Given>{{cite web|url=https://www.british-history.ac.uk/no-series/parliament-rolls-medieval/october-1386|title=Richard II: October 1386|last=Parliament Rolls of Medieval England|date=2005|editor-last=Given-Wilson|editor-first=C.|website=British History Online|publisher=Boydell and Brewer|location=Woodbridge|access-date=2026-04-01|archive-date=2018-03-08|archive-url=https://archive.today/20180308100806/https://www.british-history.ac.uk/no-series/parliament-rolls-medieval/october-1386|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref> Although the King's purpose is to secure funding to defend against an imminent invasion from France, the parliament members begin plans to reform the unpopular king's government.
* [[August 17]] – [[Karl Thopia]], [[Principality of Albania (medieval)|Prince of Albania]], enters into an alliance with the [[Republic of Venice]]. Albania agrees to participate in all wars of the Republic or to pay auxiliary funds and supply grain, as well as to protect Venetian buyers in Albania. [19] In return, Venice supplies a galley to Albania and protect Albania's coast from the Ottoman Empire.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Succession in the House of Thopia |url=https://europeanmonarchies.net/karl-thopia-successors |access-date=July 10, 2025 |website=European Monarchies Review |language=en}}</ref>
* [[September 23]] – [[Dan I of Wallachia]] (modern-day southern [[Romania]]) is killed in battle against the [[Bulgaria]]ns and is succeeded by [[Mircea I of Wallachia|Mircea the Elder]], one of the greatest rulers of Wallachia.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 1]] – The "[[Wonderful Parliament]]" is opened at Westminster by King Richard's Chancellor Michael de la Pole, while King Richard declines to attend after failing to call off his decision to summon the members.<ref name=Given/> 
* [[October 18]] – [[Heidelberg University]] (''Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg''), the oldest in [[Germany]], is founded at the behest of [[Rupert I, Elector Palatine]], by charter of [[Pope Urban VI]].
* [[November 21]] – The [[Turco-Mongol|Mongol]] conqueror [[Timur]], called "Tamerlane" in the west, [[Timur's invasions of Georgia|captures and sacks]] the [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]n capital of [[Tbilisi]], taking [[Bagrat V of Georgia|King Bagrat V]] prisoner.
* [[December 24]] – Al-Burhan Ahmad al-Zahiri, (Burhan), Khalid al-Himsi, and Amin ad-Din Ibn al-Najib, arrested in September on [[Zahiri Revolt|charges of conspiring to assassinate]] the Egyptian Sultan [[Barquq]], are brought to Cairo to face trial.<ref>Al-Maqrizi, ''Al Selouk Leme'refatt Dewall al-Melouk'', vol. 3, part 2, pg. 555</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Abu al-Abbas is reinstated as ruler of the [[Marinid dynasty]] in modern-day [[Morocco]].
* Construction begins on the [[Brancacci Chapel]] in [[Florence]].
* [[Rozhdestvensky monastery]] is built in [[Grand Duchy of Moscow|Muscovy]].</onlyinclude>

1387.events:
=== January–March ===
* [[January 1]] – [[Charles III of Navarre|Charles III]] ascends to the throne of [[Kingdom of Navarre|Navarre]], after the death of his father, [[Charles II of Navarre|Charles II]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Woodward |first1=Bernard Bolingbroke |last2=Cates |first2=William Leist Readwin |title=Encyclopaedia of Chronology: Historical and Biographical |date=1872 |publisher=Lee and Shepard |page=313 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZeI0AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA313|language=en}}</ref>
* [[January 5]] – [[John I of Aragon|John I]] succeeds his father, [[Peter IV of Aragon|Peter IV]], as King of [[Kingdom of Aragon|Aragon]], [[Kingdom of Valencia|Valencia]] and Count of [[Principality of Catalonia|Barcelona]] and forms an alliance with France and Castile.
* [[January 16]] – [[Elizabeth of Bosnia|Elizabeta Kotromanic]], the regent of [[Hungary]] for her daughter, [[Mary, Queen of Hungary|Queen Mary]], is murdered in prison by Croatian rebels.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130216053027/http://stanak.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=315:izvjetaj-sa-okruglug-stola-qene-u-srednjovjekovnoj-bosniq&catid=38:radovi-izvjetaji-i-kratke-biljeke&Itemid=100 ''Izvještaj sa okruglug stola "Žene u srednjovjekovnoj Bosni, stanak.org'']</ref> 
* [[March 11]] – [[Battle of Castagnaro]]: [[Padua]], led by [[John Hawkwood]], is victorious over [[Giovanni Ordelaffi]] of [[Verona]].
* [[March 25]]– The [[Battle of Margate]], a naval battle off the coast of England at [[Margate]], ends with the England navy, commanded by the Earl of Arundel, victorious over a combined fleet of shipsf rom the [[Kingdom of France]], the [[Crown of Castile]] and the [[County of Flanders]].<ref name="SV3">Jonathan Sumption,''The Hundred Years War'', Volume 3: Divided Houses (Faber & Faber, 2011) pp.604-605 ISBN 9780571266562,</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 12]]– Admiral Arundel of the English Navy brings 68 captured ships from Margate battle to the port of [[Orwell]].<ref name="SV3"/>
* [[May 1]]– With a larger squadron of almost 60 ships, Arundel departs from Orwell and sails to the British-controlled French port of [[Brest, France|Brest]], at the time under siege by Jean de Montfort.<ref name="SV3"/>
* [[May 17]]–  At Caffa, one of the Balkan colonies of the [[Republic of Genoa]], the Genoese Army thwarts an attack at Solkhat (Sorcati) by the Tatars.<ref>Evgeny Khvalkov, ''The Colonies of Genoa in the Black Sea Region'' (Taylor & Francis, 2017) ISBN 9781351623063</ref>
* [[May 28]]– Anticipating a war with Burma, China's Emperor orders the troops at his forts on the Burmese border to increase the height of their walls and to begin making gunpowder to increase their supply.<ref>Michael Charney, ''Southeast Asian Warfare, 1300-1900'' (Brill, 2018) p.44 ISBN 9789047406921</ref>
* [[June 2]] –  [[John Holland, 1st Duke of Exeter|John Holland]], a maternal half-brother of [[Richard II of England]], is created [[Earl of Huntingdon]].
* [[June 4]] – Queen Mary of Hungary is rescued from imprisonment after being held captive by Croatian rebels.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 7]] – A Mongol Army unit, led by Naghachu, ambushes and massacres a Chinese Army division led by Chen Yong (陳鏞), Marquis of Linjiang, who is killed in the attack.<ref name=Dreyer>{{cite book|chapter=Military origins of Ming China|title=The Cambridge History of China Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1|first=Edward L|last=Dreyer|editor-first1=Frederick W.|editor-last1=Mote|editor-link1=Frederick W. Mote|editor-first2=Denis C|editor-last2=Twitchett|editor-link2=Denis Twitchett|year=1988|publisher=Cambridge University Press|url=|location=Cambridge|isbn=0521243327}}</ref>
* [[July 14]] – The Chinese Army commander, [[Feng Sheng (general)|General Feng Sheng]], leads troops across the [[Liao River]] defeats Naghachu's Mongol troops and takes Naghachu as a prisoner of war.<ref name=Dreyer/> 
* [[August 22]] – [[Olaf IV of Norway|Olaf]], King of Norway and Denmark and claimant to the throne of Sweden, dies. The vacant thrones come under the [[Regent|regency]] of his mother [[Margaret I of Denmark]], who will soon become queen in her own right.
* [[September 8]] – General Feng Sheng is removed from command of the Chinese Army by Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang<ref name=Dreyer/> and replaced by General Lan Yu.<ref>{{cite book|title=Dictionary of Ming Biography, 1368-1644|first1=L. Carington |last1=Goodrich |author-link1=Luther Carrington Goodrich|first2=Chaoying|last2=Fang|author-link2=Fang Chao-ying|year=1976|publisher=Columbia University Press|page=454|location=New York|isbn=0-231-03801-1}}</ref>
* [[September 27]] – [[Petru II of Moldavia|Petru of Moldavia]] pays homage to [[Władysław II Jagiełło]], making Moldavia a Polish fief (which it will remain until [[1497]]).

=== October–December ===
* [[October 19]] – The [[Scaliger]] rule over the independent Lordship of Verona comes to an end after 125 years when the dictator [[Antonio I della Scala]] is forced by the nobles of the [[Duchy of Milan|Lordship of Milan]], led by [[Gian Galeazzo Visconti]], to flee the city.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Varanini|first=Gian Maria|chapter=Vicenza nel Trecento: Istituzioni, classe dirigente, economia|title=Storia di Vicenza, II, L'Età Medievale|publisher=Neri Pozza editore|location=Vicenza|year=1988|language=Italian|trans-title=Vicenza in the 14th Century: Institutions, Ruling Class, Economy|trans-chapter=History of Vicenza, II, The Medieval Era|page=239}}</ref>
* [[November 17]] – The three rebel Lords Appellant— [[Thomas of Woodstock, 1st Duke of Gloucester]], [[Richard FitzAlan, 11th Earl of Arundel]] and [[Thomas de Beauchamp, 12th Earl of Warwick]] arrive at King Richard's palace at Westminster after traveling with 300 men on horseback to confront the King, and effectively take control of the government of England. The Lords demand that advisers Neville, Pole, De Vere, Tresilian and Brembre be held in custody until a trial can take place, and the King agrees after they threaten to take  the government by force.<ref>Jonathan Sumption,''The Hundred Years War'', Volume 3: Divided Houses (Faber & Faber, 2011) ISBN 9780571266562,</ref> 
* [[November 19]] – By order of the Lords Appellant, Sir [[Robert Tresilian]], Chief Justice of the King's Bench of England, is arrested along with other nobles loyal to King Richard II, and charged with treason for malfeasance in office, with trial to take place four months later at Parliament in February.<ref>{{cite book |first=Gerald |last=Harriss| title=Shaping the Nation: England, 1360–1461 |publisher=Oxford University Press| location=Oxford |year=2005 |page=463 |isbn=0-19-822816-3}}</ref>
* [[November]] – The [[Hongwu Emperor|Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang of China]] directs General Lan Yu to attack the Mongol forces led by [[Tögüs Temür]], whom the Emperor Zhu had deposed. The confrontation between Lan Yu and Tögüs Temür will culminate six months later at the Battle of Buir Lake, {{convert|500|mi}} north of [[Beijing]]. 
* [[December 19]] – At the [[Battle of Radcot Bridge]] in England, forces loyal to [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] are defeated by the [[Lords Appellant]], a group of three rebellious barons—. King Richard is taken prisoner, and not freed until he agrees to dismiss all the councillors in his court.<ref>[http://www.berkshirehistory.com/articles/radcot_bridge_bat.html Royal Berkshire History: The Battle of Radcot Bridge]</ref> Richard continues as the nominal King of England, with the Lords Appellant administering the kingdom.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Timur]] conquers the [[Muzaffarids (Iran)|Muzaffarid Empire]] in central [[Persia]], and appoints three puppet rulers.
* Khan [[Tokhtamysh]] of the [[Golden Horde]] invades the [[Timurid dynasty|Timurid]] Empire, but has to withdraw soon after, due to heavy snow.
* [[Maghan II]] succeeds his brother, [[Musa II of Mali|Musa II]], as [[Mansa (title)|Mansa]] of the [[Mali Empire]]

1392.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 16]] – The semi-independent Serbian state ([[sanjak]]) of [[Skopje|Uskup]] is annexed by the [[Ottoman Empire]] and General [[Pasha Yiğit Bey]] becomes the first Ottoman governor of the new province.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skopskokale.com.mk/en/aboutkale.php |title=Archeological Excavations: "Skopsko Kale" |publisher = skopskokale.com.mk |access-date = 2011-02-07|quote = The handwriting of the triod of the Khludov collection in the Moscow Historical Museum no. 162, completed on 6 January 1392, on the day of the Ottoman conquest of Skopje.|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110207061943/http://skopskokale.com.mk/en/aboutkale.php|archive-date = 7 February 2011}}</ref>
* [[January 20]] – A treaty halts the first of the [[Florentine–Milanese Wars]] after the [[Republic of Florence]] has liberated [[Padua]] from control by the [[Duchy of Milan]]. The treaty confirms the boundaries of Florence and Milan as they existed before the war, with the exception of Padua's new independence.<ref>{{cite book |last=Caferro |first=William |title = John Hawkwood: An English Mercenary in Fourteenth-Century Italy |year=2006 |location = Baltimore |publisher = The Johns Hopkins University Press |page=308 |isbn = 0-8018-8323-7 }}</ref>
* [[February 3]] – [[Brancaleone Doria]], the conqueror of most of the island of [[Sardinia]], announces that he has recovered most of the territories that had been captured by his challenger, [[Martin of Aragon]].<ref>Raimondo Carta Raspi, ''Storia della Sardegna'' (Milan: Mursia, 1981)</ref>
* [[February 10]] – [[Helena Dragaš]], a descendant of [[Stefan Dečanski|King Stefan III Dečanski]] of [[Serbia]], marries the Byzantine Emperor [[Manuel II Palaiologos]],<ref>{{cite book |title=Manuel II Palaeologus (1391-1425): A Study in Late Byzantine Statesmanship |first=John W. |last=Barker |publisher=Rutgers University Press |year=1969|page=xxiv}}</ref> and is crowned the next day as the Empress Consort of the Byzantine Empire.<ref>Mario Philippides, ''Constantine XI Dragaš Palaeologus (1404–1453): The Last Emperor of Byzantium'' (Taylor & Francis, 2018) p.36.</ref>
* [[March 16]] – A fleet from [[Sicily]], commanded by King [[Martin of Aragon]], arrives at [[:it:Capo San Marco|Capo San Marco]] on the island of [[Sardinia]] and makes, an unsuccessful attempt to capture the Sardinian leader [[Brancaleone Doria]].<ref>Alessandra Cioppi, ''Battaglie e protagonisti della Sardegna medioevale'' (Cagliari: AM-D, 2008)</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 11]] – In order to prevent an attack by the [[Duchy of Milan]], led by Lord [[Gian Galeazzo Visconti]], the [[Republic of Florence]] forms the [[League of Bologna]], a defensive alliance with other Italian city-states of Bologna, Padua, Ferrara, Imola, Faenza and Ravenna.<ref>{{cite book |last=Bueno de Mesquita |first=D. M. |title =Giangaleazzo Visconti, Duke of Milan (1351–1402): A Study in the Political Career of an Italian Despot |year = 1941| publisher=Cambridge University Press|page=144}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Kohl |first=Benjamin G. |title=Padua under the Carrara, 1318–1405 |publisher = Johns Hopkins University Press |year=1998 |location = Baltimore |page=303 |isbn = 0-8018-5703-1 }}</ref>
* [[May 29]] – After the [[Fleet Street riot]] in [[London]], King Richard II of England summons Lord Mayor of London, [[John Hende]], along with the London sheriff and deputies, and aldermen to appear before him at [[Nottingham Castle]] on June 25 for a hearing on unspecified charges.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last = Rawcliffe |first=Carole |encyclopedia=[[The History of Parliament]] |title= Vanner, Henry (d.1395), of London |volume= The House of Commons 1386–1421 |year= 1993 |publisher= Boydell and Brewer |url= https://www.historyofparliamentonline.org/volume/1386-1421/member/vanner-henry-1395 |access-date = 16 December 2025}}</ref> 
* [[June 4]] – [[Louis I, Duke of Orléans|Louis de Valois]] is created first [[Duke of Orléans]] of the second creation.<ref>{{cite book |title=Material Culture and Queenship in 14th-century France: The Testament of Blanche of Navarre (1331–1398) |first=Marguerite |last=Keane |publisher=Brill |year=2016 }}</ref>
* [[June 13]] – An assassination attempt by [[Pierre de Craon]] against [[Olivier V de Clisson]], [[Constable of France]], fails.
* [[June 16]] – [[Antoniotto di Montaldo]] is elected as the new [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Genoa]] upon the resignation of [[Antoniotto I Adorno|Antoniotto Adorno]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Oreste |first=Giuseppe |title=Dizionario biografico degli Italiano |url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/antoniotto-adorno_(Dizionario_Biografico)/|year=1960}}</ref>
* [[June 25]] – At a hearing at Nottingham Council concerning the [[Fleet Street riot]], King Richard II of England orders that London's Mayor Hende is to be arrested, removed from office and imprisoned.<ref name=BCR>{{cite journal|author-link1=Caroline Barron|author-last1=Barron|author-first1=Caroline|author-last2=Carlin|author-first2=Martha|author-last3=Rosenthal|author-first3=Joel T.|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/250624128.pdf |title=Medieval London: Collected Papers of Caroline M. Barron|year=2017|journal=Research in Medieval and Early Modern Culture|number=9|pages=33-36}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 1]] – King [[Charles VI of France]], outraged at an attempt to assassinate his advisor [[Olivier V de Clisson]], leads an invasion against the [[Duchy of Brittany]] and [[John V of Brittany|Duke Jean V]] for harboring the perpetrator, [[Pierre de Craon]].
* [[July 22]] – After a second hearing at Nottingham Council concerning the [[Fleet Street riot]], former London Mayor John Hende and other imprisoned city officials are assessed a fine and released from prison after posting bond to secure their return for future charges.<ref name=BCR/>
* [[August 4]] –  King [[Jogaila]] of [[Poland]] and [[Lithuania]] appoints his cousin [[Vytautas the Great]] as regent of Lithuania, in return for Vytautas giving up his claim to the Lithuanian throne. Vytautas replaces Jogaila's unpopular brother [[Skirgaila]] as regent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jučas |first=Mečislovas |title=Astravos sutartis |url=https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/astravos-sutartis/ |access-date=5 January 2026 |website=[[Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija]]}}</ref>
* [[August 5]]
** At [[Gaegyeong]], General Yi Sŏng-gye crowns himself [[Taejo of Joseon|King Taejo of Korea]], ending the [[Goryeo]] dynasty in the [[Korean Peninsula]], and establishing the [[Joseon]] dynasty, which will last for more than 500 years.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Seth |first=Michael J. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-3eSDwAAQBAJ |title=A Brief History of Korea: Isolation, War, Despotism and Revival: The Fascinating Story of a Resilient But Divided People |publisher=Tuttle Publishing |year=2019 |isbn=9781462921119 |language=en}}</ref>
** King [[Charles VI of France]] (later known as "Charles the Mad") first displays symptoms of [[psychosis]] while crossing through the forests of Le Mans, attacking his own soldiers with his sword while under the delusion that they are enemy troops from the Duchy of Brittany. Charles' madness enables Philip II, Duke of Burgundy, to strengthen his power in the French court.<ref>{{cite book |last=Ryder |first=Alan |editor-last=Abulafia |editor-first=David |title=The French Descent into Renaissance Italy, 1494–95: Antecedents and Effects |publisher=Routledge |year=2016 |pages=56 |chapter=The Angevin bid for Naples, 1380–1480 |isbn=9780860785507 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Sumption |first=Jonathan |author-link=Jonathan Sumption, Lord Sumption |year=2009 |title=The Hundred Years War, Volume III: Divided Houses |publisher=Faber and Faber |pages=802-803|isbn=978-0-571-24012-8 }}</ref>
* [[September 7]] – [[Yi Pangsŏk, Grand Prince Ŭian|Yi Pangsŏk]], at 10 years old the youngest son of King Taejo of Korea, is designated as the heir to the throne.<ref>[https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kaa_10206019_001]《Annals of the Joseon Dynasty》 Volume 3 of the Annals of King Taejo, the second year of King Taejo reign (1393)</ref>
* [[September 23]] – [[Aleid van Poelgeest]], the mistress of [[Albert I, Duke of Bavaria|Count Albert of Holland]], is found dead at the [[Altena Castle (Almkerk)|Altena Castle]] in [[The Hague]], along with the Count's [[chamberlain (office)|chamberlain]], Willem Cuser, the victim of Hook nobles who were opposed to Count Albert.<ref>{{cite book |title=Court and Culture: Dutch Literature, 1350-1450 |first=F. P. |last=van Oostrom |translator-first=Arnold J. |translator-last=Pomerans |publisher=University of California Press |year=1992|page=37 }}</ref>
* [[September 24]] – [[Hongwu Emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]], the Hongwu Emperor of [[Ming dynasty]] [[China]], declares that all males must wear the [[queue (hairstyle)|queue]] hairstyle.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chan |first1=Hok-Lam|title=Ming Taizu's 'Placards' on Harsh Regulations and Punishments Revealed in Gu Qiyuan's 'Kezuo Zhuiyu.' |journal=Asia Major |date=2009 |volume=22 |issue=1 |page=28 |jstor=41649963 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41649963 |access-date=16 April 2021}}</ref>
* [[September 28]] – [[Jianwen Emperor|Prince Zhu Yunwen]] is designated as the heir to the throne of China by his father, the Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Tsai |first=Shih-Shan Henry |url=https://archive.org/details/perpetualhappine0000tsai |title=Perpetual Happiness: The Ming Emperor Yongle |publisher=University of Washington Press; Combined Academic |year=2002 |isbn=0295981245 |location=Seattle|page=59}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 5]] – (16 [[Dhu al-Qadah]] [[Islamic calendar|794 AH]]) [[Muhammad VII of Granada|Muhammed VII]] succeeds his father, [[Yusuf II of Granada|Yusuf II]], as [[Nasrid dynasty|Sultan]] of the [[Emirate of Granada]] (modern-day southern Spain).<ref>{{cite book|last=Harvey|first=L. P.|author-link=L. P. Harvey|title=Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500|url=https://archive.org/details/islamicspain12500000harv|year=1992|publisher=University of Chicago Press|location=Chicago|page=221|isbn=978-0-226-31962-9}}</ref>
* [[October 15]] – (28th year of 9th month of [[Meitoku|Meitoku 3]]) The division of Japan between the [[Southern Court]] (with a capital at [[Yoshino, Nara|Yoshino]]) and the [[Northern Court]]) (with a capital at [[Heian-kyō]], now [[Kyoto]]) ends as the southern Emperor Go-Kameyama agrees to recognize northern Emperor Go-Komatsu as the ruler of the entire nation. 
* [[November 19]] – (5th day of the leap month of [[Meitoku|Meitoku 3]]) [[Emperor Go-Kameyama of Japan]] abdicates in favor of rival claimant [[Emperor Go-Komatsu|Go-Komatsu]], in order to end the ''nanboku-cho'' period of conflict between the Northern and Southern imperial courts.
* [[November 23]] – King Richard II of England summons the English Parliament to assemble at [[Winchester]] on January 20. 
* [[December 10]] – The Parliament of France condemns the kingdom's Constable, [[Olivier V de Clisson]], for having illegally enriched himself at the expense of King Charles VI.<ref>Michael Jones, ''Ducal Brittany, 1364-1399: relations with England and France during the reign of Duke John IV'', Oxford University Press, 1970)</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Franciscan]] friar [[James of Jülich]] is boiled alive, for impersonating a bishop and ordaining his own priests.
* [[Maria, Queen of Sicily]] defeats an army of rebel barons.
* [[William le Scrope, 1st Earl of Wiltshire|William le Scrope]] succeeds [[William Montacute, 2nd Earl of Salisbury|William II de Montacute]], as [[King of Mann]].
* Seoan mac Pilib succeeds Tomas mor mac Mathghamhna as King of [[Kings of East Breifne|East Breifne]], in north-central [[Ireland]].
* The city of [[Afyonkarahisar]] (in modern-day western [[Turkey]]) is conquered by Sultan [[Beyazid I]], of the [[Ottoman Empire]].
* [[Erfurt University]] is founded in [[Erfurt]], central Germany.
* [[Penistone Grammar School]], later to be one of the first community comprehensive schools in [[Kingdom of England|England]], is founded near [[Barnsley]], England.
</onlyinclude>

1391.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 16]] – [[Yusuf II of Granada|Yusuf II]] succeeds [[Muhammad V of Granada|Muhammad V]], as [[Nasrid dynasty|Nasrid]] Sultan of [[Granada]] (now southern Spain).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Harvey |first=Leonard Patrick |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nWyXAwAAQBAJ |title=Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500 |publisher=University of Chigaco Press |year=1990 |page=219|isbn=0226319628}}</ref>
* [[January 21]] – [[Vytautas the Great]], claimant to the throne of [[Lithuania]], forges an alliance with the [[Grand Duchy of Moscow]] as his daughter, [[Sophia of Lithuania|Sophia]] marries [[Vasily I of Moscow|Vasily, Grand Prince of Muscovy]].<ref>"Sofija Vytautaitė", in ''Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija'' (''Universal Lithuanian Encyclopedia''), ed. by Edvardas Gudavičius and Algirdas Matulevičius (2021) </ref>
* [[February 16]] –[[Manuel II Palaiologos]] becomes [[Byzantine emperor]] after his father, [[John V Palaiologos]], dies from a nervous breakdown, due to his continued humiliation by the [[Ottoman Empire]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Barker |first=John W. |title=Manuel II Palaeologus (1391-1425); a study in late Byzantine statesmanship |date=1969 |publisher=Rutgers University Press |isbn=0-8135-0582-8 |location=New Brunswick, N.J. |pages=xxiv |oclc=11370}}</ref>
* [[March 4]]– The [[University of Ferrara]] is founded on the [[Italian Peninsula]].<ref>{{cite book |chapter=Loyalty to the church, loyalty to the duke: conflicts of power in late medieval Ferrara |first=Beatrice |last=Saletti |pages=223-238 |title=Religion and Conflict in Medieval and Early Modern Worlds: Identities, Communities and Authorities |editor-first1=Amy |editor-last1=Fuller |editor-first2=John |editor-last2=McCallum |editor-first3=Natasha |editor-last3=Hodgson |editor-first4=Nicholas |editor-last4=Morton |publisher=Taylor & Francis |year=2020 |isbn=9780429836008 }}</ref>
* [[March 10]] – [[Stephen Dabiša of Bosnia|Stephen Dabiša]] succeeds [[Tvrtko I of Bosnia|Stephen Tvrtko I]], as [[King of Bosnia]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ćirković|first=Sima|author-link=Sima Ćirković|title=Историја средњовековне босанске државе|trans-title=History of the medieval Bosnian state|publisher=Srpska književna zadruga (Serbian Literary Cooperative)|year=1964|page=165|language=sh}}</ref>
* [[March 12]] – [[Konrad von Wallenrode]] succeeds Konrad Zöllner von Rotenstein, as Grand Master of the [[Teutonic Knights]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Feldkamp|first=Michael F.|title=Regentenlisten und Stammtafeln zur Geschichte Europas: vom Mittelalter bis zur Gegenwart|trans-title=Lists of rulers and genealogical tables on the history of Europe: from the Middle Ages to the present|location=Stuttgart|publisher=Reclam|date=2002|isbn=9783150170342|page=293|language=German}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 1]] – Rebelling against the rule of [[Martin of Aragon|King Martin of Sicily]], the rebel [[Brancaleone Doria]] begins the takeover of the island of [[Sardinia]] by laying siege to the [[:it:Castello (Cagliari)|Castel di Cagliari]].<ref name=Fusero>{{cite book|first=Clemente |last=Fusero|title=I Doria|publisher=dall'Oglio |year=1973}}</ref>  
* [[April 6]] – [[Antoniotto I Adorno|Antoniotto Adorno]] returns to office as [[Doge of Genoa|Doge]] of the [[Republic of Genoa]] after persuading Doge [[Giacomo Fregoso]] (who had replaced him eight months earlier) to resign.<ref >{{cite web |last=Oreste |first=Giuseppe |title=Dizionario biografico degli Italiano |url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/antoniotto-adorno_(Dizionario_Biografico)/| year=1960}}</ref>
* [[May 27]] – [[:fr:Dominique de Flourence|Dominique de Flourence]], [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Saint-Pons-de-Thomières|Bishop of Saint-Pons-de-Thomières]], helps conclude a peace agreement between the [[Kingdom of France]] and the [[Crown of Castile]], based  on his influence as France's legate to King Juan I of Castile.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Gauchat|first1=Patritius (Patrice)|title=Hierarchia catholica IV (1592-1667)|date=1935|publisher=Libraria Regensbergiana|location=Münster|url=https://archive.org/details/hierarchiacathol04eubeuoft|access-date=2016-07-06}} p. 219</ref>
* [[June 6]] – [[Massacre of 1391]]: [[Antisemitism|Anti-Jewish]] [[pogroms]] erupt in [[Seville#Middle Ages|Seville]], Spain.<ref name="Freund">{{cite book |last1=Freund |first1=Scarlett |title=Jewish-Christian Encounters Over the Centuries: Symbiosis, Prejudice, Holocaust, Dialogue |last2=Ruiz |date=1994 |publisher=P. Lang |isbn=978-0-8204-2082-0 |editor1-last=Perry |editor1-first=Marvin |pages=169–195 |chapter=Jews, Conversos, and the Inquisition in Spain, 1391–1492: The Ambiguities of History |editor2-last=Schweitzer |editor2-first=Frederick M.}}</ref> Many thousands of Jews are massacred, and the violence spreads throughout Spain and Portugal, especially to [[Toledo, Spain|Toledo]], [[Barcelona]] and [[Palma de Mallorca|Mallorca]]. This event marks a turning-point in the [[History of the Jews in Spain|history of the Spanish Jews]], with most of the survivors leaving the Iberian Peninsula or being forced to convert.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 18]] – [[Tokhtamysh–Timur war]] – [[Battle of the Kondurcha River]]: [[Timur]] defeats [[Tokhtamysh]] of the [[Golden Horde]], in present day southeast Russia.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Tucker |first=Spencer C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=h5_tSnygvbIC |title=A Global Chronology of Conflict: From the Ancient World to the Modern Middle East [6 volumes]: From the Ancient World to the Modern Middle East |date=2009-12-23 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-85109-672-5 |pages=428 |language=en}}</ref>
* [[August 16]] – [[Brancaleone Doria]] takes control of [[Sassari]] and [[Osilo]] as he gains further power in [[Sardinia]].<ref name=Fusero/>
* [[September 7]] – [[Richard II of England|King Richard II]] summons the English Parliament and directs the members to assemble at Winchester on November 3. 

=== October–December ===
* [[October 3]] – Brancaleone Doria captures [[Villa di Chiesa]] in [[Sardinia]].<ref name=Fusero/>
* [[October 7]] – [[Bridget of Sweden]] is canonized by [[Pope Boniface IX]].
* [[November 2]] – At [[Chambéry]] (now in France), [[Amadeus VIII, Duke of Savoy|Amadeus the Peaceful]] becomes the new [[Duchy of Savoy|Count of Savoy]] at the age of 8<ref>Max Bruchet, [https://books.google.com/books?id=ZTE_AAAAYAAJ&pg=PA120 ''Le château de Ripaille'']. {{in lang|fr}}. (Paris: Delagrave 1907) pp. 43–48; 50–54</ref> upon the death from [[tetanus]] of his 31-year-old father, [[Amadeus VII, Count of Savoy|Amadeus VII]], the Red Count, who was injured in a hunting accident.<ref name=HDS>{{HDS|17859|Amadeus VII of Savoy|author=Bernard Andenmatten|date=8 June 2022}}</ref> [[Bonne of Bourbon]], the mother of the older Amadeus, serves as regent for her grandson until 1397. 
* [[November 2]] – [[Al-Nasir Muhammad Salah al-Din]], [[Imam]] of the [[Zaydism|Zaydi]] sect of [[Shia Islam]] in [[Yemen]], dies at [[San'a]] from injuries sustained from being thrown off of his mule.<ref>''Encyclopaedia of Islam'', Vol. VII (Leiden 1993) p. 996.</ref> Nasir's death is not announced for two months while his son [[Al-Mansur Ali bin Salah ad-Din]] becomes the new Imam but three other claimants attempt to claim the office as well.<ref>''Encyclopaedia of Islam'', Vol. VII (Leiden 1993) p. 1218</ref> 
* [[November 3]] – King Richard II opens the new session of Parliament at Westminster.
* [[December 3]] – The Parliament ends its session after passing numerous acts, and King Richard gives [[royal assent]] to multiple acts, including the [[Forcible Entry Act 1391]] and the [[Admiralty Jurisdiction Act 1391]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Chronological Table of the Statutes: Covering the Period from 1235 to the End of 1971 |publisher=Her Majesty's Stationery Office |location=London |date=1972 |url={{GBurl|lUMIAAAAMAAJ|page=26}} |pages=26 |isbn=978-0-11-840096-1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
* [[December 29]] – Representatives of Prince [[Amadeus, Prince of Achaea|Amadeo of Savoy]] meet with [[Nerio I Acciaioli]], [[Duchy of Athens|Duke of Athens]] at the [[Acropolis]] in a pact against the [[Navarrese Company]]. The parties agree to oppose the Navarrese control of [[Morea]] and Nerio agrees to recognize Amadeo as Prince of Achaea.<ref>Setton, Kenneth M. (general editor) ''A History of the Crusades: Volume III – The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries''. Harry W. Hazard, editor. University of Wisconsin Press: Madison, 1975</ref>
* [[December 25]] – [[Jean II Le Maingre]] is named as the [[Marshal of France]] by [[Charles V of France|King Charles V]] in a ceremony at the cathedral of St. Martin at [[Tours]]. <ref>Lalande, Denis, ''Jean II le Meingre, dit Boucicaut: (1366–1421) - étude d'une biographie héroïque'', Genève 1988.
*{{cite book |first=Kenneth |last=Meyer Setton |title=The Papacy and the Levant, 1204-1571: The thirteenth and fourteenth centuries |year=1976 |publisher=American Philosophical Society |isbn=9780871691149 }}</ref>
