* The possible discovery of the island of "[[Bacalao (phantom island)|Bacalao]]" (which some historians believe to have been [[Newfoundland (island)|Newfoundland]] off North America, 20 years before Christopher Columbus had arrived in the "New World") is made by [[João Vaz Corte-Real]]. The suggestion that Corte-Real found lands that he called the "Terras do Bacalhau" (and was granted lands in the Azores by the king of Portugal as a result) will be advanced by Italian writer [[Gaspar Frutuoso]] a century later in his work ''Saudades da Terra'', although the reliability of Frutuoso's 1570 book is questioned by later historians because of the book's misinformation on other matters.<ref name=DiffieEtAt1977 />

1470.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 9]] – Grand Prince Jalsan of Joseon becomes the new King of Korea upon the death of his uncle, [[Yejong of Joseon|King Yejong]]. Jalisan takes the regnal name of [[Seongjong of Joseon|King Seongjong]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Han |first1=Hee-Sook |title=Women's Life during the Chosŏn Dynasty |journal=International Journal of Korean History |date=2004 |volume=6 |page=159 |url=https://ijkh.khistory.org/upload/pdf/6_05.pdf |access-date=17 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Jeong |first1=Yoo-Cheol |work=K스피릿 |script-title=ko:예종의 갑작스런 승하로 왕이 된 성종, 조선 조 첫 수렴청정이 시작되다 |url=https://www.ikoreanspirit.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=41483 |access-date=17 January 2024 |agency=Korean Spirit |date=February 21, 2014}}</ref>
* [[January 21]] – [[Jacquetta of Luxembourg]], mother of England's Queen Consort [[Elizabeth Woodville]] and mother-in-law of [[Edward IV|King Edward IV]], is cleared of allegations of witchcraft that had been made against her in 1469 by a follower of the rebel [[Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick|Earl of Warwick]].<ref>[https://archive.org/details/calendarpatentr15offigoog/page/n720 <!-- pg=711 --> ''Calendar of the Patent Rolls Preserved in the Public Record Office'', Volume 3] p. 53 Web. 17 November 2014.</ref>
* [[March 12]] – [[Wars of the Roses]] in England – At the [[Battle of Losecoat Field]], the [[House of York]] (supporters of King Edward IV) defeats the [[House of Lancaster]] (supporters of the former King Henry VI, led by Sir Robert Welles).<ref>{{cite book|author=Michael Rayner|title=English Battlefields: An Illustrated Encyclopaedia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=X2tnAAAAMAAJ|year=2004|publisher=Tempus|isbn=978-0-7524-2978-6|page=212}}</ref> Welles is captured and confesses that he had been hired by the Earl of Warwick and by King Edward's brother, [[George Plantagenet, Duke of Clarence]] to overthrow the King. Warwick and Clarence flee England and Welles is beheaded.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Richardson |first=Douglas |year=2011 |title=Magna Carta Ancestry: A Study in Colonial and Medieval Families |editor-first=Kimball G. |editor-last=Everingham |publisher=Douglas Richardson |location=Salt Lake City |edition=2nd |volume=IV |page=307|isbn=978-1460992708 }}</ref>
* [[March 20]] – The [[Battle of Nibley Green]] is the last fought between the private armies of feudal magnates in England.<ref name="Society2007">{{cite book|author=Bristol and Gloucestershire Archaeological Society|title=Transactions - Bristol and Gloucestershire Archaeological Society|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DAMMAQAAMAAJ|year=2007|publisher=Bristol and Gloucestershire Archaeological Society}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 5]] – At [[Srinagar]] in the [[Kashmir Sultanate]], the [[List of monarchs of Kashmir|Sultan]] [[Zayn al-Abidin the Great]] dies after a reign of almost 52 years, and his succeeded by his son, Prince Haji Khan, who takes the name [[Haider Shah Miri]]  on his proclamation as Sultan on May 12.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hasan |first=Mohibbul |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EUlwmXjE9DQC&pg=PA42 |title=Kashmir Under the Sultans |date=2005 |publisher=Aakar Books |isbn=978-81-87879-49-7 |pages=42 |language=en}}</ref>  
* [[May 6]] – [[:ko:윤자운|Yun Chaun]] becomes the new [[Yŏngŭijŏng|Chief State Councillor]] (''Yonguijong'', equivalent to a prime minister as head of government) of Korea, when he is appointed by [[Seongjong of Joseon|King Seongjong]] to replace [[Hong Yunsŏng]]. 
* [[May 15]] – [[Charles VIII of Sweden]], who has served three terms as [[List of Swedish monarchs|King of Sweden]], dies. [[Sten Sture the Elder]] proclaims himself Regent of Sweden the following day.<ref name=BLF>{{BLF|157|Sten Sture the Elder}}</ref> 
* [[June 1]] – Sten Sture is recognised as the new King of Sweden by the estates.<ref>{{Cite EB1911 |first=Robert |last=Bain |author-link=Robert Nisbet Bain  |wstitle=Sture |volume=25 |pages=1051–1052}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 12]] – During the Ottoman–Venetian War, the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottomans]] capture the Greek island of [[Euboea]], territory of the [[Republic of Venice]], after a four week [[Siege of Negroponte (1470)|siege of the fortified city]] of [[Chalkis|Negroponte]] by the Sultan Mehmed II.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Tansel |first1=Selahattin |title=Fatih Sultan Mehmed'in Siyasi ve Âskerî Faaliyetleri |url=https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1047941693749592094/1059126027655315566/Osmanl_Kaynaklarna_Gore_Fatih_Sultan_Mehmedin_Siyasi_ve_Askeri_Faaliyeti_Selahattin_Tansel_z-lib.org.pdf |page=204 |archive-date=2023-12-25 |access-date=2025-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231225195151/https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1047941693749592094/1059126027655315566/Osmanl_Kaynaklarna_Gore_Fatih_Sultan_Mehmedin_Siyasi_ve_Askeri_Faaliyeti_Selahattin_Tansel_z-lib.org.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[August 20]] – [[Battle of Lipnic]]: [[Stephen the Great]] defeats the [[Volga Tatars]] of the [[Golden Horde]], led by Ahmed Khan.
* [[September 13]] – A rebellion orchestrated by King [[Edward IV]] of England's former ally, [[Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick]], forces the King to flee England to seek support from his brother-in-law, [[Charles the Bold]] of Burgundy.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Wilkinson |first=Bertie |title=The later Middle Ages in England, 1216–1485 |publisher=Longmans |date=1969 |page=293|isbn=0-5824-8265-8 |location=Harlow}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 3]] – The Earl of Warwick releases King [[Henry VI of England]] from imprisonment in the [[Tower of London]], and [[Readeption of Henry VI|restores him to the throne]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Weir|first=Alison|authorlink=Alison Weir|title=Lancaster And York: The Wars of the Roses|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=isN2jgYtHRcC|date=2011|publisher=Random House|page=177|isbn=978-1-4464-4917-2}}</ref> 
* [[November 28]] –  Emperor [[Lê Thánh Tông]] of [[Đại Việt]] launches a naval expedition against [[Champa]], beginning the [[Cham–Annamese War (1471)|Cham–Annamese War]].<ref name=Zottoli>{{citation|last=Zottoli|first=Brian A.|year=2011|title=Reconceptualizing Southern Vietnamese History from the 15th to 18th Centuries: Competition along the Coasts from Guangdong to Cambodia|publisher=University of Michigan|page=78}}</ref>
* [[December 18]] – [[Lê Thánh Tông]] leads the [[Đại Việt]] army into [[Champa]], conquering the country in less than three months.<ref name=Zottoli/>

=== Date unknown ===
* The [[Pahang Sultanate]] is established at Pahang Darul Makmur (in modern-day Malaysia).
* The first contact occurs between Europeans and the [[Fante people|Fante]] nation of the [[Gold Coast (British colony)|Gold Coast]], when a party of Portuguese land and meet with the King of [[Elmina]].
* [[Johann Heynlin]] introduces the printing press into France and prints his first book this same year.
* In [[Tonga]], in or around 1470, the [[Tuʻi Tonga]] Dynasty cedes its temporal powers to the [[Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua]] Dynasty, which will remain prominent until about [[1600]].
* Between this year and [[1700]], 8,888 witches are tried in the [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Swiss Confederation]]; 5,417 of them are executed.
* Sir [[George Ripley (alchemist)|George Ripley]] dedicates his book, ''The Compound of Alchemy'', to the King [[Edward IV]] of England.</onlyinclude>
* The [[Chimor–Inca War]] ends with an Inca victory. The Chimor Empire is absorbed into the [[Inca Empire]].

1468.events:
=== January–March ===
* [[January 31]] – [[Qaitbay|Abu Al-Nasr Sayf ad-Din Al-Ashraf Qaitbay]] (generally referred to as "Qaitbay") is installed by Mamluk Egyptian nobles as the new [[List of Mamluk sultans|Sultan of Egypt and Syria]], the day after the Sultan [[Timurbugha]] had been removed after less than two months on the throne.<ref>{{cite book |last=Petry |first=C. F.|year=1993|title=Twilight of Majesty: the reigns of the Mamlūk Sultans al-Ashrāf Qāytbāy and Qānṣūh al-Ghawrī in Egypt |place=Seattle|publisher= University of Washington Press |pages=36–43|isbn=9780295973074}}</ref>
* [[February 15]] – The [[Thomas FitzGerald, 7th Earl of Desmond|Earl of Desmond]], Thomas FitzGerald, until recently the Kingdom of England's [[Lord Deputy of Ireland]], is beheaded on orders of his successor, [[John Tiptoft, 1st Earl of Worcester|John Tiptoft]], shortly after being arrested on accusations of treason against the Crown, then quickly tried and convicted in a show trial.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zYwdY_H0LOoC&dq=February+1468+Desmond&pg=PA109 |last=Lydon |first=James |year=2012 |title=The Making of Ireland: From Ancient Times to the Present |publisher= Taylor & Francis |page=109 |isbn=9781134981502}}</ref>
* [[February 16]] – A "marriage treaty" is signed between representatives of the Kingdom of England and the Duchy of Burgundy, providing for the marriage of King [[Edward IV]]'s sister, [[Margaret of York]], to [[Charles the Bold]], Duke of Burgundy.<ref name=Ross>{{cite book |last=Ross |first=Charles |year=2023 |title=Edward IV |publisher= University of California Press |isbn=9780520322561}}</ref>
* [[March 14]] – King Edward IV ratifies the treaty permitting his sister to marry the Duke of Burgundy <ref name=Ross/>
* [[March 31]] – [[Matthias Corvinus|King Matyas of Hungary]] issues a declaration of war against [[George of Poděbrady|King Jiri of Bohemia]], starting [[Bohemian War (1468–1478)|a war that will last 10 years]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Engel |first=Pál |year=2001|title=The Realm of St Stephen: A History of Medieval Hungary, 895–1526 |publisher= I.B. Tauris Publishers |page=304|isbn=1-86064-061-3}}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 1]] – King [[Louis XI]] summons a meeting of France's parliament, the [[Estates General (France)|Estates-General]], and obtains approval of all concessions he had previously made to the Kingdom of England, including those with reference to Normandy.<ref name=Guizot>François Guizot, ''The History of France from the Earliest Times to the Outbreak of the Revolution'' (S. Low, Marston, Searle, & Rivington, 1879) p.204</ref>
* [[April 25]] – At [[Stirling]] in Scotland, the Lord Boyd, the regent for King James III, enters an agreement for joint rule with the members of his council (the bishops of Glasgow and of Aberdeen, the earls of Argyll and of Arran, the provost of Lincluden, and Archibald Whitelaw) to co-operate in the governing of Scotland.<ref>Roland Tanner, ''The Late Medieval Scottish Parliament: Politics and the Three Estates, 1424–1488'' (Birlinn, 2022)</ref>
* [[May 30]] – After invading Syria, [[Shah Suwar]], the Ottoman Governor of [[Beylik of Dulkadir|Dulkadir]], triumphs in battle over various Mamluk Syrian governors and emirs and captures Kulaksiz.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Yinanç |first=Refet |title=Dulkadir Beyliği |date=1989 |publisher=Turkish Historical Society Press |isbn=9751601711 |location=Ankara |language=tr |oclc=21676736 |pages=64–66}}</ref> The Governor of Damascus, [[Uzbek Bey]], is seriously wounded but manages to escape.
* [[June 7]] – King Edward IV of England gives royal assent to numerous laws passed by the English Parliament, including the Cloths Act, the Liveries Act and the Sheriffs Act.<ref>{{cite book |chapter=8° Edw. IV. |chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=pst.000017915526&seq=446 |title=The Statutes of the Realm | date=1963 |volume=2: 1377 to 1509 |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=pst.000017915526 |via=[[HathiTrust]] |pages=424–430 | publisher=Dawsons of Pall Mall }}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 24]] – (5th waxing of [[Wagaung]], [[Burmese calendar|830 ME]]) At [[Pyay]] (now in [[Myanmar]]) [[Thihathura of Ava]] becomes the new Burmese [[List of Burmese monarchs|King of Ava]] upon the death of his father, [[Narapati I of Ava]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Royal Historical Commission of Burma |title=[[Hmannan Yazawin]] |volume=2 |year=1832 |location=Yangon |language=my |edition=2003 |publisher=Ministry of Information, Myanmar}}</ref>
* [[July 30]] – [[Catherine Cornaro]] is married by proxy to [[James II of Cyprus]], beginning the [[Venetian Cyprus|Venetian conquest of Cyprus]].<ref>{{cite book |chapter=Caterina Cornaro, Queen of Cyprus |first=Liana |last=De Girolami Cheney |author-link = Liana Cheney|editor-first=Debra |editor-last=Barrett-Graves |title=The Emblematic Queen Extra-Literary Representations of Early Modern Queenship |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |year=2013 }}</ref>
* [[August 14]] – The [[House of Lancaster|Lancastrians]] surrender [[Harlech Castle]] to King [[Edward IV]] after a seven-year siege.<ref>{{cite book |last=Taylor |first=Arnold  |title=Harlech Castle |isbn= 978-1-85760-257-9 |year=2007 |publisher=Cadw| location=Cardiff, Wales}}</ref>
* [[August 26]] – [[Baeda Maryam of Ethiopia|Baeda Maryam]] succeeds his father Zara Yaqob, as Emperor of [[Ethiopian Empire|Ethiopia]].
* [[September 8]] – The [[Orkney Islands]] are pledged to [[Scotland]] by [[Christian I of Denmark|King Christian I]] of [[Kingdom of Norway]] in consideration of an agreement for the marriage of 16-year-old King [[James III of Scotland]] to [[Margaret of Denmark, Queen of Scotland|Princess Margrete]], King Christian's daughter, with the islands pledged as security against the payment of the [[dowry]]. As the money is never paid, the connection with the crown of Scotland becomes perpetual.<ref>{{EB1911 |wstitle=Boyd, Robert Boyd, Lord |volume=3 |pages=353-354}}</ref>
* [[September 9]] – At [[Seoul|Hanseong]], Prince Yi Hwang of the [[Joseon dynasty]] becomes the new [[List of monarchs of Korea|King of Korea]], taking the regnal name [[Yejong of Joseon|Yejong]], upon the death of his father, [[Sejo of Joseon|King Sejo]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Han |first1=Hee-Sook |title=Women's Life during the Chosŏn Dynasty |journal=International Journal of Korean History |date=2004 |volume=6 |page=159 |url=https://ijkh.khistory.org/upload/pdf/6_05.pdf |access-date=17 January 2024}}</ref>
* [[September 18]] –  The Great Council of the [[Republic of Venice]] curbs the power of the [[Council of Ten]] through legislation restricting them to acting on emergency matters.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Grubb |first= James S. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bhK9DwAAQBAJ&dq=1468+Venice+Council+republic&pg=PT35|title=Firstborn of Venice: Vicenza in the Early Renaissance State |date=2019 |publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press |page=10 |isbn=9781421431888}}</ref>
* [[September 19]] – In the [[Kingdom of Castile]] in Spain, near [[El Tiemblo]], the "[[Treaty of the Bulls of Guisando]]" (''Tratado de los Toros de Guisando'') is signed between [[Henry IV of Castile|King Enrique IV the Impotent]] and his half-sister, [[Isabella I of Castile|Princess Isabella]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Rubin|first=Nancy|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SW_BIgAACAAJ|title=Isabella of Castile: The First Renaissance Queen|date=1992|publisher=[[St. Martin's Press]]|isbn=978-0-312-08511-7|at=Chapters 8-9|language=en}}</ref> The treaty, executed at the [[Bulls of Guisando|ancient sculpture of bulls]] near [[Ávila]], designates Isabella as heiress to the throne of Castile and León. She will become the Queen upon Enrique's death six years later.

=== October–December ===
* [[October 14]] – The [[Treaty of Péronne (1468)|Treaty of Péronne]] is signed by [[Charles I, Duke of Burgundy|Charles the Bold]], Duke of Burgundy, and [[Louis XI]] of France.<ref>{{cite book|author=Philippe de Commynes|title=The Memoirs of Philip de Commines, Lord of Argenton: Containing the Histories of Louis XI, and Charles VIII. Kings of France and of Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ivtKAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA130|year=1892|publisher=G. Bell and Sons|pages=130}}</ref>
* [[October 30]] – Troops of [[Charles the Bold]] conduct the [[Wars of Liège#Third Liège war (1468)|Sack of Liège]].
* [[November 20]] – The [[Hanseatic League|Hanseatic]] warship ''[[Hanneke Vrome]]'' capsizes and sinks off of the coast of [[Finland]], killing its estimated 180 passengers and crew, along with a valuable cargo including 10,000 [[Rhenish gulden|Rheingulden]] coins, equivalent to at least {{convert|34000|kg|lb}} of gold.<ref>Rauno Koivusaari and Mikko Heikkilä: ''Suomen rannikon aarrelaivat'' (''Treasure ships of the Finnish coast'') (Kustannusosakeyhtiö Otava, 2000) {{ISBN|951-1-16734-0}}, p. 11</ref> The ship had been sailing between the Hanseatic cities of [[Lübeck]] (in Germany) and [[Reval]] (now [[Tallinn]], capital of [[Estonia]]) when it ran into a [[gale]].
* [[December 9]] – In the course of the "[[:de:Böcklerkrieg|Boeckler War]]" in the [[Bavaria-Munich|Duchy of Bavaria-Munich]], the troops of [[Albert IV of Bavaria|Duke Albert IV]] begin the siege of [[Weißenstein Castle (Lower Bavaria)|Weissenstein Castle]]  in reprisal for the rebellion of [[:de:Degenberg|Lord Eberwein von Degenburg]]. The troops, commanded by Georg of Lerchenfeld capture the castle before Christmas and burn it to the ground.<ref>[https://www.hdbg.eu/burgen/burgen_suche-burgen_detail.php?id=brn-0137 Weißenstein Castle of the website of the House of Bavarian History]</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* Fire breaks out at [[Metz Cathedral]] in France.
* [[Sonni Ali]], king of the [[Songhai Empire]], takes power over [[Timbuktu]].

1467.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 7]] – At [[Rome]], [[Pope Paul II]] holds a secret [[papal consistory]], with the Albanian general [[Skanderbeg]], to ask the cardinals assembled to provide Skanderbeg with 5,000 [[ducat]]s (equivalent to {{convert|17.5|kg|lb}} of gold based on the worth of a ducat of 3.5g of gold). While the cardinals respond that 5,000 ducats is insufficient, the Pope explains that the additional money will have to wait until the war in Italy is concluded.<ref>{{citation |last=Freely |first=John |year=2009 |title=The Grand Turk: Sultan Mehmet II, conqueror of Constantinople and master of an empire |location=New York |publisher=The Overlook Press |page=111 |isbn=978-1-59020-248-7}}</ref>
* [[January 15]] – In one of his first acts as the new Patriarch of the Eastern Orthodox Church, [[Dionysius I of Constantinople|Dionysius I]] removes George Galesiotes and Manuel Christonymos from office in the Church as an act of revenge against their failure to support his candidacy.<ref>{{Cite journal |language=fr |last=Petit |first=L. |title=Déposition du Patriarche Mark Xylocarvi |journal=Revue de l'Orient Chrétien |issue=8 |date=1903 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0fsLAAAAIAAJ |pages=144–149}}</ref>
* [[February 14]] – Still unable to receive more than 7,500 ducats, General Skanderbeg departs from Rome with no plans for future aid to the Papal States, and receives word that he is needed back in Albania to defend the kingdom against the Ottoman invasion.<ref name=Frasheri>{{cite book |last=Frashëri |first=Kristo |title=Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu: jeta dhe vepra, 1405–1468 |trans-title=George Kastrioti Skanderbeg: life and works, 1405–1468 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vwR3PQAACAAJ |year=2002 |publisher=Botimet Toena |location=Tiranë |language=Albanian |isbn=99927-1-627-4 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230412005921/https://books.google.com/books?id=vwR3PQAACAAJ |archive-date=12 April 2023 |pages=448–455}}</ref>
* [[February 23]] – (19th day of 1st month of [[Bunshō|Bunshō 2]]) The [[Ōnin War]] begins with the [[:ja:御霊合戦|Battle of Goryo]], also called the "Battle of the Spirits", ends after two days near [[Kyoto]] initially as a battle between to factions in the Hatakeyama clan. [[Hatakeyama Yoshinari]] defeats [[Hatakeyama Masanaga]] for control of the Kami-Goryo Shrine.<ref>''History of Osaka Prefecture'', Volume 4: Medieval Period 2, (Osaka Prefecture government, 1981, pp.56-65</ref> The Onin War will continue for more than 10 years until ending on 25 December 1477.
* [[March 29]] – On [[Easter Sunday]], in the Bohemian city of [[Kunvald]] (now part of the Czech Republic), the [[Moravian Church|Unity of the Brethren]] (commonly called the Moravian Church) is formed as one of the first [[Protestantism|Protestant]] churches by four Hussite bishops.<ref>{{cite book |first1=Maurice |last1=Vernes |title=Revue de l'histoire des religions |trans-title=Review of the History of Religions |volume=217 |publisher=Presses universitaires de France |year=2001}}</ref> Despite persecution, it progresses to as many as 100,000 adherents within 100 years.

=== April–June ===
* [[April 23]] – The Albanian [[League of Lezhë]], aided by troops from the [[Republic of Venice]], is successful in ending the  [[Siege of Krujë (1466–1467)|Ottoman siege]] of the fortress at [[Krujë]] after 10 months.<ref name=Frasheri/> 
* [[May 8]] – [[Henry IV, Duke of Mecklenburg]] and [[Frederick III, Elector of Saxony]], send a warning to the various dukes of Pomerania to abide by the 1466 [[Treaty of Soldin (1466)|Treaty of Soldin]], or face an economic boycott by both nations.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Geschichte in Daten. Mecklenburg-Vorpommern|first1=Gerhard|last1=Heitz|first2=Henning|last2=Rischer|publisher=Koehler&Amelang|location=Münster-Berlin|year=1995|page=196|isbn=3-7338-0195-4|language=German}}</ref> The Duchy of Pomerania-Stettin refuses to swear allegiance to Brandenburg, which begins a war with Stettin a year later.
* [[June 15]] – [[Philip the Good]] is succeeded as [[Duke of Burgundy]], by [[Charles the Bold]]. 
* [[June 27]] – (26th day of 5th month of [[Ōnin|Ōnin 1]]) In Japan, the Battle of Kamigyo begins in [[Kyoto]] as the "Eastern Army" of Takeda Nobutaka and Jōshin'in Mitsunobu (the aide to Hatakeyama Masanaga, who lost the Battle of Goryo) invade temples on both sides of the Ogawa River with 160,000 troops, and seize control of Kyoto in an attempt to capture its military governor, Isshiki Yoshinao.<ref>Haruo Ishida, ''Japanese History of War 9: The Onin and Bunmei Wars'' (Yoshikawa Kobunkan , 2008) pp.203-212</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 25]] – In one of the largest battles of the 15th century in Italy, the [[Battle of Molinella]] is fought along the [[Idice]] River near [[Bologna]] by the army of the [[Republic of Venice]] against the armies of the [[Republic of Florence]] and the [[Duchy of Milan]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Primoratz |first=Igor |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=agskDwAAQBAJ |title=Military Ethics |year=2017 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-351-91756-8 |pages=494–495 |language=en}}</ref> The battle marks the first extensive use of artillery and firearms in combat in Italy,<ref>{{Citation|first=Fabrizio |last=Ansani |date=2021|title=Imitazione, adattamento, appropriazione. Tecnologia e tattica delle artiglierie «minute» nell'Italia del Quattrocento|trans-title= Imitation, Adaptation, Appropriation. Technology and Tactics of Small Artillery in Fifteenth-Century Italy |journal=Nuova Antologia Militare|volume=5|pages=306–309|language=Italian|url=https://www.tabedizioni.it/web/content/64783}}</ref> and while relatively few of the 27,000 troops from both sides sustain casualties (500 dead, 1,000 wounded) the battle is notable for the killing of almost 1,000 horses. Although both sides withdraw, the Venetian General [[Bartolomeo Colleoni]] abandons further attempts to conquer Milan.
* [[August 20]] – As the [[War of the Castilian Succession]] continues, an attempt by [[Alfonso, Prince of Asturias (1453–1468)|Alfonso, Prince of Asturias]] to defeat his half-brother, [[Henry IV of Castile|King Enrique IV of Castile]], in the [[Second Battle of Olmedo]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Martin|first=José Luis |year=2003|title=Enrique IV|location=Hondarribia|publisher=Nerea|isbn= 8489569827}}</ref> 
* [[September 11]] – [[Sejo of Joseon|Sejo]], Emperor of Korea (in the [[Joseon]] dynasty) receives the imperial edict from China's [[Chenghua Emperor|Xianzong of Ming]], directing the Koreans to join Chinese forces in subjugating the [[Jurchen people|Jurchen state]] in Manchuria. Sejo orders the mobilization of 10,000 Korean troops but instructs the Joseon commander to keep the Korean troops independent from the Chinese force, to wait until the Chinese attack before assisting with Korean troops, and to avoid confrontation with the Jurchen cavalry unless it appears that the Chinese army is winning.<ref>Robert Kong Chan, ''Korea-China Relations in History and Contemporary Implications'' (Springer International Publishing, 2017) pp.60-61 ISBN 9783319622651</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 9]] – (10 [[Jumada I]] 872 [[Anno Hegirae|AH]]) [[Sayf al-Din Bilbay]] becomes the new [[List of Mamluk sultans|Sultan of Egypt and Syria]] upon the death of the Sultan [[Sayf al-Din Khushqadam]], who had reigned since 1461.<ref>{{cite book |first=H. A. R. |last=Gibb |chapter=Khushqadam |title=The Encyclopaedia of Islam
|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cJQ3AAAAIAAJ&dq=%22October+1467%22+Mamluk&pg=PA73|publisher=Brill|year=1960|volume=5|page=73|isbn=}}</ref> 
* [[October 17]] – 
**King James III of Scotland gives royal assent to numerous laws passed by the Scottish Parliament in its six day session at [[Edinburgh]], including the Ferries Act requiring the ramps of [[ferry]] boats be improved to support the weight of horses being shipped ("That briggis of buirdis be maide at ferryis for the eis of schipping of hors") and three acts relating to coins and currency.<ref>{{cite book |chapter=Acta Parliamentorum Regis Jacobi Tertii |title=An Abridgement of the Acts of the Parliaments of Scotland |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0HgDAAAAQAAJ&pg=RA2-PA7 |first=William |last=Alexander |publisher=Adam and Charles Black |location=Edinburgh |date=1841 |pages=442–443 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>
**[[Ch'oe Hang (Joseon civil minister)|Choe Hang]] is appointed as the news prime minister (''yonguijong'') of Korea by the Emperor Sejo, succeeding Sim Hoe.<ref>[http://encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Contents/Index?contents_id=E0057745 Ch'oe Hang] on the ''[[Encyclopedia of Korean Culture]]'' {{in lang|ko}}</ref>
* [[October 29]] – At the [[Battle of Brustem]], [[Charles the Bold]] defeats the [[Prince-Bishopric of Liège]].
* [[November 11]] – At the [[Battle of Chapakchur]], in what is now the [[Bingöl Province]] of [[Turkey]], the tribal confederation of [[Aq Qoyunlu]], with 12,000 cavalry and infantry led by [[Uzun Hasan]], makes a surprise attack against 6,000 troops of the [[Qara Qoyunlu]] nation, commanded by the Sultan [[Jahan Shah]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fY01Tc2SZVEC&q=jahan+shah+defeated+by+uzun+hasan|title=The Cambridge History of Iran, Volume 6|author=Peter Jackson, Lawrence Lockhart|year=1986|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521200943|pages=1120|access-date=2013-02-04}}</ref> The Sultan is decapitated in the battle while trying to flee.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Woods |first1=John E. |title=The Aqquyunlu: Clan, Confederation, Empire |date=1999 |page=96 |url=https://www.academia.edu/91011925}}</ref>
* [[November 12]] – [[List of Swedish monarchs|Regent of Sweden]] [[Erik Axelsson Tott]] supports the re-election of deposed [[Charles VIII of Sweden]] to the throne.
* [[December 5]] – [[Sayf al-Din Bilbay]], Sultan of Egypt and Syria, is overthrown less than two months after becoming the monarch, as the Dhahiri branch of the Mamluks captures him.<ref>{{cite book|first=Kadir I.|last=Natho|title=Circassian History|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eE2pDLgibVoC&q=Sayf+Din+Inal+Gaza|publisher=Xlibris Corporation|year=2010|pages=218–219|isbn=978-1441523884}}</ref> The Dhahiris proclaim [[Timurbugha|Al-Malik al-Zahir Timurbugha al-Rumi]] (referred to as "Timurbugha") as the new Sultan.
* [[December 15]] – At the [[Battle of Baia]], troops under [[Stephen III of Moldavia]] decisively defeat the forces of [[Matthias Corvinus]], [[King of Hungary]], at [[Baia]] (present-day [[Romania]]). This is the last Hungarian attempt to subdue the Principality of [[Moldavia]].

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Siege of Krujë (1467)|Third Siege of Krujë]]: A few months after the failure of the second siege, [[Mehmed II]] leads another unsuccessful [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] invasion of [[Albania]]. 
* While [[Hassan III of the Maldives]] is on [[Hajj]], Sayyidh Muhammad deposes his son, acting regent.  On his return, Hassan regains the throne.
* Some papal [[abbreviator]]s are arrested and tortured on the orders of [[Pope Paul II]], among them [[Filippo Buonaccorsi]].
* King [[Matthias Corvinus]] founds the first university in [[Slovakia]], the ''[[Universitas Istropolitana]]'' in [[Bratislava]].
* The first European [[polyalphabetic cipher]] is invented by [[Leon Battista Alberti]] (approximate date).
* [[Juan de Torquemada (cardinal)|Juan de Torquemada]]'s book, {{Lang|la|Meditationes, seu Contemplationes devotissimae}}, is published.<ref name="WDL">{{cite web |url = http://www.wdl.org/en/item/11359/ |title = Meditations, or the Contemplations of the Most Devout |website = [[World Digital Library]] |date = 1479 |access-date = 2013-09-03 }}</ref>
</onlyinclude>

1466.events:
<onlyinclude>
=== January–March ===
* [[January 1]] – King Edward IV of England gives royal assent to a 40-year extension to the 1464 [[Treaty of York (1464)|Treaty of York]] between England and Scotland. The treaty, signed on June 1, 1464, was originally set for 15 years, to expire June 30, 1479. With the extension, approved by Scotland as well, peace between the two nations in Britain is extended to last until October 31, 1519.<ref>Norman Macdougall, ''James III: A Political Study'', (John Donald Publishing, 1982), pp. 58–61</ref>
* [[January 21]] – The [[War of the Succession of Stettin]] is halted as the [[Treaty of Soldin (1466)|Treaty of Soldin]] is signed by [[Frederick II, Elector of Brandenburg]], and two of the [[List of Pomeranian duchies and dukes|dukes of Pomerania]], the brothers [[Eric II, Duke of Pomerania|Erich II]], [[Wolgast|Duke of Wolgast]], and [[Wartislaw X]], [[Duchy of Rügen|Duke of Rügen]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Geschichte in Daten. Mecklenburg-Vorpommern|trans-title=History in Dates: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania |first1=Gerhard |last1=Heitz |first2=Henning |last2=Rischer |publisher=Koehler&Amelang |location=Münster-Berlin |year=1995 |page=194 |isbn=3-7338-0195-4 |language=German}}</ref> The signing takes place at the town of Soldin in the [[Electorate of Brandenburg]], now the city of [[Myślibórz]] in Poland. The brothers recognize Frederick II as their [[liege lord]], and Brandenburg recognizes their rights to their fiefdoms. 
* [[February 9]] – [[Pope Gabriel VI of Alexandria|Gabriel VI]] is elected as the new Pope of the Coptic Christian Church, succeeding the late [[Pope Matthew II of Alexandria|Matthew II]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Coptic Encyclopedia |title-link=Coptic Encyclopedia |publisher=[[Macmillan Publishers]] |others=Provided by [[Claremont Graduate University]] |year=1991 |editor-last=Atiya |editor-first=Aziz S. |editor-link=Aziz Suryal Atiya |volume=4 |location=[[New York City]] |chapter=Gabriel VI |chapter-url=https://ccdl.libraries.claremont.edu/digital/collection/cce/id/877/rec/1}}</ref>
* [[March 8]] – [[Galeazzo Maria Sforza]] becomes the new [[List of dukes of Milan|Duke of Milan]] upon the death of his father [[Francesco I Sforza]], though at the time he is in France in a military expedition to help King Louis XI fight the Duke of Burgundy.<ref>{{cite book |title= The French Descent into Renaissance Italy, 1494–1495: Antecedents and Effects |first=David |last=Abulafia |publisher=Routledge |year=1995 |page=43}}</ref>
* [[March 20]] – Galezzo Sforza enters Milan after working his way across the Duchy of Savoy, where he is in danger of being captured.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Welch |first=Evelyn Samuels |date=September 1989 |title=Galeazzo Maria Sforza and the Castello di Pavia, 1469 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3051134 |journal=The Art Bulletin |volume=71 |issue=3 |pages=352–375 |doi=10.2307/3051134 |jstor=3051134 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 19]] – News reaches the Republic of Venice that the Ottoman Sultan is marching toward Italy with an army of 100,000 men.<ref>{{cite book |last=Frashëri |first=Kristo |title=Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu: jeta dhe vepra, 1405–1468 |trans-title=George Kastrioti Skanderbeg: life and works, 1405–1468 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vwR3PQAACAAJ |year=2002 |publisher=Botimet Toena |location=Tiranë |language=Albanian |isbn=99927-1-627-4 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230412005921/https://books.google.com/books?id=vwR3PQAACAAJ |archive-date=12 April 2023 |page=423}}</ref>
* [[May 16]] – [[Jahan Shah]], [[List of rulers of Qara Qoyunlu|Sultan]] of the Empire of [[Qara Qoyunlu]] that comprises most of what is now Iran, and parts of Azerbaijan, Armenia, Turkey and Iraq, begins an attempt to reclaim imperial territories from his younger brother, Uzun Hasan, and sets off from [[Tabriz]] with a large army.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Safavid Iran : rebirth of a Persian empire|last=Newman |first=Andrew J.|date=2009|publisher=I.B. Tauris|isbn=9781441616050|edition= Paperback|location=London|pages=129|oclc=430224867}}</ref> 
* [[May 21]] – On his deathbed, Bosnian nobleman [[Stjepan Vukčić Kosača]], Grand Duke of Bosnia, dictates a testament proclaiming that his son [[Vladislav Hercegović]], "brought the great Turk to Bosnia to the death and destruction of us all" and blames Vladislav for the end of the [[Kingdom of Bosnia]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ćirković|first=Sima|author-link=Sima Ćirković | trans-title = History of the medieval Bosnian state | script-title = sr:Историја средњовековне босанске државе|publisher=Srpska književna zadruga|year=1964 |page=341 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PO02AAAAMAAJ&q=editions:OQ9SR41mPXUC |language=sr}}</ref> Vladislav becomes the Grand Duke of Bosnia the next day with the approval of the Ottoman governor.
* [[June 13]] – [[Sin Sukchu]] resigns as [[Yŏngŭijŏng#List of Joseon Yŏngŭijŏng|Chief State Councillor]] (''Yonguijong'') of the Korean Empire, an office equivalent to prime minister, and is succeeded by [[:ko:구치관|Ku Ch'igwan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=조선왕조실록 |url=https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kga_11204018_002 |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=sillok.history.go.kr}}</ref>
* [[June 17]] – [[Mulhouse|Mülhausen]], a free city within the Holy Roman Empire, joins the [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]] in an alliance against the [[Habsburg dynasty]] including the [[Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor|Emperor Frederick III]].

=== July–September ===
* [[July 9]] – King [[James III of Scotland]] is taken hostage while he is hunting near his palace at Linlithgow, in a coup d'etat led by [[Robert Boyd, 1st Lord Boyd|Lord Robert Boyd]].<ref name=Tytler>Patrick Fraser Tytler, ''History of Scotland'' (William Tait, 1841), pp. 191-192</ref>
* [[July 12]] – In the fourth year of the [[Ottoman–Venetian War (1463–1479)|Ottoman–Venetian War]], Admiral [[Vettore Cappello]] of the Republic of Venice Navy lands on the Greek mainland at [[Piraeus]] and the Venetians begin marching toward [[Athens]] to free it from Ottoman control.<ref>{{cite book| last1=Setton |first1= Kenneth M.|last2=Hazard|first2= Harry W.|last3=Zacour|first3= Norman P.|year=1989|title=A History of the Crusades, Volume VI: The Impact of the Crusades on Europe|publisher=University of Wisconsin Press| pages=283-284 |isbn=0-299-10740-X}}</ref>
* [[August 19]] – With troops led by [[Charles the Bold]], the Burgundian State commences a siege of the city of [[Dinant]] (now in Belgium). The city falls after six days on August 25.
* [[August 21]] – [[Eric II, Duke of Pomerania]], reconciles with King Casimir IV of Poland after six years of feuding.<ref name=Buchholz>{{cite book |editor1-last= Buchholz |editor1-first= Werner |title= Pommern |year=2002 |publisher= Siedler |page=186|language=de|isbn= 3-88680-780-0}}</ref> 
* [[August 26]] – In the [[Republic of Florence]], an attempted coup d'etat against [[Piero di Cosimo de' Medici]] fails after his son Lorenzo discovers a roadblock that had been set by the conspirators to capture Medici during his planned trip to the Medici estate at [[Villa di Careggi]].<ref>{{cite book|title=A History of Florence 1200–1575|last=Najemy|first=John M.|publisher=Blackwell Publishing|isbn=978-1405119542|year=2006}}</ref>
* [[August 30]] – A group of 41 Bavarian knights from the Straubing region gather at [[Regensburg]] and form an alliance against the Duke of Bavaria Munich, Albrecht IV. They refer to themselves as [[:de:Böcklerkrieg#Der Böcklerbund|The Boeckler League]]" (''Der Böcklerbundbund''), led by Hans von Degenberg, and soon start a rebellion, the "[[:de:Böcklerkrieg|Boeckler War]]". The League is dissolved by Imperial Decree from the Holy Roman Emperor Frederick III on October 28, 1467, and the League members vote for dissolution, but some continue the war.<ref>Max Piendl, ''Die Ritterbünde der Böckler und Löwler im Bayerischen Wald'' ("The Knightly Leagues of the Böckler and Löwler in the Bavarian Forest"), in ''Unbekanntes Bayern'' (''Unknown Bavaria'')(Munich: Süddeutscher Verlag, 1960) ISBN 3-7991-5839-1</ref>
* [[September 23]] – Peace talks begin in the city of [[Mała Nieszawka|Nieszawka]] in [[Poland]] to end the [[Thirteen Years' War (1454–1466)|Thirteen Years' War]] between the Kingdom of Poland and the [[Teutonic Knights]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Górski |first=Karol |title=Związek Pruski i poddanie się Prus Polsce: zbiór tekstów źródłowych |trans-title=The Prussian Confederation and Prussia's Submission to Poland: A Collection of Source Texts |year=1949 |publisher=Instytut Zachodni |location=[[Poznań]] |page=lxxiv |language=pl}}</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 9]] – King James III of Scotland gives [[royal assent]] Among the many [[List of acts of the Parliament of Scotland from 1466|acts passed into law by the Parliament]], including the Hospitals Act ("for the reformacioune of the hospitalis") and the Benefices Act against Englishmen being allowed to receive a [[benefice]] (payment of a reward for services rendered) from the Crown or from the Church ("na Inglis man have benefice with Scotlande")<ref>{{cite web |title=Index of Statutes: James III (1460-1488) |url=https://www.rps.ac.uk/static/statutes_jamesiii.html |website=Records of the Parliaments of Scotland to 1707 |publisher=University of St Andrews}}</ref>
* [[October 11]] – Eric of Pomerania buys the town of [[Lębork|Lauenburg]] back from the Kingdom of Poland, seven years after it had been captured.<ref name=Buchholz/>
* [[October 13]] – King James III of Scotland is forced by Lord Boyd to appear before the Scottish Parliament and to forgive Boyd and the other conspirators in the kidnapping that took place on July 9.<ref name=Tytler/>  
* [[October 19]] – The [[Second Peace of Thorn (1466)|Second Peace of Thorn]] is signed between King [[Casimir IV Jagiellon]] of Poland and the Teutonic Knights Grand Master, [[Ludwig von Erlichshausen]], ending the [[Thirteen Years' War (1454–1466)|Thirteen Years' War]].
* [[November 22]] – A messenger from the Venetian front in the war in Albania against the Ottomans brings news of planned attacks by the Ottoman General Sinan Bey against the [[Republic of Venice]]'s Albanian territory, and an offer received from the Ottomans to negotiate a ceasefire or treaty.<ref name=Schmitt/>
* [[November 26]] – [[Han Myŏnghoe]] becomes the new Chief State Councillor (''Yonguijong'') of the Korea, succeeding Ku Ch'igwan, who served for less than six months.<ref>{{Cite web |title=조선왕조실록 |url=https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kga_11210019_003 |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=sillok.history.go.kr}}</ref>
* [[December 12]] – The Albanian General [[Skanderbeg]] arrives in [[Rome]] to offer his aid to the Christian League in the defense of Italy against the Ottoman Empire.<ref name=Schmitt>{{citation |last=Schmitt |first=Oliver Jens |authorlink=Oliver Jens Schmitt |year=2009 |title=Skënderbeu |publisher=K&B |location=Tiranë |pages=382-393 |isbn=978-3-7917-2229-0}}</ref>
* [[December 23]] – [[Pope Paul II]] [[excommunication|excommunicates]] the King of Bohemia, [[George of Poděbrady]], releasing all Bohemian citizens from their oaths of to the king.<ref>Frederick G. Heymann, ''George of Bohemia: King of Heretics'' (Princeton, N.J.: Princeton University Press, 1965)</ref>

1464.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 6]] – The [[Estates General of 1464|first assembly ever]] of the [[States General of the Netherlands]] is held as representatives from at least [[Seventeen Provinces|17 provinces]] of the [[Burgundian Netherlands]] gather at [[Bruges]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Koenigsberger|first=H.G.|title=Monarchies, States Generals and Parliaments: The Netherlands in the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Centuries|year=2001|publisher=Cambridge University Press|pages=5-15}}</ref> At least 81 delegates come from the clergy, nobility and general public from the [[Duchy of Brabant]], the [[County of Flanders]], [[Walloon Flanders|Lille, Douai and Orchies]], the [[County of Artois]], the [[County of Hainaut]], the [[County of Holland]], the [[County of Zeeland]], the [[County of Namur]], the [[Lordship of Mechelen]], and the [[Boulonnais (region)|Boulonnais]], all with the reluctant assent of [[Philip the Good]], [[Duke of Burgundy]].<ref name=Blockmans>[[Wim Blockmans]], "De samenstelling van de staten van de Bourgondische landsheerlijkheden omstreeks 1464", ''Standen en Landen'' 47 (1968), pp. 57–112.</ref> 
* [[January 21]] – The [[English Parliament]] opens its second session during the reign of King Edward IV, gathering at Westminster, and will remain in session until March 28, 1465.
* [[February 7]] – After leading the Ottoman Empire's conquest of his native [[Bosnia]], General [[Isa-beg Isaković]] becomes the first [[List of Ottoman governors of Bosnia|Ottoman Governor of Bosnia]]. The province will remain under Turkish control for more than 400 years until 1878.<ref>{{cite book|title=Enciclopedia Croatica|url=https://www.scribd.com/doc/24124044/Hrvatska-enciklopedija-Sv-III-Boja-Bra%C5%BE%C4%91enje|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111205111654/http://www.scribd.com/doc/24124044/Hrvatska-enciklopedija-Sv-III-Boja-Bra%C5%BE%C4%91enje|archive-date=2011-12-05|access-date=March 15, 2011|edition=III|year=1942|publisher=Naklada Hrvatskog izdavalačkog bibliografskog zavoda|location=Zagreb|language=hr|page=157|quote=Krajišnik Isabeg imenovan je 1463 sandžakbegom novoustrojenog sandžaka Bosna|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[February 12]] – The first Estates General in the Netherlands adjourns after five weeks.<ref name=Blockmans/>
* [[February 23]] – Prince Zhu Jianshen becomes the new [[Ming dynasty]] [[Emperor of China]], taking the regnal name [[Chenghua Emperor|Emperor Xianzong]] upon the death of his father, the [[Emperor Yingzong of Ming]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mote |first=Frederick W. |author-link=Frederick W. Mote |title=The Cambridge History of China Volume 7: The Ming Dynasty, 1368–1644, Part 1 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1998 |isbn=0521243327 |editor-last=Mote |editor-first=Frederick W. |location=Cambridge |pages=367 |chapter=The Ch'eng-hua and Hung-chih reigns, 1465—1505 |editor-last2=Twitchett |editor-first2=Denis C |editor-link2=Denis Twitchett}}</ref> His reign is subsequently designated as the Chenghua Era.
* [[March 23]] – [[Pope Pius II]] [[excommunication|excommunicates]] the entire town of [[Prudnik]] (now part of Poland and its Roman Catholic inhabitants for its failure to pay its share of the debts owed to the [[Duchy of Oels|Duke of Oels]], [[Konrad IV the Elder]].Tadeusz Kwaśniewski, (16 August 2002).<ref>[https://nto.pl/nie-zaplacili-za-ksiecia/ar/3960397 "Nie zapłacili za księcia" ("They Didn't Pay the Prince"]. ''Nowa Trybuna Opolska'' (in Polish). Retrieved 18 December 2020</ref>
* [[March 25]] – The coronation ceremony of [[Matthias Corvinus|Matthias Hunyadi]] as [[King of Hungary|King Mátyás I of Hungary]] takes place in [[Székesfehérvár]] as [[Dénes Szécsi]] places the [[Crown of Saint Stephen]] on the King's head.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Matthias-I|title=Matthias I | King of Hungary & Holy Roman Emperor | Britannica|website=www.britannica.com}}</ref> Corvinus has reigned for more than six years at the time of his formal coronation.

=== April–June ===
* [[April 17]] –Swedish separatist rebel Kettil Karlsson leads his troops to victory over King Christian I of Sweden in the [[Battle of Haraker]].
* [[April 25]] – [[Battle of Hedgeley Moor]] in [[Kingdom of England|England]]: Yorkist forces under [[John Neville, 1st Marquess of Montagu|John Neville]] defeat the Lancastrians under Sir [[Ralph Percy]], who is killed.<ref name=CBH>{{cite book|last1=Palmer|first1=Alan|last2=Palmer|first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=128–131|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[May 1]] – [[Edward IV of England]] secretly marries [[Elizabeth Woodville]], and keeps the marriage a secret for five months afterwards.<ref name=CBH/>
* [[May 15]] – [[Battle of Hexham]]: Neville defeats another Lancastrian army, this one led by King [[Henry VI of England|Henry]] and [[Margaret of Anjou|Queen Margaret]] themselves. This marks the end of organized Lancastrian resistance for several years.<ref>{{cite book|author=Clive Kristen|title=Battle Trails of Northumbria|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fjq6BAAAQBAJ&pg=PT49|date=2014|publisher=Andrews UK Limited|isbn=978-1-84989-438-8|pages=49}}</ref>
* [[June 1]] – The [[Treaty of York (1464)|Treaty of York]], a 15-year-truce is signed by representatives of the kingdoms of [[Kingdom of England|England]] (ruled by King Edward IV) and [[Kingdom of Scotland|Scotland]] (ruled by King James III).<ref>{{cite book|author=R. B. Dobson|title=Church and Society in the Medieval North of England|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Church_and_Society_in_the_Medieval_North/NfTUAwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=truce+england+scotland+york+%22June+1464%22&pg=PA117&printsec=frontcover|date=1996|place=London|publisher=The Hambledon Press|isbn=1-85285-120-1|page=117}}</ref><ref name=CBH/>
* [[June 18]] – [[Pope Pius II]] himself shoulders the cross of the [[Crusades]], and departs for [[Ancona]] to participate in person. He names [[Skanderbeg]] general captain of the [[Holy See]], under the title [[Athleta Christi]]. This plan forces Skanderbeg to break his ten-year peace treaty with the [[Ottoman Turks|Ottomans]] signed in [[1463]], by attacking their forces near [[Ohrid]].
* [[June 23]] – [[Christian I of Denmark|King Christian of Sweden]] who is also King of Denmark and of Norway in the union of the three kingdoms, is declared deposed from the latter throne. His deposed predecessor [[Charles VIII of Sweden]] is re-elected to the throne on [[August 9]].

=== July–September ===
* [[July 10]] – The [[Siege of Jajce (1464)|siege]] of [[Jajce]] in Bosnia, a strategic fortress under the control of Hungary, is started by [[Mehmed II|the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II]] with 30,000 troops under his command.<ref name=Jacques>{{cite book |last1=Jaques |first1=Tony |last2=Showalter |first2=Dennis E. |title=Dictionary of Battles and Sieges: F-O |publisher=Greenwood Press |year=2007 |page=484 |isbn=978-0-313-33538-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Dh6jydKXikoC&pg=PA483}}J</ref>
* [[August 21]] – [[Emperor Go-Hanazono]] of Japan abdicates, and is succeeded by his son, [[Emperor Go-Tsuchimikado]].
* [[August 22]] – Sultan Mehmed II abandons the [[Siege of Jajce (1464)|siege of Jajce]] after the Hungarian defenders have resisted for more than six weeks. The Sultan makes his decision after learning that King Mátyás I of Hungary has mobilized troops to come to the fortresses defense.<ref name=Jacques/>
* [[August 28]] – Nine days after the death of Pope Pius II, 19 of the 29 Roman Catholic cardinals meet in Rome for the [[1464 conclave|conclave]] to elect a successor. On the first day, before voting for Pope, the cardinals vote to continue Pius's planned crusade against the Ottoman Empire, limiting the college of cardinals to only 24, and allowing only one [[cardinal-nephew]] to serve as a candidate.<ref name="Miranda">{{cite web |author-link=Salvador Miranda (historian) |last=Miranda |first=Salvador |title=Conclave of August 27-30, 1464 (Paul II) |url=https://cardinals.fiu.edu/conclave-xv.htm#1464 |work=The Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church |publisher=[[Florida International University]] |access-date=2019-06-02|oclc=53276621 }}</ref>
* [[August 30]] – Cardinal Pietro Barbo, Bishop of Vicenza, is elected as the new Pope, receiving 14 of the 19 votes<ref name="Miranda"/> On the first ballot, Cardinal Barbo had 11 of the 14 required, while the other eight were divided among [[Ludovico Trevisan]] and [[Guillaume d'Estouteville]]. Barbo takes the regnal name of [[Pope Paul II]], 211th pope of the Roman Catholic Church.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Johann Carl Ludwig Gieseler|author2=John C. L. Gieseler|title=A Text-book of Church History: A.D. 1305-1517|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pIEeAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA265|year=1855|publisher=Harper|pages=265–}}</ref>
* [[August]] – [[Sophronius I of Constantinople]], Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople and leader of the Eastern Orthodox Christian Church, dies after a reign of 11 years and is succeeded by the former Partriarch, [[Gennadius II of Constantinople|Gennadius II]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Ecumenical Patriarchate |last=Kiminas |first=Demetrius |date=2009 |publisher=[[Wildside Press]] |isbn=978-1-4344-5876-6 |pages=37, 45}}</ref>
* [[September 7]] – At [[Leipzig]], [[Ernest, Elector of Saxony|Ernest, Landgrave of Thuringia]], 23, becomes the new [[Elector of Saxony]] upon the death of his father, [[Frederick II, Elector of Saxony|Friederich II]], while his younger brother [[Albert III, Duke of Saxony|Albert III]], 21, succeeds his father as the new [[Duchy of Saxony|Duke of Saxony]].<ref>{{EB1911|inline=y|wstitle=Frederick II., Elector of Saxony|volume=11|page=60}}</ref>
* [[September 15]] – At the [[Battle of Ohrid]] in what is now [[North Macedonia]], ends with the Albanian leader [[Skanderbeg]] and a supplementary force from the Venetian Republic, luring an estimated 10,000 Ottoman Empire soldiers out of the walled city of [[Ohrid]], then captures the group as prisoners and seizes the city.<ref>{{citation |last=Franco |first=Demetrio |year=1480 |title=Comentario de le cose de' Turchi, et del S. Georgio Scanderbeg, principe d' Epyr |publisher=Altobello Salkato |page=335 |isbn=99943-1-042-9}}</ref>
* [[September 26]] – A group of merchants from the Republic of Venice arrive in London, apparently infected with the [[bubonic plague]] and the disease begins to spread rapidly.<ref name=Creighton/>
* [[September 29]] – [[Edward IV of England|King Edward IV]] of England surprises his advisors and the nation by introducing [[Elizabeth Woodville]] as his wife at [[Reading Abbey]], and revealing that he had been married for almost five months, the ceremony having taken place on May 1.<ref>Ron Baxter, ''The Royal Abbey of Reading'' (Woodbridge: The Boydell Press, 2016) pp. 122–123. ISBN 978-1-78327-084-2.</ref> The marriage outrages King Edward's mentor, [[Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick]], who had been arranging a marriage between the King and [[Bona of Savoy]], sister-in-law of France's King [[Louis XI]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Charles |title=Edward IV |publisher=Yale University Press |date=1997 |isbn=0-3000-7372-0 |edition=new |location=New Haven, London |author-link=Charles Ross (historian)|page=81}} Ross (1997), p. 91.</ref>

=== October–December ===
* [[October 5]] – An intelligence report sent by a Venetian agent in [[Bruges]] to the Seignory of Venice reports that the death rate in London from the plague has reached 200 people per day, only nine days after the first case was discovered.<ref name=Creighton>Charles Creighton, ''A History of Epidemics in Britain From A.D. 664 to the extinction of plague'', Volume 1 (Cambridge University Press, 1891) p.230</ref>
* [[November 11]] – [[Philip I, Metropolitan of Moscow|Filip I]] is appointed by the Grand Duke of Moscow as the new [[List of metropolitans and patriarchs of Moscow]], leader of the [[Russian Orthodox Church]], after the September 13 death of [[Theodosius, Metropolitan of Moscow|the Patriarch Theodosius]].<ref>Archimandrite Makariy (Veretennikov), Archimandrite (2016), "Saint Metropolitan Philip I (1464–1473)", in ''Metropolitans of Ancient Rus' (10th–16th Centuries)'' (in Russian)</ref> 
* [[December 26]] – [[Kettil Karlsson (Vasa)|Kettil Karlsson]] takes the title of ''[[:sv:Sveriges riksföreståndare|riksföreståndare]]'' (national director) and reduces the role of [[Karl Knutsson|King Karl VIII]] to [[figurehead]] status.<ref>{{cite book |last=Gillingstam |first=Hans |title=Ätterna Oxenstierna och Vasa under medeltiden: släkthistoriska studier |trans-title=The Oxenstierna and Vasa families during the Middle Ages: family history studies |year=1952 |publisher=Almqvist & Wiksell |place=Stockholm}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* In China, a small rebellion occurs in the interior province of [[Huguang]], during the [[Ming Dynasty]]; a subsequent rebellion springs up in [[Guangxi]], where a rebellion of the [[Miao people]] and [[Yao people (Asia)|Yao people]] forces the Ming throne to respond, by sending 30,000 troops (including 1,000 Mongol cavalry) to aid the 160,000 local troops stationed in the region, to crush the rebellion that will end in [[1466]].<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pg5Qi28akwEC&q=miao+and+yao+tribes+rebel&pg=PA43 |title=Columbia Chronologies of Asian History and Culture - Google Books |first=John Stewart|last= Bowman|publisher=Columbia University Press|year=2000|isbn=9780231110044 | access-date = 9 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.san.beck.org/3-7-MingEmpire.html#2 | title = Ming Empire 1368-1644 by Sanderson Beck | first= Sanderson | last= Beck | work = san.beck.org | year = 2010 | access-date = 9 November 2014 }}</ref>
* Jehan Lagadeuc writes a Breton-French-Latin dictionary called the ''[[Catholicon (trilingual dictionary)|Catholicon]]''. It is the first French dictionary as well as the first Breton dictionary of world history, and it will be published in [[1499]].
* [[Tenguella]], the founder of the [[Empire of Great Fulo]], becomes chief of the [[Fula people]].
</onlyinclude>

1463.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 5]] – French poet [[François Villon]] receives a reprieve from death by hanging, and is banished from Paris (his further life is undocumented).
* [[February 6]] – [[Otto II, Duke of Brunswick-Göttingen]], a semi-independent principality within the [[Holy Roman Empire]], dies after a reging of more than 68 years. Because Otto has no heirs, the [[Principality of Göttingen]] comes to an end and is annexed by the [[principality of Calenberg]].<ref>{{cite ADB|24|685|686|Otto der Einäugige|[[:de:Paul Zimmermann (Historiker)|Paul Zimmermann]]|ADB:Otto der Einäugige}}</ref>
* [[February 22]] – At the [[University of Cambridge]] in England, [[Henry Abyngdon]] becomes the first person in the world to receive a degree of [[Bachelor of Music]]<ref>{{acad|id=ABNN463H|name=Abyngton, Henry, Cambridge Alumni Database}} University of Cambridge.</ref>
* [[March 10]] – [[Henry Beaufort, 3rd Duke of Somerset]] receives a general pardon from [[King Edward IV]] of England after having had his lands confiscated for his support of King Henry VI in the War of the Roses.<ref>{{cite DNBSupp|last=Pollard |year=1901a |first=Albert Frederick |wstitle=Beaufort, Henry (1436–1464)|volume=I | pages=157–158 }}</ref> Beaufort's renewed status lasts only until the [[Battle of Hexham]] 14 months later and he is beheaded on May 15, 1464.
* [[March 26]] – By order of Sultan Mehmed II of the Ottoman Empire, [[David of Trebizond|David Komnenos]], the last Emperor of Trebizond, is arrested at Adrianople and put in jail along with his sons Basil, Manuel and Georgios and his nephew Alexios, on charges of conspiracy to overthrow the Ottoman imperial government.<ref>William Miller, [https://www.jstor.org/stable/552176 "The Chronology of Trebizond"], ''The English Historical Review'' (1923), p. 410</ref>

=== April–June ===
* [[April 3]] – The Ottoman Army under the command of [[Isa Bey Ishaković]] captures the town of [[Argos, Peloponnese|Argos]], located in Greece but territory of the Republic of Venice, prompting concerns that the Ottoman Empire intends to spread their conquests to the Italian peninsula.<ref name=Setton>{{cite book| last1=Setton |first1= Kenneth M.|last2=Hazard|first2= Harry W.|last3=Zacour|first3= Norman P.|year=1989|title=A History of the Crusades, Volume VI: The Impact of the Crusades on Europe|publisher=University of Wisconsin Press|pages=241–243| isbn=0-299-10740-X}}</ref> 
* [[April 28]] – [[Pope Pius II|Pope Pius]] issues the [[papal bull]] ''In Minoribus Agnetes'', retracting his earlier complaint against the late [[Pope Eugene IV]] and endorsing the previous work at the Council of Basel.<ref>Carolus Fea (ed.), [https://books.google.com/books?id=l-HjYkc_ZtsC&pg=PR1 ''Pius II. Pont. Max. a calumniis vindicatus ternis retractationibus eius quibus dicta et scripta pro concilio Basileensi contra Eugenium PP. IV. eiuravit.''], pp. 148-164, at p. 152. Gregorovius, [https://books.google.com/books?id=P1MZAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA171 ''History of the City of Rome in the Middle Ages'']. Volume 7, Part 1, p. 171.</ref> 
* [[May 19]] – [[Battle of Ključ (1463)]]: Under the leadership of General [[Mahmud Pasha Angelović]], the Ottomans begin the siege of the city of Babovac while King Stephen of Bosnia flees to the [[Jajce]] fortress.<ref name=Babinger/>
* [[May 25]] – The [[Kingdom of Bosnia]] falls to the [[Ottoman Empire]] as the last monarch, [[Stephen Tomašević of Bosnia|King Stephen Tomašević]], is captured and executed by orders of the Sultan Mehmed II. According to the chronicle of [[Benedetto Dei]], the Sultan himself carries out the beheading.<ref name=Babinger>{{cite book|last=Babinger|first=Franz|author-link=Franz Babinger|title=Mehmed the Conqueror and His Time|publisher=Princeton University Press|location=Princeton NJ|year=1992|pages=220–222|isbn=0-691-01078-1}}</ref>
* [[June 18]] – The [[free imperial city]] of [[Rottweil]], part of the [[Holy Roman Empire]] and now a part of Germany, becomes an associate state of the [[Growth of the Old Swiss Confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hecht |first1=Winfried |title=The Julius Banner of the Village of Rottweil |url=https://www.e-periodica.ch/digbib/view?pid=gfr-001:1973:126::424#149 |journal=Der Geschichtsfreund: Mitteilungen des Historischen Vereins der Fünf Orte Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden und Zug |date=1973 |volume=126-127 |page=141 |doi=10.5169/seals-118647 |access-date=2019-01-25}}</ref>

=== July–September ===
* [[July 19]] – The [[Treaty of Wiener Neustadt]] is signed between the Kingdom of Hungary and the Holy Roman Empire.<ref>{{cite book|author=Pál Engel|author2=Andrew Ayton |author3=Tamás Pálosfalvi |title=The realm of St. Stephen: a history of medieval Hungary, 895-1526|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vEJNBqanT_8C&pg=PA309|publisher=I. B. Tauris|location=[[London]], [[United Kingdom]]|year=2005|isbn=1-85043-977-X|pages=309–310}}</ref> 
* [[July 28]] – The Senate of the [[Republic of Venice]] votes to declare war on the Ottoman Empire.<ref name=Setton/>
* [[July 30]] – In India, [[Muhammad Shah III Lashkari]] becomes the new ruler of the [[Bahmani Sultanate]] upon the death of his older brother, the Sultan [[Nizam-Ud-Din Ahmad III]] at [[Bidar]] (now in the state of Karnataka)  <ref>.{{Cite book |last=Sherwani |first=Haroon Khan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3kIeAAAAMAAJ |title=The Bahmanis of the Deccan |date=1985 |publisher=Munshiram Manoharlal|page=291}}</ref>
* [[August 1]] – The [[Importation Act 1463]], given royal assent on April 29 by King Edward IV goes into effect, setting a minimum price for imported grain at 6 shillings, 8 pence per unit.<ref>William Cunningham, ''The Growth of English Industry and Commerce during the Early and Middle Ages. Fifth Edition'' (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1915), p. 407.</ref> The legislation had been passed to encourage the purpose of farmers raising grain in England.
* [[August 14]] – Upon the death of his father, [[Mani' ibn Rabi'a al-Muraydi]], [[Rabi'a ibn Mani' al-Muraydi]] becomes the new ruler of the [[First Saudi state|Emirate of Diriyah]] at its capital, [[Diriyah]], near [[Riyadh]] in what is now [[Saudi Arabia]].Munir al-Ajlani, ''History of Saudi Arabia, Part One: The First Saudi State'' (in Arabic) (2nd ed.).(Riyadh, 1933) pp. 53–54. Mani's descendants in the [[House of Saud]], most notably Mani's great-great-great-great-great-great-grandson [[Ibn Saud]], become the founders of Saudi Arabia.
* [[August 20]] – The Republic of Venice renews its 1448 peace treaty with [[Albania]], pledging that any treaty between Venice and the Ottoman Empire will include a guarantee of Albanian independence. The amended treaty also guarantees the presence of Venetian Navy ships in the Adriatic Sea to protect Albania, as well as the right to asylum in Venice for Albanians.<ref>{{Citation|last=Noli|first=Fan S.|author-link=Fan S. Noli|year=1947|title=George Castrioti Scanderbeg (1405–1468)|publisher=International Universities Press|location=New York|pages=35–36|oclc=732882}}</ref> 
* [[September 12]] – [[Pope Pius II]] calls for all Christians to participate in a crusade against the Ottoman Empire.
* [[September 15]] – [[Battle of Vistula Lagoon]]: The navy of the [[Prussian Confederation]] defeats that of the [[Teutonic Order]].

=== October–December ===
* [[October 8]] – The Truce of Hesdin ends French support for the [[House of Lancaster]] in [[Kingdom of England|England]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Palmer|first1=Alan|last2=Palmer|first2=Veronica|year=1992|title=The Chronology of British History|publisher=Century Ltd|location=London|pages=128–131|isbn=0-7126-5616-2}}</ref>
* [[October 22]] – [[Pope Pius II]] issues the [[papal bull]] ''[[Ezechielis prophetae]]'', offering an [[indulgence]] to any Christians who take part in a crusade against the Ottoman Empire for at least six months or who donate funds to support it.<ref>Ludwig Pastor, ''The History of the Popes from the Close of the Middle Ages, Volume III'' (London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner, & Co., 1894), p. 332.</ref>  
* [[November 1]] – The last emperor of [[Trebizond]], [[David of Trebizond|David Megas Komnenos]], is [[decapitation|beheaded]] in Constantinople two years after his capture by the Ottoman Empire, by orders of the Sultan Mehmed II, in addition to his sons Basil and Manuel and his daughter [[Anna Komnene (daughter of David of Trebizond)|Anna]] (who had been a concubine of the Sultan) and two other people.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jackson Williams|first=Kelsey|date=2006|title=A Genealogy of the Grand Komnenoi of Trebizond|url=https://www.academia.edu/167375|journal=Foundations|volume=2|issue=3|pages=171–189|archive-date=2023-11-08|access-date=2025-07-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108225832/https://www.academia.edu/167375|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
* [[November 27]] – [[Skanderbeg]] declares war on the Ottoman Empire and attacks its troops near [[Ohrid]].  
* [[December 1]] – [[Mary of Guelders]], Queen regent of Scotland for her 12-year-old son, [[James III of Scotland|King James III]], dies at the age of 30, prompting the new regent, [[James Kennedy (bishop)|Bishop James Kennedy]], to contact the former King Henry VI of England to mediate a peace between England and Scotland.

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Muhammad Rumfa]] starts to rule in [[Kano (city)|Kano]].
* ''[[Corpus Hermeticum]]'' is translated into [[Latin language|Latin]], by [[Marsilio Ficino]].
</onlyinclude>

1460.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 14]] – After gaining a consensus at  the Council of Mantua, [[Pope Pius II]] formally declares a Christian crusade against the Muslim [[Ottoman Empire]] to recapture [[Constantinople]], which had been captured by the Ottomans in [[1453]].
* [[January 15]] – At the [[Battle of Sandwich (1460)|Battle of Sandwich]] in England, [[Yorkists]] raid [[Sandwich, Kent]], and capture the royal fleet.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Peter Burley|author2=Michael Elliot|author3=Harvey Watson|title=The Battles of St Albans|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DlR-AwAAQBAJ&pg=PA46|date=9 September 2013|publisher=Pen and Sword|isbn=978-1-84415-569-9|pages=46}}</ref>
* [[February 29]] – [[John IV, Duke of Bavaria|Johann IV]] and his brother [[Sigismund, Duke of Bavaria|Sigismund]] of the [[House of Wittelsbach]] become the joint rulers of "[[Bavaria-Munich]]", one of several smaller states that had been fragmented from the original [[Duchy of Bavaria]], upon the death of their father, [[Albert III, Duke of Bavaria|Albrecht III the Pious]]. Albrecht III's third son, [[Albert IV, Duke of Bavaria|Albrecht IV]], will reunite Bavaria-Munich with the other states ([[Bavaria-Landshut]], [[Bavaria-Ingolstadt]] and [[Bavaria-Straubing]]) into a single Duchy of Bavaria in 1503.<ref>{{cite book |title= A House Divided: Wittelsbach Confessional Court Cultures in the Holy Roman Empire, c. 1550-1650 |first=Andrew L. |last=Thomas |publisher=Brill |year=2010|page=387}}</ref>
* [[March 4]] – At Rome on the Wednesday during [[Ember Days]], Pope Pius II addresses an assembly of the College of Cardinals and criticizes most of them, declaring that "Your lifestyle is such that you would appear to have been chosen, not to govern the state, but called to enjoy pleasures. You avoid neither hunting, nor games, nor the company of women. You put together parties that are more opulent than is fitting. You wear clothes that are far too expensive. You overflow with gold and silver."<ref>Pius II, [https://books.google.com/books?id=0DI8AAAAcAAJ&pg=PA176 ''Commentarii'' (1584)], p. 177.</ref> He then directs them to consider the qualities of new candidates for the College. The next day, six cardinals are elected, including [[Pope Pius III|Francesco Nanni-Todeschini-Piccolomini]], the Pope's nephew, who will later become [[Pope Pius III]].
* [[March 5]] – King [[Christian I of Denmark]], the various nobles of the [[Duchy of Schleswig]] and the [[Holstein-Rendsburg|County of Holstein]] agree to the [[Treaty of Ribe]], electing King Christian as the new Duke of Schleswig and Count of Holstein, and placing both political entities under Denmark's control.<ref>Robert Bohn, ''Geschichte Schleswig-Holsteins'' (Munich: Beck Publishing, 2006), ISBN 978-3-406-50891-2</ref> 
* [[March 21]] – After having control of [[Malbork Castle]], the Polish Army begins a siege against the Prussian town of [[Malbork|Marienburg]].

=== April–June ===
* [[April 4]] – The [[University of Basel]] is founded in [[Old Swiss Confederacy|Switzerland]].
* [[May 30]] – [[Demetrios Palaiologos]], the ruler of the Byzantine [[despotate of Morea]] in southern Greece surrenders the capital, [[Mystras]],to the Ottomans. The Ottoman sultan [[Mehmed II]] grants some islands in the Aegean Sea to Palaiologos, and he lives for several years in relative comfort.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last= Gregory |first= Timothy E. |last2= Ševčenko |first2= Nancy Patterson |title= Mistra |editor-last= Kazhdan |editor-first= Alexander |editor-link= Alexander Kazhdan |year=1991 |encyclopedia=[[The Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium]] |publisher= Oxford University Press |isbn= 978-0-19-504652-6 |pages= 1382–1385}}</ref> 
* [[June 3]] – Pope Pius II re-imposes a [[1454]] ban against trade with the [[Prussian Confederation]], and extends it to include a ban against trading with the [[Kingdom of Poland]], after the Prussian states and Poland refuse to join in the proposed crusade against the Ottoman Empire.
* [[June 26]] – [[Wars of the Roses]]: [[Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick]] and [[Edward IV|Edward, Earl of March]] (eldest son of [[Richard Plantagenet, Duke of York]]) land in [[Kingdom of England|England]] at [[Sandwich, Kent]] with an army, and march on London.

=== July–September ===
* [[July 2]] – The city of London opens its gates to the Yorkist invaders and puts up no resistance to their occupation.
* [[July 4]] – The cannons of the [[Tower of London]], still in [[House of Lancaster|Lancastrian]] hands, are fired on the [[city of London]], which is mostly in [[House of York|Yorkist]]. The Tower is surrendered on [[July 19]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Vanora |last=Bennett |author-link=Vanora Bennett |title=London and the Wars of the Roses |url=http://vanorabennett.com/book/figures-in-silk-aka-queen-of-silks-london-and-the-wars-of-the-roses/ |access-date=2013-08-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130914035651/http://vanorabennett.com/book/figures-in-silk-aka-queen-of-silks-london-and-the-wars-of-the-roses/ |archive-date=September 14, 2013 }}</ref>
* [[July 5]] – The town of [[Malbork|Marienburg]] is captured by the Polish army after a four-month siege that had been started by General Proandota Lubieszowski, who had died during the fighting.  
* [[July 10]] – Wars of the Roses – King Henry VI of England is captured as prisoner of war after his army is defeated at the [[Battle of Northampton (1460)|Battle of Northampton]] by the earls of [[Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick|Warwick]] and [[Edward IV of England|March]].<ref name="Cassell's Chronology">{{cite book|last=Williams|first=Hywel|title=Cassell's Chronology of World History|url=https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will|url-access=registration|location=London|publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson|year=2005|isbn=0-304-35730-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/183 183–185]}}</ref> It is agreed that York will be Henry's heir, disinheriting the King's son [[Edward of Westminster, Prince of Wales]]. 
* [[July 30]] – King Henry VI summons the English Parliament to assemble at Westminster on October 7.
* [[August 3]] – King [[James II of Scotland]] is killed by the explosion of a [[cannon]] which he had purchased from [[Flanders]] as part of acquiring the most up-to-date military technology for Scotland. The King had been supervising the bombardment of [[Roxburgh Castle]] during a siege to force out the English occupation troops.<ref name=Royle/> Historian [[Robert Lindsay of Pitscottie]] later writes "as the King stood near a piece of artillery, his thigh bone was dug in two with a piece of misframed gun that brake in shooting, by which he was stricken to the ground and died hastily.<ref>quoted in {{Cite web |url=http://www.englishmonarchs.co.uk/stewart_4.htm |title=Scottish Monarchs – Kings and Queens of Scotland – James II |last=Mahoney |first=Mike |website=www.englishmonarchs.co.uk |access-date=11 October 2016}}</ref>  He is succeeded by his 8-year-old son, who becomes [[James III of Scotland|King James III]], with power exercised by the boy's mother, the Queen Regent [[Mary of Guelders]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Scottish Queens, 1034–1714 |last=Marshall |first=Rosalind K. |year=2003 |publisher=Tuckwell Press|page=66}}</ref> 
* [[August 8]] – [[Sigismund of Austria|Sigismund]], the [[Duke of Austria]], is [[excommunication|excommunicated]] from the Roman Catholic Church by Pope Pius II and has his domains placed under an [[interdict]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Creighton | title= A History of the Papacy during the period of the Reformation| date= 21 March 1882|volume= II|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PfdJAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA412}}, pp. 412-413.</ref> 
* [[September 14]] – The [[Siege of Trebizond (1461)|siege]] of [[Trabzond|Trebizond]], the capital of the [[Empire of Trebizond]], is started by the Ottoman Empire.<ref>Franz Babinger, [http://www.persee.fr/web/revues/home/prescript/article/rebyz_0766-5598_1949_num_7_1_1014 "La date de la prise de Trébizonde par les Turcs (1461)"], ''Revue des études byzantines'', '''7''' (1949), pp.
205–207 {{doi|10.3406/rebyz.1949.1014}}</ref> The Trebizond Emperor, [[David of Trebizond|David Megas Komnenos]] withstands the siege for almost a year.

=== October–December === 
* [[October 7]] – The 22nd parliament of Henry VI is opened, and the House of Commons elects [[John Green (speaker)|John Green]] as its speaker. 
* [[October 10]] – [[Richard of York|Richard, Duke of York]] enters the Council Chamber, places his hand upon the throne, and announces that he is the rightful King of England. He then takes up residence at the royal palace.<ref>{{cite book |title=Soldier, Rebel, Traitor: John, Lord Wenlock and the Wars of the Roses |last=Brondarbit |first=A. R .|publisher=Pen & Sword |isbn=978-1-39900-347-6 |year=2022 |page=117 |location=Barnsley}}</ref>  
* [[October 25]] – The [[Act of Accord]], passed by the Parliament of England, is given royal assent by [[Henry VI of England|King Henry VI]] as a compromise to end the War of the Roses between King Henry's supporters (the Lancastrians) and the supporters of [[Richard of York]] (the Yorkists). Under the law, King Henry is permitted to rule England for the rest of his life, but his son, [[Edward of Westminster, Prince of Wales]] is removed from the right of succession and Richard of York and his descendants are granted the right to rule upon King Henry's death.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Haigh |first=P. A. |title=From Wakefield to Towton: The Wars of the Roses |date=2002|publisher=Leo Cooper |page=38 |isbn=978-0-85052-825-1 | location=Bradford}}</ref>
* [[November 7]] – King [[James II of Cyprus]] orders his chief minister, George Boustronios, to travel to [[Larnaca]], and to round up "both the serfs and emancipated peasants, both mounted and on foot", to be delivered to the King at Nicosia to be drafted into the King's army, with the promise of  benefits to the peasants and emancipation to the serfs.<ref>"The Hospitallers and their manumissions of Rhodian and Cypriot serfes (1409—1459)", by Nicholas Coureas, in ''The Military Orders Volume VII: Piety, Pugnacity and Property'', ed. by Nicholas Morton (Taylor & Francis, 2019) p.157</ref> 
* [[December 2]] – In Spain, the popular [[Charles, Prince of Viana|Prince Carlos de Viana]], heir to the throne of Navarre, is arrested at [[Lleida]] and jailed in [[Morella, Castellón|Morella]] by order of his father, [[John II of Aragon|King Juan II]], leading to an uprising in [[Catalonia]]. King Juan eventually yields and frees Prince Carlos two months later on February 25.<ref name=bisson148>{{cite book |last=Bisson |first=T. N. |year=1986 |title=The Medieval Crown of Aragon: A Short History |publisher=Clarendon Press |isbn=0-19-820236-9 |page=[https://books.google.com/books?id=b_NncxsOhdQC&PA=148 148]}}</ref>
* [[December 30]] – [[Wars of the Roses]] – [[Richard of York]], set to be the next King of England, is killed along with his son, [[Edmund, Earl of Rutland]], at the [[Battle of Wakefield]] as a Lancastrian army under [[Henry Beaufort, 3rd Duke of Somerset|Henry Beaufort, Duke of Somerset]] and [[Henry Percy, 3rd Earl of Northumberland|Henry Percy, Earl of Northumberland]] decisively defeats the Yorkists. York's son [[Edward IV of England|Edward]] becomes leader of the Yorkist faction and the heir to the English throne.<ref>{{cite book|author=Philip A. Haigh|title=The Battle of Wakefield, 30 December 1460|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=N1txAAAAIAAJ|year=1996|publisher=Sutton|isbn=978-0-7509-1342-3}}</ref>

=== Date unknown ===
* [[Ali Bey Mihaloğlu]] captures [[Michael Szilágyi]].
* Portuguese navigator [[Pedro de Sintra]] reaches the coast of modern-day [[Sierra Leone]].
* A famine breaks out in the [[Deccan Plateau]] of India.
* A monk, Leonardo da Pistoia, arrives in [[Florence]] from [[Macedonia (region)|Macedonia]], with the ''[[Corpus Hermeticum]]''.</onlyinclude>

1456.events:
<onlyinclude>

=== January–March ===
* [[January 6]] – After two years as [[List of ecumenical patriarchs of Constantinople|Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople]], the Eastern Orthodox Christian partriarch in the Islamic Ottoman Empire, [[Gennadius Scholarius]] resigns, and [[Isidore II of Constantinople|Isidore II]] is elected to replace him.<ref>{{EB1911|wstitle=Gennadius II|volume=11|pages=596–597}}</ref><ref>{{Catholic|wstitle=Gennadius II}}</ref>
* [[January 24]] – After [[Dorino II Gattilusio]] seizes ownership of the Greek mainland harbor of [[Enez|Ainos]] and the islands of [[Samothrace]] and [[Imbros]], Ottoman Sultan [[Mehmed II]] orders a blockade the port with 10 ships and leads a ground invasion. After the surrender off Ainos, Mehmed II sends his Admiral [[:tr:Has Yunus Bey|Mirza Yunus Beg]] commences the [[Aegan Expedition (1456)|take control of Samothrace and Imbros]].<ref>{{cite book |last = Babinger |first = Franz |author-link = Franz Babinger |others = Translated from the German by [[Ralph Manheim]]. Edited, with a preface, by William C. Hickman |title = Mehmed the Conqueror and His Time |publisher = Princeton University Press |location = Princeton, New Jersey |series = Bollingen Series 96|year=1978|isbn=0-691-09900-6}}</ref>
* [[February 25]] –
**The [[Treaty of Yazhelbitsy]] is signed between the [[Grand Principality of Moscow]] (led by Grand Prince Vasily II) and the [[Novgorod Republic]] (governed by [[:ru:Шуйский, Василий Васильевич Гребёнка|Vasily Shuisky]]) with Vasily II becoming the [[Prince of Novgorod]].<ref>"Vasily II Vasilievich", in ''Veliky Novgorod: History and Culture of the 9th to 17th centuries'', ed. by A. M. Stepanov (St. Petersburg: Nestor-Istoriya 2007)</ref>
**As King [[Henry VI of England]] recovers from a three-month bout with mental illness, [[Richard Plantagenet, Duke of York]] steps down as [[Lord Protector#Feudal royal regent|Protector of the Realm]] and the King resumes his duties.<ref>{{cite book |last=Lewis |date=2016 |first=Matthew |title=Richard, Duke of York: King by Right |publisher=Amberley Publishing |place=Stroud  |isbn=978-1-4456-4744-9}}</ref> The Duke of York had served as regent since November 19, and had previously been Lord Protector for 10 months during  1454 and 1455.<ref>{{Cite EB1911|wstitle= York, Richard, Duke of |volume= 28 |last= Kingsford |first= Charles Lethbridge |author-link= Charles Lethbridge Kingsford | pages=926–927}}</ref>
* [[March 12]] – After a session of eight months that had started on July 9, 1455, the [[English Parliament]] adjourns at Westminster. Royal assent is given by King Henry VI to bills passed, including the [[Importation Act 1455]], banning the import for the next five years of woven silk goods (including ribbons and girdles) that had been manufactured outside of England, and subjecting importers to heavy fines.<ref>William Cunningham, ''The Growth of English Industry and Commerce during the Early and Middle Ages.
